items.description: Four hours of ReBoot. Mainframe's finest battling viruses in full CGI. This looked like the future in the '90s and honestly it still kind of does.

items.description: Six hours of '90s animated kids' shows on VHS. The tape that has everything. Whatever you're looking for, it's probably in here somewhere. Dig in.

items.title: Fox Box: Shaman, Turtles, Funky & Sonic
items.description: Shaman King, Ninja Turtles, Funky Cops, and Sonic X. The Fox Box Saturday lineup. Wake up, pour the cereal, watch all of them. In that order.

items.title: Cartoon Tape: Boomerang, CN & Kids' WB
items.description: Boomerang, Cartoon Network, and Kids' WB all on one tape. Over two hours of cartoon chaos. Three channels, one remote, zero plans to go outside today.

items.title: All in the Family — Five-Hour Marathon
items.description: Five straight hours in Archie Bunker's living room — the show that made half the country argue with the other half from the same couch. Stifle yourself and settle in; the block runs back to back.

items.id: 14-may-1993-lawrence-welk-major-dad-roanna-murphy-brown-last-cheers-dr.-quinn/14- May 1993 Lawrence Welk Major Dad Roanna Murphy Brown Last Cheers Dr. Quinn.mp4
items.title: Murphy Brown, Cheers & Dr. Quinn (May '93)
items.description: A night off the antenna in mid-May '93: Major Dad, Murphy Brown trading fire, Cheers pouring its very last rounds, and Dr. Quinn riding in to close. Somebody's VCR saved the whole evening, commercials and all.

items.id: alfred-hitchcock-any-griffith-man-from-uncle-get-smart-x-2-mr.-and-mrs.-notyh-the-persuaders/Alfred Hitchcock Any Griffith Man from Uncle Get Smart x2 Mr. and  Mrs. Notyh The Persuaders.mp4
items.title: Hitchcock, Andy Griffith & Get Smart
items.description: Welcome to the goodness: Hitchcock's droll menace, Mayberry front porches, and a double dose of Maxwell Smart missing it by that much, with The Man from U.N.C.L.E. and The Persuaders riding along. Black-and-white primetime by the yard.

items.id: dick-tracy-outer-limits-ben-casey-flying-nun-i-spy-mission-impossible/Dick Tracy Outer Limits Ben Casey Flying Nun I Spy  Mission Impossible.mp4
items.title: Outer Limits, I Spy & Mission: Impossible
items.description: The goodness continues: a nun that flies, doctors in crisis, and tapes that self-destruct in five seconds. Do not attempt to adjust your set — that's just how the cassette came.

items.id: one-step-beyond-dobie-gillis-maya-x-2-the-new-zorro-x-2-combat-x-2/One Step Beyond Dobie Gillis Maya x2 The New Zorro x2 Combat x2.mp4
items.title: One Step Beyond, Zorro & Combat!
items.description: Around the world on a single cassette: Dobie Gillis mooning, double helpings of jungle-adventure Maya, a new Zorro carving his initials, and two rounds of Combat! — with One Step Beyond up front to make sure you don't sleep well.

items.title: NBC Thursday — Family Ties, Cheers & Night Court (Jan. '86)
items.description: Family Ties, Cheers, Night Court and Hill Street Blues: the whole Thursday ladder, taped by someone who knew what they had.

items.id: nbc-aarons-way-highway-to-heaven/NBC Aaron's Way Highway to Heaven.ia.mp4
items.title: NBC Wednesday — Aaron's Way & Highway to Heaven (Mar. '88)
items.description: Aaron's Way settles an Amish family into California, then Highway to Heaven sends its angel to fix someone's week. A Wednesday night with a tissue box in reach.

items.id: vhs-tape-1989-knbc-three-episodes-of-quantum-leap-tape-2-of-2/VHS Tape - 1989 - KNBC - Three Episodes of Quantum Leap - Tape 2 of 2.ia.mp4
items.title: Quantum Leap — Three Episodes ('89)
items.description: Three straight leaps taped off KNBC in '89, Los Angeles commercials intact. Oh boy — Sam sets right what once went wrong while the VCR quietly does the same for television history.

items.id: space-rangers-january-20-1993-seinfeld-x-2-spies-mata-hari-the-seductive-spy/Space Rangers (January 20, 1993) ~ Seinfeld x2 ~ Spies- Mata Hari The Seductive Spy.mp4
items.title: Space Rangers & Double Seinfeld (Jan. '93)
items.description: A sci-fi show that lasted six episodes, then two Seinfelds about nothing. Nobody programmed this lineup twice, and that's what makes it perfect.

items.id: vhs-tape-1993-09-15-wftv-home-improvement-thea-moon-over-miami-coach-lottery-drawing-news/VHS Tape - 1993-09-15 - WFTV - Home Improvement, Thea, Moon Over Miami, Coach, Lottery Drawing, News.mp4
items.title: ABC Night — Home Improvement, Coach & Thea (Sept. '93)
items.description: Tim Taylor grunts, brand-new fall shows Thea and Moon Over Miami take their shot, and Coach hollers. A whole ABC night on one tape, commercials and all.

items.id: vhs-tape-1993-11-06-wesh-mad-about-you-wings-seinfeld-frasier-1993-11-24-wftv-ho/VHS Tape - 1993-11-06 - WESH - Mad About You, Wings, Seinfeld, Frasier - 1993-11-24 - WFTV - Home Improvement, Grace Under Fire, A Gala for the President at Ford's Theatre, News.mp4
items.title: NBC Must See — Mad About You, Seinfeld & Frasier (Nov 1993)
items.description: The lineup NBC built Thursdays on — Mad About You, Wings, Seinfeld, first-season Frasier — plus a side of Home Improvement and a presidential gala for the road. Appointment television; appointment kept.

items.id: vhs-tape-october-1993-wcpx-star-trek-the-next-generation-star-trek-deep-space-ni/VHS Tape - October 1993 - WCPX - Star Trek the Next Generation, Star Trek Deep Space Nine, ALCS Chicago White Sox vs. Toronto Blue Jays.mp4
items.title: Star Trek: TNG & Deep Space Nine (Oct. '93)
items.description: An October night off Orlando's Channel 6: the Enterprise-D in its final season and Deep Space Nine in its second. Syndication, boldly taped.

items.title: NBC & Fox Wednesday — Prime Time to Beverly Hills, 90210 (Sept. '95)
items.description: Beverly Hills, 90210 on a local tape, where the zip code drama and the Wendy's ad get exactly the same respect.

items.id: 3rd-rock-from-the-sun-wull-and-grace-the-jeff-foxworthy-show-mr.-rock-the-ring-o/3rd Rock from the Sun Wull and Grace The Jeff Foxworthy Show Mr. Rock The Ring Orlando night news partial.mp4
items.title: 3rd Rock, Boston Common, Foxworthy & Mr. Rhodes ('96)
items.description: A fall NBC night off a Florida VCR: aliens in Ohio, two college kids in Boston, a comic dad, a novelist back at prep school. The commercials stayed in, and the last thing on the tape is a promise of more.

items.title: NBC Saturday — Profiler (May '97)
items.description: Two hours of Profiler, a killer named Jack with a taste for the dark, and a Chevy Blazer lease ad that keeps the mood from getting too comfortable.

items.title: NBC Saturday — The Pretender & Profiler (Nov. '97)
items.description: Saturday on NBC means two dark dramas back to back. A genius with a hundred faces, then a woman who can read a killer from the crime scene.

items.title: Seinfeld — The Finale (May '98)
items.description: The whole country sat down to watch four people get judged for a show about nothing. The commercials stayed in, which is right, because everyone was watching those too.

items.title: The Drew Carey Show / Whose Line Is It Anyway? (1998)
items.description: ABC's 1998 Wednesday one-two: Cleveland rocks, then improv where everything's made up and the points don't matter. Commercials intact — a thousand points to whoever kept this tape.

items.title: ABC Wednesday — Dharma & Greg & The Drew Carey Show (Sept. '98)
items.description: Dharma & Greg, Two Guys, a Girl and a Pizza Place, and The Drew Carey Show on an ABC Wednesday. The New Beetle ad is in the mix too, still unbelievably cute.

items.title: ABC TGIF — Two of a Kind to Brother's Keeper (Dec. '98)
items.description: Friday night in Christmas week, with Two of a Kind and Brother's Keeper in the Santa hat. A black cat in one is the most dignified thing between the shows.

items.id: vhs-tape-1999.08.22-wofl-three-episodes-of-magnum-p.i.-1999.08.24-wofl-remington-steele/VHS Tape - 1999.08.22 - WOFL - Three Episodes of Magnum P.I., 1999.08.24 - WOFL - Remington Steele.mp4
items.title: Magnum, P.I. & Remington Steele (Aug. '99)
items.description: Late-August 1999 syndication off WOFL: three Hawaiian-shirted Magnums back to back, then Remington Steele solving crimes in better suits. The little voice says keep watching.

items.title: CBS Thursday — Survivor, CSI & Big Apple (Mar. '01)
items.description: Survivor, CSI and Big Apple on one CBS Thursday. The tribe gets voted out, the lab gets its close-ups, and the Doritos ad wins every time.

items.title: TV Land — All in the Family Tribute Marathon (June '01)
items.description: Carroll O'Connor died on June 21, 2001; the next day TV Land cleared the schedule and let Archie hold the chair all night. A tribute marathon exactly as it aired — bumpers, ads, and a nation grieving in reruns.

items.title: TBS Superstation & TNT — July 2001
items.description: High summer 2001 on the superstations — basic-cable movies-and-reruns comfort food and every commercial that paid for it. The air conditioner hums; nobody reaches for the remote.

items.title: NBC Thursday — ER Season Finale (May '01)
items.description: A season finale hour of ER, with the Thursday promos intact and a late-night host promising a movie star. Somebody taped over an old tape for it, which tells you what the night was worth.

items.id: wb-friday-night-sabrina-raising-dad-reba-maybe-its-me-2002-04-05-kdaf-woc/WB Friday Night (Sabrina, Raising Dad, Reba, Maybe It's Me) 2002-04-05 -KDAF WOC.mp4
items.title: WB Friday Night — Sabrina, Reba & More (2002)
items.description: The WB's family-hour Friday, spring 2002: Sabrina's spells, Raising Dad, Reba's one-liners, and Maybe It's Me — with every Michigan J. Frog promo left right where it aired.

items.title: FOX Sunday — The Simpsons & the X-Files Finale (May '02)
items.description: Sunday on FOX: Springfield first, then Mulder's long case closes. The tape opens on VCR blue, so you know someone pressed record with real intent.

items.id: AFarewellToFriendsADatelineSpecial20040505KXAS/A Farewell to Friends - A Dateline Special - 2004-05-05  -KXAS.mp4
items.title: A Farewell to Friends — Dateline Special (May '04)
items.description: May 2004, the week the couch at Central Perk emptied out: Dateline throws primetime's biggest going-away party, taped off Dallas–Fort Worth's KXAS with commercials intact. Could this tape BE any more of a time capsule?

items.id: vhs-fb-market-box-2-tape-36-part-3-discovery-channel-real-tv-lapd-jerry-springer-a-e-real-tv/VHS FB Market Box 2 Tape 36 part 1 - Real TV - Unsolved Mysteries -Cochran & Company - Primetime Live.mp4
items.title: Basic Cable Grab Bag — Real TV, Jerry Springer & Discovery
items.description: Part three of a flea-market shoebox tape: Real TV's dashboard-cam mayhem, Springer's chair ballet, LAPD ride-alongs, and Discovery filler. You never knew what the tape had next; neither did whoever recorded it.

items.title: NBC Primetime — The Seinfeld Finale (May 1998)
items.description: May 14, 1998: NBC says goodbye to the show about nothing, with the wall-to-wall hype, clip retrospectives, and commercials that came with 76 million people watching at once. An era ends, yada yada yada.

items.id: vhs-tape-hbo-two-episodes-of-perversions-of-science-entertainment-news-special-e/VHS Tape - HBO - Two Episodes of Perversions of Science, Entertainment News Special Edition - Spawn - House of Cards.mp4
items.title: HBO Late Night — Perversions of Science & Spawn
items.description: Premium cable after the kids went to bed: two twisted tales from Perversions of Science, HBO's animated Spawn brooding in the dark, and entertainment-news chatter in between. This is what the descrambler was for.

items.title: ABC Night — Home Improvement & Michael Jackson Talks to Oprah (Feb 1993)
items.description: Tim and Al open the Tool Time mail, then ABC hands ninety minutes to Oprah Winfrey and Michael Jackson at his Neverland ranch, with Elizabeth Taylor dropping by. A sitcom and an event, same couch, same night.

items.title: ABC Friday Night — Family Matters, Step by Step & Sabrina in 3D (May 1997)
items.description: The last spring Family Matters and Step by Step called ABC home, before both moved to CBS that fall. Here they have the TGIF block, Mother's Day ads and Sabrina in 3D, glasses bug and all.

items.id: local-nbc-and-abc-shows-labelled-tdk-black-ehg/Local, NBC, and ABC Shows [labelled tdk black ehg].mp4
items.title: Five Hours of Local, NBC & ABC (Unlabeled TDK Tape)
items.description: A black TDK tape with no label and five hours of somebody's ordinary television — local news, network primetime, whatever came on next. Nobody meant to make a time capsule; that's what makes it one.

items.title: Pilot (Millennium)
items.description: The Blacks settle in Seattle, and Frank Black begins tracking a serial killer whose victims include a stripper. It opens backstage in a dressing room. The Millennium Group is about to enter the file.

items.title: Gehenna (Millennium)
items.description: Frank travels to San Francisco to investigate a series of gruesome cult killings. Rain, headlights on a wet road, a hospital corridor late at night. The memo says cult. We have notes.

items.title: Dead Letters (Millennium)
items.description: A murder in Portland, Oregon puts Frank beside a Millennium Group member who is struggling personally. A clown doll, twin children and a hospital nursery are on the exhibit list. Partners, officially.

items.title: Moving Targets (Dark Skies)
items.description: Dark Skies picks the day of the JFK assassination for John Loengard and Kim Sayers to visit Jesse Marcel and learn how Majestic 12 began in 1947. A grey alien is somewhere in the file.

items.title: Mercury Rising (Dark Skies)
items.description: Kim has visions of an astronaut being taken by the Hive, so she and John head to Florida as Ranger 6 readies the first close-up images of the Moon for NASA. Somebody has a head start.

items.title: Traces to Nowhere (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Cooper checks into the Great Northern Hotel and meets Audrey Horne, an unruly teenager. With Sheriff Truman he questions Laura's boyfriend, James Hurley, and the other names on the list. Politely, for now.

items.id: twin-peaks-1x-00-pilot/Twin Peaks [1x02] Zen, or the Skill to Catch a Killer.mp4
items.title: Zen, or the Skill to Catch a Killer (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Cooper tries an unusual technique on his list of suspects, while forensic specialist Albert Rosenfield arrives to do Laura's autopsy. Cooper also starts having vivid dreams about the case. Procedure is a loose term.

items.title: Rest in Pain (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Audrey offers Cooper a clue about One Eyed Jacks, and Laura's funeral is arranged. Cooper is also introduced to the Bookhouse Boys, a secret society tracking drug trafficking in town. Small town, big filing system.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 03 - Eine Kleine Frohike.ia.mp4
items.title: Eine Kleine Frohike (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: With Yves's help, Frohike tries to convince a woman suspected of being a Nazi war criminal that he is her long-lost son. The disguises are terrible. The Gunmen's ethics committee was not consulted.

items.title: Subject: Fearsum (FreakyLinks)
items.description: Internet sleuth Derek Barnes looks into the death of his twin brother and is drawn into the mystery of a vanished colonial settlement. A family matter, then a historical one. Someone named Adam keeps coming up.

items.id: freakylinks_202603/Freakylinks S01E03 Subject Edith Keeler Must Die.mp4
items.title: Subject: Edith Keeler Must Die (FreakyLinks)
items.description: Field trip. Derek and his friends set out to hunt alligators in New York City's sewers, and find that something more dangerous has targeted them. Bring a flashlight and a very good excuse.

items.title: Subject: Coelacanth This! (FreakyLinks)
items.description: A small town's mysterious deaths go back about 150 years, and Derek's group follows them to a secret hidden in the nearby woods. Cold cases do not get much colder.

items.title: The Judge (Millennium)
items.description: Grisly evidence leads Frank to a vengeful killer who recruits ex-convicts to do the violence for him. John Hawkes and Marshall Bell guest. Think of it as a staffing problem with a body count.

items.title: 522666 (Millennium)
items.description: A bomb goes off in a crowded Washington, D.C. bar, and the clever bomber behind it taunts the authorities while planning another attack. He wants an audience, and he is getting one.

items.title: Kingdom Come (Millennium)
items.description: A killer is targeting members of the clergy, apparently out of shattered faith. Frank pursues him alongside a Group member he once worked with on a case that went unsolved. There is a confessional on the set.

items.title: Dark Days Night (Dark Skies)
items.description: In New York, John and Kim learn the Hive plans to hijack the Beatles' appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show. Dark Skies has a theory about that night, and it is not the haircuts.

items.title: Inhuman Nature (Dark Skies)
items.description: In Wisconsin, John and Kim suspect the recent cattle mutilations hide a Hive plan to build a genetic weapon. The farmers are counting cows. The file is counting something else.

items.title: Ancient Future (Dark Skies)
items.description: An earthquake exposes an ancient spacecraft buried in Alaska, and John and Kim have to make a deal with Majestic 12 to head off catastrophe. The lesser risk is, apparently, the people who lie to them.

items.title: The One-Armed Man (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Cooper tries to match the figures from his dream to real people in town. Hawk goes looking for the one-armed man, and the investigators look into a veterinarian named Bob. The dream is evidence now.

items.title: Cooper's Dreams (Twin Peaks)
items.description: The police search Jacques Renault's apartment and cabin, and Cooper meets the Log Lady, who claims her log witnessed events the night of the murder. A witness list with an unusual entry.

items.title: Realization Time (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Audrey gets a job at One Eyed Jacks. Maddy Ferguson agrees to pose as Laura to lure Dr. Jacoby out of his office so James and Donna can search it. Amateur surveillance, with a borrowed face.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 04 - Like Water for Octane.ia.mp4
items.title: Like Water for Octane (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: The Gunmen go looking for a water-powered car and run into missile silos, government clerks who help no one, and cows. The cows are the part nobody briefed them on.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 05 - Three Men and a Smoking Diaper.ia.mp4
items.title: Three Men and a Smoking Diaper (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: While investigating a murder linked to a senator running for reelection, the Gunmen get stuck babysitting. Research, a campaign rally and one baby, all at once. Jimmy and Yves are along for it.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 07 - Planet of the Frohikes.ia.mp4
items.title: Planet of the Frohikes (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: The Gunmen receive an email from a clever chimp calling himself Simon White-Thatch Potentloins, who is trying to escape a government laboratory. Reply-all is not recommended.

items.id: freakylinks_202603/Freakylinks S01E05 Subject Desert Squid! Myth or Legend.mp4
items.title: Subject: Desert Squid! Myth or Legend (FreakyLinks)
items.description: East Texas, a camper, a labeled VHS tape and a rumor about a desert squid. De Santo's logo is on the box. Findings: [REDACTED]. Trust the tape, and nobody else in the camper.

items.title: Subject: The Harbingers (FreakyLinks)
items.description: Derek and the group follow Adam's final days to a quirky town full of psychics. Amelinda Smith guests. In a town where everyone claims to know what comes next, the group has questions about what already happened.

items.id: freakylinks_202603/Freakylinks S01E07 Subject Still I Rise.mp4
items.title: Subject: Still I Rise (FreakyLinks)
items.description: Derek examines the case of a dead hip-hop singer who is believed to have returned from the grave as a zombie. Rumour has the singer up and about. The site's job is to ask who is saying so.

items.title: Encounters: The Hidden Truth (FOX, July '94)
items.description: Fox's answer to Sightings: a man with a camcorder full of UFOs, a Midwest herd with its own cattle-mutilation mystery, and a disclaimer up front inviting you to make up your own mind. Recorded off Fox with the ads in.

items.title: Encounters: The Hidden Truth on FOX (July '94)
items.description: A psychic on a missing-girl case, an exorcism in St. Louis, and kids who remember earlier lives. A UFO hotline number runs between the news breaks, so have a pen ready.

items.title: Blood Relatives (Millennium)
items.description: Catherine Black, a clinical social worker, applies her expertise to murders of people recently bereaved. Frank's usual beat is the killer; hers is the people left behind. Different file, same house.

items.title: The Well-Worn Lock (Millennium)
items.description: An incest case leads Catherine Black to a woman who has kept a secret for 23 years. Support group, courtroom, a troubled household. A drama about people first and a case second.

items.title: Wide Open (Millennium)
items.description: A shadowy killer commits brutal murders, and the only clues sit in the memory of a traumatized child who watched her parents die. A kindergarten teacher is in the frame. Not an easy hour.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: Season three of Sightings opens at a house where a couple says a ghost named Sally leaves scratches and a freezing aura, with an artist describing his process in between.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: Tunguska, spontaneous human combustion, a Chehalis crop circle and electronic voices: a fast lap of the unexplained. Tunguska, for the record, flattened forest across a stretch of Siberia.

items.title: The X-Files: X-Cops
items.description: A handheld COPS-style crew rides along with Los Angeles sheriff's deputies on a creature call, and two FBI agents turn up uninvited. Vince Gilligan wrote it, and the camera never leaves the shoulder.

items.title: Hostile Convergence (Dark Skies)
items.description: A reported close encounter in Socorro, New Mexico sends John and Jesse Marcel after secret UFO blueprints, in a race against Majestic 12. Whoever reaches the paperwork first writes the history.

items.title: We Shall Overcome (Dark Skies)
items.description: Dark Skies files real history under alien business. Amid a string of civil rights murders, John reconnects with Mark Simonson, his former supervisor from Congressman Pratt's office. Raphael Sbarge plays him.

items.title: The Last Wave (Dark Skies)
items.description: A funeral for an old college friend brings John and Kim to Los Angeles, where they uncover a Hive plot involving the water supply. A surf party figures in, and it has a dark side.

items.title: The Last Evening (Twin Peaks)
items.description: Cooper goes undercover at One Eyed Jacks as a drug financier. Meanwhile the investigators examine Laura's tapes. Two ways of finding out what a person was really doing.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 08 - Maximum Byers.ia.mp4
items.title: Maximum Byers (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: A mother asks for help, so Byers and Jimmy Bond get themselves into a Texas prison posing as death row inmates, to prove her son innocent. Not their usual stakeout.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 09 - Diagnosis, Jimmy.ia.mp4
items.title: Diagnosis, Jimmy (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: Laid up in the hospital, Jimmy begins to suspect his doctor is a wanted killer. Meanwhile the Gunmen try to stop a man who kills grizzly bears to sell their gallbladders. Two cases; one of them is on a drip.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 10 - Tango de los Pistoleros.ia.mp4
items.title: Tango de los Pistoleros (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: Yves and Frohike go undercover as tango dancers to stop a man who is selling government secrets. The secrets are the serious part. Frohike in dance shoes is the rest.

items.id: freakylinks_202603/Freakylinks S01E08 Subject Me and My Shadow.mp4
items.title: Subject: Me and My Shadow (FreakyLinks)
items.description: Chloe is asked to consult on a boy who is terrified of the dark after witnessing a mass-murder scene where the cause of death is unknown. Hard to blame him for wanting the lights on.

items.title: Weeds (Millennium)
items.description: Kidnappings and assaults of teenage boys inside a guarded, affluent community lead Frank to suspect a resident of vigilante violence. The security was excellent. It was pointed outward.

items.title: Loin Like a Hunting Flame (Millennium)
items.description: In Colorado, Frank and an insightful associate go after a killer driven by sexual compulsions who uses mood-altering drugs on his victims. Millennium goes lurid here; the memo notes it and moves on.

items.title: Force Majeure (Millennium)
items.description: An enigmatic man obsessed with the Millennium Group haunts Frank through a case built on planetary alignments, genetic cloning and Judgment Day. The watcher is, for once, not Frank. Brad Dourif guests.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel with a Houston werewolf story as the headliner, and promos for Farscape and Lexx running beside the credits: the channel's weird-science evening on one tape.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: Sightings leaning conspiracy: a small plane vanishes and its tower transcript leaks, and the HAARP antenna array in Alaska is on the docket.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: Sightings pairs a haunting with a taste for paranormal pranks with 1950s UFO photographs from the archives and a space rock heading for Earth.

items.title: The Enemy Within (Dark Skies)
items.description: John visits his family in Fresno to cash in savings bonds, an errand as ordinary as Dark Skies gets, until the visit takes a troubling turn involving his brother. Home, with a file attached.

items.id: the-lone-gunmen-complete-series/The LONE Gunmen - Ep. 11 - The Lying Game.ia.mp4
items.title: The Lying Game (The Lone Gunmen)
items.description: The death of Byers's college roommate sends the Gunmen digging, and the evidence points at FBI Assistant Director Walter Skinner. It opens on a stand-up in a Delaware club.

items.title: The X-Files: Fight the Future
items.description: Between seasons five and six, the conspiracy went theatrical: bees, black oil, and a ship under the Antarctic ice. The rare mythology episode with a catering budget.

items.title: Sightings on the Sci-Fi Channel
items.description: UFO reports around Chillicothe and a computer said to be able to hold a person's thoughts: Sightings goes from Ohio skies to the future of the mind, then pyramids and, finally, the Moon.

items.title: Worm City
items.description: Eric Glass's sketch show for teenagers, the edgy one: a plunger, rubbery warped faces, a newscast staffed by kids, and two men in wigs at a diner. Stay for the credits. They wrote their own theme song.

items.title: Snow Ghost: Making your own fun
items.description: Bruce and Mike visit an art festival and talk to people about making your own fun. Topics include boy bands, bike lanes, and the Road to the Metal Kingdoms. This is not a metaphor.

items.title: Countrockula's Theater for the Insane
items.description: A Minneapolis cable-access horror host and an hour of barrage-edited public domain oddities. Nobody asked for it at 2 AM, which is exactly when it works.

items.title: Zontar, The Show From Bedford: The Beach Girls and the Monster
items.description: A local horror host walks you into a beach-party monster picture the old local-TV way: the intros come first. Some titles need an announcer, and this one found his.

items.title: Fronk: To Catch a Fronk
items.description: A Humboldt County mini-series about the world ending on schedule, and this chapter goes hunting. The effects are homemade, the conviction is total, and the stakeout is the show.

items.title: Southern Oregon News Network: Don't Press the Button
items.description: Jimmy "the tool" talks boxing and nudity. Aspen interviews the Freckin Tinkers. Gordon presses the button. Nobody explains what the button does.

items.title: Shilling Shockers: Penny Dreadful and Garou in Worcester
items.description: A horror host arrives by broom at a Worcester book shop and explains how Garou brought her back to life. Mad monster love at first sight, kept short, as it should be.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Oma-Ha! hands the half hour to Yer Mom's Comedy Show: Betsy Miller, Patty Fanciullo and Kendra Karbowski, against the same brick wall and blue curtain, at one point all three on stools. Call yer mom.

items.title: Everybody's Channel
items.description: A documentary about public access television in America — its history, its ideology, and the beautiful delusion that anyone would watch it. They were right. You're watching it.

items.title: Fronk: In the Nick of Time
items.description: Doomsday is on the calendar in Humboldt County, and it gets covered like a local news special: sober, a little hurried, and running out of time right on cue.

items.title: Let The Truth Be Told Ted Gunderson Talks The Illuminati
items.description: A former FBI agent goes on public access to discuss the Illuminati for a full hour. The host does not push back. There is no reason to push back. This is public access.

items.title: The Uncle Floyd Show: Clips
items.description: A zany New Jersey UHF kiddie show that grown-ups tuned in to on purpose, in on a joke the kids never needed. Vivino hosts, the clips are from the 80s, and there is no plot to catch up on.

items.title: Atomic TV: The 200th Episode
items.description: Atomic TV throws itself a 200th-episode party at Baltimore's Senator Theater, with Jeff Krulik's Worst of Public Access overview on the bill. Krulik co-made Heavy Metal Parking Lot, so he knows.

items.title: Home Videos Experimental Video
items.description: Ohio access TV, experimental video, and a title that promises nothing. That is the setup 2 AM was built for: you will know what it was when it ends, or you will not, and either way you watched.

items.title: The Staged Life
items.description: ONTV's sketch show premieres with Kayla Sharp and Sydney Ryan making Halloween crafts in a kitchen for longer than you would think. A man in a wig holds down a log cabin. Lake Orion commits.

items.title: Off The Hook
items.description: From deep in the WCCA TV video vault — Ricky Jam hosts the wacky Off The Hook show, circa 1990. Channel 39. Episode 13. Lucky number.

items.title: Mysterious Norwood
items.description: Norwood, Ohio, tells its ghost stories: interviews against black, a statue of Mary, a house that is no longer there. It signs off with a card that says happy halloween, in lower case, like a note left on a door.

items.title: Snow Ghost Community Show
items.description: Bruce and Mike interview a Catholic Worker about the medicinal effects of the Three Stooges. The effects have not been investigated. The conversation happens anyway.

items.title: Count Gore De Vol's Creature Feature: Gore Meets the Langley Punks
items.description: Washington's Count Gore De Vol hands his Creature Feature to the Langley Punks, who show seven of their own homemade films. Usually the host gets the best seat in the crypt. This time the screen is theirs.

items.title: Snow Ghost Community Show: Bone Zone
items.description: Bone Zone performs live in Worcester, September 2008. You can download their album for free. The album is called Perching on the Beam. This is all true.

items.title: Glendora and Her Cat
items.description: Glendora has opinions on Cablevision and a free Happy Book for anyone who writes in, but the cat at the edge of the frame wins the show. The uploader thought so too, and posted only this clip.

items.title: All Color News
items.description: An artists' collective files the city's news: subway riders, rats in the meat markets, a bombing claim, and the Golden Gloves at the Garden. Murky and dim, and exactly the hour for it.

items.title: The Wacky Factory: Halloween Special
items.description: A local children's show gets a holiday of its own, and public access treats Halloween the way a network would: with a whole special and everything. Stay up for it.

items.title: Pizza Boy
items.description: Pizza Boy must get a pizza to granny's house. His car is hijacked, and granny turns out to prefer blood to pepperoni. A black-and-white picture by Amanda Weiss and Molly Brittsan, class of '02. Tip accordingly.

items.title: This Week in Joe's Basement: UFOs
items.description: The crew asks a laundromat and a McDonald's whether they believe in UFOs, a science lecturer checks the theories, and the Mole recruits a guest for his saucer. Chicago access, asking the real questions.

items.title: Saturday Night Special
items.description: Comedy from the craft brew underground: stand-ups work a stone-walled cellar bar in Portland, Maine. The station calls it hilarious and uncensored. The cellar has heard worse.

items.title: Haunted Indiana
items.description: Bloomington's own scare special, made with Indiana University's folklore department by brothers Michael and Stephen White. Ask anyone who grew up there. They have a story, and probably a nightmare.

items.title: Grave Matters & Untimely Deaths
items.description: Actors perform stories in a graveyard in Fortuna, California. The stories are about death. The graveyard is real. The audience is whoever showed up.

items.title: Crowdsourced Cinema: The Princess Bride
items.description: Northampton Community Television cut a beloved fairy-tale movie into 48 scenes and gave one to each team of neighbors. The seams show, and the love in it is doing the stitching.

items.title: Time Travel: All the Time in the World Again
items.description: Five years of research and building went into a full-scale replica of the Time Machine from George Pal's 1960 film. Carl Piermarini then made a mockumentary to show it off. Worth the wait.

items.title: The Wacky Factory
items.description: More Wacky Factory from the cable access studio. Kids' TV with no network behind it, so whatever happens next got past nobody's focus group.

items.title: Snow Ghost Community Show: 100th episode!
items.description: Bruce and a very tired Mike celebrate the "100th" episode of the Community Show. Topics include neighborhood revitalization, vegan cookbooks, and zombie films. A normal Tuesday.

items.title: The Hypnotic Eye: The 1 Year Anniversary
items.description: Mr. Eye marks a year on Dallas cable access in the pre-YouTube world by explaining his origins, quitting the show, and cruising Richardson, Texas at night for fried chicken. Commitment to the bit.

items.title: Fronk: The Countdown Begins
items.description: This Fronk starts with NASA, moves to a church, then puts the whole town on the phone, which is the correct order for bad news. Watch it in any order you like; the show won't mind.

items.title: Worm City
items.description: Eric Glass, producer of the Wacky Factory, aims an edgy sketch show at 14-to-18-year-olds out of Worcester community TV. This is number three. Public access, still going in the 2010s.

items.title: Pocket Calculator (Ms Divine's Sketch Comedy Film)
items.description: A one-lady sketch film by Ms. Divine, set to Kraftwerk's Pocket Calculator and the old Batman Mr. Freeze music. The magic calculator is pink. The verdict on the audience: Useless people!

items.title: Southern Oregon News Network: Moving Up In The World
items.description: The least qualified news team in Oregon covers a rocket launch, a sea stack and the weather from a desk that was not expensive. Guests drop by. Nothing is turned away, least of all the news.

items.title: The Wacky Factory show
items.description: The Wacky Factory — a WCCA TV children's program. Segments include Driving Teacher Crazy and a visit to the Amherst Railway Society Railroad Hobby Show. Written, produced, and willed into existence by Eric Glass.

items.id: thedlpolonskybamboobarrierexperience2009originalshortvideodirectedbylawrencehollie/The DL Polonsky Bamboo Barrier Experience 2009 [Original Short Video] directed by Lawrence Hollie.mp4
items.title: The DL Polonsky Bamboo Barrier Experience
items.description: Poet and filmmaker DL Polonsky tells jokes, and mostly just exists on camera, for a Brookline cable access show. Lawrence Hollie directed and edited. We respect the verb.

items.title: A Short History of Vladivostock
items.description: A puppet show, on blue foam, telling the short history of Vladivostock: a green monster, campaign signs for Ted, Fred and Ned, and something called News Sharks. History is written by the puppeteers.

items.id: 1989-08-19-beyond-vaudeville-ep-20-brother-theodore-oddville-public-access-the-burbs/1989-08-19 BEYOND VAUDEVILLE EP 20 Brother Theodore Oddville Public Access The Burbs .mp4
items.title: Beyond Vaudeville: Brother Theodore
items.description: Brother Theodore, the doom-laden monologist who became a Letterman regular, turns up alongside Leslie Holcomb and Uncle Sam Joe Erdelyi in a stars-and-stripes hat. Cheerful company for him.

items.title: In Your Drawers
items.description: A CHET TV original. Comedy performed entirely with sock puppets. The show is called In Your Drawers. It contains adult content. Viewer discretion is advised. The puppets don't care.

items.title: Bobby G, Space Monkey: The Voo - Part 1
items.description: Bobby G, a gorilla from space, wants to drive, so Bobby G gets a fake driver's license. Then a bird-headed alien turns up and it ends on To Be Continued. The DMV has not commented.

items.title: Sketch Worcester 31: Conspiracy Theories, Worst Clown, and Talking Cat
items.description: Uncle Daniel explains the moon landing from his recliner, the world's worst clown works a little girl's party, and a talking cat lands an interview with the director of the FBI. The cat is the professional in the room.

items.title: The Church of Shooting Yourself: 1993 Episodes
items.description: Part three of Rik Little's NYC access show, captured from the same VHS rental. Two hours across the set, so you can join the congregation midway. Nobody here is taking attendance.

items.title: Shaving Cream
items.description: A Schenectady access sketch with, in the uploader's words, little sense, kept as proof of what community TV looked like in the mid-80s. Two minutes, and it earns its place by being exactly that.

items.title: Fronk: A Twist of Fate
items.description: Secrets are revealed as a being from space arrives on a public access show from Humboldt County. This is episode seventeen. You missed the first sixteen. It's fine.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Stand-up comedy out of Omaha, with the city's name already turned into the joke in the title. Every set is one person, one mic and a room deciding, on tape, whether to laugh.

items.title: The Carol Escobar Show: Puppets
items.description: Bobby Keene's Corporate World premieres on this Humboldt County show and ends on a card reading One Week Later, the cheapest time machine in television. Two puppets take the table.

items.title: Star Horns
items.description: The Cougars' Den kids of Converse Middle School take on Star Wars with cardboard-box helmets, one light sabre, and a school gym standing in for the galaxy. The Force is strong in this hallway.

items.title: Public Domain Theatre: The Amazing Transparent Man
items.description: Longmeadow's own station hosts Edgar G. Ulmer's invisible-crook picture, the man who made Detour doing science fiction on a budget you can see through. Fitting, for a movie about a man you can't.

items.title: Hypnotist Show
items.description: A hypnotist performs for seventy-three minutes. The description says "3/30/17." That's all the context you get. That's all the context there is.

items.title: Paperface Theater: Bins, Buys and Birthdays
items.description: "Pulpy polychromatic puppets poorly pantomime poppycock," says its maker, and that is the review. Cut-paper puppets do the Broken News, visit a graveyard and get a birthday cake. A real cat has the last word.

items.title: Off The Hook: Premiere Episode
items.description: The first one. Bands in a painted studio, a man taking a phone call from bed, a Santa sketch and a dance number with its own credit. Worcester had no idea what was starting. Neither did the show.

items.title: Portland Cable Access 1989: Video Free Portland and Deep Dish TV
items.description: Local access from Portland, then a Deep Dish TV block from the Paper Tiger collective. Somewhere in there, Fritz Bacher's short is called Ronald Reagan Goes to Hell. The title is the whole forecast.

items.title: Countrockula's Theater for the Insane
items.description: A Minneapolis cable access horror host with a pun for a name and a full hour to fill. Nobody hands you a plot at 2 AM; you just join the haunting already in progress.

items.title: Steal This Show: Marijuana
items.description: Steal This Show digs up the warning film in which Sonny Bono, of Sonny and Cher, tells the kids why they should not try marijuana. The teen party is staged and the poster on the wall says Smoke Astro Joints. Sonny is unmoved.

items.title: Fronk: The Mini-Series - The Invasion
items.description: Alien ships are spotted Earthbound, and a caption reports a 9.2 earthquake in New York City. In Humboldt County people keep shopping, which is either denial or courage. A ghostly figure waits in a dark room.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: More Omaha stand-up. Kil Theodrick hosts. Jeremy Plumb, Haley Raven, and Quionez Berry perform. The KPAO studio audience laughs. This is a real thing that happened.

items.title: Glenbrook Edition Parody
items.description: Corey Miller, class of '92, rewrites his own school's newscast. One anchor wears a clown wig, one a goalie mask, and Jukebox Guy gets a caption. The credits hand out job titles nobody applied for.

items.title: Mysterious Norwood III
items.description: Ghost hunters investigate an abandoned school in Norwood. This is the third investigation. The school has not gotten less abandoned.

items.title: The Hypnotic Eye: The Multi-cultural Episode
items.description: Joe Riley's Dallas cable access hour is a pop-culture grab bag from before YouTube, when a local channel was how you shared a weird obsession. Mr. Eye is ready, and The Shat sings Rocket Man.

items.title: Random Acts of Comedy: After Intermission
items.description: The second half of the monthly improv night at the Arcata Theatre Lounge: players in coloured T-shirts, a red curtain, and games made up as they go. You missed the first half. So did the tape.

items.title: UFOs and Atlantis
items.description: Nobody knows the name of this show, its host or his guest. What survives: a man in a white cowboy hat, and sky footage labelled LIGHTSHIP and CIGARSHIP BEHIND CLOUD. The UFOs come from Atlantis. That part is settled.

items.title: I've Got Munchies: S'mores in a Bowl
items.description: Mary Jane gets cancelled after eighteen years and formally apologizes to the public. She makes s'mores in a bowl as her final recipe. The finale of a show most of the world never knew existed.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Maura Gillan hosts. Cameron Logsdon, who hosted episode seven, is back as one of the comics, with Ali Kareem and Angi Sada. In Omaha this is either a promotion or the opposite.

items.title: Rapid T. Rabbit: It's Not Easy Being a Rabbit
items.description: Rapid T. Rabbit takes his grievance to a New York rooftop: it's not easy being a rabbit. He backs it up with a picture book of drawn bunnies. Nobody is in a position to argue.

items.title: Static Age
items.description: Octavius tries to shoot a show inside his own house, tells jokes to nobody, then he and Gary drive to Santa Ana to interview Curbside Journal. Cable access, made at home and proud of it.

items.title: Countrockula's Theater for the Insane
items.description: The uploader's first edit in the Minneapolis access studio, and the fades are still blue because nobody had found the black yet. Ralph Bakshi's Wizards is the feature. Learning curve included.

items.title: Magic Show: Brian Christie
items.description: Local-TV magic is a hard room: the live trick has to land on a lens, and the gasp has to come from your couch. The magician does the work. You supply the gasp.

items.title: Art Fein's Poker Party: Timothy Carey
items.description: Art Fein mostly interviewed musicians. Tonight it's Timothy Carey, who wrote, directed and starred in The World's Greatest Sinner and talks about it, clips included. Art just has to hold on.

items.title: The Apartment Inspector - Part 1 of 2 (Ms Divine's Sketch Comedy Film)
items.description: Inspector Ox Malford arrives to inspect Senor Nacho's apartment, and Ms. Divine plays everyone, phone calls included. A one-lady film in two parts, so the inspection is not over tonight.

items.title: Snow Ghost Community Show: Zombies
items.description: A Catholic Worker, Scott Schaeffer-Duffy, is asked about the undead, with clips from Night of the Living Dead and White Zombie as exhibits. A public access booking nobody else would dream of.

items.title: PTV Presents: The 2019 Holiday Special
items.description: PTV's colorful cast of hosts and celebrities celebrate the most magical time of year. Please keep your sins at the door. The holiday special runs sixty-six minutes.

items.title: The Roommate Game
items.description: Roommates compete to see how well they know each other, filmed in an actual bar. This is the first episode. Warning: adult language. The roommates are honest.

items.title: Southern Oregon News Network: Slow News Day
items.description: A slow news day in southern Oregon, so the desk fills the half hour with a pterodactyl, a Gangsta Weatherman and a sequel to To Kill a Mockingbird. A band plays them out.

items.title: SMC Comedy Showcase
items.description: Seven Boston-area comics take turns on a brick-wall set with one red chair and a sign full of social-media handles. Near the end two of them try it as a team. Somerville stays up for all of it.

items.title: Wuz That Funny?: Decision 2018 Town Hall Debate
items.description: Jack Lanni and an ensemble stage a mock Congressional debate for Rogue TV, town-hall style. Shorter than the real thing, and nobody has to pretend to be undecided.

items.title: Crowdsourced Cinema: Beetlejuice
items.description: 37 teams each shot one scene of Beetlejuice in whatever style they liked, for Northampton Community Television's fourth year of remaking a famous film. Say the name three times and a whole town shows up.

items.title: Rebel Clowns Without A Cause
items.description: Freaky the clown and his cousin Rocky perform Twisted Sister's "We're Not Gonna Take It" in a doorway, in full face paint, with their rebel lines captioned. They are not going to take it.

items.title: Fronk: The Beginning of the End
items.description: Episode ten of Fronk, the Humboldt County mini-series, is called The Beginning of the End, which is a bold title for episode ten. Episode eleven is promised, so the end is clearly in no hurry.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Cameron Logsdon hosts, with David Kousgaard, Ben Webb and Stephanie Hillier. The lights have gone blue. Omaha's live studio audience has been here for seven episodes and shows no sign of going home.

items.title: The Carol Escobar Show
items.description: Carol has claymation, an interview with Neal Schoonmaker and the Humboldt County Fair, and still finds room for a puppet and a walk-and-talk on weed management. Carol covers the county. All of it.

items.title: Drive-In Movie
items.description: Written and performed by artists at The Studio: an epic adventure in a fantasy world. The epic is forty minutes. The fantasy is community access. The adventure is real.

items.title: Countrockula's Theater for the Insane
items.description: The host's own notes: the last full episode made at MTN, the best tape-to-tape barrage editing of the run, and a feature on Superstarlet A.D. GWAR drops by, and by the host's account it did not go well.

items.id: jr-christian-science-bible-program-with-david-liebe-hart-nsu-0-iz-hl-ts-a/Junior Christian Science Bible Lesson Programme (1990s) Comp.ia.mp4
items.title: The Junior Christian Science Bible Lesson Program
items.description: David Liebe Hart, later of Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!, in his own habitat: a children's Bible lesson with puppets, anti-drug lectures and video editing nobody can explain.

items.title: Survival
items.description: Winnipeg friends in balaclavas play anonymous survivalists bracing for the coming cataclysm. Guy Maddin was in the cast. These are the station's Beta masters, so the dread comes through clean.

items.title: Steal This Show: Being Young, 1950s Style
items.description: Steal This Show presents Being Young, 1950s Style — an afternoon and evening in the complicated lives of six teenagers, as seen through the lens of public access hindsight.

items.title: Southern Oregon News Network: Space Mashup
items.description: Oregon's least trusted news team does the whole broadcast from space, by green screen. A puppet dog reads the horoscopes and there is a commercial for real estate on the moon. Lots are going fast.

items.title: Saturday Night Special
items.description: Saturday Night Special, episode one, from the Portland Media Center. The description is just social media links. The show is fifty minutes. Everything else is a mystery.

items.title: Bobby G, Space Monkey
items.description: The title says space monkey, the Archive says gorilla from space, and Bobby G. corrects neither. Humboldt County science fiction satire, episode one, with saucers parked over the redwoods.

items.title: The Uncle Floyd Show: Clips
items.description: The first of six clip tapes from Uncle Floyd Vivino's New Jersey UHF kiddie show. Low budget, high silliness, and a host who clearly knew exactly what he was doing. Start here, then keep going.

items.title: This is My World
items.description: A man wanders into a cave and becomes the prisoner of a supernatural being. Trapped in a surreal 1950s-themed loop, he adapts to the brainwashing and repetition. A mysterious woman appears at the breakfast table offering a way out.

items.id: AtomicTV1997XmasHolidayAtGroundZeroArchive.org/Atomic TV 1997 Xmas Holiday at Ground Zero archive.org.mp4
items.title: Atomic TV: Holiday at Ground Zero
items.description: A Baltimore public access Christmas special where a politically incorrect Santa visits Atomic Books to teach an elf the true meaning of the season. Nobody involved was aiming at Hallmark.

items.title: The Moon-Dust Story Hour
items.description: A host in a yellow hat and sunglasses plays guitar to an audience of teddy bears. A detective in a trench coat takes the case of a sock, and real children play Word Family Feud. Stories, songs and puppets, as promised.

items.title: Puppeteers For Fears: The Mummy's Purse [ADULT]
items.description: Puppeteers For Fears presents The Mummy's Purse. An all-original play featuring puppets and live music. The mummy has a purse. The puppets have range.

items.title: John's Home Movies: Home Edition
items.description: John points his camera around and outside the house for Access Humboldt and calls it experimental video. He is right on both counts. The living room finally gets its close-up.

items.title: Technical Difficulties
items.description: Matt Lawrence directs a school-made parody of everything on television, one genre at a time. The ambition is a full broadcast day, and the cast plays it as if the ratings were on the line.

items.title: The Chess Show
items.description: The Chess Show ran on Portland cable for eight years, hosted by Cybele and Botielus, who also played accordion as Samsonite and DelightYa. Tonight, three accordionists in a garden. Chess not required.

items.title: Off the Hook
items.description: From the dusty corner of the WCCA video vault: Off the Hook episode 18, a comedy and music production from 1990. The dust is real. The show is preserved.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Oma-Ha! episode nine. Maura Gillan hosts. Bill Queen, Pete Sakaris, and Mark Sibbitt perform. The live studio audience in Omaha continues to exist.

items.title: Clowning Around: Puppets
items.description: Mr. Twists 'N Juggles lays out finger puppets, sock puppets and stick puppets on a table and explains each one. Then his friend Bingo the Clown, also a puppet, gets two clips of his own. Bingo has representation.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Oma-Ha! episode five. Kil Theodrick hosts again. Jason Regan, Kent Masloskie, and Carmela Anderson perform. The KPAO audience has not left.

items.title: Off The Hook
items.description: Ricky Jam hosts from a painted studio on Worcester's channel 39. There is a puppet in a blue tie, a telephone gag, a singer, and a prop that says Damn I'm Good. Tonight the prop has a case.

items.title: Fronk: Enigma
items.description: Fronk: Enigma, episode eighteen. More secrets are revealed. New characters appear. If you don't know Fronk by now, this is a strange place to start. Start anyway.

items.title: Wormtown: The Premiere
items.description: Eric Glass, the man behind The Wacky Factory, makes a sketch show for the fourteen-to-eighteen crowd: teens loose in a grocery store, a kid in a cop hat, a band, a clown in sunglasses. Edgy, by Worcester's count.

items.title: Clowning Around: Good Clown vs. Bad Clown
items.description: The clown host makes the distinction between good clowns and bad clowns. What they do and don't do. The line exists. The clown is drawing it.

items.title: Ms. Divine's Le Tee Hee Hee Heure: A Peculiar Bank Heist, Part 1
items.description: Part one of four. A lonely girl with a dead-end corporate job meets a puppet that comes to life, and they plan a bank robbery. The puppet's weakness is nachos, which is a flaw in the plan.

items.title: Junktape
items.description: Greg the Bunny, back when the puppet lived on New York access and the network and cable years were still ahead of him. Everything that came later grew out of this scrappy half hour.

items.title: Public Domain Theatre Halloween Special Pt.1
items.description: Public Domain Theatre's Halloween Special, part one. Eighty minutes. No description provided. The public domain asks nothing of you and gives everything.

items.title: The Wacky Factory
items.description: Every odd decision on this local kids' show traces back to one desk: Eric Glass wrote it, directed it and produced it. No committee, no notes, and a free hand.

items.title: Ox Malford Gets Hunted (Ms Divine's Sketch Comedy Film)
items.description: Ox Malford, now in charge of Homeland Security, kicks in an apartment door after some suspicious individuals and finds that he is the one being hunted. A one-lady film: Ms. Divine is hunter, hunted and sofa.

items.title: Clowning Around: Jokes, Physical Comedy & Props
items.description: Mr. Twists N' Juggles does jokes, physical comedy, and props. Sometimes in combination. The clown is versatile. The family is entertained. Presumably.

items.title: The Wacky Factory show
items.description: The Mating Game with three contestants, a commercial for a cleaning spray called Blotto, and a kid with a toy car to sell you, the QUADRA. Written, directed and produced by Eric Glass, like everything else at the factory.

items.title: Steal This Show: LSD
items.description: Steal This Show presents "Mr. LSD," a throwback educational film in which LSD himself explains the horrible things he can do to the human mind. Rebroadcast by people who know exactly how funny this is.

items.title: The Hypnotic Eye: Half Assed Puppets and Magic
items.description: Tiny Bob messes with magic and transmogrifies himself, and Mr. Eye, no help at all, ridicules him while he works out the undo. The 5,6,7,8's and the MC5 are on the soundtrack.

items.title: Super Ultra Mega Happy Fun Show
items.description: Sketch comedy by teenagers in Billerica: a man in a shopping cart, a fake record label, a film about scuba diving, and somebody in a pink costume. The title promised a great deal. They went for all of it.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Oma-Ha! episode one. Stephanie Finklea hosts. Trish Sullivan, Karl Houser, and Brooke Barsell take the stage at KPAO. The beginning of something Omaha didn't know it needed.

items.title: American Conspiracy: UFOs
items.description: In this classic RBTV series, host Scott Zak talks to author Kevin Randle about UFOs in American history. The conspiracies are American. The perspectives are unique. The cable channel is basic.

items.title: SCAT Halloween Loop Tape: Frankenstein's Planet of Monsters and Shorts
items.description: Late night only, the uploader says, and that is fair. Frankenstein's Planet of Monsters is a Halloween show from Somerville access, plus shorts, on a loop tape. Plan to be up.

items.title: Dirty Stars
items.description: Six college kids in Denver doing sketch comedy: a news desk covering Wall St and the Economy, trouble in a restaurant kitchen, and a man face down on the carpet. From serious to slapstick, they say. The carpet is slapstick.

items.title: The Uncle Floyd Show: Clips
items.description: Floyd Vivino's New Jersey UHF kiddie show, boiled down to an hour of 80s puppets, bits and a host who knew exactly how silly it all was. That was the whole charm.

items.title: IN THE CAN: "Being Elmo: A Puppeteer's Journey"
items.description: Director Constance Marks and puppeteer Kevin Clash discuss the documentary "Being Elmo" on Park City Television's IN THE CAN. Ten minutes of earnest conversation about a man inside a red puppet.

items.title: Organic Vapor: Debbie
items.description: Ricky Jam wrote it and plays it opposite Jim Rasicot, two minutes of pure performance art. The uploader says you won't find this on mainstream TV, and nobody has argued yet.

items.title: Twin Geeks
items.description: A home-video Twin Peaks spoof whose maker admits he never quite finished it. Title cards explain who is whose illegitimate twin, a woman in pink feathers waits by candlelight, and the finale is a polka he wrote himself.

items.title: Downtown Tonight: Flag Show, Anti-Utopia Show
items.description: Craig Silver and Lynn Seeney's weekly arts show on Manhattan cable's Channel D visits a Flag Show and an Anti-Utopia Show. The Lower East Side art scene, documented while it was happening.

items.title: EXP-TV
items.description: Tim Manning produces, John Zavala co-writes, and Salina, Kansas gets a sketch show with real ambition and a cable access budget. The ambition wins most rounds.

items.title: The Church of Shooting Yourself: 1993 Episodes
items.description: Rik Little's Church of Shooting Yourself, the NYC access show, survives as a VHS rental someone captured. Part one of the 1993 run. Whatever the tape adds along the way is part of the service.

items.title: This Week in Joe's Basement: Moon Blob
items.description: A letter from King Zeke on a paper crown, then a song built on a failed toy the crew found at a surplus store, with heads bouncing around Michelle's lips. Chicago public access, fully committed.

items.title: Science or Superstition
items.description: Seattle Community Media gives an hour to Mayan calendars, solar flares and a December 21, 2012 deadline, and asks the question in the title. We can report back: the calendar kept going.

items.title: Blobs: A Claymation Short by Maggie Brown
items.description: One Blob must find the courage to stop a monster from attacking the local school. Claymation by Maggie Brown, from a kids' workshop at Greenbelt Access Television. The sign says SCHOOL BLOBS. The monster can read.

items.title: The Feedback Zone
items.description: Quantum Leap's premise moves into the television set: a hero lost somewhere between channels and a rescue crew with a plan. A variety show gets its own sci-fi episode for the price of a few props.

items.title: Atomic TV: Underdog Battles Satan Claus
items.description: Atomic TV's Tom Warner and Scott Huffines escort Underdog to the Hampden holiday parade, with a late train and a car chase they say tops The French Connection. Baltimore access, at holiday length.

items.title: Oma-Ha! A Stand-Up Comedy TV Show
items.description: Don Seager hosts. Matt Wedlock, Katie Pirruccello and Kil Theodrick perform under purple light at KPAO, and the camera keeps checking on the front row. The front row is holding up.

items.title: Sketch Worcester: Thanksgiving, Running Man, Worcester Witch Trials
items.description: Matthew Cory's hometown sketches take on Worcester's first Thanksgiving, derailed by Uncle Daniel's political rants, and a history professor on the witch trials. Public access that loves its city.

items.title: We Try Wednesday: Drawing Childhood Nickelodeon Characters From Memory
items.description: Interns attempt to draw childhood Nickelodeon characters from memory. Who drew the character better? You decide. We Try Wednesday. They tried.

items.title: VOX POP Opening Night Comedy Show
items.description: Somerville Media Center opens its VOX POP space the right way: seven of the city's comics, Caitlin Arcand hosting, one microphone and a dark stage. The room has presumably been funny ever since.

items.title: AwPT -Sept 27 - Weaponized Weather!?!
items.description: All-ways Pursuing Truth: weaponized weather. The host has a correction about which Clinton-era Defense Secretary he meant. The weather remains weaponized. Allegedly.

items.title: Space Barbie
items.description: A visitor from space takes over an innocent woman's mind with one demand: buy your daughter a Barbie. Advertising as an invasion, in a sketch that knows exactly what it is selling.

items.title: Zombies of the Redwoods
items.description: The College of the Redwoods Digital Art and Media club spent over a year on this zombie short and wants you to know no kids were harmed, "maybe ha-ha." A first for the club, and they say so.

items.title: The Wacky Factory
items.description: Another Wacky Factory, a kids' program out of local access. The production values are homemade, and that is the whole draw.

items.title: Jill Thatcher - Puppet Show at the Nolensville Library
items.description: Jill Thatcher's puppet show at the Nolensville Library, taped June 12, 2019 and kept in full. It was made for a daytime library room. At this hour you're the matinee audience, and the puppets don't mind.

items.title: The Uncle Floyd Show: Clips
items.description: Clip tape two of six from Uncle Floyd's New Jersey UHF show. It is a kids' show the way a clown car is transportation: technically accurate, and nowhere near the point.

items.title: The Wacky Factory: demo
items.description: The sales pitch for a children's show, made at a Worcester access studio. A demo has to promise everything at once, so the wackiness is front-loaded and the sincerity comes free.

items.title: Public Access Prank Calls: Free Psychic Energy Reading
items.description: Call-in shows open the phone lines to the whole world, and somebody heard that as a dare. A reel of prank calls aimed at the public access dial, from the era of dialing.

items.title: Somerville Kitchenette Show
items.description: Two men in aprons host a cooking show that keeps leaving the kitchen. The Archive's entire description is "a comedy program," which is accurate. Two episodes back to back, and nobody explains the tent.

items.title: The Hypnotic Eye
items.description: Mr. Eye and M.C. Tiny Bob take cable access on an hour of pop culture, with Gamera 2 and video psychotherapy for shut-ins. Made before YouTube, back when this was the only way to be this strange.

items.title: The Apartment Inspector - Part2 of 2 (Ms Divine's Sketch Comedy Film)
items.description: Ms. Divine's sketch comedy: Inspector Ox Malford inspects Senor Nacho's apartment. Part two of two. You missed part one. Don't forget to download it. The apartment has not improved.

items.title: Film Sprint: Superhero Film by Comedy As A Weapon
items.description: Seven days, a genre drawn at random, and Tim Lovett of Comedy As A Weapon drew superhero. The result is The Bubbler: a red mask, a Spider-Man shirt, a brick warehouse and a woman in a long coat who is not convinced.

items.title: Ms. Divine's Le Tee Hee Hee Heure: A Peculiar Bank Heist, Part 2
items.description: Part two of four, and the uploader asks you to catch part one for the full film. The synopsis: a puppet, a bank, nachos, and an Army General determined to spread democracy to anything in his way.

items.title: A Job Interview with Darth Vader
items.description: Darth Vader and a job interview, five minutes of community TV spoof built on exactly one idea. Late night has run on less. Dress for it; the Force does not count as a reference.

items.title: A Chat With Glendora
items.description: Glendora Folsom Buell is a physicist, philosopher, and self-made television personality who creates weekly public access shows. She's been doing this for a while. Fifty-eight minutes of chatting with Glendora.

items.title: Fronk: Day of the Reapers
items.description: Fronk's eighth episode brings in the Reapers, and Humboldt County's 2012 doom finally has a villain. Somewhere in the frame, a few cats remain unworried.

items.title: The Tyranny of Symmetry
items.description: Paul Sandresky makes three experimental shorts, among them Wishbone Keystone and The Horse Latitudes. The titles alone beat most of what airs at 2 AM, and the pieces are short enough to survive.

items.title: Off the Hook
items.description: Off the Hook episode 19. From the WCCA TV video vault. Another half hour of whatever Ricky Jam and company were doing in 1990. The hook remains elusive.

items.title: Puppet Show
items.description: Shot on Super 8 by Todd Kneedy and Sam Sterlin: a doll in a box, a blue flame, a knife. The school's own notes say it may make you queasy and that this was the idea. The puppets did not sign up for it.

items.title: This Week in Joe's Basement: Delayed Gratification (Remix)
items.description: The remix, which the uploader says has much more entertainment value than the original. Viewer mail, a favorable Tribune review Joe answers, four sketches, and Basement commercials with the Cigarette Man.

items.title: Big Muddy Opera Company Backyard Magic Show
items.description: The Big Muddy Opera Company performs a backyard magic show, captured by Columbia Access Television. Fifty-six minutes of opera and magic in someone's actual backyard.

items.title: An Evening of Improv with On the Spot
items.description: The On the Spot players trade scenes on a blue-curtained stage with the audience sitting around it, and the host reads from a card. Nothing here was planned, which on this channel is not a warning.

items.title: Beyond the Headlines: Understanding the Illuminati
items.description: AJ interviews Fritz Springmeier about the Illuminati on Seattle Community Media. The Illuminati are controlling things. Fritz has details. The special report has no time limit.

items.title: The Ripoff
items.description: Austin Peay State's comedy showcase, written and performed by the students of Live Studio Production, course COMM 3810. Anchors at a desk, couch interviews, a man at a lectern. It counted toward their degrees.

items.title: Off The Hook
items.description: Off The Hook episode 12. From the deepest, darkest, dustiest corner of the WCCA TV video vault. Ricky Jam. Channel 39. 1990. Still wacky.

items.title: The Camp is Out There: A ConcordTV Parody
items.description: ConcordTV's best camp instructor is missing, and Agents Scarelli and Sweatty have until the kids arrive. Their leads: a silver alien and a horse in a yellow bow tie. No aliens or puppets were harmed, says the card.

items.title: Ms. Divine's Le Tee Hee Hee Heure: Dancing Girl
items.description: Mr. Weird Man blows his IRS refund on a show, and the Russian Mafia Super keeps raising the price and swinging a hammer. One woman plays everyone. Refund season, 2 AM style.

items.title: Off The Hook
items.description: Off The Hook episode 11. Same vault. Same dust. Same Ricky Jam. Same channel 39. The show doesn't change. The tape just keeps going.

items.title: Ms. Divine's Tee Hee Heure: The Great Big Fight
items.description: Scottish Girl goes looking for friends at a pub and finds Inspector Ox Malford and the Russian Mafia Super. Her photo album fills up fast, and then the pub gets loud. A one-woman sketch film.

items.title: Bobby G, Space Monkey: The Occuloid Affair
items.description: Bobby G, the gorilla from space, is in a laboratory full of glowing jars, and the jars have faces in them. Two men with blasters hold the corridor. There is a credit for Alien Woman Voice. Stay for it.

items.title: Rapid T. Rabbit: H.R. Pufnstuf
items.description: By episode 413 Rapid T. Rabbit has a red scarf, a sign with his name on it, and H.R. Pufnstuf in green felt for a guest. Kids mailed in drawings of rabbits, and the show airs them, correctly.

items.title: A Most Particularly Peculiar Bank Heist (Ms Divine's Sketch Film)
items.description: A lonely office worker, a puppet with a weakness for nachos, a Russian mafia super with a leaky ceiling to deal with, and a general set on spreading freedom. Ms. Divine's feature, and the nachos wreck the plan.

items.title: Übergetränk
items.description: A struggling novelist and her one-night stand become addicted to a mysterious German energy drink. A public access original that plays like an art film made by people who have never seen an art film. This is a compliment.

items.title: Southern Oregon News Network: Gordon Mackey's Day Off
items.description: Gordon is late because another Snow is getting married, and an anchor ends up officiating. Also tonight: a 1950s medical film, a slice of toast, and the discovery of "Pam." The guest in red flannel takes it hard.

items.title: Snow Ghost Community Show: American Antiquarian Society
items.description: Bruce and Mike take a video tour of the American Antiquarian Society in Worcester, Massachusetts. The society is antiquarian. The community show is Snow Ghost. The twenty-fourth minutes fly by.

items.title: Paul Alien
items.description: A Seattle mockumentary builds its case that Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen is the aliens' front man, with street performers and an anti-alien resistance cell as witnesses. The evidence is airtight.

items.title: The Around the World Show
items.description: Bobby Burns and Professor Willikers, both puppets, take a whirlwind tour: the pyramids, a beach, Times Square in the rain. A skeleton waits in a window and a green dinosaur turns up. Pack light.

items.title: The Basement Tapes
items.description: A full live hour of Dead Air Live, a show whose name is both a promise and a warning. Nobody gets a second take on public access, and this crew plainly wouldn't want one.

items.title: EXP TV: Here, There, Everywhere
items.description: Salina, Kansas had a community access comedy show, and Tim Manning and Paul Weaver Jr. wrote this half hour of it. The town's sense of humor, on tape, treated as appointment television.

items.title: Crowdsourced Cinema: Ferris Bueller's Day Off
items.description: The community of Northampton collaboratively remakes Ferris Bueller's Day Off, scene by scene. Eighty-eight minutes. Every scene a different crew. The day is off. The commitment is on.

items.title: Off The Hook
items.description: Episode two, and the host is already dancing with the telephone. A shirtless bald man takes the mic, somebody ends up in a ring on crutches, and a band plays through it. Some of this happens in the dark.

items.title: The Hypnotic Eye: Deep Ellum Cerebellum
items.description: Mr. Eye wins best cable access show from a trend-obsessed local paper, so naturally he goes goth for the hipsters he expects. A visit to Toys From The Crypt in Garland is on the itinerary.

items.title: Myspace
items.description: Ever look at someone's Myspace page and think "too much information"? Denver Open Media made a show about it. Fifty-two minutes. The Myspace era preserved in community access amber.

items.title: Man in the Box
items.description: Thirteen minutes of video art from Somerville access. The uploader filed it under two words, and we are not the ones to add more. The title is the whole briefing.

items.title: Computers in Education
items.description: LOGO and BASIC in the classroom. A Stanford professor and an author named Kleiman explain why every kid needs a computer. They weren't wrong — they were just thirty years early.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence
items.description: Artificial intelligence in 1984. The promises are enormous, the demos are modest, and nobody's worried about it taking their job yet.

items.title: Computer Entrepreneurs
items.description: Wozniak, Osborne, Amdahl, and Harp talk startups before the word meant anything. Four people who built the industry sitting in folding chairs on a PBS set.

items.title: Decision Support Systems
items.description: Expert systems and AI for business decisions. Gary Kildall explains why computers should help managers think. The software costs more than most cars.

items.title: Utilities
items.description: Norton Utilities, SideKick, and the essential tools no DOS user could live without. An era when 'utility software' was its own product category.

items.title: Mainframes to Minis to Micros
items.description: The very first episode. September 1983. Gary Kildall and Stewart Cheifet trace the computer's family tree from room-sized mainframes to the thing on your desk. It all starts here.

items.title: Integrated Software
items.description: VisiOn, DESQ, and the Apple Lisa. The dream of software that works together instead of fighting. John Couch from Apple shows off a $10,000 computer.

items.title: Computer Music
items.description: MIDI before MIDI was cool. Syntauri, Electronic Arts' music tools, and Stanford's John Chowning, the man who made FM synthesis happen. Your phone does this now.

items.title: Computer Ergonomics
items.description: Carpal tunnel, screen radiation, and back pain — the health crisis nobody saw coming when they put a computer on every desk. HP's ergonomics lab looks like a torture chamber.

items.title: Simulator Software
items.description: Flight sims, architecture walkthroughs, and military training. The pixels are enormous but the ambition is real.

items.title: Operating Systems
items.description: CP/M vs. DOS vs. Apple vs. whatever HP is doing. Five people argue about operating systems. The winner isn't in the room yet.

items.title: Word Processing Software
items.description: WordStar, WordPerfect, and the new kid — Microsoft Word. Paul Schindler reviews them all. The hot feature? Mail merge.

items.title: Computer Security
items.description: Hackers, phone phreaks, and passwords on sticky notes. Computer security in 1984 means locking the door to the computer room.

items.title: Robotics
items.description: SRI International's robots, Microbot's robot arm, and dreams of automated everything. The robots are slow, expensive, and absolutely fascinating.

items.title: Computer Graphics
items.description: Silicon Graphics demos, freelance digital art, and pixel counts you could track on your fingers. Computer graphics before Pixar changed everything.

items.title: Speech Synthesis
items.description: Computers that talk. A Minolta camera that announces your f-stop. Texas Instruments' Speak & Spell. The future sounds like a robot reading a phone book.

items.title: Networking
items.description: Ethernet, broadband, baseband — getting computers to talk to each other is harder than it sounds. 3Com's Bob Metcalfe explains why cables matter.

items.title: Microchip Technology
items.description: AMD's 4-bit and 16-bit chips under a microscope. The entire history of the microprocessor condensed into 28 minutes by the people who built them.

items.title: Business Application Software
items.description: Lotus 1-2-3, IBM's finest, and Levi Strauss explaining why they bought computers for the office. Stanford's Stewart Reges teaches programming to business majors.

items.title: Printers
items.description: Daisy wheel, dot matrix, and the first laser printers. Xerox PARC shows off tech that costs as much as a car. The sound of a dot matrix is the soundtrack of the decade.

items.title: Database Software
items.description: Dialog, CompuServe, and Dow Jones — the internet before the internet. You pay by the minute to search databases over a phone line.

items.title: Programming
items.description: COBOL, FORTH, Pascal, and Apple BASIC. Gary Kildall demos languages that half the industry swears by and the other half has never heard of.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: Trip Hawkins founded Electronic Arts. Bill Budge made Pinball Construction Set. Chris Crawford left Atari to theorize about fun. The game industry starts in garages.

items.title: Computer Entrepreneurs
items.description: Wozniak, Osborne, Amdahl, and Lore Harp — the people who bet everything on the idea that normal humans would want a computer. Most of their companies won't survive the decade.

items.title: Fifth Generation Computers
items.description: Japan's billion-dollar moonshot to build thinking machines. Shot in Tokyo. Gary Kildall investigates. The project will produce impressive research and zero products.

items.title: The Macintosh Computer
items.description: The original Mac, circa 1985. Joanna Hoffman from Apple shows off 128K of RAM and no hard drive. Everyone agrees it will change everything. It will.

items.title: Christmas Buyers Guide
items.description: Holiday 1985. Gary and Stewart pick the year's best tech gifts. Everything costs too much and does too little, but the excitement is infectious.

items.title: Lasers and Computers
items.description: LaserDiscs, optical storage, and a CD-ROM the size of a pizza box. Rick Dyer demos the future of interactive entertainment. The future has other plans.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: More games, more platforms, more arguments about whether computers will replace board games. Spoiler: yes.

items.title: IBM Clones
items.description: The clones are coming. Tandy, Radio Shack, and a dozen companies you've never heard of building IBM PCs for half the price. Big Blue should be worried.

items.title: Software Piracy
items.description: Teenage hackers with handles like 'Frankie Mouse' vs. the Software Publishers Association. The battle over who owns code. Both sides make good points.

items.title: UNIX
items.description: Bill Joy at Sun Microsystems, Bell Labs, and the operating system that refused to die. AT&T's UNIX is threatening IBM's monopoly. Decades later, it runs your phone.

items.title: Computers in Sports
items.description: The Oakland A's manager uses a computer in the dugout. Moneyball, thirty years early. The sports world thinks he's crazy.

items.title: Personal Finance Software
