items.description: TurboTax before TurboTax. Bank of America goes digital. Price Waterhouse explains computerized accounting. Your CPA is nervous.

items.title: Profile of Big Blue - IBM
items.description: The IBM profile. Dataquest, Intel, InfoWorld, and Kleiner Perkins weigh in on the most powerful company in tech. Nobody predicts what happens next.

items.title: Computers in Communications
items.description: 3Com, Charles Schwab, and the idea that computers and phones should be the same thing. Bob Metcalfe is right about everything, as usual.

items.title: Japanese PC's
items.description: NEC, ASCII, and the Japanese PC market — shot on location in Tokyo. Kay Nishi explains why Japan's computers are years ahead. The US market doesn't care.

items.title: Low End Computers
items.description: Jack Tramiel's Atari vs. Commodore for the cheapest computer in America. The Commodore 128 costs less than dinner for four.

items.title: Computer Graphics
items.description: Silicon Graphics, Pacific Data Images, and Imagic push pixels in ways nobody thought possible. Professional 3D graphics for the cost of a luxury sedan.

items.title: Robots - Japanese Style
items.description: Live from the High Tech Expo in Tsukuba, Japan. Sony, Toshiba, Fujitsu, and a robot that plays piano. Japan is living in the future.

items.title: Printers & Business Graphics
items.description: Okidata, HP, and the art of making spreadsheets look good on paper. The LaserJet changes everything. Harvard Graphics makes your boss think you're a designer.

items.title: Computers & the Media
items.description: USA Today's newsroom, KRON-TV's graphics, and the digital revolution in media. Ray Douglas explains how newspapers will survive computers. They won't.

items.title: Modems & Bulletin Boards
items.description: Bulletin boards, CompuServe romances, and 300-baud modems. The Well is San Francisco's digital town square. Social media before social media.

items.title: Computer Networks
items.description: Gary Kildall, 3Com's Metcalfe, and the dream of every computer talking to every other. The demos are slow, the wiring is expensive, and the idea is unstoppable.

items.title: Computers & Politics
items.description: Voter profiling, computerized fundraising, and the 1985 election cycle. Campaigns discover that databases win races. Nothing has changed since.

items.title: Computers & Medicine
items.description: Doctors, diagnosis software, and UC Berkeley's medical databases. Gary Kildall asks whether you'd trust a computer with your health. Give it twenty years.

items.title: Optical Storage Devices
items.description: CD-ROM, the compact disc as data storage, and the promise of putting an encyclopedia on a shiny disc. Tim Oren from Activenture sees the future.

items.title: Amiga and Atari
items.description: The Commodore Amiga vs. the Atari 520ST — the people's computers. How much machine can you get for under a grand? More than you'd expect.

items.title: Computers and the Pentagon Part One
items.description: The world's biggest computer customer is the US military. Part one of a tour through defense computing — shot at research centers around the country.

items.title: Computers & the Pentagon Part Two
items.description: SDI, the Strategic Defense Initiative, and Star Wars (the defense program, not the movie). The Pentagon's computing budget could buy a small country.

items.title: MIDI Music
items.description: MIDI machines, music composition software, and the democratization of music production. Chris French and Hybrid Arts prove you don't need a studio.

items.title: Computers in Law Enforcement
items.description: The FBI's databases, police department computers, and surveillance tech. The Hawthorne PD shows off their system. Privacy advocates are not on this episode.

items.title: Investment Software
items.description: Wall Street meets the PC. Telescan, Investek, and the dream of beating the market with a 286. The charts are green-screen and the confidence is unlimited.

items.title: Psychological Software
items.description: Software that analyzes your personality and diagnoses relationship problems. Dr. Jim Johnson from Human Edge demonstrates. Your therapist is a floppy disk.

items.title: Astronomy Software
items.description: Halley's Comet is coming and your PC can track it. Software for amateur astronomers, from star charts to orbital mechanics.

items.title: Educational Software Part 1
items.description: Part one: software for schools. Teachers from Hillsborough and Cupertino show what happens when you put an Apple IIe in every classroom.

items.title: Educational Software Part 2
items.description: Part two: online learning and self-teaching software. First Byte and Terrapin teach kids programming. Control Data puts college courses on a mainframe.

items.title: Second Hand Computers
items.description: The used computer market. Who's selling, who's buying, and why your two-year-old PC is worth less than your office chair.

items.title: Desktop Publishing Part 1
items.description: Desktop publishing part one. The Macintosh turns everyone into a typographer. Manhattan Graphics and PageMaker change how the world makes documents.

items.title: Comdex
items.description: COMDEX '86 from Las Vegas. The biggest tech trade show on earth. Hal Glatzer and Tim Bajarin walk the floor. Everything is beige and revolutionary.

items.title: Christmas Buyers Guide
items.description: Holiday gift guide. Calendar Creator, HP's financial calculator, and Muppet Learning Keys. Perfect gifts for the nerd who has everything (except enough RAM).

items.title: Electronic Mail
items.description: Email in 1987. MCI Mail, Lotus cc:Mail, and the radical idea that you could send a letter without a stamp. Stuart Davidson explains why this will catch on.

items.title: Asian Clones
items.description: Taiwan: clone capital of the world. Monitors, motherboards, and scanners — all built in Taipei for a fraction of the price. Shot on location.

items.title: Intel 386 - The Fast Lane
items.description: The Intel 386 is here and it's fast. Compaq, Zenith, and Intel demo machines that make last year's PC look like a calculator. 32-bit computing for the masses.

items.title: Intelligent Buildings
items.description: Smart buildings in Hong Kong. Elevators that think, offices that adjust, and the Chinese University of HK wiring the future. Shot on location.

items.title: Portable Computers
items.description: Laptops circa 1988. Tandy, NEC, and Zenith build portables that weigh less than a bowling ball. The screens are dim but the dream is bright.

items.title: Computer Kids
items.description: Kids and computers. Aaron from Nueva Learning Center and Laura from Aptos Middle School show what happens when you give a twelve-year-old a modem.

items.title: Computers and the Arts
items.description: Artists discover the mouse. Stanford, Electronic Arts, and freelance digital artists push computers beyond spreadsheets and into the gallery.

items.title: Computers and Gambling
items.description: High-tech slot machines, computerized horse racing, and lottery systems. Las Vegas meets Silicon Valley. The house always wins, but now it wins faster.

items.title: The New Macs
items.description: Apple's new Macs can run DOS software. The faithful react to the idea of IBM compatibility. Heresy or progress?

items.title: Supercomputers
items.description: Supercomputers at NASA, NOAA, and across Asia. Machines that fill rooms and crunch numbers that would take your PC a thousand years.

items.title: Spreadsheet Wars
items.description: Excel vs. Lotus 1-2-3 vs. Quattro Pro. The spreadsheet wars of the late '80s. Only one will survive.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: Late '80s gaming. Chuck Yeager's Flight Trainer, Mean 18 Golf, and Beyond Dark Castle. EA's customer support takes calls from frustrated gamers.

items.title: Amiga
items.description: The Amiga 2500 and its world of creative possibilities. Commodore's Tom Stearns and Amiga World's Lou Wallace show why the faithful believe.

items.title: Amiga
items.description: The Amiga 3000 arrives at $4,000. Commodore bets big on a machine that can do everything. Video toasting, 3D rendering, and a fanbase that will never let go.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: Earl Weaver Baseball, Ferrari Formula One, and Shanghai. Early PC games that devoured entire weekends. Trip Hawkins at EA is building an empire.

items.title: Bus Wars
items.description: EISA vs. MCA vs. ISA vs. Nubus. The war over how data moves inside your computer. The most boring fight that matters most.

items.title: Consumer Buyers Guide
items.description: Another buyer's guide. Another year of tech products reviewed, ranked, and recommended. The gadgets change, the gift-giving anxiety doesn't.

items.title: Comdex
items.description: COMDEX '88 from Vegas. The trade show floor is a mile long and everything on it will be obsolete by spring. Globalink demos real-time translation.

items.title: Computers in Space
items.description: How NASA runs the space program on computers. Shuttle systems, orbital mechanics, and the computing power that put humans in orbit.

items.title: Viruses
items.description: Computer viruses are real and spreading. John Dickinson from PC Labs explains how a floppy disk can destroy your hard drive. Antivirus software is born.

items.title: MacWorld San Francisco
items.description: MacWorld '89 at Moscone Center. Adobe's John Warnock, Silicon Beach, and the faithful gather to worship at the altar of Cupertino.

items.title: High Tech India - Part One
items.description: Part one: India's software industry. Bangalore, Bombay, and the programmers who will reshape the global economy. Shot on location.

items.title: High Tech India - Part Two
items.description: Part two: more from India's tech boom. Tata, Infosys, and engineers writing code for American companies at a fraction of the cost. Nobody in the Valley is paying attention. Yet.

items.title: Foreign Language Software
items.description: Software that translates and teaches languages. Delphi, Anonae, and a machine that turns English into German. The translations are charming in their wrongness.

items.title: Atari St
items.description: The Atari ST — huge in Europe, invisible in America. Jim Kent and the faithful demo what makes it special. The ST will never win, but its fans don't care.

items.title: Laptops
items.description: Laptops 1990. Toshiba, Zenith, and the race for lighter, brighter portables. Backlit displays are the killer feature. Four pounds is ultralight.

items.title: Flight Simulators
items.description: Falcon AT, F-15 Strike Eagle II, and Microsoft Flight Simulator. The golden age of flight sims. Every PC gamer owns a joystick.

items.title: Windows 3.0
items.description: Windows 3.0 just shipped and everything changes. Microsoft's first real GUI contender. The world goes from C:\> to Program Manager.

items.title: Home PCs
items.description: After the PC Jr disaster and the death of Atari and TI, home computers looked doomed. Then 1990 happened. Affordable PCs bring computing home.

items.title: Gary Kildall Special
items.description: A tribute to the show's own co-host. Gary Kildall wrote CP/M, the first PC operating system, and this is the real story of how IBM ended up with MS-DOS instead. Tom Rolander, Gordon Eubanks, and the people who were in the room.

items.title: Font City
items.description: Desktop publishing made everyone think about fonts. Bitstream, Adobe, and the art of choosing between Helvetica and Times New Roman. Typography nerds rejoice.

items.title: Macintosh System 7.0
items.description: System 7 for the Mac. File sharing, virtual memory, aliases, and the Finder update that made Mac users feel superior all over again.

items.title: CES
items.description: CES 1991 from Las Vegas. Nolan Bushnell is back. Heidi Roizen walks the floor. Consumer electronics and personal computers are starting to merge.

items.title: MIDI Music
items.description: MIDI machines, music composition software, and the democratization of music production. Chris French and Hybrid Arts prove you don't need a studio anymore.

items.title: Virtual Reality
items.description: VR in the early '90s. Lots of promises, enormous headsets, and very few pixels. The holy grail of computing. We're still chasing it.

items.title: CD-ROM Software
items.description: CD-ROMs are here and they hold 650 megabytes. An encyclopedia on one disc. Educorp, Wayzata, and the software that makes optical drives worth buying.

items.title: Windows Enhancements - Hardware
items.description: Early Windows needed help. Hardware add-ons, accelerator cards, and memory managers that made Windows 3.0 actually usable. Aftermarket salvation.

items.title: OS/2
items.description: IBM's OS/2 vs. Microsoft's Windows. They built it together, then went to war. John Soyring from IBM makes the case. History picks the other side.

items.title: Baseball Software
items.description: Hardball III, Tony LaRussa Baseball, and APBA stats. Computer baseball before fantasy leagues went mainstream. Al Michaels does the play-by-play.

items.title: Digital Journalism
items.description: Reporters with laptops, digital cameras that cost a mortgage payment, and the first online news services. Journalism discovers the computer.

items.title: Windows NT
items.description: Windows NT arrives. Microsoft's serious OS for serious people. Networking, security, and the blue screen of death in enterprise-grade.

items.title: The Internet
items.description: Stewart and Gary explain the internet. In 1994. Mosaic, email, and the World Wide Web. The guests are cautiously optimistic. They have no idea.

items.title: Creative Writing Software
items.description: WritePro, Plots Unlimited, and Movie Master. Software that helps you write a screenplay, structure a novel, or outline a mystery.

items.title: CES
items.description: CES 1994. The show floor is a preview of the rest of the decade. Digital cameras, PDAs, and multimedia PCs. Everything is converging.

items.title: Windows 95
items.description: Windows 95. The launch that changed computing. Start button, taskbar, long filenames. Microsoft spent more on marketing than most countries spend on defense.

items.title: Power PC & PowerMac
items.description: The PowerPC chip. Apple and IBM team up against Intel. The PowerMac arrives with benchmarks that embarrass Pentium. Apple fans celebrate. It won't last.

items.title: Greatest Computer Games
items.description: The greatest PC games of the mid-'90s. The titles that made you forget to eat dinner, go outside, or maintain relationships.

items.title: Smart TV
items.description: Smart TV before smart TV. The dream of merging your television with your computer. WebTV, interactive programming, and convergence. The living room isn't ready.

items.title: Computing Seniors
items.description: Seniors discover computers. Email to grandchildren, online communities, and the digital divide. It turns out retirement has bandwidth.

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '96. The annual gift guide for the gadget-obsessed. Products are getting smaller, cheaper, and more confusing.

items.title: Online Tips
items.description: Tips for getting the most out of your internet connection. Bookmarks, search strategies, and why you shouldn't believe everything you read online.

items.title: Greatest Games
items.description: More greatest games. The titles that defined PC gaming in the mid-'90s. First-person shooters, strategy games, and adventures that required a hint book.

items.title: Best of Comdex
items.description: Best of COMDEX '96. Trade show highlights from Vegas. New hardware, new software, and the dot-com bubble inflating in real time.

items.title: Search Engines
items.description: Finding anything online was the hard part, so the show tours the early sites that tried to fix it. Check your own bookmarks against the lineup. The one you use probably isn't on this tape.

items.title: MacWorld Expo Boston
items.description: MacWorld Boston '96. The faithful gather on the east coast. Apple is struggling, Gil Amelio is at the helm, and Steve Jobs is about to come home.

items.title: OS & Browser Updates
items.description: Windows XP, Home against Pro, and the eternal question of whether the upgrade is worth the money. An early iPod wanders in, and the Xbox specs close the show. The upgrade question, the year it was new.

items.title: ETRE Berlin
items.description: ETRE Berlin 1996. European technology conference. The transatlantic tech scene compares notes on where computing is headed.

items.title: Information Overload
items.description: Too much data, too many emails, too many websites. Information overload becomes a real problem. We still haven't figured it out.

items.title: Online Shopping
items.description: Stewart Cheifet goes shopping on the early web: onsale.com's live auctions, CyberCash and DigiCash for paying online, and NetRadio's targeted ads. Jeff Bezos stops by to talk about Amazon.

items.title: Battle of the Browsers
items.description: Netscape vs. Internet Explorer. The browser war that defined the late '90s. Market share, features, and the DOJ lurking around the corner.

items.title: Mac Update
items.description: Mac update. Apple's latest hardware and software. The iMac era is approaching. Cupertino is about to get weird.

items.title: Online Games
items.description: Online gaming over dial-up. Multiplayer matches, MUDs, and the social experience of fragging strangers through a phone line. Lag is a feature.

items.title: Comdex
items.description: COMDEX '98. The trade show at peak dot-com. Everything has an 'e' in front of it. The booths are lavish. The business plans are napkins.

items.title: Parenting
items.description: Computers and parenting. Internet safety, educational software, and the eternal question: how much screen time is too much? Nobody agrees.

items.title: The Virtual University
items.description: The virtual university. Online degrees, distance learning, and the promise of education without walls. The campus of the future is a modem and a dream.

items.title: Cyber Fiction
items.description: Cyber fiction. The novels, films, and cultural moments that imagined our digital future. William Gibson got it right. Most others got it weird.

items.title: Best of Comdex
items.description: Best of COMDEX '97. USB ports, DVD drives, and the gadgets that will define the next two years. The Vegas show floor never disappoints.

items.title: Cyber Privacy
items.description: Privacy on the internet. Cookies, tracking, and data collection. Who's watching you browse? Everyone.

items.title: Best Online Computer Games
items.description: The best online games of the late '90s. Quake, Ultima Online, and the communities that live inside them. Gaming goes multiplayer and never comes back.

items.title: Creating Your Own Website
items.description: How to build your own website. HTML, FTP, and GeoCities. The tools are primitive, the designs are terrible, and it's the most democratic moment in media history.

items.title: Desktop Video
items.description: Desktop video editing. Affordable cameras, FireWire, and software that lets you edit movies on a PC. Hollywood on your desk for under $5,000.

items.title: Travel Planning Online
items.description: Planning vacations on the internet. Travelocity, Expedia, and the end of the travel agent. Book flights in your pajamas.

items.title: Digital Living Room
items.description: The digital living room. DVD players, surround sound, and one remote to rule them all. Your TV and your computer want to be friends.

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '98. Another year, another gift guide. The gadgets are shinier, the prices are lower, and dial-up internet is in every stocking.

items.title: PDAs
items.description: Palm Pilot, Windows CE, and the tiny computers that lived in your pocket before the smartphone ate them all.

items.title: Internet Showcase
items.description: Internet showcase '99. The best websites, online services, and digital experiences of the year. The dot-com boom is at full volume.

items.title: Programming Languages
items.description: Programming languages in 1999. Java, C++, Visual Basic, and the tools that build the internet. Every language has disciples and enemies.

items.title: Web Radio
items.description: Web radio. Streaming audio, internet-only stations, and the promise of infinite channels. Broadband is still a fantasy for most.

items.title: Y2K
items.description: Y2K. The millennium bug. Two digits in a date field might end civilization. Programmers are fixing COBOL at midnight. Banks are stockpiling cash.

items.title: Bill Gates Profile
items.description: Up close with Bill Gates. Sun's John Gage, Fortune's Kirkpatrick, and Red Herring's Perkins assess the most powerful man in technology. He's not done yet.

items.title: Computer Crime
items.description: Computer crime. Hacking, identity theft, and cyber fraud. The criminals are getting smarter and the law is struggling to keep up.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: Computer games at the millennium. Better graphics, bigger worlds, and the LAN party as social event. Gaming is no longer a niche.

items.title: DVD 101
items.description: DVD 101. The shiny disc that replaced your VCR. How it works, why it's better, and which player to buy. The format war is over before it starts.

items.title: Digital Home Movies
items.description: Digital home movies. Consumer camcorders, editing software, and the death of 8mm film. Everyone is a filmmaker now. Most films are of the cat.

items.title: Robots
items.description: Robots in 2000. AIBO, Roomba prototypes, and the machines that will definitely be doing our laundry by 2010. (They won't.)

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '99. The last gift guide of the millennium. Y2K-compliant gadgets, DVD players, and the MP3 player that will change everything.

items.title: ETRE Monte Carlo 1999 Part One
items.description: ETRE Monte Carlo '99, part one. European tech leaders discuss the internet and convergence. The Riviera is a nice place to predict the future.

items.title: ETRE Monte Carlo 1999 - Part Two
items.description: ETRE Monte Carlo '99, part two. E-commerce, broadband, and what happens when the bubble pops. (Spoiler: it pops.)

items.title: Best of COMDEX
items.description: Best of COMDEX '99. The last great COMDEX. Wireless everything, internet appliances, and startups burning cash like firewood. Peak dot-com.

items.title: Computer Games & Gamers
items.description: Games and the people who play them. LAN parties, online clans, and bedroom setups that cost more than the furniture.

items.title: Computer Buyers Guide
items.description: Buying a computer in 2000. Pentium III, iMac, and the question every consumer asks: Mac or PC? The answer depends on who you ask.

items.title: Music on the PC
items.description: Music on the PC. MP3s, Napster's shadow, and the software that turns your computer into a recording studio. The music industry is about to have a very bad decade.

items.title: Computers Without Keyboards
items.description: Computers without keyboards. Voice recognition, touchscreens, and handwriting tablets. The input devices of tomorrow. Some of them actually work.

items.title: Internet Showcase Special Part 1
items.description: Internet showcase special, part one. The best of the web in 2000. Streaming video, online shopping, and websites that load in under thirty seconds.

items.title: Internet Showcase Special Part 2
items.description: Internet showcase special, part two. More gems from the early web. Flash animations, web portals, and the sites that defined an era.

items.title: Cooking with Your PC
items.description: Cooking with your computer. Recipe databases, nutritional software, and the internet as your personal cookbook. Silicon Valley discovers the kitchen.

items.title: Computers & Politics
items.description: Computers and the 2000 election. Online fundraising, voter databases, and digital campaign strategy. Florida's hanging chads are analog, though.

items.title: High Tech Dayton
items.description: High tech in Dayton, Ohio. Wright-Patterson AFB, NCR, and the tech economy outside Silicon Valley. Innovation doesn't need a California address.

items.title: Digital Living Room 2000 Part 1
items.description: The digital living room in 2000, part one. TiVo, DVD, and home theater systems that require an engineering degree to set up.

items.title: Digital Living Room 2000 Part 2
items.description: The digital living room, part two. The convergence box that does everything. It doesn't exist yet, but give it a few years.

items.title: Interactive Television
items.description: Interactive TV. Pressing buttons on your remote to vote, shop, and play along. The technology works, but nobody wants to interact with their television.

items.title: Shareware
items.description: Try it, keep it, mail the author a check. The show explains a software business that ran on floppy disks, bulletin boards and trust, and nobody could make you pay, which was the whole design.

items.title: Home Networking
items.description: Home networking. Ethernet through your walls, wireless routers the size of textbooks, and the dream of every device connected. Your house is becoming a LAN.

items.title: Easy Web Cams
items.description: Webcams. Cheap cameras, grainy video, and the novelty of seeing someone's face through the internet. Video chat is primitive and magical.

items.title: TV Meets PC
items.description: TV meets PC. Tuner cards, picture-in-picture, and watching cable on your monitor. Two screens become one. Nobody asks if they should.

items.title: Creating Your Own Website
items.description: Building a website, part two. Dreamweaver, FrontPage, and the WYSIWYG editors that made HTML optional. Everyone deserves a homepage.

items.title: Wireless Technology
items.description: Wireless technology. 802.11b, Bluetooth, and the dream of cutting every cable. The signals are weak, the speeds are modest, and the freedom is intoxicating.

items.title: Finding a Job Online
items.description: Job hunting on the internet. Monster.com, CareerBuilder, and the death of the newspaper classified. Your resume is now a .doc attachment.

items.title: Security and Viruses
items.description: ILOVEYOU, Code Red, and the worms that brought the internet to its knees. Norton Antivirus is working overtime.

items.title: Online Universities
items.description: Online universities. Distance learning goes mainstream. Accredited degrees from your living room. The campus is everywhere and nowhere.

items.title: Web Surfing on your TV
items.description: Web surfing on your TV. WebTV and its descendants try to bring the internet to people who don't want a computer.

items.title: MP3 Secrets
items.description: MP3 tips and tricks. Ripping CDs, building playlists, and portable players that hold twenty songs. Napster changed everything. The labels are suing everyone.

items.title: Preventing Spam
items.description: Spam. The inbox is under attack. Nigerian princes, pharmacy ads, and the filters that barely work. You've got mail. Thousands of it.

items.title: Windows 98
items.description: Windows 98. USB support, Internet Explorer integration, and the DOJ antitrust case. Microsoft bundles everything and dares you to complain.

items.title: CD ROMs
items.description: The shiny disc is the news: Microsoft Bookshelf, a Boeing manual and an Electronic Arts driving game, all presented as the future. A drive that writes once and never again rounds it out, as a selling point.

items.title: Electronic Publishing
items.description: Electronic publishing. E-books, PDF, and the dream of paperless reading. The screen resolution isn't there yet, but the vision is twenty years ahead.

items.title: Year 2000 (Y2K)
items.description: Y2K again. The millennium bug won't stop being news. COBOL programmers are the most employable people on earth. Planes will not fall from the sky.

items.title: E-Commerce
items.description: E-commerce. Amazon sells books. eBay sells everything else. Online shopping goes from novelty to necessity. Your credit card lives on a server now.

items.title: Computer Games
items.description: More computer games. The late '90s library of titles that turned PCs into entertainment centers. Better sound, better graphics, same addictive gameplay.

items.title: Digital Photography
items.description: Digital photography. The Epson PhotoPC, ink jet printers, and imaging software. Film cameras don't know it yet, but they're already obsolete.

items.title: Portable Computers
items.description: Portable computers in the late '90s. Thinner, lighter, and almost affordable. The laptop is becoming the primary PC for road warriors and students.

items.title: Commodore 64
items.description: The Commodore 64. The best-selling computer in history gets its retrospective. 64K of RAM, BASIC, and a generation of programmers who started here.

items.title: HyperCard
items.description: The man who wrote MacPaint walks the show through his tool for linking cards into stacks, built for people who never planned to program. It came free with the Mac, so plenty of first programs started here.

items.title: Holiday Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '95. The gift guide that reflects a year of massive change. Windows 95, Pentium PCs, and the internet is suddenly in every ad.

items.title: CES
items.description: CES 1997. The Consumer Electronics Show at the height of digital convergence. DVD players launch, PDAs multiply, and everything has a website.

items.title: Notebook Computers
items.description: Notebook computers. The latest portables reviewed. Battery life, screen quality, and weight are the three numbers that matter.

items.title: Personal CAD
items.description: Personal CAD. AutoCAD, TurboCAD, and the software that puts architecture and engineering on a PC. What used to need a drafting table now fits on a floppy.

items.title: Apple II Forever
items.description: The Mac is four years old and Apple II owners are not budging. John Sculley takes the interview, a rare Apple I turns up, and the IIGS gets its turn. Fandom, covered with a straight face.

items.title: Video Game Consoles
items.description: PlayStation, N64, Saturn, and the battle for your living room. The console wars are here and the casualties include your free time.

items.title: Cyber Cafes
items.description: Cyber cafes. Coffee, keyboards, and $8-per-hour internet access. The social spaces of the early web. Checking email has never been this expensive or this hip.

items.title: Buyer's Guide
items.description: Another buyer's guide. Another year of tech products reviewed, ranked, and recommended. The gadgets change, the gift-giving anxiety doesn't.

items.title: Virtual Meetings
items.description: Virtual meetings. Video conferencing, screen sharing, and the promise of never commuting again. The picture is blocky and the audio drops, but the idea is perfect.

items.title: JAVA Tools
items.description: Java tools. Sun's programming language is taking over the web. Applets, servlets, and 'write once, run anywhere.' Enterprise software will never be the same.

items.title: Cars & Computers
items.description: Cars and computers. GPS navigation, engine management, and the onboard computers that mechanics now need a degree to service.

items.title: New Laptops
items.description: New laptops. The latest portables reviewed. Thinner bezels, brighter screens, and battery life measured in hours instead of minutes.

items.title: Interactive Music
items.description: Interactive music. CD-ROMs with music videos, karaoke software, and the multimedia experiences that blur the line between listener and performer.

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '91. The gift guide at the dawn of multimedia. Sound cards, CD-ROM drives, and the first inklings of what PCs will become.

items.title: PC Expo
items.description: PC Expo 1994 from New York. Symantec, IBM, Apple, Motorola, and the companies building the next generation of personal computers.

items.title: Consumers Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '93. Another year of tech gifts reviewed and recommended. Multimedia PCs, inkjet printers, and software that comes on CD-ROM now.

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '93. More product picks, more arguments about which printer to buy, more certainty that next year's tech will be twice as good.

items.title: IBM Personal System/2
items.description: IBM tries to take the PC back from the clones: 3.5-inch drives, VGA and Micro Channel, a bus the clone makers declined to copy. Two of the three became standard. Watch for the third.

items.title: Computer Displays
items.description: Computer displays. CRT monitors from 14 to 21 inches. Dot pitch, refresh rate, and the radiation question. Flat screens are a decade away.

items.title: 3D Graphics
items.description: 3D graphics cards and software. The polygon counts are low, the frame rates are worse, and the future of computing is being rendered in real time.

items.title: Winter CES
items.description: Winter CES '96. The Consumer Electronics Show kicks off the year. New gadgets, new standards, and the consumer tech industry at full sprint.

items.title: New PCs
items.description: New PCs for 1996. Pentium Pro, Windows 95 machines, and affordable desktops that bring computing to every household. The beige box era at its peak.

items.title: Mobile Computing
items.description: Mobile computing. Palm Pilots, Windows CE handhelds, and cellular modems that deliver data at agonizing speeds. The mobile revolution, in its larval stage.

items.title: Best of Comdex
items.description: Best of COMDEX '96, take two. More highlights from the biggest tech trade show. USB, DVD, and the technologies that will define the next five years.

items.title: CES
items.description: CES 2001. The first show of the new millennium. The dot-com crash is underway but the gadgets don't care. XBox previews. Broadband arrives.

items.title: Consumer Buying Guide
items.description: Holiday '92. Gift ideas from the early multimedia era. Sound Blaster cards, 486 PCs, and the software that makes them sing.

items.title: PC Expo
items.description: PC Expo from New York. The industry gathers to show off hardware, software, and networking gear. The trade show circuit is how news travels before the web.

items.title: Buying a New Computer
items.description: How to buy a new computer. Consumer advice that sounds obvious now but was useful when a PC cost two mortgage payments and came with no instructions.

items.title: Holiday Buyers Guide
items.description: Holiday '89. Gary Kildall's last years co-hosting. The gift guide picks are modest by today's standards and enormous by 1989's. A 40MB hard drive is extravagant.

items.title: The Ultimate Gamer's PC
items.description: Building the ultimate gaming PC. CPUs, sound cards, graphics accelerators, and the art of assembling a machine that plays Quake at 30fps.

items.title: Creativity Software
items.description: Creativity software. Computers evolved from calculators to word processors to creative tools. Drawing, animation, and design programs that turn your PC into a canvas.

items.title: Concert in the Park 2018: Brass Connection
items.description: Brass Connection fills the park with horns and harmony on a warm summer night. Classic sound, open air, and a crowd on folding chairs.

items.title: You Can Be a Star (TNN): Contestant Clips (c. 1988)
items.description: Hopefuls compete on TNN, and someone with a VCR saved the clips. One contestant takes on Marty Robbins' "My Woman, My Woman, My Wife," which is a brave pick on a country network.

items.title: Amp It Up: Dan Dragich and the Trainwreck (2013)
items.description: Dan Dragich and the Trainwreck play five folk rock songs for Town Square Television in Dakota County, Minnesota, House of the Rising Sun among them. Host Colleen Fuentes does the introductions in purple light in front of a brick wall.

items.title: Glenbrook South Variety Show: Spellbound (1992)
items.description: Act one of a suburban Illinois high school's annual variety show, with the stage fright left in. Students ran it, the whole school came, and the curtain goes up here.

items.title: St. John's Talent Show (1998)
items.description: Beverly, Massachusetts, May 29, 1998: students at St. John's take the stage and somebody in the audience presses record. Most of this channel exists because of that someone.

items.title: Bass Notes: Mere Mortals (2012)
items.description: Mere Mortals play banjo, mandolin, guitar, ukulele and upright bass on Bass Notes, a local band show made by JCTV volunteer Jeff Bassinson in Jefferson City, Missouri. A brick wall, an acoustic band, and one sit down chat in the middle.

items.title: Hamilton County Fair Junior Talent Show (1993)
items.description: Kids take the stage at the Hamilton County Fair under a big tent, with judges at a table and an MC keeping it moving. Every act walked up there and tried, which is the whole show.

items.title: The Painkillers Blues Band (2016)
items.description: Community radio's studio doubles as a TV set: the Painkillers Blues Band play in one wide shot that never cuts away, a harmonica player in the mix and CD shelves behind. Recorded in Champaign-Urbana, Illinois.

items.title: Foxborough Music: FHS Symphony Orchestra - Lord of the Rings (2010)
items.description: The Foxborough High School Symphony Orchestra takes on Middle-earth at the annual POPS Concert. One does not simply walk past a student orchestra swinging for the epic fences.

items.title: Vermont Youth Philharmonia — The Barber of Seville Overture
items.description: The event is called OrchestraChorusPalooza, which is the right amount of excitement for a youth orchestra and Rossini. Vermont's young players take the Barber of Seville overture at speed.

items.title: Polka Party!: The Mandan Eagles Club (2015)
items.description: Local musicians play polkas, waltzes and old time songs at the Mandan Eagles Club in Mandan, North Dakota, while the dancers kick up their heels. The band is good, but the couples in cowboy hats are the show.

items.title: The DAAC Music Showcase (Grand Rapids, around 2004)
items.description: Nobody labeled this tape, so we say Grand Rapids, around 2004, at the Division Avenue Arts Collective. Eight bands, Cat Time and 25 Suaves among them, and the uploader kept the set list.

items.title: My Craft Show: My Rap Show (Manhattan public access, 1990s)
items.description: Mark Heskin hosted and filmed My Craft Show for Manhattan cable in the early 1990s, and this episode is the one he called his rap show. A bow tie, balloons, a Barbie in a sparkly dress and a puppet each get a turn.

items.title: Somerville Dance Party: Element 109 and Inspector Rick (1989)
items.description: Singers, rappers and dancers take over a Somerville community access studio under a hand painted Dance Party banner. The matching jerseys and the host's tinted glasses are period perfect.

items.title: Paradiddling Percussionist's Panorama: Battle of the Bands
items.description: Young local bands take turns on a plywood stage under a party tent for ACTV's battle of the bands, with a drumstick wielding host. The amps are bigger than the tent, which is part of the fun.

items.title: Swallow Union Lip Sync Contest (1986)
items.description: The lip sync contest at Swallow Union Elementary School in Dunstable, Massachusetts, taped at a school assembly in March 1986. Matching outfits, pom poms and guitars nobody is playing, and afterwards the camera wanders out with the crowd.

items.title: The 2015 Local Music Awards, Live from Hopedale
items.description: A hometown awards night recorded live at Liz's Diamond Bar and Grille in Massachusetts, presented by Ray Auger. When the winners are your neighbors, the applause is on a first-name basis.

items.title: Koto Radio Lip Sync on Telluride TV: Oops I Did It Again (2010)
items.description: Colorado mountain-town winners give Britney's hit a full-commitment performance, and Jeb Berrier catches one of them for a chat. Miming this well is a skill, and nobody here is faking the effort.

items.title: The Uncle Floyd Show: Halloween Special with The Misfits (1998)
items.description: Uncle Floyd, in a jacket louder than the band, hosts the Misfits on North Jersey cable. The uploader says it's the only record of the Michale Graves lineup lip-syncing, which makes this a rare punk oddity.

items.title: Flipside Video Fanzine (1983)
items.description: A punk fanzine you can watch: Flipside went from paper to camcorder, with Perkins Palace, the Starwood and a Darby Crash Band set. Smeared colour is the house style, and the stage dives are in frame.

items.title: "what." a local music tv show: Lily Liver (1994)
items.description: Lily Liver play a dark blue Saint Paul studio, and host Chris Strouth holds court in a red diner booth between songs. The show's pitch was the bands at their best, with the best audio and camera work they could manage.

items.title: Out to Lunch: Finley Creek and the Old Time Fiddlers (1991)
items.description: Missoula spends a lunch hour at Caras Park with a children's theatre troupe, a band and a stage full of fiddlers. Bring a blanket. Nothing about this picnic is in a hurry, and the tape knows it.

items.title: Spotlight: Drinking Water (2011)
items.description: Local band Drinking Water plays live on Spotlight, the student made show at Arizona Western College TV in Yuma. The set has a hand lettered sign for a backdrop and a singer in a plain white T shirt who gives it everything.

items.title: Sessions at Pete's: Chris Hatfield, and Battle of the Bands
items.description: Chris Hatfield and his band play a studio session for Columbia Access Television in Columbia, Missouri, then a teen battle of the bands takes a dark stage. Keyboard, sax, violins and a great deal of purple light.

items.title: Wiky Lip Sync Show (Wikwemikong, Ontario)
items.description: Lip sync from Wikwemikong on Manitoulin Island, Ontario, off a home tape, with paper reindeer and tinsel on the wall behind the stage. The uploader's note says it plainly: not a fundraising event, all done for fun.

items.title: Downbeat TV - Episode Two
items.description: Another round of rhymes and live performance with hosts Joshua Silverstein and Joe Hernandez-Kolski, backed by DJ Jedi Joshua. Tonight's lineup: Lillian Cates, Ryan Haberfeld, and Rawdre & Geniuz.

items.title: Band Edge Christmas Special 2013
items.description: Worcester's local bands and songwriters give a full hour to Christmas songs, played live. Whatever the calendar says, it is December on this channel, and the room sounds happy about it.

items.id: 18.-foxboro-music-video-you-live-too-far-1980s/18.Foxboro Music Video - You Live Too Far 1980s.mp4
items.title: You Live Too Far: Music Video (1980s)
items.description: A 1980s music video for You Live Too Far, shot around a school bus with a band in white shirts and a bus full of kids singing the chorus. It carries Foxboro cable access credits and a Boston production house.

items.title: 2014 Youth Battle of the Bands — Zafro and the 3 Ladies
items.description: Zafro and the 3 Ladies swing for the fences with Metallica's "For Whom the Bell Tolls" and Green Day's "21 Guns." Courthouse-park metal, teenage edition — turn it up.

items.title: Somerfest Youth Talent Show (1989)
items.description: Somerville kids dance, lip sync and ham it up on an outdoor stage, including one very committed KISS fan in full make up. Shot from the back of the crowd as the sun goes down.

items.title: Country Music Jam at Lenox Community Center (Part 2)
items.description: The year's final jam winds down the only proper way, with the whole room joining in on 'Will the Circle Be Unbroken.' A warm and fitting sendoff.

items.title: Old Country Fair: String Music from the Hills (1994)
items.description: Fiddles, banjos and guitars at a hometown fair, shot by the community media crew in Waycross, Georgia. Hill music travels well, even on tape.

items.title: Unalaska This Week: PCR Lip Sync Contest (1989)
items.description: Live from the Community Center in Unalaska, Lynn Fitch hosting, December 1989: a lip sync contest in the Aleutians. Channel 8 later pulled it for Unalaska Rewind, so the town gets to watch itself again.

items.title: A New Vaudeville Revue: Christmas 2012
items.description: The holidays get the full variety-show treatment: music, poetry and skits, played to a live audience that came to be entertained. It bills itself as zany, and on this channel that is a promise.

items.title: CapZeyeZ: SEED in Studio Performance (1996)
items.description: SEED, an unsigned Texas guitar band, plays a studio set for CapZeyeZ, the cable access show about bands nobody has heard of. Several guitars and a leopard print amp on a pink floor.

items.title: Access to Bluegrass: Deadwood and Cedar Creek Junction (2003)
items.description: Bluegrass played in a Battle Creek cable studio for Michigan viewers: banjo breaks, high harmonies, and bands who drove in to play for local TV.

items.title: Mr. Dartmouth 1999: Kyle's Cannon Act
items.description: Kyle takes on a cardboard cannon at Mr. Dartmouth, a high school talent show in 1999, with a prom ticket on the line. Two emcees in formal wear keep order, more or less.

items.title: Elvis Tribute Artist: Cody Ray Slaughter - 2017 Williamson County Fair
items.description: The King lives on under the fairground lights as Cody Ray Slaughter shakes, croons, and curls a lip for the Williamson County crowd. Thank you very much.

items.title: Elvis Bishop Performs (Missoula, 2005)
items.description: Elvis Bishop sings the Presley greatest hits somewhere in Missoula, Montana, 2005, and nobody can say which stage. The tribute is committed. The venue is the only thing that has left the building.

items.title: Melted Cassettes Live
items.description: Somewhere between Skinny Puppy and the Residents lives this live set. Strange, loud, and exactly what late-night community access was made for.

items.title: Comedy Fight Club
items.description: Stand-up served up live from Golden's Deli in Lowertown, St. Paul. The first rule of Comedy Fight Club is you absolutely tell everyone about Comedy Fight Club.

items.title: Coffee House: Zydeco Connection (2011)
items.description: Accordion and rubboard up front, built for dancing. Zydeco is Louisiana Creole party music, and a coffee house floor is a fine place to try the two-step.

items.title: Jam Session in Judique: Cape Breton Fiddlers at the Campbells' (1991)
items.description: Cape Breton fiddlers gather at the Campbells' in Judique, and the Cheticamp community station brought a camera. Judique is fiddle country, so expect speed, and a room that knows every tune.

items.title: Sons of Pitches in Concert
items.description: Six college-age guys, an outdoor brick plaza, hand mics and no instruments. South Burlington's community TV taped the whole set, and each soloist gets a step forward and a turn.

items.title: Country Music Jam at Lenox Community Center (Part 1)
items.description: The last jam of the year moves into the gym, where pickers and players trade country tunes for the pure joy of it. Pull up a folding chair; everybody's welcome.

items.title: The Dazzlin' Days of Rock (Forest Park, 1990)
items.description: A middle school musical revue in a gym with the basketball lines still on the floor. Students in matching black T-shirts take solos while their director plays keyboard. Full commitment, no curtain.

items.title: 2014 Youth Battle of the Bands — Runner-Up (tie): Good Side of Mayhem
items.description: A runner-up finish in Janesville for Good Side of Mayhem, covering Shinedown's ".45" and Sublime's "Santeria." Close enough to the top that you'll want to see why.

items.title: Finneytown Middle School Talent Show (2001)
items.description: A middle school talent show from Cincinnati in 2001, taped from the back of the room for Waycross Community Media: piano, violin, a singer, a karate demonstration and a dance line. The curtain is pink and the nerves are real.

items.title: Hometown Pickin' Show: Rare Combination and the Irish Dancers (2008)
items.description: A monthly acoustic show from Kalamazoo's community access station. Rare Combination plays, and the Hubbardston Irish Dance Troupe steps in to join them. Joe Thorstenson hosts, and nobody hurries.

items.title: Berkshire Television Cerebral Palsy Telethon: The Wanderers (1989)
items.description: The Wanderers play a set for a Berkshire Television cerebral palsy telethon in 1989. Local band, hotel ballroom stage, pledge numbers on screen the whole way, and a very pink guitar shirt.

items.title: Innervision DB69: Six Denver Bands (2009)
items.description: Six Denver-area bands on one club stage, Invisible Orange and Death & Lovers among them, and hosts who take the microphone between sets. The credits end on a phone number for any band that wants on.

items.title: Telethon '91: The Ides of March, Vehicle (1991)
items.description: Vehicle went to number two in 1970, and the Ides of March were still playing it on a 1991 telethon. When you have a hit like that, every room is a big room, and they play it like the charts are listening.

items.title: Hometown Pickin' Show: The Williams Family Band (2007)
items.description: Kalamazoo's traditional-music hour hands the stage to the Williams Family Band. Front-porch harmonies from folks who learned to play the room together.

items.title: Concert in the Park 2018: Super Chief
items.description: Super Chief closes out a warm evening in the park with a set built for the whole neighborhood. Kick off your shoes and stay through the last song.

items.title: Old Time Country Music Fest: Long Time Coming (Chetwynd, 2018)
items.description: Long Time Coming play their full set at the Old Time Country Music Fest in Chetwynd, British Columbia, for CHET TV. Guitars, a ukulele and a fiddle on stage, and older couples dancing across the hall floor.

items.title: Live Oak High School Gong Show: RAD, The Green Manalishi (1983)
items.description: Fleetwood Mac recorded it, Judas Priest covered it, and a high school punk band brings it to a Gong Show anyway. The uploader promises rawness. The tape is not shy about delivering.

items.title: Video Art Music (Tucson, 1984)
items.description: Tucson's local bands made the videos and public access played them: a club stage here, a living-room crooner there, a host who signs off behind a drum kit. Homegrown MTV.

items.title: All the Way Alive: Live at e2 (2010)
items.description: Tod Shelton plays an experimental set after Arts Alive on June 5, 2010, and the uploader kept clips. There is no genre to file it under, so we file it under live.

items.title: The Studio Sessions: Pitz Quattrone and the Earthman Band (2010)
items.description: Pitz Quattrone leads the Earthman Band through an original on didgeridoo, violin, guitar, djembe and bass in the ORCA Media studio in Montpelier, Vermont. Nobody on this stage dresses to match, and it works.

items.title: Olmstead School Lip Sync Contest (2001)
items.description: Fourth, fifth and sixth graders at Richard Olmstead School in Easton, Massachusetts stage their lip sync contest on a gym stage. The costumes are committed, the choreography is ambitious and the interviews are earnest.

items.title: King Louie One Man Band at Dixie's Tavern, New Orleans (2002)
items.description: King Louie plays a one man band set at Dixie's Tavern in New Orleans, guitar and harmonica with a kick drum at his side, filmed in grainy sepia. The microphone has seen worse nights.

items.title: 2014 Youth Battle of the Bands — Runner-Up (tie): Uncut Chaos
items.description: Uncut Chaos lives up to the name with AC/DC's "TNT" and Metallica's "Enter Sandman" in the courthouse park. A tie for runner-up, and every decibel of it earned.

items.title: Threshold: Sean Bruce (2012)
items.description: A live music show for young unsigned bands: invitation only, original songs only, clean lyrics, and you bring your own gear. Community access with a setlist policy, and nobody here is above it.

items.title: Attleboro High School Presents: Battle of the Bands (2011)
items.description: Student bands square off for bragging rights and a roaring gymnasium crowd. Amps up, judges scoring, and one act about to become school legend.

items.title: Live On Reserve: The Hi Matics (2015)
items.description: The Hi Matics play the student run TV studio at the University of Wisconsin in Stevens Point, bearded and in plaid, between the show's own skits and a cartoon. College television, made by people with a deadline and a key to the building.

items.title: "what." a local music tv show: Saucer (1995)
items.description: Saucer plays a set on the purple studio stage of Saint Paul's 'what.' while host Chris Strouth chats with the band in a diner booth. Alternative rock from the Twin Cities, with lunch at the Roadside Inn.

items.title: Live at RFG: Last Waking Moment (2022)
items.description: Greensboro thrash metal in a Boone, North Carolina studio of wood and tapestries, on the music show of Appalachian State's student station. The band plays first, then sits down at the mixing desk to talk it over.

items.title: Glenbrook South Variety Show: GBS B.C. (1989)
items.description: A school's own prime time: student acts, a house full of classmates and parents, and nothing between them and the stage. This is the first half.

items.title: Organic Vapor: The Typewriter Concert (1990)
items.description: The second episode of Organic Vapor, a 1990 Worcester access show of music, poetry and skits hosted by O. Vapor, found in a locked box in the station's vault. Mark plays a mean typewriter, and yes, that is the headline act.

items.title: Capron Park Summer Concert: The Little German Band (2008)
items.description: Oompah in a park: the tuba does the heavy lifting and everyone else does the polka. Best watched with a pretzel and nowhere to be.

items.title: Farmer's Market: The Mandolinquents
items.description: A four-piece string band on a Vermont bandshell: mandolin, guitar, upright bass and fiddle, with the market tents right behind them. MMCTV taped the set. Bring a tomato.

items.title: Groton-Dunstable Regional Middle School Talent Show (2002)
items.description: Everyone in a middle school auditorium knows someone on stage, and that is the whole point. Groton and Dunstable, Massachusetts, February 15, 2002, and a tape that kept the nerves.

items.title: Studio Session: Andre Thierry and Zydeco Magic (2011)
items.description: Andre Thierry's accordion carries zydeco into blues, funk and rock, at an open house for a Palo Alto media center celebrating its community TV award. Clifton Chenier's rule applies: dance, and aches vanish.

items.title: HLPtv Live: Colleen Green
items.description: Colleen Green plays a live set in the HLPtv studio in Los Angeles, guitar and sunglasses under pink and purple lights on a checkerboard floor. It looks like a dream you had after a late movie.

items.title: Ontario Battle of the Bands: Battle 2 (2020)
items.description: Local bands play an outdoor stage on a ballfield under the floodlights for the City of Ontario, California, and the town votes for the winner. Drummers shot from above, one Hawaiian shirt, and a lot of garages emptied onto the grass.

items.title: It's About Time: The Style Band Medley (2012)
items.description: The Style Band, an R&B dance band from the Washington, D.C. area, plays a cover medley on Prince George's Community Television's It's About Time. Pink curtains and stage lights, and nobody is in a hurry.

items.title: Project Coda: Elvis Tribute (2009)
items.description: A singer in black satin and dark glasses does an Elvis tribute for Project Coda on Mountain View's KMVT15, from a studio set out to a sunny patio and a hall full of dancers. The cardboard Elvis never says a word.

items.title: Broward Seniors Got Talent: Pembroke Pines (2019)
items.description: Seniors from a Pembroke Pines center take the stage for the county talent contest in front of a painted street and a Model T. Every act wears a contestant number, and one walks on in a sombrero.

items.title: Billerica Teen Idol: Broadway
items.description: Billerica's teens take turns at the mic against bright chroma-key backdrops while the judges listen. Local access TV at its bravest: no safety net, just a song and a judges' table.

items.title: Quarter Notes: Dave Karr and Gary Berg Dueling Saxophones (1998)
items.description: The Artists' Quarter was a downtown St. Paul jazz club, and SPNN reran this series to mark its closing. Two tenors do the dueling-saxophones tradition in a small room while the piano trio keeps out of the way.

items.title: Accordion Cool with Coach Dave (2022)
items.description: Coach Dave Laprise is on a mission to make the accordion cool again, one old American standard at a time, from a stool in the Attleboro access studio. Fedora, yellow glasses, and half an hour of squeezebox without one apology.

items.title: Culture & Main: York Local Music Showcase (2013)
items.description: Ronn Benway hosts a York, Pennsylvania music showcase from a plaid couch on White Rose Community TV. The walls have flowers on them and so does his shirt; the bill runs from fiddle and banjo to an electric band.

items.title: CMAC'n Live From Fresno: Bobby Joe Neely, Part 2 (2015)
items.description: One man band Bobby Joe Neely sings and plays guitar and drums at the same time on a blue lit studio stage in Fresno, in a red beret. He does it all, as the station put it, and he does not look tired.

items.title: Richmond Summer Concert Series: Red Wing (2001)
items.description: A summer-series set and a talent show share one tape, a double bill of hometown stages. Music first, nerves welcome.

items.title: Sounds of the Tamburitza
items.description: Pittsburgh is a tamburitza town, home of the Tamburitzans, and Pittsburgh's community TV gave the music a show of its own. A band plays Croatian and Serbian folk songs, introduced in English by the host.

items.title: Kids Talent Show: Hosted by Danny Mydlok (1986)
items.description: Danny Mydlok hosts a live Somerville kids' talent contest with puppets, singers, cheerleaders and a square dance on stilts. Call-in voting included, and the tux is something.

items.title: Biggest Turkey Lip Sync Contest (2014)
items.description: Lip syncing in a tent in McMinnville raised over $140,000 for charity, a better return than most real singing. Dorothy gingham, tie dye, and a crowd that knew it was worth it.

items.title: First Fridays Live: Gregory Alan Isakov (2007)
items.description: A South African-born songwriter who farms in Colorado plays community TV's monthly showcase. Quiet songs, a close camera, and nobody talking over the music.

items.title: Music in the Round: Gary Moreau (2001)
items.description: A musician, a full set, and a community access camera that never cuts away. Nobody hurries the song along here, which is the whole reason this channel exists.

items.title: SCAT Talent Show: Folk Trio, Guitarists and Kid Rappers (1991)
items.description: Somerville's community access station stages a talent show on a set of coloured curtains: a folk trio, a poodle skirt dancer, kid rappers and an improv pair. The host reads every intro off a yellow card.

items.title: Dynamite: Christmas Show (1970)
items.description: Mountain kids put on the Christmas edition of Dynamite: skits, dance, lip-synch and a marching band doing 'Winter Wonderland.' The opening montage runs to Bachman-Turner Overdrive, a few years newer than the label.

items.title: Batchelor Middle School Battle of the Bands: Kurdled Milk (2011)
items.description: Kurdled Milk, a band of teachers and one student, plays its one and only Battle of the Bands at Batchelor Middle School in Bloomington, Indiana. There is someone in a cow costume on stage, which seems about right.

items.title: Live & Local at the KiMo Theater: Le Chat Lunatique (2016)
items.description: Le Chat Lunatique get the KiMo, a 1927 theater, for violin, guitars and upright bass under purple light. The city's own Live & Local cameras make sure a neighborhood band gets the good room.

items.title: Big Sky High School Christmas Talent Show (Missoula, 1999)
items.description: Low lights in a Missoula, Montana high school gym, and a Christmas talent show that has room for drummers in Santa hats, a barber skit, the school band and one man dressed in a plastic bag.

items.title: One Hand Clapping (Athens, Ohio public access, 1992)
items.description: Athens, Ohio's public access channel at its loosest: local bands in living rooms, a picture that feeds back on itself, and a man in an apple tree. Ken Dobo's video art, proudly homemade.

items.title: Stay Home Be Social Concert Series: Hosty (2020)
items.description: The city of Norman books its favorite one-man band to play for living rooms during the stay-at-home order. The tip jar is a Venmo handle. Civic spirit, delivered by webcam.

items.title: CapZeyeZ: Near Dark at The Back Room, Austin (1990)
items.description: A band called Near Dark, live at The Back Room in Austin. Not the vampire film. CapZeyeZ taped unsigned bands nobody had heard of, as it really happens, and the crew worked for free.

items.title: Lickety Split: Live at The Back Room, Austin (1990)
items.description: Lickety Split plays a full late night set at The Back Room in Austin, Texas, shot on a camcorder from the floor. The light rig is doing a lot of work and the hair is doing the rest.

items.title: The Brick Wall: Open Mic Variety Show Highlights
items.description: A highlights reel from The Brick Wall, a live open mic variety show from North Shore TV on Long Island: bands, a string band, a Superman sketch and a host who keeps it moving. Brick backdrop, red curtains, everyone trying.

items.title: Video Jam: Jimmy Buffett and Toby Keith (2013)
items.description: A Worcester public access show plays music videos back to back: indie bands nobody sent a limo for, then Jimmy Buffett and Toby Keith. A horse head mask, a pool party and a karaoke bar get three minutes each.

items.title: Hamilton County Fair Junior Talent Show (1994)
items.description: Cincinnati's Hamilton County Fairgrounds: packed bleachers, three judges at a long table and a banner that says Puttin' on the Hits. Waycross brought the camera, the kids brought everything else.

items.title: Downbeat TV - Episode Three
items.description: Hosts Joshua Silverstein and Joe Hernandez-Kolski spin the mic with DJ Jedi Joshua, welcoming Nick Yatroussis, Jake Sonny, and Ka'lynn Youngblood. Public-access variety with a hip-hop pulse.

items.title: ICTN: Randy Erwin, the Yodeling Cowboy (1998)
items.description: Randy Erwin yodels, strums and twirls a rope for a room of kids at a public library in Irving, Texas. The kids sit on the carpet and a few of them end up dancing with him.

items.title: New Wave Theatre (1981)
items.description: A Los Angeles new music show from a Burbank studio, with a host, a ghost host and a string of bands playing in the dark. Bring a flashlight, because the picture does not come with one.

items.title: Open Mic Night at Cape Media
items.description: A Wednesday night at Cape Cod's community media center, and every local who signed up gets a turn at the mic. The upload's only note is an email for next time. Consider it an invitation.

items.title: Belmont Idol 2014
items.description: Belmont's answer to a certain TV singing contest, staged for the hometown crowd. Local voices, high stakes, one shot at the title.

items.title: Alternative Views: The Worldly Warblers (1983)
items.description: Satire in song, pulled from earlier Alternative Views shows: Esther's Follies, Charlie King and Blackberri. The mailing address on screen is long dead, but the opinions kept.

items.title: Willard Alternative High School Talent Show (Fall 2002)
items.description: Willard Alternative High School's first talent show put a skateboarder and a harmonica player on the same bill. Talent was defined generously, which is the right call.

items.title: ABC No Rio's Cardboard Air Band (1982)
items.description: Christy Rupp, Joseph Nechvatal and Walter Robinson, all artists, play a band in cardboard outside ABC No Rio, the Lower East Side art space. The saxophones fool nobody, which is the point.

items.title: Feehan's Got Talent (2014)
items.description: A home-grown talent show with a name on the door and an audience in the room. The upload gives only the title, so you meet the acts cold, the way the folding chairs did.

items.title: Dana Gray Fine Arts Night & Talent Show 2013
items.description: Fine Arts Night doubles as a talent show, and the whole school gets its turn to shine. The kind of evening that lives forever on a camcorder tape.

items.title: "what." a local music tv show: The Cows (1995)
items.description: The Cows, the Twin Cities noise-rock band on Amphetamine Reptile, sit down to lunch at the Roadside Inn with host Chris Strouth. The show's promise was bands at their best, and lunch.

items.title: Ricky Jam: It's Your Time (1989)
items.description: Mauro DePasquale writes and produces, a Worcester access studio supplies the cameras, and everybody commits. Ambition on a public-access budget, with no one in the room telling it no.

items.title: Talent Show for the Organ Fund (Richmond, Vt.)
items.description: A Vermont town raises money for a church organ the way small towns do: a talent show. Singers, dancers, a guitar, an old-time band in hats, and a school auditorium full of neighbors.

items.title: Electric Earth Music Video Showcase
items.description: Homegrown music videos set to original local music, all in one showcase. Proof that a scene can make its own picture and its own sound.

items.title: Big Nick and the Homewreckers: Reunion Concert (1991)
items.description: A blues-rock reunion in a small room, harmonica up front and a hand-lettered bedsheet for a banner. Waycross Community Television in Forest Park, Ohio, taped it. The band got back together.

items.title: HughShows: Weird Paul Rock Band
items.description: Host Hugh Twyman sits down with lo-fi cult heroes Weird Paul Rock Band for a live set and chat at Pittsburgh Community Television. Scrappy, sincere, and proudly homemade.

items.title: Keeping It Bluegrass: Local Bluegrass Jam (2013)
items.description: A local bluegrass jam for Access Nashville on a log cabin set hung with flags: fiddle, banjo, mandolin, guitars and an upright bass. The players take turns at the microphone and nobody rushes anybody.

items.title: CapZeyeZ Live! with Hanover Fist and Razbone (1991)
items.description: CapZeyeZ exists to cover unsigned bands nobody has heard of, live as it happens. This Austin public access broadcast has Hanover Fist and Razbone in the studio, the phone line on screen and club clips of a dozen bands.

items.title: The Gong Show (1988)
items.description: Emcee Don Bleu runs another round of amateur acts with the Fat Boys, Rebeca Arthur and Kurt Rambis on the judges' panel. A pair of singing security guards are on the bill and the gong is never far away.

items.title: This Ascension: Live at Zelo's Nightclub, Santa Barbara (1989)
items.description: This Ascension plays a live set at Zelo's Nightclub in Santa Barbara, billed as ambient goth techno. Dim stage, coloured lights and a singer who means every word.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1980 Episode 1473 Windstorm in Bubbleland Part 3.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Mister Rogers Makes an Opera
items.description: King Friday and Daniel Striped Tiger both sound like Fred Rogers, and the Neighborhood of Make-Believe is about to stage an opera. A bakery visit comes first, and a banana sandwich.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1982 Episode 1499 Pets Part 4.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Pets, Part 4
items.description: A golden retriever walks in, cats turn up along a street, and the puppets take their turn. Then the jacket goes back on, and the goodbye is as kind as the hello.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Gila Monsters Meet You at the Airport
items.description: A boy dreads the West, so LeVar Burton goes to Arizona to meet a biologist and the real lizard. Being afraid of a place gets easier once you've met the neighbors.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: The Tortoise and the Hare
items.description: Aesop says slow and steady wins, so LeVar Burton goes and asks cyclists, gymnasts and a karate class. The old fable finally gets some evidence.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 1/Arthur - S01E11-E12 - Locked in the Library! + Arthur Accused! SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: Locked in the Library! / Arthur Accused!
items.description: Buster pulls on a detective coat to solve a brownie-mix mess at school and treats it as the case of the year. Somebody has to take the small mysteries seriously.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 1/Arthur - S01E33-E34 - Meek for a Week + Arthur, World's Greatest Gleeper SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: Meek for a Week / Arthur, World's Greatest Gleeper
items.description: Arthur gets blamed for something he knows nothing about, a feeling every kid has had. The little film of a child reading in the middle was left in, and we're glad it was.

items.title: Clifford: Clifford's Carnival / Clifford's Doggy Reunion
items.description: Emily Elizabeth is named for the author's own daughter. A pumpkin patch and a carousel, then a beach and a swing, and Cleo and T-Bone stop by at the end.

items.title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
items.description: Clifford's name came from somebody's childhood imaginary friend, which may be why he's so big. He shares a small city apartment, then heads to the park to see the neighborhood dogs.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: Inside Ralphie
items.description: Ralphie is home sick, so Ms. Frizzle drives the whole class inside him. A tour of blood cells and one enormous nose, and a better lesson than any diagram.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: Kicks Up a Storm
items.description: Take chances, make mistakes, get messy: weather is a messy subject, so Ms. Frizzle is in her element. The class rides the sun's heat up into the sky and meets the storm there.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1983 Episode 1524 Conflict Part 4.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Conflict, Part 4
items.description: Fred Rogers once defended public television before the Senate by reciting a song about feeling mad. Here neighbors and puppets handle the same feeling plainly, without a lecture.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1985 Episode 1549 Music Part 4.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Music, Part 4
items.description: Fred Rogers studied music composition, and you can hear it when a tuba, French horn and trumpet play together. Then the knights hold a festival in the Neighborhood of Make-Believe.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: The Paper Crane
items.description: A picture book turns into animation, then LeVar Burton visits origami and taiko drumming. A boy reviews a book about two cultures learning each other's table manners, and says it well.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Mufaro's Beautiful Daughters
items.description: John Steptoe published his first picture book at 18; this tale of two sisters came years later and won a Caldecott Honor. LeVar Burton brings a drum maker and a park full of dancing kids.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 1/Arthur - S01E55-E56 - I'm a Poet + The Scare-Your-Pants-Off Club! SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: I'm a Poet / The Scare Your Pants Off Club!
items.description: Marc Brown first told Arthur as a bedtime story, which may be why a scary-book club knows exactly how the dark feels. A poetry story among the stacks comes first.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 2/Arthur - S02E15-E16 - Arthur vs. the Piano + The Big Blow-Up SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: Arthur vs. the Piano / The Big Blow-Up
items.description: Piano lessons, band class and a soccer game: three childhood worries in a row. A young trumpet player stops by in the middle. Most of us can still hear the metronome.

items.title: Clifford: Clifford on Parade / Follow the Leader
items.description: Clifford's home is Birdwell Island, where a pier day rolls into a swap meet and a big red dog wanders among the piles of junk. The island runs on small errands.

items.title: Clifford: Babysitter Blues / Saturday Morning
items.description: A painter and a scientist on the dunes, a neighborhood cookout, a sheriff who plays with T-Bone at his desk. Everyone in this town has time for a dog, and it looks like a good town.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: In the Haunted House
items.description: A dark old mansion full of instruments and portraits, and a name worth remembering: Professor Contralto. Liz the lizard comes along as witness, which is what a spooky house needs.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: Blows its Top
items.description: Volcanoes are hard to explain from a desk, so Ms. Frizzle turns the bus into a submarine and takes the class to one. The lava is already on the move when they arrive.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1987 Episode 1575 Dance Part 5.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Dance, Part 5
items.description: A weaver at her loom, a dancer, and folk dancers in costume all get the same unhurried attention. The loom is allowed to be exactly as interesting as the dance.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1988 Episode 1600 Secrets Part 5.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Secrets, Part 5
items.description: Fred Rogers trusted children with the subject of secrets, which plenty of grown-ups duck. The puppets and a birthday party carry it, and nobody hurries.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Sunken Treasure
items.description: A diving robot, a wreck, and a dog hunting treasure on a beach. LeVar Burton's treasure maps always ended at the library shelf, and that was the point.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Come a Tide
items.description: Stephen Gammell, who drew Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark, also illustrated a picture book about a flood. LeVar Burton adds clouds, lightning and what to do in a tornado: the useful kind of weather lesson.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 2/Arthur - S02E37-E38 - D.W.'s Name Game + Finders Key-pers SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: D.W.'s Name Game / Finders Key-pers
items.description: D.W. is short for Dora Winifred, so a name game is home turf for her. Then Arthur and Buster follow a lost key, with the kids' segment still sitting between the stories.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 3/Arthur - S03E19-E20 - Attack of the Turbo Tibbles + D.W. Tricks the Tooth Fairy SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: Attack of the Turbo Tibbles / D.W. Tricks the Tooth Fairy
items.description: The Tibbles twins in robot costumes, D.W. matching wits with the tooth fairy. The stakes are bedtime-sized, which are the biggest stakes there are.

items.title: Clifford: Potluck Party Pooper / The Best Gift
items.description: John Ritter voiced Clifford, which may be why the biggest dog on television always sounds so easily amused. Two quiet stories: a neighbor's painting, then shells by the sea at sunset.

items.title: Clifford: Stinky Friends / He's Wonderful Mr. Bleakman
items.description: A sign in a field, an outing on a pier, Clifford curled up in a fountain with the kids. The plot is small. The dog is not.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: The Busasaurus
items.description: Ms. Frizzle will drive a school bus anywhere, and this time it's a dinosaur dig, then a prehistoric jungle with herds, eggs and a T. rex. A phone call closes it out, as one does.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: Ups and Downs
items.description: A submarine dives by taking on water and rises by pushing it out, so the bus turns submarine for a lakeside look at floating and sinking. Ms. Frizzle's sister calls at the end.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1990 Episode 1626 Mouths and Feelings Part 1.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Mouths and Feelings, Part 1
items.description: Fred Rogers held that anything mentionable can be made more manageable, and he starts with something as ordinary as a mouth. Gingerbread cookies bake along the way.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1992 Episode 1651 Learning Part 1.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Learning, Part 1
items.description: A week about learning, and nobody is in a hurry to finish it. A visitor stops at the porch with a wooden box, and you get to wonder what's inside too.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Nosey Mrs. Rat
items.description: The rat can't mind her own business, and a primatologist gets paid to watch chimpanzees. Curiosity gets a book and then a career, and kids sit as the jury.

items.title: Reading Rainbow: Uncle Jed's Barbershop
items.description: A traveling barber saves for a shop of his own, and the book lets the saving take as long as it takes. Kids then pass along what to read next.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 4/Arthur - S04E07-E08 - The Contest + Prove It SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: The Contest / Prove It
items.description: A torn sticker is a real crisis in Arthur's world, and the show never pretends otherwise. Kept as aired, with the live-action kids' segment right where it landed.

items.id: arthur-1996-complete_202203/Season 5/Arthur - S05E07-E08 - The World Record + The Cave SDTV.mp4
items.title: Arthur: The World Record / The Cave
items.description: A world record, then a cave full of bats, with the kids' segment in the middle just as it aired. If you like the dark, the second half is a friendly one.

items.title: Clifford: When I Grow Up / Not Now, I'm Busy
items.description: Everybody tries on a new job, from doctor to karate student, while Clifford herds in a cowboy hat. Being enormous has never once been his problem.

items.title: Clifford: A Big Help / The Trouble with Kittens
items.description: The trouble is a kitten, a sprinkler and a hula hoop, exactly the size a small kid can follow. Clifford is red because red paint was on hand.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: In the Rainforest
items.description: The class takes the bus into a rainforest, where cocoa trees, a stuck truck and a man in a white suit with a plan all want attention. Ms. Frizzle stays calm through every bit of it.

items.title: The Magic School Bus: Sees Stars
items.description: A pitchman in a star-covered suit will sell you a star on TV. Ms. Frizzle's class goes to see where the real ones come from, and the real ones don't charge.

items.id: mister-rogers-neighborhood-complete-50th-anniversary-tv-series/Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Season 1994 Episode 1677 Going Away & Coming Back Part 2.mp4
items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Going Away and Coming Back, Part 2
