items.title: ARTU German Quality Drill Bits from New Style Direct
items.description: German drill bits, an Australian budget and a taping date of 18 April 2009: the bits go through brick, hardened steel and a padlock, and the production values stop well short of that.

items.title: Ronco Showtime Rotisserie and BBQ (2000)
items.description: A man in a green apron sets a rotisserie and walks away, to applause. The chickens, shrimp and kebabs keep turning, and so does the studio audience.

items.title: Mind Power from Gateways Research Institute
items.description: The case for training your mind is made in a study full of bookshelves, by a calm host who brings an elephant as evidence. It's the best-furnished argument on the channel.

items.title: Mutual Fund Profits with Steve Crowley (1992)
items.description: A system to beat the system, with Peter Lynch and Norman Fosback lined up as the credentials. The promise is a thousand funds narrowed to five. Nobody is selling it now, which is the safest way to watch.

items.title: Infomercial for Orbitrek Elite
items.description: Mark Spitz won seven golds in 1972 and, by this Australian tape, is lending his face to the Orbitrek Elite. The recording runs out in the middle of a hair laser, as the best 3 a.m. tapes do.

items.title: Total Trolley (2003)
items.description: The Total Trolley's pitch is that it replaces three things, the oldest move in the genre: a gadget sold as a way to own fewer gadgets. The Archive saved the rest of Sylmark's catalogue too.

items.title: Sci Fi Channel Late Night Infomercials (c. 1996)
items.description: Mr. C from Happy Days turns up at the end hosting Money Makers Live!, after an acne kit and a psychic network have had their turn. The Sci Fi Channel's night shift, as the 1990s sold it.

items.title: 1984 Computer Store Display Disc: Computers and Software (1984)
items.description: A demo reel for a computer store that never existed, pressed on RCA's CED videodisc, the one a stylus played like a record. The format was nearly out of road; the green screens look sure of themselves.

items.title: Arnold's Gourmet Kitchen: The Daily Mixer Demonstration (1989)
items.description: An estate sale in Parma, Ohio gave up the mixer pitch somebody had kept all those years. It ends in fireworks, which no mayonnaise has ever earned.

items.title: Overnight on Discovery: ProCede, AeroGarden and Bowflex (2008)
items.description: Les Stroud spends an episode of Survivorman alone in the wild, then Discovery hands you three ways to survive the living room: hair, herbs and abs, in that order.

items.id: uanvideo/Kmart Smart Plan Sales VHS Video.mp4
items.title: Kmart Smart Plan Sales Video
items.description: An infomercial whose audience is the Kmart employee: a presenter teaches the floor staff how to sell you a service plan. In the role plays the shopper says no twice, politely, and the training carries on.

items.title: NBC Infomercial Block: Worx GT and Dual Action Cleanser (2008)
items.description: A Roanoke NBC station's overnight block from June 2008, still wearing the 'Newschannel 10' tags it had dropped the year before. Even the branding was working the night shift past its time.

items.title: Tony Little's Gazelle Experience 2K10
items.description: Naming a workout glider '2K10' puts a use-by date on it, but Tony Little, ponytail and all, is the kind of pitchman who outlasts his model numbers. A countdown clock keeps the hurry going.

items.title: TNT Amusements Showroom Video (1995)
items.description: The way to sell a reconditioned pinball machine in 1995, apparently, was to put the showroom on tape and let a man in a suit walk you through it. You can't hear the flippers, but he swears.

items.title: Atari Jaguar 64-Bit Infomercial
items.description: Atari's last home console gets sold in a cave, where a guide in a leather jacket teaches a man named Bob what 64-bit means. The couch is nice. The company was out of hardware by 1996.

items.title: Philips CD-i: A Day with Sid, Ed and CD-i
items.description: A day on a delivery route where every household turns out to need a Philips CD-i. It's a lovely fantasy; in the real 1990s the machine sold poorly and Philips gave up on it.

items.title: DR Trimmer/Mower Video (1999)
items.description: A Vermont company's sales video, built mostly from owners vouching for the machine from Pennsylvania to Alberta. Most infomercials sell you a lifestyle; this one sells you taller grass.

items.title: RCA DSS Digital Satellite System with DirecTV
items.description: RCA's little dish launched with DirecTV in 1994, and this is the sales pitch for it. Rare for this channel: the pitch turned out right.

items.title: FoodSaver Compact II Vacuum Sealer (1999)
items.description: FoodSaver is still on kitchen shelves today, which most gadgets sold at this hour can't say. The nuts and cheese get sealed first; the can crushing is promised after the break.

items.title: Proactiv Solution: The Answer for Acne (1999)
items.description: Proactiv came from two dermatologists, Katie Rodan and Kathy Fields, and Guthy-Renker sold it to the world. One woman here says she heard about it from an infomercial: the pitch, working.

items.id: mean-machines-sega-issue-1-vhs-uk/Mean Machines Sega issue 1 VHS UK.ia.mp4
items.title: Mean Machines Sega Mega Preview Tape (1992)
items.description: Before game trailers lived online, a British magazine publisher put them on tape. Sonic 2 is the headliner, and the closing price on a console is the real cliffhanger.

items.title: Richard Simmons: Food Mover and Groovin' in the House (1999)
items.description: Richard Simmons sells a board of magnets for counting food, taped between two preachers on a religious cable channel, and he never turns it down. He left public life in 2014, so this is the volume we miss.

items.title: Aero ExtraBed by Imaginair (1998)
items.description: Every family has the weekend the relatives arrive and nobody has a bed, and the Aero ExtraBed sells itself to that fear with a stopwatch, twice. The cushions are the ones who suffer.

items.title: Psychic Friends Network: Psychic Friends Fair at the Mall of America (1996)
items.description: Dionne Warwick fronted the Psychic Friends on television; here the psychics go to the Mall of America and set up tables, so the future competes with the shopping bags. The hotline gets a better seat than the guests.

items.title: HomeRight Paint Stick Painting System (1992)
items.description: The whole suspense of this half hour is whether anyone drips. Pink goes up, yellow goes up, the paint feeds through the handle of the roller, and the studio wall stays spotless.

items.id: assortment-of-instructional-tapes-public-domain-videos-and-infomercials/1996 Hoover Dirt Finder Power Drive Infomercial.mp4
items.title: Hoover Self-Propelled Dirt Finder Power Drive (1996)
items.description: Hoover's name is a verb in Britain, and here it sells a light that turns green when the carpet is clean, which is more feedback than any other chore has ever offered. The birdcage gets vacuumed bravely.

items.title: Kitchenmate Chopper (1995)
items.description: No cord, no battery, no plug: the whole pitch is that your arm is the motor. The man in the maroon sweater looks honoured to be the demonstration, and the woman in the blue apron has seen him do it before.

items.title: Facial Magic with Cynthia Rowland (1998)
items.description: A face-lift you do yourself, with exercises and a gel mask, pitched to two women on a pastel sofa who agree on everything. Sylmark made a catalog of these, and somebody saved the whole catalog.

items.title: Sylmark Mighty Pro Grill (1999)
items.description: A chef in a red neckerchief promises that the fat rolls out and the flavor steams in, over a stovetop plate and a meatloaf. The uploader filed it with Sylmark's other pitches, which is how you archive a catalog.

items.title: Light Relief
items.description: A hand-held light pad for aches, pitched on a garden lawn, in direct competition with the sun. The golf course testimonial is the one that stays with you.

items.title: Walkfit Platinum Orthotics
items.description: Insoles are the product, but the free slippers are the plot: they return every few minutes, which tells you what the audience was really being sold. The doctor's bar chart can't compete.

items.title: The Drum Buddy Show: Midwest Industries International (1999)
items.description: A tin can and a wooden box promise you'll play like a pro by the end of the show, and a puppet show is called in to help, which tells you how that's going. The New Orleans audience stays polite.

items.title: Luminess Air Airbrush Makeup (2015)
items.description: Taped off ABC Family a couple of months before it became Freeform, so the channel is getting a makeover too. The airbrush's new no-mess tip gets its own graphic, like a moon landing.

items.title: Enforma System: Fat Trapper and Exercise Bottle (1999)
items.description: Eat what you like, the testimonials say. The FTC took a different view of the Fat Trapper and Exercise in a Bottle claims, which makes this half hour evidence with a bikini loop.

items.title: OxiClean from Orange Glo International (1998)
items.description: Billy Mays, before the shout made him famous, stands in a laundry room and pitches OxiClean one stain at a time. Church & Dwight bought the company in 2006.

items.title: Dick Clark's Rock 'n' Roll Era: Time Life Music (1995)
items.description: Dick Clark spent decades presenting this music on American Bandstand, free with your television. Here it comes in a box, and the diner he does it from is the friendliest checkout counter on cable.

items.id: succes-n-life-with-robert-tilton-infomercial-1991-most/Succes 'N Life with Robert Tilton infomercial (1991, most).mp4
items.title: Success 'N Life with Robert Tilton (1991)
items.description: Pastor Robert Tilton talks to the camera about a growth program built on Biblical principles and offers a free book to callers. His hands do about half the work.

items.title: Toast and Coffee Video Magazine, Volume 1 Number 1 (1992)
items.description: A VHS magazine for a computer card that promised every town its own TV studio. It did get Babylon 5's spaceships, rendered on Amigas and Toasters, which is a better outcome than most revolutions.

items.title: Solera Sunrooms by KoolVent (1987)
items.description: It interrupted The Wild Geese, a film about mercenaries on a mission, to sell a glass room with a hot tub. Both promised an escape, and only one needed a bank of operators standing by.

items.title: Psychic Solution: Amazing Psychic Readings (1998)
items.description: Taped off CFCN in Calgary, where a psychic who already knows the callers' affairs invites the whole country to call in. Canada is a lot of lines to read. The yellow jacket seems up to it.

items.title: Peter Popoff Miracle Ministries: Miracle Spring Water
items.description: James Randi showed the Tonight Show audience in 1986 how Peter Popoff's 'revelations' reached him by radio. The comeback is on this tape: free miracle spring water, and a number that never leaves the screen.

items.title: Lionel Video Catalog (1991)
items.description: The 1991 line, read aloud by a narrator who never raises the volume, because a company selling trains since 1900 knows its customer is already sold. Snoopy and Mickey ride the hand cars.

items.title: Sega 32X: Absolutely Rose Street (1994)
items.description: Sega put the 32X inside a soap opera, which makes sense: the add-on had the lifespan of a sweeps-week romance, gone by 1996. The Archive says it sat unseen for twenty years.

items.title: As Seen On TVPC: Systemax AMD Athlon 1.4 GHz
items.description: The 1.4 GHz Athlon was a very fast chip for about a minute in 2001, and this bundle still hands you a joystick and a printer to go with it. Complete meant something different then.

items.title: Flowbee Haircut System with Rick Hunt (1988)
items.description: That is the inventor, Rick Hunt, doing his own pitching, and a clipper wired to a vacuum outlasted nearly every gadget of its day: the Flowbee is still sold.

items.title: AirCore Cookware on Teleshop Mall (1999)
items.description: From Seven Sydney's Teleshop Mall, so the 3 a.m. pitch has an Australian accent: a pan that cooks dinner while you run errands, and two women delighted that nobody touches the stove.

items.title: Philips CD-i: The Imagination Machine (1994)
items.description: Philips sells the CD-i player as the Imagination Machine, from a glowing futuristic set with an encyclopedia, a tennis game and a very patient pair of hosts. The set looks like an airport at the end of the world.

items.title: Bose Acoustic Wave Music System with Herbie Hancock
items.description: Herbie Hancock played in Miles Davis's quintet in the sixties, so when he sits at a piano and tells you a small Bose box can hold up beside it, that is the best-credentialed endorsement on the channel.

items.title: Dream Swing Golf Trainer
items.description: The pitch is that you can fix a golf swing by being strapped to a tripod, and credit where it's due: they shot it at PGA National and brought a touring pro to stand next to the contraption.

items.title: Roadshow Home Video: October 1984 Dealer Presentation
items.description: A tape for video store owners, not customers: the big October release is Sean Connery's unofficial Bond comeback, Never Say Never Again, sold by two guys in VIDEO VIDEO VIDEO T-shirts.

items.title: Video Professor: Learn Computers Free (2004)
items.description: That is the founder himself, John Scherer, in a Denver mall, and the trick of the pitch is that every skeptic he meets is converted on camera before the half hour is out.

items.title: New Rock-afire Explosion Demo Tape
items.description: Creative Engineering built the animatronic band behind ShowBiz Pizza Place, and here it sells the animals to any restaurant with a stage. The host promises a pop quiz, an unusual thing to threaten restaurateurs with.

items.title: The Satellite TV Story: Dealer Demo Tape (1980)
items.description: A dealer tape for the backyard dish boom, which got a rude shock when HBO began scrambling its signal in 1986. The man in the Showtime shirt explains every bolt like someone with no idea what's coming.

items.id: powerwalk-plus-with-bruce-and-kris-jenner-1994-infomercial/PowerWalk Plus with Bruce and Kris Jenner - 1994 Infomercial.mp4
items.title: PowerWalk Plus with Bruce and Kris Jenner (1994)
items.description: Thirteen years before Keeping Up with the Kardashians, Bruce and Kris Jenner were already a camera-ready couple selling a lifestyle, and this time the product is a walking machine with no motor.

items.id: jane-fonda-s-walk-to-the-music-fitness-tread-1994-infomercial/Jane Fonda's Walk to the Music Fitness Tread - 1994 Infomercial.mp4
items.title: Jane Fonda's Walk to the Music Fitness Tread (1994)
items.description: Jane Fonda's 1982 workout tape helped launch the home-video fitness boom, which is why her name alone sells this treadmill. The pitch assumes you already trust Jane, and that is most of the pitch.

items.title: Ab Swing V4 (2003)
items.description: This is the early ab-gadget market in miniature: a seat that swings you through sit-ups, a free meal plan to fix whatever the seat can't, and a patio sunny enough to need no weather report.

items.title: Chrysler 300M, LHS and Concorde Promotional Video (1999)
items.description: Chrysler revived the 300 badge from its 1950s letter cars for this one, and the tape knows it: everyone speaks softly, as if loud would scuff the leather. A brochure with a speaking part.

items.title: Q-Ray Ionized Bracelet (2003)
items.description: The FTC later sued the seller, and won, which makes the calm of the man in the blue polo by the pond the real attraction.

items.id: TheVistaGroup-TheSeeClearlyMethod2002/The See Clearly Method VHS • 60 FPS BV 2002.ia.mp4
items.title: The See Clearly Method (2002)
items.description: Mariette Hartley made her name in Polaroid ads opposite James Garner, so the host here already knows how to make a sales pitch sound like affectionate couple's banter.

items.title: Rejuvenique with Linda Evans (2002)
items.description: Dynasty's Linda Evans sells a pulse mask that the uploader says looks like Jason Voorhees, and the flowery couch goes right on pretending it's skincare.

items.title: QVC Gadgets & Gizmos with Dan Wheeler (1996)
items.description: Dan Wheeler hosts the kind of QVC hour where a duck-shaped fan sits beside the binoculars as if they were related, and the vacuum sealer sells out on air to nobody's surprise but his.

items.title: Pee-Wee's Playhouse Video Collection Box Set (1996)
items.description: The King of Cartoons was William Marshall, who also played Blacula, and here he's on a talk-show couch selling you your Saturday mornings on VHS.

items.id: the-fabulous-fifties-cds-promo-with-regis-philbin-and-paul-doherty/The Fabulous Fifties CDs promo with Regis Philbin and Paul Doherty.mp4
items.title: The Fabulous Fifties CD Collection with Regis Philbin and Paul Doherty (2001)
items.description: Regis Philbin was hosting Who Wants to Be a Millionaire when he made this, so he went from asking the final question to selling you the fifties hits at 3 a.m.

items.title: Bowflex Power Pro (2002)
items.description: Taped off FX in March 2002, with the company's VP of Marketing co-hosting, which tells you who owned this pitch. BowFlex filed for bankruptcy in 2024.

items.title: The Balance Bracelet (2002)
items.description: Taped off FX in March 2002: a booth host, a bracelet that gets more close-ups than anyone in the cast, and a golfer, a cowboy and a man on a ladder as the supporting players.

items.title: Cardio Twister on the Expo Channel
items.description: An American infomercial that wound up on Australian screens, taped in April 2009 by someone who pressed record in time. The platform twists, the class twists, and the number never leaves the screen.

items.title: VCR Voice Programmer (1993)
items.description: The blinking 12:00 gets a spoken cure: a man in a blue shirt, fed up with the manual, tells the VCR what to record, and Ma watches it obey. Every house with a VCR knew the problem.

items.title: Kodak ESP 7 All-in-One Printer (2009)
items.description: Kodak's pitch was cheap ink, a bold line from a company that would file for bankruptcy in January 2012. The studio audience holds up its prints, and the bonuses stack up on schedule.

items.title: Chef-O-Matic Pro Ten in One Cooker (2011)
items.description: Ten cooking jobs in one pot, and a payment plan that loses an instalment mid-show, from four to three, while the pot roast and the cake keep coming. The cooker was not the only thing getting reduced.

items.id: billy-mays_202505/Space Savers_Wash-Matik_Super Shammy infomercial, 7_23_1989 (EARLY Billy Mays appearance!!).mp4
items.title: What's New? Space Savers, Wash-Matik and Super Shammy (1989)
items.description: Billy Mays, who worked the Atlantic City boardwalk before he worked television, gets three products into one half hour, and the closet hangers get the warmest welcome by far.

items.title: Turbo Tiger with Billy Mays (2001)
items.description: Billy Mays sets a gold handheld vacuum on pushpins, beans and cat hair, and the order card shows up twice in case you missed it.

items.title: Kmart 1989 Christmas In-Store Video
items.description: Milli Vanilli shares Kmart's Christmas reel with Aerosmith and Tracy Chapman, within a year of losing the Grammy. The songs run, nobody speaks, and the cassettes do the selling.

items.title: Dual Saw: Infusion Brands
items.description: Two blades, one baseball bat with a nail in it, and a car sacrificed for proof. Somewhere a contractor is still waiting for this saw to find something it can't cut.

items.title: Ultimate Ladder with Billy Mays (2005)
items.description: The living room is the size of a hotel lobby, which is how the ladder gets to be an A-frame, a platform and a Christmas tree helper without anyone hitting a wall.

items.id: billy-mays_202505/Orange Glo Hardwood Floor Care System.mp4
items.title: Orange Glo Hardwood Floor Care System with Billy Mays
items.description: The company behind OxiClean, sold to Church & Dwight in 2006, once needed only Billy Mays and a washable mop pad to make the dirty bucket look like a bad idea.

items.title: Miracle Blade World Class Knife Set: Ideal Living
items.description: A tomato, an olive jar and a watermelon do all the arguing for the Miracle Blade, and the offer cuts itself another slicer every time you think it is done.

items.title: Paint Zoom Paid Program
items.description: A countdown clock sits in the corner so you buy faster than the fence dries. Doors and a play structure get the coat, and a man in denim makes it look like a Saturday you would enjoy.

items.title: Ultimate Chopper with Chef Tony (2003)
items.description: The pitchman who made Miracle Blade famous puts the knife down for a locking-lid chopper. Onions, eggs and ice go in, and the sunny kitchen set insists nobody scrapes a knuckle.

items.title: As Seen On TV PC Back To School Special: Systemax PC (2000)
items.description: The free internet gets mentioned again and again, which tells you what was actually scarce in 2000. A man in a suit sells the rest like it is a bonus.

items.title: 3DO Interactive Multiplayer Demo Tape (1993)
items.description: Everyone at the 3DO press conference wanted to know the price, and the launch answer, $699, explains most of what happened next.

items.title: Esteban's Gift of Guitar on HSN
items.description: He trades licks with a friend on a magenta set, sunglasses on indoors, and the starter guitar sells itself. The lesson video, the case and the extra strings wait in the corner like backup singers.

items.title: Hulk Hogan's Ultimate Grill
items.description: Hulk Hogan goes after the George Foreman grill's territory with a bandana and a waffle plate, and the rival gadgets sit on the counter labelled Competitor, like a promo before a title match.

items.title: Ronco Showtime Rotisserie and BBQ
items.description: 'Set it and forget it,' Ron Popeil's line, comes around again with a giant turkey and lobster tails turning behind glass. Ronco itself filed for bankruptcy in 2007, which is one way to be forgotten.

items.id: sears-brand-central-in-store-demo-laserdisc-cycle-5-may-16june-12-1993/Sears Brand Central In-Store Demo Laserdisc [Cycle 5, May 16][June 12, 1993] (1080p_60fps_H264-128kbit_AAC).ia.mp4
items.title: Sears Brand Central In-Store Demo Laserdisc: Cycle 5 (1993)
items.description: A showroom loop built for a wall of televisions, on laserdisc because VHS looked mushy on them. Trailers, basketball and a waterfall play, nobody says a word, and the screens do the closing.

items.title: The Juiceman II: Power of Juicing (2000)
items.description: Jay Kordich was the original Juiceman, and by the Juiceman II he was throwing in a free bread machine. The carrot juice is real and so is the conviction.

items.title: Aero ExtraBed with Imaginair
items.description: Nobody ever wanted houseguests this badly. The whole pitch is that the in-laws can now stay, and the bed is up faster than anyone can think of an excuse.

items.title: Proactiv Solution (Australian Infomercial)
items.description: Two dermatologists, Katie Rodan and Kathy Fields, built the Proactiv template, and this is the Australian cut taped off Expo in 2009. The unflattering before photos do all the selling.

items.title: ProForm Cross Trainer with Roger Staubach and Peggy Fleming (1994)
items.description: A Cowboys quarterback and an Olympic skating champion sell you a home gym, taped off Discovery at 12:30 a.m. Roger Staubach and Peggy Fleming: two retired legends and a smart card.

items.title: Ab Circle Pro on Expo
items.description: Three minutes a day, said over and over until it sounds like physics. An American pitch that reached Australian cable, where somebody pressed record on an April evening in 2009.

items.id: y-2mate.com-2004-infomercial-body-by-jake-ab-scissor-480p/y2mate.com - 2004  INFOMERCIAL Body By Jake AB SCISSOR_480p.ia.mp4
items.title: Body By Jake Ab Scissor (2004)
items.description: Jake Steinfeld made his name as a trainer to Hollywood before he sold the rest of us the crunch. The old price gets crossed out three times, which is a lot of crossing out.

items.title: Ronco Food Dehydrator on Incredible Inventions (1993)
items.description: Ron Popeil's Ronco taught America to buy kitchen gadgets from the TV, and went bankrupt in 2007. Here it only wants to dry your pineapple, and the tape runs out before the trays do.

items.title: Bowflex (2004 to 2008)
items.description: Bowflex went bankrupt in 2024 and was bought by Johnson Health Tech, a long way from this studio where the men by the machine nod like the whole thing is settled.

items.title: Cross Bow by Weider (2002)
items.description: Joe Weider helped create Mr. Olympia, and here the family name is chasing Bowflex with one confident chart. Taped off Court TV in October 2002, a very specific place to shop for a home gym.

items.id: beach-body-power-90-infomercial-2003-bargain-bin-cinema-360p-h-264-youtube/Beach Body Power 90 Infomercial 2003 - Bargain Bin Cinema (360p, h264, youtube).mp4
items.title: Power 90 with Tony Horton (2003)
items.description: Power 90 is the prototype for P90X, the program that made Tony Horton the face of 'muscle confusion'. Here the clock counts down and the pitch is simpler: ninety days, no confusion at all.

items.title: Aero Mattress Topper (2002)
items.description: It can withstand 548 sharp nails, the uploader notes, a figure no mattress topper has ever needed. Taped off Hallmark Channel in December 2002, where the cozy and the improbable shared a half hour.

items.title: Winston Select Lights Sales Video (1993)
items.description: Winston paid for NASCAR's top series from 1971 to 2003, so a boxing ring for its own sales force counts as restraint. The bow-tied ringside host is a detail no one could invent.

items.title: Focus Factor Vital Basics Health Show with Bill Begley (2001)
items.description: A supplement from a 2001 Boise broadcast that is, improbably, still on drugstore shelves. Creator Kyl Smith sits next to the host, which is more founder than most pitches ever risk.

items.title: Go Duster on the Expo Channel (2008)
items.description: Nobody's chandelier has ever been this clean. The taper left in Expo's ads, promos and IDs around it, so you get the rest of an Australian evening in 2008, which is the real bonus.

items.title: Smartware Cookware with Chef Tony (2005)
items.description: Chef Tony Notaro, the Miracle Blade man, trades his knives for blue bakeware and still checks the lens to be sure you saw it. The muffins slide out clean, as they do in every orange kitchen.

items.title: Xpress Redi Set Go (2009)
items.description: The whole pitch is dinner with no oven, so the proof is pizza, steak and brownies, and the pizza has to be bitten on camera. Somebody on this crew got to eat the evidence.

items.id: assortment-of-instructional-tapes-public-domain-videos-and-infomercials/2010 Jay Kordich Power Grind Pro Infomercial.mp4
items.title: Jay Kordich PowerGrind Pro (2010)
items.description: Jay Kordich, the original Juiceman, was pushing carrots into his late eighties and died in 2017, which makes this one of the last pitches of a very long career.

items.title: Richard Simmons: Move, Groove and Lose on INSP (1999)
items.description: Richard Simmons stepped out of public life in 2014, which makes the patchwork vest and a studio applauding every pound feel like a time capsule. On this tape he is sandwiched between two preachers.

items.title: Miracle Blade III Perfection Series (2003)
items.description: A chef in a tall hat, a knife designer to vouch for him, and a pitch that only gets louder. The lifetime pledge gets its own card, in case you missed it.

items.title: Soloflex Home Gym (1986)
items.description: Soloflex sold a home gym the way a cologne ad sells cologne, with a narrator, a bike in the rain and not one person shouting. It is the quietest half hour on the channel, and it knows it.

items.title: Creativity in the Classroom: Commodore Amiga (1989)
items.description: Commodore wanted an Amiga on every school desk, and the kids' pixel drawings argue the case better than the dealer does. The company was bankrupt by 1994, but the drawings hold up.

items.id: SierraOnLineVideoCatalogue1988/Sierra On-Line Video Catalogue 1988 (Sierra On-Line, Inc.)(1988) [VHS].ia.mp4
items.title: Sierra On-Line Video Catalogue (1988)
items.description: The year of King's Quest IV, Sierra's catalogue is a narrator sprinting through a troll's lair and a gold rush trail. It is a sixteen-colour world, and the pitch is that you will want to live in it.

items.title: Zoom: A Laser Video Magazine, Pioneer LaserActive Special Edition (1993)
items.description: A video magazine made for Pioneer's retailers, slipped in with some LaserActive players, so the pitch comes from the people who sold it to the people who sold it. A man reads the manual aloud.

items.title: United Sciences of America: A Nutrition Opportunity (1984)
items.description: William Shatner was in the middle of T. J. Hooker when he narrated this vitamin recruitment film, with Joe Montana and Steve Garvey signed on to make the sunsets credible.

items.title: The Fizzazz Fashion Video Catalog: Coca-Cola and Murjani (1986)
items.description: Murjani, the company behind Gloria Vanderbilt jeans, borrows a soda's name for a clothing line and sells it on a cassette from a junk shop. The sleeve promise is the whole argument: this tape has fizzazz.

items.title: Teleshopper: What Is Teleshopper? (1971)
items.description: Home shopping is supposed to start with the cable channels, but a San Diego station was pitching advertisers on call-in buying in 1971. It is the pitch for the pitch, rescued from a liquidation sale.

items.title: MGM/UA Home Video Buyer's Club: Lion's Roar Video Magazine (1990)
items.description: A studio mailing list that turns its own back catalog into a magazine you watch: clips, box art and a host in a tan jacket making ownership sound like a reasonable next step. Leo the Lion wants you on it.

items.title: Time Life Music: The Singers and Songwriters Collection (2002)
items.description: Time Life's box sets lived in late-night ads, and this one aims at anyone who wore out a Cat Stevens record. The fireplace is doing real work.

items.title: Roadshow Home Video: September 1984 Dealer Presentation
items.description: A sales pitch to video shops, not to you: the box office chart, then trailers. Never Say Never Again, Sean Connery's unofficial return as Bond, is on the coming-soon list, so you see the rack before it is stocked.

items.title: Time Life 60s Gold Music Collection (2002)
items.description: Peace and love, repackaged for 2002 insomniacs, with a beaded curtain trying very hard to be 1967. One hundred fifty-two songs is the sixties sold by the pound.

items.id: the-secret-to-creating-your-future-tad-james-1992-infomercial-vhs_1/The Secret to Creating Your Future Tad James 1992 Infomercial VHS_1.mp4
items.title: The Secret to Creating Your Future with Tad James (1992)
items.description: Tad James is the NLP trainer behind Time Line Therapy, and here he sells the cassette version of the future from a sunroom. Houseplants everywhere: a bold backdrop for a man pitching personal growth.

items.id: channelten-infomercials-19951124/15 - Dr. John Gray video series.m4v
items.title: Dr. John Gray Video Series (1995)
items.description: Mars and Venus went from a 1992 bestseller to a VHS set, with couples on couches vouching. This airing is an Australian one, taped between a Ruth Rendell promo and a Tony Robbins that runs out.

items.title: Body by Jake Ab Scissor (2003)
items.description: Jake Steinfeld started out training Hollywood stars and ended up selling a padded seat. The hidden camera in the mall is the real trial: strangers, a chair, and no floor to blame.

items.title: The Magic Bullet System
items.description: Nobody in an infomercial kitchen is ever alone with a gadget, so the small blender gets a party. Homeland Housewares' Magic Bullet left the late-night ad for store shelves.

items.title: George Foreman Lean Mean Grilling Machine (1995)
items.description: George Foreman has said the grill paid him more than boxing ever did. The robe makes a cameo for old times' sake, but the grill is the one landing every punch now.

items.id: macho-man-randy-savage-guests-on-wwf-qvc-special-03-24-1994/Macho Man Randy Savage Guests on WWF QVC Special (03-24-1994).ia.mp4
items.title: WWF Merchandise Special on QVC with Macho Man Randy Savage (1994)
items.description: Macho Man sells the WWF's belts and foam hands to QVC, and he would be a WCW star soon after. Someone asks if this really will be an hour, and the answer is yes.

items.id: buy_20201125/WCW QVC Special With Buff Bagwell.ia.mp4
items.title: WCW nWo Special with Buff Bagwell on QVC
items.description: In 2001 the WWF bought WCW's name and tape library, which turns a catalog of nWo shirts and die-cast cars into merchandise for a company with an end date.

items.title: Dick's Picks and The Other Ones on QVC with Dick Latvala (1998)
items.description: Dick Latvala was the Dead's tape archivist, the man who picked the shows for Dick's Picks, and here he sells his taste to QVC. He died in 1999, so it is the vault keeper out in public.

items.title: Shop at Home: Graded Japanese Pokemon Cards with Betty Leigh (1999)
items.description: Pokemon had barely landed in America and a shopping channel was already selling its cards in graded plastic slabs, which is where the collectors' market was headed. The sets-left number only goes one way.

items.title: Esteban on HSN: At Home with Esteban and What Child Is This (circa 2000)
items.description: He plays a Christmas carol and the order bar never takes a breath. Somebody at HSN worked out that a guitarist is the perfect salesman, because nobody interrupts a song.

items.title: Cremation Society of Pennsylvania: The Simple Dignified Choice (1997)
items.description: The calmest pitch on the channel: no countdown, no bonus gift, just a gentle voice and a great many lamps. At 3 a.m. it is oddly restful, and it never once raises its voice.

items.title: Ab Roller Plus (1996)
items.description: The taper caught it twice on September 22, 1996, the repeat from TNN in the early hours, which is the kind of reach a pitch dreams about. The crowd lying down on the beach is the best touch.

items.id: miscellaneous-music-videos-all-you-need-is-love-the-story-of-popular-music-20-20/1980.00.00 - Miscellaneous Music Videos, All You Need Is Love The Story of Popular Music, 20-20 Fleetwood Mac, The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson with Elton John, QUBE Sight on Sound.mp4
items.title: Music Videos & More ('80)
items.description: Before MTV existed, someone was already taping music off the TV. Fleetwood Mac docs, Elton on Carson, and a proto-music-video show called QUBE. This is year zero.

items.id: vhs-tape-1981-queens-greatest-flix-1984-the-cars-live-at-the-summit-rock-of-the-/VHS Tape - 1981 - Queen's Greatest Flix, 1984 - The Cars Live at the Summit, Rock of the 80's Live at the Palace, Videos.mp4
items.title: Queen, The Cars & Rock of the '80s
items.description: Queen's Greatest Flix followed by The Cars live followed by Rock of the '80s at the Palace. Someone filled this tape like they were building a time capsule. They were.

items.id: 1982.09.27-kron-friday-night-videos-music-videos/1982.09.27 - KRON - Friday Night Videos - Music Videos.mp4
items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. '82)
items.description: Friday Night Videos on KRON — the only way to see music videos if your parents wouldn't spring for cable. Antenna up, VCR rolling, lights off.

items.id: Simon_And_Garfunkel_The_Concert_In_Central_Park_1982_CBS-FOX_Music_Video_Tape/Simon And Garfunkel The Concert In Central Park 1982 CBS-FOX Music Video Tape.mp4
items.title: Simon & Garfunkel in Central Park ('82)
items.description: Half a million people in Central Park and a CBS-FOX tape someone dubbed to death. The hiss on this one is part of the experience.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. 9, '83)
items.description: Friday Night Videos, September '83. NBC's free music video hour. You taped it because MTV cost money and this was the next best thing. It was pretty good, actually.

items.title: Friday Night Videos: Thriller Premiere (Dec. '83)
items.description: The night NBC premiered Thriller. Every VCR in America was rolling. If your copy still exists, it's because nobody ever taped over this one.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Nov. 4, '83)
items.description: Partial episode — the tape ran out or someone hit STOP too early. You take what the VHS gods give you.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Oct. 14, '83)
items.description: Mid-October '83. Friday Night Videos. The leaves are falling and the hits keep coming. Someone's taping this for the weekend rewatch.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. 16, '83)
items.description: Another Friday night, another ninety minutes of free music videos. The September '83 run was golden. Every week delivered.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Oct. 21, '83)
items.description: Late October '83. The VCR timer is set, the tape is fresh, and Friday Night Videos keeps being the best free music on television.

items.title: Friday Night Videos Special (Oct. 29, '83)
items.description: A special edition. Ninety minutes instead of the usual hour. Whoever set the VCR timer adjusted the end time. That's a pro move.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. '83)
items.description: KRON San Francisco. The Bay Area broadcast of Friday Night Videos. Same show, local commercials, different vibe when it's foggy outside.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. 30, '83)
items.description: End of September '83. Friday Night Videos closing out the month. Ninety minutes of whoever was on the charts and whoever was about to be.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (July 29, '83)
items.description: Summer of '83. July heat and Friday Night Videos. The air conditioning is on, the tape is recording, and you're not going anywhere.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Oct. 28, '83)
items.description: Night before Halloween, 1983. Friday Night Videos. The video selection probably wasn't spooky but the late-night energy absolutely was.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Aug. '83)
items.description: KRON, August '83. Late summer on the Bay Area airwaves. Friday Night Videos and whatever local ads were running between the hits.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Aug. 5, '83)
items.description: Early August, ninety minutes of Friday Night Videos. Summer '83 was peak music television whether you had cable or not.

items.title: Friday Night Videos Double Feature (July-Aug. '83)
items.description: Two episodes back to back. Someone let the tape run through both Fridays. Four hours of summer '83 videos. The dedication is real.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Oct. 7, '83)
items.description: October 7th on KRON. The Bay Area's free music video fix. Same show, different affiliate, and whoever was selling cars in San Francisco that week.

items.title: Friday Night Videos & St. Elsewhere (Dec. '83)
items.description: Friday Night Videos plus some St. Elsewhere on the same tape. December '83 San Francisco late night. Someone was watching everything.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Sept. '83)
items.description: Alternate KRON recording from September '83. Different night, same ritual — VCR on, antenna adjusted, tape rolling.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (March 16, '84)
items.description: March '84. Friday Night Videos. The hits are shifting, the hairstyles are getting bigger, and the VCR doesn't care — it records everything the same.

items.title: Friday Night Videos & MTV ('84)
items.description: Friday Night Videos mixed with MTV from 1984. Two hours of the two best music video sources on one tape. Someone knew what they were doing.

items.title: Friday Night Videos & MTV ('84, Alt.)
items.description: More FNV and MTV from '84. Two hours of music television from the year that belonged to Prince and Bruce and everyone trying to keep up.

items.id: 1984.01.07-mtv-recording-of-h2o-we-got-it-made-s01e14-1984.01.13-the-n/1984.01.07 - MTV - Recording of H2O - We Got it Made S01E14 - 1984.01.13 - The New Show S01E02.mp4
items.title: MTV Block (Jan. '84)
items.description: January '84 MTV with H2O and We Got It Made. Early cable TV from someone who taped first and sorted later. Two hours of whatever was on.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (March 2, '84)
items.description: March 2nd, '84. Friday Night Videos. Ninety minutes of the videos that were defining the spring. The tape quality says someone watched this more than once.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Nov. 2, '84)
items.description: November '84. Friday Night Videos. Fall sweaters and synthesizers. The year is winding down but the videos are still coming.

items.id: 1984.03.30-kron-friday-night-videos-music-videos/1984.03.30 - KRON - Friday Night Videos - Music Videos.mp4
items.title: Friday Night Videos (Mar. 30, '84)
items.description: KRON, March 30th. End of March '84 energy — spring break is either happening or just happened and the videos match the mood.

items.id: 1984.01.00-kron-two-episodes-of-friday-night-videos/1984.01.00 - KRON - Two Episodes of Friday Night Videos.mp4
items.title: Friday Night Videos Double (Jan. '84)
items.description: Two episodes of Friday Night Videos from January '84. Two hours of post-holiday music television. The Christmas decorations are down but the VCR is still running.

items.title: Video Hits: Canadian Music Show ('84-'85)
items.description: Video Hits — a rare Canadian music video show. If you've never seen this, that's the point. An hour of videos from across the border that MTV never played.

items.title: Friday Night Videos ('85)
items.description: Friday Night Videos on KNBC 4 out of SoCal. The Southern California broadcast. Same show, warmer weather, different local car dealership ads.

items.title: Australian Music Videos, Vol. 1 ('85)
items.description: Three hours of Australian music videos from TEN-10. The other side of the world had its own music TV and someone shipped this tape across an ocean.

items.title: MTV Block (March '85)
items.description: Two hours of MTV from March '85. The channel is four years old and still figuring out what it is. Which means it's still perfect.

items.title: Australian Music Videos, Vol. 2 ('85)
items.description: More TEN-10 from Australia. Two and a half hours of the Aussie music scene. Bands you know, bands you don't, and that unmistakable '80s Australian sound.

items.title: Australian Music Videos, Vol. 3 ('85)
items.description: An hour of Australian music television. TEN-10 with the hits from Down Under. Short tape, but every minute is a window into another continent's charts.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Jan. '85)
items.description: Two and a half hours of Friday Night Videos from January '85. New year, new videos, same ritual of staying up late with the VCR timer set.

items.title: Australian Music Videos, Vol. 4 ('85)
items.description: Two hours of Australian music from TEN-10, March '85. The autumn recordings from the Southern Hemisphere. Global music nerd territory.

items.id: vhs-tape-3-hours-of-music-videos-from-the-80s/VHS Tape - 3 Hours of Music Videos from the 80s.mp4
items.title: 3 Hours of '80s Music Videos
items.description: Three hours of '80s music videos on one tape. No channel ID, no commercials — someone edited this down to pure videos. A personal mixtape in VHS form.

items.title: MTV New Year's Eve ('87)
items.description: MTV's New Year's Eve. Ringing in '88 on the channel that threw the best party on cable. Partial recording — someone's tape ran out at midnight. Or right after.

items.title: MTV ('86/'88)
items.description: Two tapes spliced: MTV from July '86 and KWWL from July '88. Two summers, one cassette. Someone was economical with their blank tapes.

items.title: VH1 Block (Spring '87)
items.description: Three and a half hours of VH1 from spring '87. The channel for people who liked MTV but wished the VJs would calm down. Softer rock, longer format, same addiction.

items.title: Friday Night Videos (Nov. '87)
items.description: Friday Night Videos, November '87. A full broadcast hour. By now you've memorized the format — host intro, videos, commercials for things that no longer exist.

items.id: 1987.00.00-mtv-with-vj-adam-curry-saturday-night-concert-with-dire-straits-headb_202406/1987.00.00 - MTV with VJ Adam Curry Saturday Night Concert with Dire Straits, Headbangers Ball Mötley Crüise to Nowhere, Miscellaneous Videos with VJ Kevin Seal.mp4
items.title: MTV: Saturday Night Concert & Motley Cruise to Nowhere ('87)
items.description: Someone set the timer for a Saturday night of MTV and never hit stop: Dire Straits in concert, Mötley Crüise to Nowhere on Headbangers Ball, Adam Curry between. The idents are still in.

items.id: 1988.10.00-vh1-4-hours-with-vjs-tim-byrd-rosie-odonnell-entertainment-watch-with/1988.10.00 - VH1 4 Hours with VJs Tim Byrd & Rosie O'Donnell, Entertainment Watch with Kathryn Kinley, New Visions with Ben Sidran - October 1988.mp4
items.title: VH1 Marathon (Oct. '88)
items.description: Four hours of VH1 with Tim Byrd and Rosie O'Donnell as VJs. Before the talk show, before the View — Rosie introduced music videos. The tape proves it.

items.title: MTV Block (Aug. '89)
items.description: Two and a half hours of MTV from August '89. The tail end of the '80s. Everything is about to change but right now the videos are still big, loud, and expensive.

items.id: mtv-headbangers-ball-halloween-1989-alice-cooper-ia-copy/MTV Headbanger's Ball Halloween 1989 Alice Cooper IA Copy.mp4
items.title: Headbangers Ball Halloween: Alice Cooper ('89)
items.description: Headbangers Ball Halloween special. Alice Cooper hosting. Two hours of the heaviest night on MTV's calendar. Someone stayed up for this with the volume way up.

items.title: VH1 Music Videos (June '90)
items.description: Five hours of VH1 music videos from June 1990. Adult contemporary on repeat. The channel your mom watched, and honestly? Some of these still hold up.

items.title: Headbangers Ball ('92)
items.description: Headbangers Ball from '92. Thrash meets grunge meets whatever Riki Rachtman is wearing. Two and a half hours of the heaviest show on cable finding its new identity.

items.title: VH1 Countdown & AMAs ('92)
items.description: VH1's 21 Countdown plus the American Music Awards. Nearly six hours of 1992 captured on one long-play tape. Someone's VCR worked overtime.

items.title: VH1: History of Music Videos (Dec. '92)
items.description: Four hours of VH1's Video History of Music Videos. From the earliest clips to the MTV explosion. A documentary about the thing you're watching, on the medium you're watching it on.

items.title: Headbangers Ball Marathon ('92)
items.description: Five hours of Headbangers Ball with Ozzy, Phil Anselmo, and Alice in Chains. Peak metal television. Whoever recorded this understood they were capturing something that wouldn't last.

items.id: mtv-plus-headbangers-ball-trail-of-noise-with-anthrax-1993/MTV Plus Headbangers Ball-Trail of Noise With Anthrax 1993.ia.mp4
items.title: Headbangers Ball: Trail of Noise ('93)
items.description: Headbangers Ball Trail of Noise with Anthrax. Three hours of thrash on MTV Plus. The Ball is rolling and the volume knob only goes one direction.

items.title: VH1: Music Video History (July '93)
items.description: More VH1 Video History from July '93. Four hours of tracing the music video from novelty to art form. The medium examining itself while you eat cereal on the couch.

items.title: Headbangers Ball ('93)
items.description: Three hours of Headbangers Ball, 1993. Riki Rachtman in the chair. The interviews, the premieres, the videos your neighbors couldn't hear through the walls. Hopefully.

items.title: MTV Block ('94)
items.description: Three hours of MTV from 1994. Grunge and hip-hop and The Real World all sharing the same channel. The most chaotic year in music television history, preserved on tape.

items.id: y-2mate.com-mtv-best-of-woodstock-94-1994-tv-special-festival-highlights-480p/y2mate.com - MTV Best of Woodstock 94 1994 TV Special Festival Highlights_480p.ia.mp4
items.title: MTV Woodstock '94 Highlights
items.description: MTV's Woodstock '94 highlights. The mud, the mosh pits, Nine Inch Nails covered in filth. The festival that tried to recapture '69 and accidentally invented '94.

items.title: VH1 Video Countdown ('94)
items.description: VH1's countdown from '94. An hour of the biggest hits ranked and played back. The songs your older sibling sang in the car whether you wanted them to or not.

items.title: MTV Australia ('91)
items.description: MTV Australia — an hour of the Aussie feed. Different VJs, different commercials, same obsession. Proof that music television was a global condition.

items.id: patti-smith-and-friends-shepherds-bush-empire-uk-7th-august-1996-jools-holland-mtv-performances/Patti Smith And Friends - Shepherds Bush Empire UK 7th August 1996 + Jools Holland & MTV performances.mp4
items.title: Patti Smith Live & MTV Performances ('96)
items.description: Patti Smith at Shepherds Bush Empire plus Jools Holland and MTV performances. Two and a half hours of punk's poet laureate across multiple stages and broadcasts.

items.title: MTV Spring Break ('97)
items.description: MTV Spring Break '97. Four hours of the beach, the bands, and the chaos. Someone taped the entire broadcast. The sunburn is implied.

items.title: VH1 Music Block (Nov. '97)
items.description: Two hours of VH1's music block from November '97. Pre-Behind the Music, pre-Pop-Up Video domination. Just videos and VJs and the hum of the VCR.

items.title: VH1 Music Block ('98)
items.description: VH1 in '98. Two hours of pop hits and power ballads. The grown-up music channel for people who still wanted videos but also needed to go to bed at a reasonable hour.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (Aug. 1, '99)
items.description: Jancee Dunn hosts a playlist that sets Pulp's Common People beside Atari Teenage Riot, and nobody blinks. The tape picks up on the tail of Undressed, so the VCR was rolling before the show was.

items.id: austin-city-limits-dave-matthews-2-others-i-cant-id-sessions-at-west-54th-sheryl/Austin City Limits Dave Matthews 2 others I can't ID Sessions at West 54th Sheryl Crowe and G-Love VH-1 Big Backyard BBQ Goo Goo Dolls Summer of 2000.mp4
items.title: Austin City Limits & VH1 BBQ (Summer '00)
items.description: Dave Matthews on Austin City Limits, Sheryl Crow and Goo Goo Dolls at VH1's Big Backyard BBQ. Summer 2000 in a nutshell. Someone taped the whole cookout.

items.title: VH1: '80s Music Marathon (Nov. '01)
items.description: Four hours of VH1's '80s music marathon from 2001. The decade that refuses to stay in the past, replayed on the channel that made nostalgia a business model.

items.title: Video Hits (Feb. '01)
items.description: Video Hits from February 2001. Three hours of Australia's music countdown show. The Southern Hemisphere summer charts. Hits you know and hits you should.

items.title: Video Hits (June '01)
items.description: Video Hits, June 2001. Two and a half hours of Australian music television in the dead of winter Down Under. The charts kept spinning regardless of the season.

items.title: Video Hits (March 17, '01)
items.description: Video Hits, mid-March 2001. Two and a half hours of Aussie chart-toppers. Someone in Australia was doing the same thing you were — taping the countdown every week.

items.title: Video Hits (Jan. 13, '01)
items.description: Video Hits from January 2001. Australian summer. Two and a half hours of the hottest season's hottest songs on the other side of the equator.

items.title: Video Hits (March 18, '01)
items.description: Three hours of Video Hits. A Sunday afternoon of music television in Australia. March 2001. The commitment to taping this show every single week is genuinely inspiring.

items.title: Video Hits (June 30, '01)
items.description: Last day of June 2001. Video Hits. Two and a half hours of mid-year Aussie hits. The collection is almost complete. Almost.

items.title: VH1 Europe (Aug. '13)
items.description: VH1 Europe, 2013. Ninety minutes of the continental feed. Music television survived longer overseas. This tape is proof.

items.id: vhs-tape-music-videos-from-mtv-and-vh1-80s-90s/VHS Tape - Music Videos from MTV and VH1 - 80s & 90s.mp4
items.title: MTV & VH1 Music Videos ('80s-'90s)
items.description: Two hours of music videos from MTV and VH1, spanning the '80s and '90s. A curated trip through two decades compiled by someone who lived through both.

items.id: vhs-tape-music-videos-from-mtv-mtv2-vh1-night-tracks-80s-90s/VHS Tape - Music Videos from MTV, MTV2, VH1 & Night Tracks - 80s & 90s.mp4
items.title: MTV, MTV2, VH1 & Night Tracks ('80s-'90s)
items.description: MTV, MTV2, VH1, and Night Tracks — all four pillars of music television on one tape. Two hours of the complete ecosystem. Someone was thorough.

items.title: Bon Jovi: MTV Hedonism Weekend
items.description: Bon Jovi's MTV Hedonism Weekend plus New Jersey promo clips. Two hours of big hair, bigger hooks, and the band that sold out arenas by showing up on your TV first.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (April '88)
items.description: 120 Minutes from April '88. The underground side of MTV. Two hours of alternative and indie before alternative and indie had a name. Dave Kendall at the helm.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (July '90)
items.description: 120 Minutes, July 1990. Two hours of the alt-rock that would conquer the mainstream within a year. The last summer before everything changed, and you can hear it coming.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (Jan. '90)
items.description: 120 Minutes, January 1990. The decade opens with two hours of alternative. The '90s don't know what they are yet. Neither does this show. That's why it's perfect.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (April '90)
items.description: April 1990. 120 Minutes. Alt-rock and post-punk after midnight. The show MTV put on when they thought nobody was watching. Joke's on them — the VCR was always watching.

items.title: Rush: Chronicles
items.description: Rush: Chronicles on VHS. An hour of Geddy, Alex, and Neil through the years. Someone dubbed this from the original and kept it labeled and shelved. Respect.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (Aug. '91)
items.description: 120 Minutes, August '91. Two hours of alt-rock recorded one month before Nevermind dropped. The last tape from the before times. Everything on here is about to go supernova.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes + Dreamtime (June '93)
items.description: 120 Minutes plus Dreamtime from June '93. Three hours of MTV's late-night alternative block. The deep cuts, the imports, the videos that only aired between midnight and dawn.

items.title: MTV Dreamtime & Rude Awakening (Dec. '94)
items.description: Dreamtime and Rude Awakening — MTV's overnight programming from December '94. Three and a half hours for people who chose music over sleep. The VCR didn't need to choose.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (July 6, '97)
items.description: 120 Minutes, July 6th, '97. Two hours of mid-'90s alt-rock and electronica. The show is evolving. The VCR doesn't care — it records the evolution faithfully.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (July 13, '97)
items.description: Another 120 Minutes from July '97. One week later. Two hours of whatever Matt Pinfield was passionate about that Sunday. The answer: everything.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (Feb. '98)
items.description: 120 Minutes, February '98. Two hours of late-'90s alternative as the genre splinters into a hundred subgenres. The show tries to cover all of them. Almost succeeds.

items.title: MTV 120 Minutes (June '99)
items.description: 120 Minutes, June '99. Two hours of the alt-rock show's late-era run. The end is coming but the music is still there if you stay up late enough to find it.

items.title: Early 2000s Hip-Hop Videos
items.description: Ninety minutes of early 2000s hip-hop videos. Bling era, chrome rims, Hype Williams angles. Someone ripped these off the air and the bass still rattles the speakers.

items.id: nickelodeon-block-mr.-wizard-ycdtot-inspector-gadget-woc-1989/Nickelodeon Block Mr. Wizard YCDTOT Inspector Gadget WOC 1989.ia.mp4
items.title: Nick Block: Mr. Wizard & Inspector Gadget ('89)
items.description: Mr. Wizard, You Can't Do That on Television, and Inspector Gadget. You got home first and Nick was already warmed up. 1989 afternoon perfection.

items.title: CBS, Fox & Nickelodeon (Sept. '90)
items.description: Four hours of flipping between CBS, Fox, and Nickelodeon. September 1990. Someone had the remote and no supervision.

items.title: CBS, Fox & Nick, Alt. Copy (Sept. '90)
items.description: Same afternoon, different tape. CBS, Fox, and Nick from September '90. Two copies survived because the afternoon was that good.

items.title: Disney Afternoon: TaleSpin & Darkwing ('91)
items.description: TaleSpin and Darkwing Duck. The Disney Afternoon was the reason you ran home. Backpack hits the floor, TV goes on, 1991.

items.title: TBS Yabba Doo Day (June '91)
items.description: TBS's Yabba Doo Day. Four hours of Hanna-Barbera cartoons on a June afternoon in '91. Yogi, Scooby, and nobody telling you to go outside.
