items.description: Saturday night, 2002. Five anime back to back, The Candidate for Goddess among them, with the ads kept in. Snapple, ADT, SummerSlam on pay-per-view. The action block runs until the VCR says stop.

items.id: adult-swim-sunday-night-2002-full-episodes-with-commercials/Adult Swim – Sunday Night   2002   Full Episodes with Commercials (360p_30fps_H264-128kbit_AAC).ia.mp4
items.title: Adult Swim Sunday Night (2002)
items.description: Sunday night, 2002. The Oblongs, Baby Blues, Harvey Birdman, The Brak Show, Yogi Bear and Mission Hill, breaks in. The pool is open. An old man in a swim cap says so.

items.title: Adult Swim Marathon (Jan.-Feb. '03)
items.description: Six hours across four nights in early 2003. A thrift store VHS nobody came back for. Home Movies, Sealab, Space Ghost, Bebop — the full roster, uncut. The swim at its deepest.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Summer '03)
items.description: A fan's rebuild of that night, not an off-air tape: The Big O and Blue Gender between the bumps and a McGriddles ad. A Space Ghost from years later got spliced in. The pool doesn't check dates.

items.title: Adult Swim: Lupin the 3rd & Inuyasha (Feb. '03)
items.description: Three nights of Adult Swim premieres, Lupin the 3rd Part II then Inuyasha each night, breaks left in: an Army recruiting spot, 1-800-COLLECT, a promo card reading Sealab 12a. Someone had a schedule and kept to it.

items.id: adult-swim-halloween-2003-full-episodes-with-commercials-bq/Rinse Repeat - [adult swim] – Halloween ¦ 2003 ¦ Full Episodes with Commercials.ia.mp4
items.title: Adult Swim Halloween Night (Oct. '03)
items.description: Sunday, October 26, 2003. The Brak Show, Aqua Teen, Space Ghost, Scooby-Doo, The Oblongs and two Trigun. The sign says swim at your own risk, and it is bleeding.

items.id: 2004-adult-swim-april-fools-prank-roughly-2-hours-of-origional-block_202610/2004 Adult Swim April Fools Prank Roughly 2 hours of Origional Block.ia.mp4
items.title: Adult Swim April Fools Block (Apr. '04)
items.description: April 2004. An anime run, Sealab 2021, Birdman, a special presentation of Flying Shark vs Flying Crocodile, then Family Guy and the Futurama pilot as a bonus hour. The block pulls a prank. The VCR keeps going.

items.title: Adult Swim Anime Block (May '04)
items.description: May 2004. Adult Swim Action with its breaks in. Case Closed, Trigun, Cowboy Bebop. A wire stripper sells for $65 between the gunfights. The tracking line never settles.

items.title: Adult Swim Anime Block (July '04)
items.description: July 2004. Case Closed, then Lupin the Third, twice over. KFC for $9.99 in the breaks, and a free month of whatever the Road Runner is selling. Conan solves it. Lupin steals it.

items.title: Adult Swim Block ('04)
items.description: The golden year. Adult Swim 2004. Every bump a mood. Every show a cult classic in waiting. The commercials are for things that don't exist yet.

items.title: Adult Swim Anime ('04)
items.description: Adult Swim by night, InuYasha first. Same channel, different dimension.

items.title: Adult Swim & Late Night Grab Bag ('04)
items.description: A VHS dump of late-night cable circa 2004. Aqua Teen, Sealab 2021, Harvey Birdman, Venture Bros., Brak Show — plus Ren & Stimpy, Reno 911, and Family Guy. Not all episodes complete. Someone's whole week on one tape.

items.title: Adult Swim Anime Night (Fall '05)
items.description: Five anime in a row and the ads left in, including a free preview of a sports package. Past bedtime, but nobody on this tape was checking.

items.title: Adult Swim Action Block (Oct. '05)
items.description: October 8, 2005. FMA, FLCL, Samurai Champloo, s-CRY-ed, Inuyasha. The anime action block firing on all cylinders. Every show a reason to stay up past midnight.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Oct. '05)
items.description: October 22, 2005. Saturday night Adult Swim, taped off the air. Whatever was on, someone stayed up for all of it.

items.title: Adult Swim Anime Block (Nov. '05)
items.description: November 2005. Inuyasha, Fullmetal Alchemist, a bit of FLCL and s-CRY-ed, with the ads in. Netscape still wants your long distance. The tracking comes and goes.

items.title: Adult Swim Block ('05 or '06)
items.description: Some night in 2005 or 2006; the taper forgot the date. Ghost in the Shell, Fullmetal Alchemist and Futurama, with the ads in. The Xbox says jump in. The VCR says play.

items.title: Inuyasha on Adult Swim (Jan.-Feb. '06)
items.description: Episodes 127 through 132. Deep Inuyasha. If you're this far in, you're not going back. The sun will come up eventually.

items.title: Adult Swim Block ('06)
items.description: The Adult Swim tape from early 2006. Someone recorded the whole block without commercials.

items.id: rinse-repeat-adult-swim-saturday-ac-tn-2006-full-episodes-with-commercials/Rinse Repeat - [adult swim] – Saturday AcTN ¦ 2006 ¦ Full Episodes with Commercials.ia.mp4
items.title: Adult Swim Saturday Block ('06)
items.description: 2006. The Boondocks, then the Action block. The Big O, Gigantor in black and white, the Super Globetrotters at dawn. Life Alert and DeVry in the breaks. Nobody awake at this hour is enrolling.

items.title: Adult Swim Movie Night (Aug. '06)
items.description: August 2006, Colorado. Inuyasha the Movie 3, Swords of an Honorable Ruler, with its breaks. Perfect Hair Forever after it, and a promo for Shin Chan starting the 21st. Friday's has a $10 menu. Even demons have feelings.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Feb. '07)
items.description: Eight Futurama episodes and a Family Guy, nine months before Bender's Big Score brought the show back. Reruns like these were the case for the revival, though nobody on the tape knows it.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (July '07)
items.description: July 2007. Three and a half hours of whatever Adult Swim decided to broadcast between pool bumps and existential silence.

items.title: Adult Swim Action Tape 02 ('07)
items.description: Tape two. Labeled "ACTN." Someone organized their Adult Swim recordings by genre. Respect.

items.title: Adult Swim Action Tape 01 ('07)
items.description: Tape one. The action block. Anime and bumps and the hum of a VCR recording what the rest of the house was sleeping through.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Oct. '07)
items.description: October 2007. Two years deeper into the weird. The bumps got stranger, the shows got darker, and nobody changed the channel.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Dec. '07)
items.description: December 1, 2007. Saturday night after Toonami signs off. Futurama, The Boondocks, Death Note, Blood+, Fullmetal Alchemist, Inuyasha. Perfect Pushup, two easy payments. The bump just says MEDIOCRITY.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Jan. '08)
items.description: January 5, 2008. The advisory card, then Bleach, Death Note, Fullmetal Alchemist and more anime through the small hours. Video Professor wants you to call now. The tape runs out to blue.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (June '08)
items.description: June 2008. Metalocalypse, Fat Guy Stuck in Internet, Assy McGee and Tim and Eric, with the ads in. The training package is still free. Nobody in this hour is well.

items.title: Adult Swim Block (Aug. '08)
items.description: August 2008. Family Guy, Robot Chicken, Aqua Teen Hunger Force and The Boondocks, with the ads between. A Christmas episode in late summer. The pool is open late.

items.title: Adult Swim (Dec. '11)
items.description: Adult Swim's December night, from the schedule card and The Oblongs on. The channel never changes. Everything else does.

items.title: Adult Swim ('13-'15)
items.description: Tape one of a three-part archive. 2013 to 2015. Someone was still recording Adult Swim on VHS. The medium refuses to die.

items.title: Adult Swim ('14-'16)
items.description: Tape two. 2014 to 2016. The collection continues. The pool is still open. The pool will always be open.

items.title: Adult Swim ('16)
items.description: Tape three. 2016. The aesthetic has changed. The feeling hasn't. Two hours of being the only person awake in the house.

items.title: Adult Swim (July '18)
items.description: July 2018. VHS tape number 1113. Someone has recorded over a thousand tapes. This is devotion. This is the swim.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Castlevania II Simon's Quest - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 1.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest
items.description: Simon Belmont is sent across Transylvania to collect Dracula's remains, with directions supplied by villagers who speak in riddles. It is a navigation system built entirely on atmosphere.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 2.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
items.description: The NES Jekyll and Hyde sends the doctor through a town that does everything it can to rattle him, and Hyde is what happens when it works. The Nerd explains the design from his chair.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/The Karate Kid - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 3.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Karate Kid
items.description: From the Nerd's early days, before the theme song: LJN's Karate Kid cartridge, a movie about discipline turned into a side-scroller with a life bar. Discipline is, at least, required.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Who Framed Roger Rabbit - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 4.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
items.description: Eddie Valiant searches rooms in LJN's Roger Rabbit while the status bar reports SEARCHING and, now and then, IT'S EMPTY. Few games describe themselves this accurately.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 5.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
items.description: Ultra's Turtles cartridge, built by Konami, features the underwater dam, where the seaweed is live and the timer is real. Anyone who remembers the dam does not need the rest of this line.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Back to the Future - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 6.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Back to the Future
items.description: The cartridge puts Marty McFly on top-down Hill Valley streets with a timer running, and the Nerd tags along. A film about time gets a game with a very visible clock, which is one way to read the brief.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/McKids - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 7.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: McKids
items.description: A McDonald's platformer where the plea for help runs out of room mid-word, somewhere around Hambur. Even the emergency had a character limit.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Wally Bear and the No! Gang - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 8.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Wally Bear and the No! Gang
items.description: A skateboarding bear fronts the No! Gang on an unlicensed cartridge from American Video Entertainment. The gang's name is a single word, which is a lean design brief.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Master Chu and the Drunkard Hu - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 9.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Master Chu and the Drunkard Hu
items.description: The Nerd sits down with a kung fu platformer, all jars, ledges and spectres, and works out who is fighting whom. The game leaves the plot to the player, a confident way to design.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Top Gun - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 10.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Top Gun
items.description: Konami's fighter-jet cartridge hands the Nerd a cockpit, a radar and a mission map, and he spends much of the flight on the landing. Carrier decks have rarely had a tougher review.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Double Dragon III - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 11.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Double Dragon III
items.description: The Nerd plays the original brawler first as a yardstick, which is sound method for anyone about to review its sequel. Then Billy and Jimmy Lee start walking right, and the measuring begins.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Friday the 13th - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 12.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Friday the 13th
items.description: LJN's camp-counselor cartridge hands the Nerd a lake map, a roster of counselors and a count of children to keep alive, with Jason somewhere out there. The slasher gets a staffing plan, and the Nerd reads the paperwork.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/A Nightmare On Elm Street - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 13.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: A Nightmare on Elm Street
items.description: Freddy's glove throws its shadow across a wall, then the cartridge starts: a blue haunted house, a suburban street, and a long, patient walk between them. Dread is on the game's list, near the bottom.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/The Power Glove - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 14.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Power Glove
items.description: The Nerd pulls on Mattel's Power Glove and tries it on NES games, Metroid and R.C. Pro-Am among them. The promise is that your hand becomes the controller. It does, in the sense that your hand is busy.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Chronologically Confused about Sequel Titles - Angry Video Game Nerd Episode 15.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Chronologically Confused
items.description: At a chalkboard, the Nerd sorts out sequel titles: Street Fighter II and its many editions, Final Fantasy VII, Zombi 2, and kung fu films renamed for each country. The numbers were always suggestions.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Rocky - Sega Master System - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 16 (Original Version) Reupload.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Rocky
items.description: Bag work, a bout with Apollo, a count from the canvas, then Lang, and a win screen that says to repeat the training and challenge again. The game understood the montage and made it the whole game.

items.title: Attack of the Show (May '11)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey meet the cast of Thor, review the BlackBerry PlayBook, and lay the TurboGrafx-16 to rest in Console Graveyard. A segment that eulogizes every dead console has the right idea.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Aug. '11)
items.description: Tales from the Console Graveyard takes up the Nintendo 64, with Michael Pena as the guest and Chris Gore on DVDuesday. Explaining a three-handled controller in one segment is the real feat.

items.title: X-Play: MLB SlugFest
items.description: A squad shooter wants your team and your location settled before anyone fires a shot, and Adam and Morgan walk through the setup. Plan first, then bullets: an order no field manual argues with.

items.title: X-Play: Tropico 2
items.description: A pirate-island builder shows up with a Calico Jack wanted poster and a harbor to run. You manage the town, which is fortunate, since somebody has to handle the paperwork once the plunder comes in.

items.title: X-Play: NBA Street Vol. 2, Galactic Civilizations
items.description: Street basketball gets a look, where tricks chain into a dunk and the dunk is the whole argument. The playground has always worked that way: nobody remembers the pass.

items.title: X-Play: Grand Theft Auto, Bruno Junqueira
items.description: Vice City's logo sits in the corner all episode, pastel streets and motorcycles on show, and Newman/Haas driver Bruno Junqueira drops in from the garage. Vice City's Miami keeps the loosest traffic code on the tape.

items.title: X-Play: Villains, Lightsabers
items.description: Popcorn on the couch and a title card that reads Villain: Adam and Morgan take the bad guy's side for a segment, lightsaber glow included. In games, the antagonist always gets the better entrance.

items.title: X-Play: K-1 World Grand Prix
items.description: A kickboxing game fields K-1 names like Ernesto Hoost, Mark Hunt and Cyril Abidi. The genre's tip is the sport's own: stay on your feet.

items.title: GamesMaster: John Fashanu
items.description: Super Mario Bros. 3 gets a coin count against the clock, and a football game gets its own head-to-head. Both are played under a gothic roof, which is where a tournament this serious belongs.

items.title: GamesMaster: Gary Mason
items.description: Sonic races the clock for rings, then Lemmings sets a target of 91 percent saved. In a game about marching cheerfully into danger, that is an ambitious pass mark.

items.title: GamesMaster: Annabel Croft
items.description: Tennis from a high angle, with Mega Man and Lotus Turbo Challenge 2 reviewed in the same sitting. From up there, at least, the line calls are easy to see.

items.title: GamesMaster: Eric Bristow
items.description: Road Rash puts motorbike racing and punching on the same road, then a boxing game with a round counter sets Jason against Lisa. The highway code was clearly read, loosely.

items.title: GamesMaster: Jimmy White, Archer MacLean and Ashley Paske
items.description: Jimmy White, snooker's Whirlwind, and games designer Archer MacLean line up at a computer snooker table, the scoreboard reading Chris and Archer. The felt is green, as the sport requires.

items.title: Cinematech: The Bouncer
items.description: A PlayStation 2 brawler gets the full trailer treatment, and the episode ends on one credit card: Tetsuya Nomura, character designer. The hair was a decision, and it was committed to.

items.title: G4 Icons: Oddworld Inhabitants
items.description: Abe's Oddysee gets its backstory from the people who made it: a PlayStation platformer where the hero is a meat-plant worker who learns he is on the menu. As motivation goes, it needs no second scene.

items.title: G4 Icons: Nolan Bushnell
items.description: Pong, Atari and a pizza parlor full of animatronic animals share one founder, and the tape draws it as a straight line. It is one: arcade or dining room, the business is a reason to stay.

items.title: G4 Icons: Pac-Man
items.description: The pizza story, the arcade rush and a gavel for the legal chapter, all for one yellow dot. Its design brief was eat everything, avoid the ghosts, and nobody has had to file a patch since.

items.title: G4 Icons: Lara Croft
items.description: Core Design's developers explain how Tomb Raider's heroine got her look and her moves, with the character art laid out beside early game footage. The brief seems to have been that no gap is too wide.

items.title: G4 Icons: Activision
items.description: Atari programmers who wanted credit on their own cartridges walked out and started the first outside publisher for the 2600. Pitfall is the exhibit. As résumés go, a vine swing beats a reference letter.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Aug. '11)
items.description: Candace Bailey and Blair Herter put the Sega Dreamcast through Tales from the Console Graveyard, with Sara Paxton, a caffeine experiment and FPS Russia. The Dreamcast shipped with a modem built in, which was early.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Jan. '12)
items.description: Silas Weir Mitchell visits Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey, Console Graveyard takes its turn, and the Twitter feed is asked what the next Xbox should have. The wish list is the most honest spec sheet there is.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Bible Games - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 17.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Bible Games
items.description: Santa hat on, the Nerd opens a stack of Bible cartridges. Wisdom Tree's Super 3D Noah's Ark runs on the Wolfenstein 3D engine, which makes the ark a first-person corridor. Two of each, one hallway.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Atari 5200 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 20.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Atari 5200
items.description: The 2600's bigger successor gets a shelf of cartridges, Donkey Kong and Frogger on screen, and a joystick that never returns to center. Its stick remembers where you were headed, which is more than most do.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Ghostbusters - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 21.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Ghostbusters
items.description: Flashing buildings on a city map, an Ecto-1 that crosses the same stretch of road again and again, and a marshmallow man standing in the shop. The driving is the game; the ghosts are a break from it.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Ghostbusters (Part 2) - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 22.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Ghostbusters (Part 2)
items.description: The follow-up visits the same franchise on other machines, and one ending screen thanks you for having the patience to sit through it. After this much driving, that reads as a fair summary.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Ghostbusters (Part 3) - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 23.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Ghostbusters (Part 3)
items.description: The conclusion lands on the sequel's game: a green Statue of Liberty, an infrared scope, and a shop with its shelves already marked sold out. Stocking a store with nothing in it is a committed design.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Spider-Man - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 24.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Spider-Man
items.description: A wall-crawler's games run from a tower climb to a Game Boy swing to a DS, with a guest in full red-and-blue costume on the couch. Every console gives him a wall, which is only fair.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Sega CD - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 25.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Sega CD
items.description: The add-on's pitch was 12.5 MHz and 64 simultaneous colors, and the discs get checked against it, Night Trap and Jurassic Park among them. The specs are the part that survives the inspection.

items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Sega 32X
items.description: A Genesis add-on promises 32-bit power and arrives with cables of its own, and the Nerd follows them wherever they go. The logic was sound on paper: more bits, more boxes.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Silver Surfer - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 27.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Silver Surfer
items.description: Marvel's herald of Galactus, keeper of the power cosmic, is sent through mazes and pipe corridors where the walls are the real enemy. A whole universe to cross, and the game picks the narrowest route.

items.title: X-Play: Dungeons & Dragons Heroes, Formula One Racing
items.description: Adam Sessler and Morgan Webb review from the TechTV couch, with a Formula One racing game taking up the middle of the show. The red X is the logo, and from across the room it also looks like a verdict.

items.title: X-Play: Project Gotham Racing 2, Football
items.description: A football sim stages Houston against Chicago and runs the first quarter on air. The game's central promise is that you call every play, a promise the real sport only makes to coaches.

items.title: X-Play: Gladiator: Sword of Vengeance, Everything or Nothing
items.description: Silent Hill 3 walks Heather into a closed amusement park, which every horror game agrees is the correct place to go. Adam and Morgan get the lights low for it.

items.title: X-Play: Mario and Wario Golf, Cruz Bustamante
items.description: Mario and Wario tee off in a Mario golf game, desert on one hole and snowcapped peaks on another, pin distance posted for each. It is golf, but the hazards come with a franchise.

items.title: X-Play: NFL Fever 2004, TopSpin
items.description: A tennis game runs from hard court to clay, and its player creator has a shop for shoes and socks, which is the right place to put the effort on a surface that rewards good traction.

items.title: Nintendo 64: Change the System
items.description: Nintendo's sales tape for the N64 opens on a crowd, then lets Super Mario 64 and Pilotwings 64 make the case, with a 360° card for the stick. The pitch is a circle, and the circle holds.

items.title: Star Fox 64 Promo Tape
items.description: Spies in Sega and Sony shirts infiltrate Nintendo of America to learn what makes Star Fox 64 work. Nintendo's answer is to show them the game, which is how you win a spy story.

items.title: Diddy Kong Racing Promo Tape
items.description: Diddy Kong Racing gets a talk show: a host in a lilac jacket, a Hot Topic ticker, a field reporter in a pith helmet. Cars, hovercraft and planes in one game is, fairly, a Hot Topic.

items.title: Banjo-Kazooie: Blockbuster Promo Tape
items.description: Jon Lovitz narrates Blockbuster's Banjo-Kazooie tape, a rental-weekend pitch that visits Treasure Trove Cove and friends. Stay for the previews, where Conker still looks like a cute platformer.

items.title: Nintendo 64 Sports Promo Tape
items.description: Nintendo's N64 sports tape fits basketball, baseball, snowboarding, hockey and WCW wrestling into nine minutes, with one-word title cards doing the introductions. The shortest season on record.

items.title: Hot Newz 64
items.description: A host in an orange shirt previews the next Nintendo 64 games, then hands the stuck players to Ask Dan, who sits in a chair. Any problem that can be fixed by asking a man in a chair is fixed here.

items.id: nintendo-promo-tapes/The Legend of Zelda - Majora's Mask (2000).mp4
items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask Promo Tape
items.description: Nintendo's tape for Majora's Mask shows Link in Termina, with a developer interview and a Collector's Gold Cartridge offer. The game gives him three days to save the world, a deadline the tape never doubts.

items.title: GamesMaster: Pat Sharp and Mick Brown
items.description: Two holes of golf, a ski jump and a virtual reality headset share one episode. Only the headset is pitched as the future, and the studio supplies the fog to match.

items.title: GamesMaster: Kendo Nagasaki
items.description: Dominik Diamond hosts from a smoky church while a masked wrestler drops in and a wrestling game sets up its isometric ring. As venues for a bout go, a nave has more atmosphere than most arenas.

items.title: GamesMaster: Pat and Emily Cash
items.description: Emily takes a turn at bat in a console baseball game, and a Terminator 2 game puts its score over Arnold's half-metal face. It is a reasonable place for a scoreboard.

items.title: GamesMaster: Barry McGuigan
items.description: Dominik Diamond hosts a boxing game with a world champion's name on the scoreboard, facing Wilson, then a round of windmill crazy golf. The windmill is the tougher opponent.

items.title: GamesMaster: Emlyn Hughes
items.description: England play Brazil on the football game, but Duck Hunt steals the show with a bar of nine ducks out of ten. The dog laughing at a miss is the most honest scoring in games.

items.title: Attack of the Show (April '12)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey gather first reactions to The Avengers, drop in at the Kidrobot shop and close on Free Beats. A film with that many heroes gets one segment of first reactions, a team-up of its own.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Feb. '12)
items.description: AT&T's data throttling gets the news desk, and Game Break takes Twisted Metal, Eat Sleep Play's car-combat revival, with 17 vehicles to choose from. Every one is a weapon with a driver attached.

items.title: G4 Icons: Miyamoto
items.description: Sitting down to talk, the man behind Donkey Kong, Mario and Zelda traces how a carpenter became a plumber and then a boy with a sword. Game design rarely gets a résumé this clean.

items.title: G4 Icons: EverQuest
items.description: Its developers trace the 3D fantasy world back through Ultima Online and the online worlds before it. Players nicknamed it EverCrack, which is a retention report in one word.

items.title: G4 Icons: BioWare
items.description: Two medical doctors, Greg Zeschuk and Ray Muzyka, started a studio, and the tape follows it from Baldur's Gate to MDK2 to Neverwinter Nights. Their prescription for role-playing: a lot of text and a pause button.

items.title: G4 Icons: Will Wright
items.description: SimCity began as the map editor built for Raid on Bungeling Bay, and the tape follows the idea on to The Sims. The method is sound: build the editor first, and sooner or later someone will want to live in it.

items.title: G4 Icons: Women in Gaming
items.description: Developers and executives, Caroline Esmurdoc of Circus Freak Studios among them, say how they got into games. On screen a wireframe becomes a character, which is the tip: every hero starts as a box.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Die Hard - Angry Video Game Nerd AVGN.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Die Hard
items.description: McClane loses his shoes, so the NES game gives him a foot meter and sends him through Nakatomi Plaza from above. The movie made the feet the plot; the game only reads the script.

items.title: Cinematech: Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly
items.description: Star Fox 64, then a Final Fantasy IV battle menu with Cecil, Kain, Rydia and Edge lined up, then a PlayStation 2 dragon. The menu's whole philosophy is wait for the bar, then act. It has held up.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/142 X-Play Episode 99 Grand Theft Auto San Andreas, Roadkill.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, Roadkill
items.description: Adam and Morgan take on Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, three cities and the countryside between them, plus Roadkill, a game that treats traffic as an opponent. The San Andreas map is the larger undertaking.

items.title: X-Play: Touring Tokyo
items.description: Adam and Morgan walk Tokyo's game and anime shops, import shelves and all, hunting for what has not reached America yet. Shopping abroad for games counts as research, and the tape documents it.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/143 X-Play Episode 195 Silent Hill 4, Resident Evil 4.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Silent Hill 4, Resident Evil 4
items.description: Resident Evil 4 takes the horror out of the mansion and into a village. Silent Hill 4 keeps you in an apartment with a chained front door. Each is a reasonable position on home safety.

items.title: X-Play: Halo 2
items.description: Adam Sessler and Morgan Webb take the Master Chief's sequel online over Xbox Live, with Juggernaut matches and a leaderboard of viewer scores. The leaderboard makes the case that the real campaign is other people.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/147 X-Play Episode 203 Metal Gear Solid 3 Special.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Metal Gear Solid 3 Special
items.description: Snake drops into a Soviet jungle with camouflage as the plan, and the hosts take its measure. Lying very still in the grass is advice that holds up in most settings.

items.title: X-Play: Non-Denominational Holiday Guide
items.description: A gift guide for every holiday at once: tree, menorah and sweaters on one set. The picks run from Katamari Damacy to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the quiet cousin and the loud one.

items.id: super-mario-all-stars-video-1993-full-vhs/Super Mario All-Stars Video (1993, Nintendo UK - VHSrip).mp4
items.title: Super Mario All-Stars Video
items.description: Craig Charles, then playing Dave Lister on Red Dwarf, hosts Nintendo UK's Super Mario All-Stars tape from a Nintendo spaceship. Four Mario games on one cartridge is exactly the news that earns one.

items.title: Donkey Kong Country Promo Tape
items.description: Exposed, the making of Donkey Kong Country, leads this Nintendo tape, then Super Metroid, Stunt Race FX and the Super Game Boy follow. Rare's rendered jungle is the main event, and the bananas get a close-up.

items.title: GamesMaster: Tony Slattery
items.description: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 gets a studio preview with its release date on screen, and two contestants settle a score at Street Fighter II. The hedgehog's sequel is treated as news, which it was.

items.title: GamesMaster: Frank Bruno
items.description: A heavyweight boxer is in the studio, and the closing round is a candy-world platformer with a ninja hero and a ticking clock. The designers treated sweets as a hazard, and the dentists agree.

items.id: ffw-gamesmaster-collection/GamesMaster S02E03 - Vinnie Jones and Nick Pickard.mp4
items.title: GamesMaster: Vinnie Jones and Nick Pickard
items.description: A football game and a timed Mario run decide two guests' standing, with Dominik Diamond in the red jacket keeping order and Patrick Moore's giant floating head handing down verdicts. A platformer settled by tribunal is only sensible.

items.title: GamesMaster: Rory Underwood
items.description: An RAF pilot is in the studio, so the flight game's cockpit view gets its toughest critic. Danny and Warren settle ice hockey on the side. The game's horizon stays level, which is a start.

items.title: GamesMaster: Take That
items.description: A helicopter run, a round of Bomberman, then a basketball grudge match between two boys in Manchester United shirts. Dominik Diamond referees and the floating head keeps the score. Nobody argues with the rules.

items.title: G4 Icons: Insomniac Games
items.description: Insomniac started with Disruptor, a PlayStation shooter, then turned to a purple dragon named Spyro. The tape covers the swerve, and it is hard to fault a plan that ends at Ratchet and Clank.

items.title: G4 Icons: Sid Meier
items.description: Solo Flight, Pirates, Railroad Tycoon, Civilization: the designer's rule is that a good game is a series of interesting decisions, and the tape holds every title to it. Civilization alone runs thousands of years of them.

items.title: G4 Icons: Scary Games
items.description: Horror games start with Haunted House, where you are a pair of eyes in a dark mansion, and run on through Resident Evil and Silent Hill. The tape's lesson is that the dark does most of the work.

items.title: G4 Icons: Richard Garriott
items.description: Lord British, the king he plays in his own games, goes from Akalabeth to Ultima to Ultima Online, and the first dungeon is a wireframe maze. The tape treats it as a perfectly good start for a kingdom.

items.title: G4 Icons: Bruce Shelley
items.description: Civilization's co-designer carries what he learned to Age of Empires at Ensemble Studios. The thesis holds up: a strategy game is a history lesson with a build queue.

items.title: G4 Icons: Madden NFL
items.description: G4 Icons traces John Madden Football from its first screens to the modern game, with Madden himself in an EA Sports cap. He insisted on a full 11 a side, a design note that has aged better than most.

items.title: Attack of the Show (June '10)
items.description: A mock Shakespeare lecture opens the show, then Around the Net catches Project Natal's River Rush and the couch turns to UFC. Natal is still wearing its working name on screen, and the tape keeps the receipt.

items.title: Attack of the Show (June '10)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Jessica Chobot wrap up E3 with a couch guest and ask Twitter for its pick of the show. A show floor with that many demos has room for every answer, and the poll allows all of them.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Paint Package, Virtual Reality
items.description: Joe and Mac Caveman Ninja gets the SNES review, with a paint package and a report on virtual reality alongside. Casting cavemen as ninjas is sound design: the dinosaurs were already in the level.

items.title: Bad Influence!: NHLPA Hockey, Amiga Assassin
items.description: NHLPA Hockey gets the Mega Drive review, with a first look at Alone in the Dark and a report on exploring other worlds. A hockey game with a players' union in its title is serious about the sport.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Super Aleste, Micro Machines
items.description: Super Aleste gets the SNES review, while the Amiga 1200 and a computer-made ballet share the show. A shooter is the easiest genre to judge: the screen is either full of bullets or it isn't.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Sonic 2, Handheld Costs
items.description: Sonic 2 gets the Mega Drive review, with a tally of what handhelds cost to run and VR at a special needs school. Sonic runs on rings, the one thing in here that costs nothing.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Mario Land 2, Humans
items.description: Super Mario Land 2 gets the Game Boy review, with the Freewheel controller and music made on an Atari ST. Six golden coins stand between Mario and his castle, and the game treats it as an errand.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Indiana Jones 3, Street Fighter 2
items.description: Indiana Jones 3 gets the Mega Drive review, and a Nintendo games help line shows who answers when a player is stuck. Any game that needs a hotline has told you something about its puzzles.

items.title: Attack of the Show (May '11)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey take Uncharted 3, Gears of War 3 and BioShock Infinite down the Road to E3, then send the Neato robot vacuum around a living room. Three games not yet on the shelf, and none of them vacuums.

items.title: Attack of the Show (June '11)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey point the Road to E3 at Skyward Sword, Assassin's Creed and Arkham City, with Rob Corddry on the couch. Every game on that road is a sequel, so the road is well paved.

items.title: X-Play: Psychonauts, Dungeon Siege 2
items.description: Psychonauts is a summer camp for psychics where the field trips go into other people's minds. Dungeon Siege 2 brings the party and the long walk. As curriculums go, Psychonauts has the better excursions.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/203 X-Play Episode 275 Games Your Momma Wouldn't Like 2.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Games Your Momma Wouldn't Like 2
items.description: Adam and Morgan return to the games Mom would rather you didn't play, with the case against and the footage for it. Parental concern has never had a better exhibit.

items.title: X-Play Goes Bananas
items.description: A capuchin monkey joins the X-Play couch, takes a keyboard and a chessboard, and the games are ape business, Donkey Kong first. As a guest reviewer it is hard to beat for relevance.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/224 X-Play Episode 306 Shadow of the Collossus, Harvest Moon A Wonderful Life.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Shadow of the Colossus, Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life
items.description: Two reviews that ask for long hours: a lone rider after colossal opponents, and a farmer who marries and becomes a father. Only one of them set out to be relaxing.

items.title: X-Play: The Zombie Episode
items.description: Adam and Morgan picnic in a cemetery, then deliver a lecture on everything you ever wanted to know about zombies. The advice is practical: learn the rules before the dead do.

items.id: british-sega-promo-video-software-lineup-1993-94-1993-uk-vhs/British Sega promo video - Software lineup 1993-94 (1993 UK VHS).ia.mp4
items.title: Sega Promo Video: Software Lineup
items.description: Sega Europe runs Master System and Mega Drive games back to back, Sonic and Streets of Rage among them. A shopping list with music, and the list is the whole argument.

items.id: lunchablessegagametips/Lunchables Sega Game Tips Video (Oscar Mayer Foods Corporation)(1995).mp4
items.title: Lunchables Sega Game Tips
items.description: Oscar Mayer packs Sega Genesis tips into a Lunchables tape: a code for the next level, Knuckles in Sonic 2, a Comix Zone sneak peek. A level skip and a snack in one box is sound planning.

items.title: PlayStation Underground: MST3K Segments
items.description: Mike Nelson, Crow and Tom Servo open and close PlayStation Underground's demo disc, with a console on the desk and theater seats for the verdict. A demo disc with a built-in riff track is being thorough.

items.id: electronic-boutique-and-game-nintendo-gamecube-promo-vhs/Electronic Boutique and Game Nintendo Gamecube Promo VHS.ia.mp4
items.title: Nintendo GameCube Promo Tape
items.description: A GameCube tape made for UK Electronics Boutique and Game stores: Luigi's Mansion, Smash Bros. Melee, Crazy Taxi, Sonic Adventure 2 Battle, then accessories. With Melee on the reel, the second controller is a sound closer.

items.title: GamesMaster: Jim Duggan
items.description: A wrestler brings a 2x4 to the studio and plays Super Mario World next to a young contestant. Mario's arsenal is a jump and a shell. Lumber was never licensed.

items.id: ffw-gamesmaster-collection/GamesMaster S02E07 - Shadow & Jet from Gladiators.mp4
items.title: GamesMaster: Shadow & Jet from Gladiators
items.description: Gladiators Shadow and Jet visit the GamesMaster set, and a Gladiators game turns up to meet them. Later two players settle a match at tennis. A sports show and a game on one tape is sound planning.

items.title: GamesMaster: Kristian Schmid
items.description: The review desk takes in computer Scrabble, a Super Nintendo and a point-and-click adventure. The Scrabble version has one real advantage: the tiles can never go missing under the sofa.

items.title: GamesMaster: John Parrott
items.description: A snooker champion meets the video game of snooker, and Prince of Persia is previewed for the Master System. A full frame here needs no chalk and no long walk round the table.

items.title: GamesMaster: Richard Norton
items.description: Super Mario Kart's split screen gets its turn, and so does a first-person crossbow maze where two players race the clock. Both games settle things with projectiles, which keeps the rules short.

items.title: G4 Icons: Splinter Cell
items.description: Ubisoft Montreal's Clint Hocking and Jacques Dussault explain the mocap suit and the shadows. The design rule is that darkness is a tool, which the whole game takes quite literally.

items.title: G4 Icons: Lord of the Rings
items.description: The Fellowship game's developers explain how a Shire, a Gandalf and a very long road fit on a console. Their answer is cutscenes up front and a lot of walking, which is faithful to the book.

items.title: G4 Icons: Atari
items.description: Nolan Bushnell and Bill Kunkel take Pong from the bar cabinet to a console in the living room. The coin slot gets its own labeled diagram, which tells you what mattered.

items.title: G4 Icons: Music Makers
items.description: Game music, from the beeps of Space Invaders and Pac-Man to Monkey Island and a composer's studio, with Tommy Tallarico among those explaining it. The hummable theme turns out to be a design decision.

items.title: G4 Icons: Unreal
items.description: Tim Sweeney and the Epic team follow a castle shooter into online deathmatch and an Xbox Live menu. The design brief appears to be one very large gun in the lower right corner.

items.title: G4 Icons: Yu Suzuki
items.description: The Sega designer behind Hang-On and OutRun explains Virtua Fighter, which starts as stick figures on paper, then goes on to Shenmue. Fighting game design begins with a pencil, apparently.

items.title: Cinematech: Super Mario Sunshine
items.description: A plumber with a water pack hoses brown goop off a sunny plaza on GameCube, then the episode swings to Malice and MechWarrior 4: Vengeance. The cleaning method is sound: aim the nozzle at the mess.

items.title: Bad Influence!: The Computer Museum
items.description: Mickey and Donald play stage magicians in World of Illusion, the Mega Drive review, with a Christmas buyers guide and a guide to importing consoles from the US. The game is a magic show where every level is a trick.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Racing Games, Tokyo Arcades
items.description: Super Mario Kart takes the main review, Take That try Virtua Racing, and the Atari Falcon and a guide to gaming in Tokyo fill out the tape. A December review suits a game about throwing shells at friends.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Ecco, Lemmings
items.description: Ecco the Dolphin gets the Mega Drive review, then Lemmings on several formats, software on CD and special effects in TV commercials. Ecco is the one hero who has to remember to breathe, and the game never lets you forget.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Cheat Devices, Code Screens
items.description: Prince of Persia gets the SNES review, with cheat devices, robots and the CES in Las Vegas. A game built on a countdown and a lot of spikes makes a better case for the Action Replay than the segment does.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Streets of Rage II, Drawing Program
items.description: Streets of Rage 2 gets the Mega Drive review, with Mario Paint, Stunt Island, puppet technology and advice on lowering the epilepsy risk of games. The plan is to walk right and clear the street. It holds up.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Surround Sound, Ariel the Little Mermaid
items.description: Super Star Wars gets the SNES review, with a virtual fish tank and a report from Universal Studios in Hollywood. The game follows the film's order, so it starts in the desert, as it should.

items.title: Attack of the Show (June '11)
items.description: Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey watch the Red Bull Soapbox Races go downhill, hear Lance Henriksen on his book, and try the Xperia PLAY. Game Break predicts E3 early, which is the safest time to predict.

items.title: Attack of the Show (April '11)
items.description: Mark Ruffalo takes the red chairs for Sympathy for Delicious and The Avengers. Game Break takes on Mortal Kombat, a game that has always treated "finish him" as a design philosophy.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/231 X-Play Episode 338 X-Play's Holiday's for the Homeland.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Holidays for the Homeland
items.description: X-Play stages a holiday special as a yellow living-room sitcom: tree, menorah, a puppet in a blue scarf. Call of Duty 2 and Mario Kart DS turn up on screen. A war game under the tree is its own tradition.

items.title: X-Play: The Classic Edition
items.description: Aquaman: Battle for Atlantis gets a hearing here, along with a costumed duel in the snow and a stop at the news desk. A hero who talks to fish has a lot to live up to.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/234 X-Play Episode 384 State Of Emergency 2, The Godfather.mp4
items.title: X-Play: State of Emergency 2, The Godfather
items.description: Adam and Morgan look at State of Emergency 2, where the whole city is a riot, and The Godfather, which has you shaking down shopkeepers for protection money. Customer relations, mob style.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/235 X-Play Episode 385 Star Wars Empire at War, C&C The First Ten Years.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Star Wars: Empire at War, Command & Conquer: The First Decade
items.description: An Imperial news conference, the Emperor on a phone call and an IG-88 infomercial, all in service of a strategy game. Then a decade of base-building gets a look back. Supply lines remain the whole job.

items.title: GamesMaster: Johnny Herbert
items.description: A red sports car, a countdown and a motorway full of roadworks cones: the racing game takes its realism seriously. A Formula One driver is in the studio to rule on it.

items.title: GamesMaster: Todd Carty
items.description: Baseball gets its turn, with contestants called up to bat on screen. Street Fighter II follows for a grudge match, and its rules explain themselves, unlike the infield fly.

items.title: GamesMaster: Bob Holness
items.description: A snowy Christmas platformer opens the games, then a puzzler about fencing off territory against the clock. Percentage covered is the score, which is a goal anyone can read.

items.title: How to Beat Home Video Games: The Best Games
items.description: Vestron Video's guide to the best home games puts a host in a blazer before a wall of monitors and a teenager on the joystick. Nearly an hour of cartridges, handled with mission-control calm.

items.title: How to Beat Home Video Games: The Hot New Games
items.description: Vestron's hour of strategy for the hot new home games, from Pitfall's jungle to the mazes, rests on a sound idea: watch someone else lose first, then borrow what they learned.

items.title: G4 Icons: Intellivision
items.description: Don Daglow and the Mattel crew make their case: Major League Baseball, Space Armada and the Blue Sky Rangers. The pitch was sports that looked like sports, and the diamond on screen backs it up.

items.title: G4 Icons: The Legend of Zelda
items.description: Zelda from the first NES overworld through Link's Awakening, Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask and Wind Waker, with Koji Kondo on the music. Each new one is a bigger world to get lost in, and the tape counts that as the point.

items.title: G4 Icons: Xbox
items.description: Microsoft's route to the Xbox: the X reveal, the big first controller, Dead or Alive 3 at launch, then Xbox Live. A console made of PC parts was the plan, and the launch-day crowds are the evidence it held.

items.title: G4 Icons: Arcade
items.description: Missile Command, Centipede and Pac-Man up through Marble Madness and Street Fighter II, with a coin going in at every turn. The game was the hook and the coin was the point, and the tape is comfortable with both.

items.title: G4 Icons: The History of E3
items.description: G4 Icons traces E3, the Los Angeles trade show where every console maker announced the future to a floor full of press and retailers. The future, by the footage, usually came with a very large booth.

items.title: G4 Icons: LucasArts
items.description: Monkey Island and Full Throttle, then an X-Wing cockpit, with Mary Bihr and Sean Clark remembering. The adventure games ship a verb list, Give, Pick up, Talk to, and it covers most of life.

items.title: Attack of the Show (March '11)
items.description: Adam Sessler brings the Nintendo 3DS to Game Break, a handheld pitched as 3D without the glasses. The Miz also stops by, belt in hand, ahead of WrestleMania XXVII.

items.title: Attack of the Show (April '11)
items.description: Morgan Webb takes Portal 2 through Game Break, where the companion cube finally gets the attention it deserves. Morgan Spurlock sits down for The Greatest Movie Ever Sold, a film funded by its sponsors.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Jurassic Park
items.description: Jurassic Park gets its Mega Drive review, and the game lets you play the raptor as well as Dr. Grant. Giving the monster a turn is a reasonable way to adapt a film about a monster getting loose.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Rocket Knight Adventures, First Samurai
items.description: Rocket Knight Adventures gets the Mega Drive review: Sparkster, an opossum in armour with a rocket pack, plus First Samurai on the SNES and a competition line. Armour for defence, rocket for offence, opossum for reasons.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Biggest Dinosaurs CD-ROM, Mario
items.description: A dinosaur encyclopedia on CD-ROM gets a page headed The Biggest Dinosaurs, then Mario goes underground on the NES. Leading with the biggest is sound editorial planning.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Scrabble, Monopoly
items.description: Scrabble and Monopoly leave the table for the computer, with a real board on the studio floor for comparison. The software never loses a piece under the sofa, which is most of the argument.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Jingle Bells, Zelda Link's Awakening
items.description: Jingle Bells lyrics scroll across a wall of monitors in the seasonal show, and Link's Awakening gets its Game Boy review. A video wall is what the sing-along was waiting for.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Atari Jaguar, Battletoads
items.description: The Atari Jaguar gets the full tour, console and circuit board included, with a run through older Atari games to show where it came from. Every console needs a family tree.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E01.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Super Metroid Grappling Beam
items.description: The Super Metroid segment stops on the grappling beam screen: select it, press and hold the button. That is the entire tip, and nothing about it needs a second paragraph.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E02.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Wario Land, Baseball
items.description: In Wario Land, how many coins does it take to earn an extra life? The show puts the question on screen and trusts you with it. Wario, a man of coins, would have known.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E03.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Zelda 3, D2: The Mighty Ducks
items.description: D2: The Mighty Ducks gets the movie slot here, between baseball and Wario Land. The show covers games, music and films, and treats a hockey sequel as a perfectly reasonable cartridge.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E04.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Lima to Kathmandu Mystery Game
items.description: A world-chase game runs from Lima to Kathmandu against a clock that names the day and the hour, while Lexa Doig, billed as the Ebert Wannabe, takes the movies. A deadline that names its hour is the honest kind.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E05.ia.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Kirby, Star Trek
items.description: Kirby's Adventure takes the long segment, the NES game's pink hero with a score and an enemy gauge under the show's frame. Inhaling the problem is, as design philosophy goes, sound.

items.title: Cinematech: Halloween 1
items.description: A pumpkin sits in the corner of the screen while Heather walks a Silent Hill 3 corridor and Resident Evil arrives on GameCube. Nobody turns on a light, which is correct for both games.

items.id: g4s-cheat-series/S02 E01 New Years Resolution Cheating.mp4
items.title: Cheat!: New Year's Resolution Cheating
items.description: A new year's list of codes: a skateboarding game, a World War II shooter and college hoops, then a Pringles poll. As resolutions go, typing in a code is one you can keep through January.

items.title: Cheat!: Cheatroid Prime
items.description: Cory Rouse takes on Metroid Prime, where the secrets involve linking a Game Boy Advance, then Grand Theft Auto, Dragon Ball Z and Frogger. A bounty hunter who needs a second console is nothing if not thorough.

items.title: Cheat!: Double O Cheat
items.description: Cory Rouse suits up for a James Bond game and its codes, then moves on to Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and a football game. The agent's method and the show's method are the same: get the gadget, skip the briefing.

items.title: Cheat!: Splinter Cheat
items.description: Cheat! stages a Splinter Cell mission on location, with a field agent in sunglasses and a figure in black crawling the rocks, then goes back to the game's dark rooms. The lesson is the game's own: dress dark, stay low.

items.id: g4s-cheat-series/S02 E23 Knights of the CHEAT! Republic.mp4
items.title: Cheat!: Knights of the CHEAT! Republic
items.description: Cory Rouse picks a side in Knights of the Old Republic, robed as a Jedi, then in the dark hood, with tips for lightsaber duels and the Pazaak card game. Both sides get the same tips, which is how a guide stays neutral.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Aug. '11)
items.description: Game Break takes apart Deus Ex: Human Revolution, a game where every problem has a vent, a door and a conversation. Sara Underwood walks Anime Expo, and Zoe Saldana drops in for Colombiana.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Oct. '11)
items.description: New York Comic Con gets the coverage, and Game Break gives Arkham City its turn. Chris Gore does DVDuesday in a Batman shirt, which is how you prepare for that segment.

items.title: G4 Icons: Red Storm
items.description: Rainbow Six turns a Tom Clancy raid into a PC game, with CEO Doug Littlejohns and PC Gamer's Daniel Morris. It asks you to plan the raid before you play it, and plenty of people did.

items.title: G4 Icons: Warren Spector
items.description: Origin and Ultima, then System Shock, then Deus Ex at Ion Storm, with Doug Church along. The design school is that the player may try something else. A locked door is an invitation.

items.title: G4 Icons: PC Gaming
items.description: Floppy disks and text adventures, then Sierra, Earl Weaver Baseball, Doom and Quake, ending on an Alienware rig. The machine bought for spreadsheets turns out to have been a games machine all along.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Thunder Seat, Aladdin
items.description: The Thunder Seat is a cockpit chair with a screen in front of it, and the show straps a presenter in and takes it up in a flight game. Sitting down is the strongest control scheme.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Jeffrey Love, Spectrum HoloByte
items.description: Pumpkins mark the Halloween show, which then visits Spectrum HoloByte to meet game designer Jeffrey Love. A pumpkin makes a fair design exercise: one idea, carved with commitment.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Sonic Spinball, Bonfire Night
items.description: Sonic Spinball takes its turn on the Mega Drive and Alien Breed 2 on the Amiga, with a lab detour under a Japanese flag. Spinball is a pinball table with Sonic inside, and that was the pitch.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Gaming Alphabet, Burning Rubber
items.description: An alphabet of gaming terms runs through the show, J for joystick or joypad and S for sprite, alongside Bomberman and the Amiga racer Burning Rubber. An A to Z is how a hobby explains itself.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Fashion Design, Oscar
items.description: The fashion edition: a workshop of mannequins, a computer in a design studio and a catwalk show, plus an Amiga 1200 review of Oscar. A catwalk is a scrolling level that someone else controls.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Theme Park Builder, Cosmic Spacehead
items.description: A theme-park builder fills the screen with paths, rides and a haunted house, and an Onyx workstation sits in the studio. The best thing about a park you build yourself is the queue length: you set it.

items.title: Video Game Tricks, Codes and Strategies Vol. 1
items.description: A ranked list of NES tricks from MPI Home Video, with Contra's Thirty-Man Trick, Iron Tank, Tiger-Heli and Blaster Master, behind a notice that Nintendo did not authorize it. Thirty lives is sound advice.

items.title: Video Game Tricks, Codes and Strategies Vol. 2
items.description: MPI Home Video's NES tape of codes and strategies runs past 20 tips, from a Blaster Master end-boss trick to a Super Dodge Ball killer throw. The killer throw gets a tutorial, which is the honest way to teach dodgeball.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E06.ia.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Top 3 Games Chosen by Viewers
items.description: A Canadian YTV game show: the Closet Gamer brings on a kid named Paul as Game Player, and the reviewers watch the play from a corner inset. Reviewing a game while someone plays it is a sound method.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E07.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: WCW SuperBrawl, Batman vs The Flash
items.description: Acclaim's Justice League Task Force is on the review desk, with Superman, Batman, the Flash and Green Arrow in a one-on-one fighter. After decades on the same side, they finally get to settle it.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E08.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Donkey Kong, Power Bracelet Dungeons
items.description: The Game Boy's Donkey Kong opens on the arcade's own girders, then keeps going past where the arcade would have stopped. Some sequels are better described as a longer visit.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E10.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Kirby, Boy George
items.description: Boy George's The Crying Game gets its video played, with EMI credited on screen, between a Star Fox run and a Kirby level. The Top 10 follows the pop charts as seriously as the cartridge ones.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E11.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Joe & Mac Lost in the Tropics
items.description: Data East sends its cavemen on holiday in Joe & Mac: Lost in the Tropics, a reviewed platformer with a stone-age bike in it. The sequel's pitch is the original's, with better weather.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Feb. '12)
items.description: Joe Lo Truglio is the guest in the red chairs with Kevin Pereira and Candace Bailey, and The Raid: Redemption gets a trailer. A film set in one apartment tower treats the level design as the plot.

items.title: Attack of the Show (March '12)
items.description: Clark Duke takes the guest chair, and viewers are asked their favorite part of Mass Effect 3, a game that expects you to remember every choice you made in the first two.

items.title: Cheat!: San Andreas
items.description: The button strings for Grand Theft Auto arrive on screen, then get used: a plane over the desert, a skydive, a bike down the highway. The game was open the whole time. The codes just point at the doors.

items.id: g4s-cheat-series/S04 E02 Oddworld and The Stranger.mp4
items.title: Cheat!: Oddworld and The Stranger
items.description: G4's Cheat takes on Oddworld: Stranger's Wrath, where the bounty hunter's ammunition is alive and has opinions. The tape covers which critter to load, and the general store that sells the rest.

items.title: Cheat!: Master Cheat!
items.description: This Cheat episode is Halo 2: sniping, dual wielding, a level-select screen, and Master Chief in the title pun. The Chief has never asked anyone for help, so the show asks on his behalf.

items.title: Cheat!: The One Freeman
items.description: Half-Life 2 gets a walkthrough of its roughest stretches: the coast road, the Combine gunships, a tripod over the city. The advice is to keep moving, which in this game has always been the whole plan.

items.id: g4s-cheat-series/S04 E05 Metal Gear Solid Cheat!.mp4
items.title: Cheat!: Metal Gear Solid Cheat!
items.description: Kristin Holt puts on dog tags for Metal Gear Solid 3: a Hideo Kojima interview, the survival viewer, and Snake vs. Monkey. Hiding in a jungle gets covered in detail, from a very well-lit studio.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Independence Day - Playstation 1  PS1 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 29.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Independence Day
items.description: The Nerd flies the PlayStation game of the alien invasion film. The movie ends the war in one sitting; the game hands out passwords so you can save the world in installments.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/The Simpsons - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 30.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Simpsons
items.description: The Nerd works through Bart Simpson's NES games, starting with Space Mutants, where X-ray specs reveal the aliens and spray paint stops them. Springfield's defense plan is a child with a spray can. It is hard to improve on.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Bugs Bunny Birthday Blowout - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 31.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Bugs Bunny Birthday Blowout
items.description: An NES game marks Bugs Bunny's 50th birthday, and the Nerd puts on the ears to celebrate properly. Fifty years of cartoon timing, handed to a jump button.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Nintendo Power - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 33.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Nintendo Power
items.description: The Nerd pages through Nintendo's house magazine, from the reader top-ten charts to the Zelda joke page. The advice was printed in color, so it was treated as settled.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Fester's Quest - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 34.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Fester's Quest
items.description: The Nerd turns up as Gomez, then as a bald-capped Fester, in black and white, for a game where Fester takes a blaster to an alien invasion. Nobody in this family needed talking into a weapon.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Texas Chainsaw Massacre - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 35.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Texas Chainsaw Massacre
items.description: Wizard Video put Leatherface on the Atari 2600, and the player is the one with the chainsaw. Fuel is the real enemy here: a horror classic, scaled down to a gas gauge and a handful of pixels.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Halloween - Atari 2600 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 36.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Halloween
items.description: The Nerd hauls out an Atari 2600 slasher cartridge, with a Michael Myers mask at his shoulder, to see how a babysitter's night translates into blocks. The film set the job; the game kept it.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Dragon's Lair - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 37.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Dragon's Lair
items.description: Don Bluth's arcade animation ran off a laserdisc. The Nerd tries the NES cartridge instead: a swinging chain, a sea serpent below, and Dirk falling in both versions. The fall is the one thing that survived the port.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Christmas Carol Part 1 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 38.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Christmas Carol (Part 1)
items.description: Part one of the Nerd's Dickens riff gets going with Home Alone 2: Lost in New York on the NES, which sends Kevin through a hotel full of obstacles. That is the plot of the film, if you squint. Squint harder.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Christmas Carol Part 2 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 39.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Christmas Carol (Part 2)
items.description: Part two brings the ghosts. Dickens gave Scrooge a lesson in generosity; the Nerd gets his in game consoles, from a sheeted visitor and a bearded one. The structure is sound.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/The Legend of Zelda Timeline - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 40.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Legend of Zelda Timeline
items.description: Chronologically confused, as the title card admits: a walk through the Legend of Zelda games, trying to line them up in order. Link has been saving Hyrule for decades, and nobody has said in what order.

items.title: Cinematech: Halloween 2
items.description: Kingdom Hearts tops a Halloween trailer list, with Luigi's Mansion, Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts and Alone in the Dark on the same reel. Luigi's Mansion handles its haunting with a vacuum cleaner, which is sound practice.

items.title: Bad Influence!: Football, Inside a Nintendo Pad
items.description: Football runs the show, from a ball in the studio to an EA football game on screen, with a Nintendo pad opened up to show the switches inside. Two thumbs for eleven players is the pad's whole job.

items.title: G4 Launch Reel ('02)
items.description: Eight seconds in, a card says G4 Media, promotional purposes only, CONFIDENTIAL, DO NOT DUPLICATE. Then the new network makes its case for games on TV. The last instruction did not take, and we're glad.

items.title: G4 Launch Reel, Part 2 ('02)
items.description: The reel's last stretch hands the floor to Rez, the rail shooter that turns every shot into music. For a channel pitching games as culture, it is a well-chosen exhibit.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E12.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Cybernator, Donkey Kong
items.description: Konami's Cybernator is on the review desk, a mech-suit shooter where the answer to every problem is a bigger suit. The logic holds up for as long as the ammunition does.

items.id: video-arcade-top-10/Video & Arcade Top 10/Season 02/Video & Arcade Top 10 S02E13.mp4
items.title: Video & Arcade Top 10: Wario Land, Justice League Taskforce
items.description: A chart on this tape lists Donkey Kong Country, Yoshi's Island and Diddy's Kong Quest, all of them Super NES. A list that is mostly Kong has a point of view, and it states it plainly.

items.title: Fails of the Weak: Halo Edition
items.description: Achievement Hunter's Geoff Ramsey and Jack Pattillo narrate a disc of Halo bloopers, accidental deaths and vehicular carnage. Halo offers a lot of ways to lose, and this is the thorough survey.

items.title: Cheat!: Resident Evil 4 Cheat!
items.description: Cheat takes on Resident Evil 4: Leon, the village, and the attaché case where every weapon has to fit like furniture. The game's real puzzle is packing, and the tips treat it that way.

items.id: g4s-cheat-series/S04 E07 Splinter Cell Cheat! Theory.mp4
items.title: Cheat!: Splinter Cell Cheat! Theory
items.description: Cheat runs Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory mostly through night vision, down a hallway and into a room of safe-deposit boxes. Sam Fisher's one rule is that nobody sees him, and the tips follow it.

items.title: Cheat!: God of Cheat!
items.description: Kristin Adams gives this Cheat! over to God of War, working through the fights and puzzle rooms for the tricks Kratos needs. The tips are thorough. Kratos has a great many rooms, and a great many enemies in them.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Rambo - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 41.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Rambo
items.description: The Nerd plays the NES version, a sidescroller with a life and experience meter, then holds it up against the Sega Master System one. One man, one bow, two different jungles.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Virtual Boy - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 42.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Virtual Boy
items.description: Red wireframes on black, seen through a visor on a tabletop stand, with Mario's Tennis and Water World in the slot. Nintendo promised 3D, and the 3D is there, in one color, up close.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/The Wizard Of Oz - Super Nintendo - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 43.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: The Wizard of Oz
items.description: Fan covers of the AVGN theme open this one, then the Nerd follows Dorothy from the cornfield to the Witch in a Wizard of Oz platformer. The film gave her a road. The game gives her a jump button.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Doublevision (Part 1) Intellivision - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 44.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Doublevision (Part 1): Intellivision
items.description: Mattel's answer to a bare joystick was a twelve-key pad, a control disc and plastic overlays saying what each key does. The manual lives on the controller, which is thorough.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Doublevision (Part 2) ColecoVision - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 45.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Doublevision (Part 2): ColecoVision
items.description: Coleco promised the arcade at home, and Donkey Kong in the box was a fair start. The tape then finds Campaign '84, a Fisher-Price dance program and a Smurf game. The home part was kept faithfully.

items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.description: Many kids met this game in the film The Wizard, and the Nerd has the tape on the shelf. The game's own case is a leaf that turns a plumber into a flying raccoon, and the logic holds.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/NES Accessories - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 47.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: NES Accessories
items.description: A tour of NES extras: the Zapper, the Power Pad underfoot, the NES Advantage stick and Konami's LaserScope headset. The LaserScope's method is to shout fire at the game, which leaves the hands free.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Indiana Jones Trilogy - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 48.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Indiana Jones Trilogy
items.description: Fedora on, the Nerd plays three Indiana Jones games: Raiders on the Atari 2600, then Temple of Doom and Last Crusade on the NES. The adventure is genuine. The instructions are the puzzle.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Star Trek - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 49.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Star Trek
items.description: Opening credits over a starfield, a floating NES, then a transporter drop into a game that warns Jim a creature looks like a dragon. As intelligence goes, it is specific.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Superman - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 50.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Superman
items.description: An Atari 2600 cartridge, then an NES game that gives Clark a Super Power meter and an Item Power meter to watch. In this version, being invincible takes bookkeeping. The Nerd reviews both.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Nov. '12)
items.description: Josh Meyers and Sara Underwood run the desk, a Star Wars Episode VII roundup lands, and The Man with the Iron Fists gets its interviews. The title is the whole plot, which saves time.

items.title: Attack of the Show (Nov. '12)
items.description: John Barrowman and Candace Bailey host Thanksgiving dinner on the set, fireplace and turkey included. The news ticker reports a monkey washing a cat, which settles the dinner conversation.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/237 X-Play Episode 388 Auto Assault, Samurai Champoo.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Auto Assault, Samurai Champloo
items.description: Auto Assault is an online game where the car is the character class. Samurai Champloo puts hip-hop and swords on one Edo-period road trip. Two ways to survive a long drive.

items.id: 144-x-play-episode-199-halo-2/238 X-Play Episode 389 Metroid Prime Hunters, Ice Age 2 The Meltdown.mp4
items.title: X-Play: Metroid Prime Hunters, Ice Age 2: The Meltdown
items.description: Adam and Morgan size up Metroid Prime Hunters, Samus Aran's first-person outing on the DS, then take apart a motorcycle sim. Aiming with a stylus is a bold use of a pen.

items.title: X-Play: Dark Void, Wolfenstein
items.description: X-Play previews Dark Void, goes hands-on with Rise of the Argonauts, and gives Wolfenstein an All Access look. The Wolfenstein pitch is the same as ever: shoot the occult Nazis. It remains a solid plan.

items.title: X-Play: Fable II, LittleBigPlanet
items.description: Adam and Morgan review Fable II, LittleBigPlanet and Dead Space, and Mirror's Edge gets an All Access visit. Kristin Holt brings Force Unleashed cheats, including a Stormtrooper costume, which the game fully supports.

items.title: X-Play: Fallout 3 Special
items.description: Todd Howard and the Bethesda crew tour the Capital Wasteland, and a Top 5 survival list includes getting your hands on a Fat Man, the mini-nuke launcher. In a wasteland, that is the correct amount of firepower.

items.title: X-Play: Wrath of the Lich King, Sacred 2
items.description: Wrath of the Lich King and Sacred 2: Fallen Angel get X-Play reviews, and Resistance 2 gets a cheat. Red Faction: Guerrilla gets an All Access visit, for a game whose whole pitch is that walls are optional.

items.title: The Electric Playground
items.description: Electric Playground drops by Electronic Arts Canada in Vancouver, asks Rare's Ken Lobb about the Nintendo 64, and reviews the original PaRappa the Rapper. The 64DD gets a blueprint of its own.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Superman 64 - Nintendo 64 - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 51.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Superman 64
items.description: Titus has the Man of Steel fly rings against a countdown, through fog so thick the city is mostly rumor. The Nerd files his report. Nobody could accuse the fog of half measures.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Batman - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 52.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Batman
items.description: In cowl and cape, the Nerd works through the NES, the Atari Lynx and the Super Nintendo in turn. The hero is famous for being prepared. Each cartridge is a chance to prove it.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Batman (Part 2) - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 53.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Batman (Part 2)
items.description: Sunsoft's NES game puts the Joker in its subtitle, and the Nerd takes it as an invitation, so the purple suit turns up on his set. Truth in advertising.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Deadly Towers - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 54.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Deadly Towers
items.description: The status screen reads 100 hit points and 50 Ludders, the local currency. The Nerd goes in on that and a castle of look-alike rooms. It is the clearest page of the manual the game ever wrote.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Battletoads - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 55.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Battletoads
items.description: A guest guitarist joins the Nerd on the couch for Rare's NES brawler about three amphibians. The game's reputation for difficulty is the one claim nobody on that couch needs to dispute.

items.title: X-Play: Watchmen The End Is Nigh, Operation Anchorage
items.description: Hands-on with Watchmen: The End Is Nigh, where Nite Owl and Rorschach settle things with their fists, plus Operation Anchorage for Fallout 3 and Sessler's Soapbox. Moral ambiguity, delivered by punching.

items.title: X-Play: Top 9 Games So Far
items.description: A midyear Top 9 of the best games so far, with inFamous, Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars and Tiger Woods PGA Tour 10 on the list, plus the biggest surprise and the most disappointing. Halftime in the Game of the Year race.

items.title: X-Play: Avatar The Game, MX vs. ATV Reflex
items.description: Avatar: The Game and MX vs. ATV Reflex get reviewed, Assassin's Creed II gets a glyph cheat at the Rialto Bridge, and Left 4 Dead 2's Dark Carnival gets a tourist guide. Sightseeing advice: keep moving.

items.title: X-Play: The Golden Mullet Awards
items.description: Adam and Morgan hand out the Golden Mullet, the not-so-coveted prize for the previous year's worst games, after a cold open that raids a temple for the idol. Awards season for the games that earned the opposite.

items.title: X-Play: BioShock Infinite, Portal 2
items.description: BioShock Infinite gets a gameplay preview, a city in the clouds where the ground is optional. Portal 2 gets a cheat, F.E.A.R. 3 a review, and the staff pick their favorite modern horror games.

items.title: X-Play: Uncharted 3, Zynga Studio Tour
items.description: Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception gets its review, with a WWE 12 exclusive, a Saints Row red carpet and a Zynga studio tour alongside. Nathan Drake's treasure hunts remain the best case for travel insurance.

items.title: Cinematech: Tippy Top
items.description: A Clone Wars crawl opens the reel, with Mace Windu enlisting a legion of Jedi, and Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball turns up later. Sending in a legion before the first level is a thorough briefing.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Dick Tracy - NES - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 56.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Dick Tracy
items.description: The Nerd opens the film on VHS, then Bandai's NES game, which splits its day between overhead driving and warehouse fistfights. A detective is expected to work both ends of town.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Dracula - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 57.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Dracula
items.description: The Nerd puts on the cape for a count's career in games, from a Commodore computer to the Sesame Street Count's own cartridge. Immortals are patient, which helps with the ports.

items.id: AVGNCompleteCollection/Frankenstein - Angry Video Game Nerd - Episode 58.ia.mp4
items.title: The Angry Video Game Nerd: Frankenstein
