items.description: X-rays: mysterious, invisible, and nothing to worry about. This film demystifies radiation with the breezy confidence of an era that let kids try on shoes with fluoroscopes.

items.title: Self-Preservation in an Atomic Bomb Attack
items.description: Plain advice for staying alive in an atomic attack, in the flat tone these pamphlets all share. Calm, certain it has covered everything, and meant to be kept somewhere you can find it.

items.title: A Is for Atom
items.description: A is for Atom. B is for Boundless Energy. C is for Consequences We Haven't Fully Considered Yet. A beautifully animated primer on atomic energy from a more optimistic time.

items.title: Infant and Child Care
items.description: Babies do not read pamphlets. Improvised infant care for a shelter, with no usual conveniences and nowhere to go. A companion to the Medical Self-Help Training course, so take notes.

items.title: Earth Satellites: Explorers of Outer Space
items.description: How do man-made satellites stay up there? What can they teach us? And what's next? A late-fifties film that looks at the space race with the wide-eyed wonder of a species that just figured out orbit.

items.title: Operation Ivy
items.description: Ivy Mike, the first hydrogen bomb, filmed for the official record. The test island was part of the experiment, and it did not survive the experiment. Please remain calm.

items.title: Operation Doorstep
items.description: The Annie test went off in Nevada on national television, and civil defense ran a study beside it. The finding is that a good shelter gets you through. It is stated very calmly.

items.title: Role of the Block Warden in the H-Bomb Era
items.description: The block warden's job in an H-bomb attack, explained mostly in drawings. The argument is that it's survivable if your block is organized. Civil defense, the narrator says, begins at the grass roots.

items.title: Atom Bomb Effects
items.description: Color footage of soldiers crouching in foxholes while a nuclear bomb detonates nearby, then climbing out and running toward the mushroom cloud. The footage is real. The safety protocols were aspirational.

items.title: Operation Teapot: Military Effects Studies
items.description: A Nevada test film whose prints went red with age, until the uploader pulled most of the red back out with Avidemux. A few patches now run green. Given the subject, a colour cast is the mild part.

items.title: Time of Disaster
items.description: Tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes. The film is evenly calm about every one of them, then gets to the disaster it actually came to discuss. Weather is the warm-up act.

items.title: News Footage 1954
items.description: Unedited newsreel from the year Oppenheimer's clearance was pulled, with segments on the man himself. No narrator to tell you what to think, just reels and a country working out how it felt.

items.title: Atom Bomb
items.description: Early atomic weapons testing footage, presented as 'Joe Bonica's Movie of the Month.' Because nothing says entertainment like watching the birth of the nuclear age in grainy black and white.

items.title: Operation Big Shot
items.description: A Los Angeles station carried an atomic test live from Nevada, and this kinescope is what survives of that broadcast. The calm voices around a mushroom cloud are the real horror here.

items.title: Trail of the Rocket
items.description: Singers Lucille and Johnny tour an Oldsmobile factory. Johnny suspects a fellow visitor might be a Martian spy. This is a real film that exists. Sponsored by Oldsmobile.

items.title: Living with the Atom
items.description: A primer that begins with what matter is made of and walks, calmly, from Alamogordo to the H-bomb. It stops to ask whether any of this is moral. That is the reassuring part.

items.title: Retrospect: Personal Responsibility
items.description: A civil defense TV show that opens with a history of WWI and the English monarchy, then pivots to your personal responsibility in the event of nuclear war. The connection is unclear but the message is firm.

items.title: Disaster Control Indoctrination: Nuclear Fallout Survival
items.description: An Air Force officer stands at a podium in front of a curtain, holding up the fallout booklet. A cutaway house shows where to sit. The curtain does not move.

items.title: EOC RADEF Operations
items.description: A training film on Emergency Operations Centers and RADEF (Radiation Defense) procedures. For when the bombs drop and someone needs to read the Geiger counter. That someone is you.

items.title: Atomic Energy Can Be a Blessing
items.description: Fred MacMurray and Father James Keller explain that atomic energy is a God-given blessing in industry, agriculture and medicine. The cheerful half of the pamphlet, with a movie star on staff.

items.title: The Waking Point
items.description: Joe Mercer, a British everyman, learns civil defense matters after his son is trapped in a sandpit. The recruitment pitch is gentle and domestic, and sure a few evenings of training will cover it.

items.title: Radioactive Fallout and Shelter
items.description: How to look after the sick and the hurt when no hospital is coming, said in the voice of someone reading you a recipe. Calm is the main supply. Keep it somewhere dry.

items.title: Ten for Survival: Who Do You Know?
items.description: Chet Huntley reads Americans their own survey answers about surviving nuclear war, and an expert marks each one right or wrong. A pop quiz, essentially, with the highest stakes available.

items.title: A Missile Named Mac
items.description: Bell Labs sends one intercontinental missile named Mac from launch to target, in Technicolor, with radar and ground computers doing the steering. The pitch is that nobody has to worry, least of all Mac.

items.title: Fallout Shelter: What Is It?
items.description: The basic course: what a fallout shelter is, how much protection it gives, which kinds exist. Orderly, unhurried, and it assumes you will be taking this very seriously by the end.

items.title: Exercise Desert Rock
items.description: About 5,000 soldiers camp 27 miles from an atomic test so the Army can dispel their fear of radiation. Classes come first. The calm is the point, and it is applied evenly.

items.title: A Concrete Plan for Civil Defense
items.description: Ready-mix concrete trucks: they deliver concrete, they carry water, and they can fight fires. Colorado's civil defense plan turned the most boring vehicles on earth into first responders.

items.title: Communism in Action
items.description: Part one of a series warning of the Red Star's relentless rise. The distributor's catalog promised a message of vital importance to every American, and the narrator never once lowers his voice.

items.title: The Hole
items.description: Two construction workers at the bottom of a hole talk about an accidental nuclear war, one voiced by Dizzy Gillespie, animated by John and Faith Hubley. The calmest conversation on the channel, and the hardest to climb out of.

items.title: Information Program Within Public Shelters
items.description: When you're sealed in a public shelter after a nuclear attack, morale matters. This film discusses how to keep occupants busy, calm, and informed — the three pillars of underground optimism.

items.title: In Our Hands: How to Keep What We Have
items.description: Part four of the American Economic Foundation's civics lecture. Maps, the Constitution, farms and factories, then ships and troops. It makes its case calmly and expects you to agree.

items.title: Retrospect: Shelter and Evacuation
items.description: Another episode of the civil defense TV show 'Retrospect,' this time weighing the merits of sheltering in place versus evacuation. Spoiler: both options assume the existence of a place to go.

items.title: The Atom Goes to Sea
items.description: True Boardman's explainer arrives the way these films do: every diagram certain, every outcome bright. Nuclear power for ships was brand new, and the narrator treats the future as already approved.

items.title: Communism in Action: Life Behind the Iron Curtain
items.description: Part two follows a border of iron, 10,515 miles by the distributor's count, from the Arctic to the Sea of Japan, with a stop in new Cuba. The narrator is certain. That is the reassurance.

items.title: Community Fallout Shelter Planning
items.description: Seen through a Bucks County commissioner's eyes in Doylestown: surveys, decisions, funding, and a shelter plan at the end of the paperwork. A young Gene Hackman plays the Civil Defense expert.

items.title: Rural Civil Defense TV Spots
items.description: Short TV spots in which marionettes teach farmers what to do when the bomb comes. The puppets are earnest, the advice is sincere, and nobody on screen looks worried, which was the brief.

items.title: Town of the Times
items.description: Two school board members, Ralph Meeker and Larry Gates, fight over a town's shelter plan. It opens on a pleasant place with a good Chinese restaurant, so you know exactly what is at stake.

items.title: Special Delivery (AV Geeks Print)
items.description: The Army Air Force celebrates its finest delivery: an atomic bomb dropped on Bikini Atoll during Operation Crossroads. The title is a pun. The mushroom cloud is not.

items.title: Public Shelter Organization and Staff
items.description: Fifty strangers, one basement, and a chain of command. A dramatization of who runs what down there, from manager to staff. The org chart is the survival plan, so read it closely.

items.title: Let's Face It
items.description: Opens on an H-bomb cloud and a headline about Russia's own, then asks you to join a drill. Sirens, shelters, rehearsals. The message is that practice is the plan, delivered very calmly.

items.id: 72742CivilDefenseANewFamilyInTown/72742 Civil Defense A new Family In Town.mp4
items.title: A New Family in Town
items.description: An English family that lived through the Blitz moves to town and builds a shelter, and the neighbors notice. Robert Preston narrates, so the unease arrives in a very good voice.

items.title: The Red Trap
items.description: A Lutheran television drama from Concordia Films: a father tries to get through to his son while the FBI closes in. The can says it won a Freedoms Foundation award. Thirty minutes, one family, no exits.

items.title: Hospitals for Disaster
items.description: Packaged disaster hospitals: a whole hospital stored in advance, to be unpacked on the worst day. The reassuring part is that someone thought to put it in a box.

items.title: Special Delivery (Prelinger Print)
items.description: Another print of the Army Air Force's tribute to Operation Crossroads — the Bikini Atoll atomic bomb tests. Same pride, same mushroom clouds, different film canister.

items.title: Public Shelter Supplies: What Does the Government Supply?
items.description: A training film for shelter managers: food, water, sanitation, medical supplies and radiation detection, itemized. You are the manager now. Please check the inventory before you need it.

items.title: Public Shelter Living: The Story of Public Shelter 104
items.description: A dramatization of the first week inside Public Shelter 104 after a nuclear attack. Seven days of rationed food, shared air, and government-mandated cooperation. A teaching tool for shelter managers who will definitely need it.

items.title: Duck and Cover (AV Geeks Print)
items.description: The same Bert the Turtle, the same desk-ducking advice, different print. Still the most famous civil defense film ever made. Still not going to save you.

items.title: Self Preservation in an Atomic Attack
items.description: Soldiers get their instructions for an atomic attack, delivered with the calm of someone reading out the fire exits. Reassuring, right up until you remember what the exits are for.

items.title: Survival Under Atomic Attack (AV Geeks Print)
items.description: Edward R. Murrow explains atomic survival one more time, in a different print. The advice hasn't changed. The odds haven't improved.

items.title: Civil Defense in Schools
items.description: It opens on a tornado drill, then explains that the atomic age asks more of teachers and school boards. Filmed in Rockville, Maryland. Everyone files out in an orderly line, which is the idea.

items.title: Local Civil Defense
items.description: Whose job is it to save you when the bombs fall? Your local government's, apparently. This film explains the civil defense chain of command with the confidence of a flowchart.

items.title: Operation Crossroads: Bikini Atoll, Summer 1946
items.description: The Able and Baker tests at Bikini Atoll, in the full documentary record. This is where the shelter business begins, and the film is calm about it, the way this channel likes its beginnings.

items.title: Medic: Flash of Darkness
items.description: Medic, the hospital drama, gives Richard Boone an atomic aftermath to work in, with Civil Defense behind the production. It aired on Valentine's Day, which is a choice.

items.id: 89744-civil-defense-a-prime-for-survival/89744 Civil Defense A Prime For Survival.mp4
items.title: A Primer for Survival
items.description: Dave Garroway, the Today show's first host, is your guide to thermonuclear war, and the news is good: it is survivable. Made to reassure an anxious public, and the reassurance is the whole product.

items.title: Radar Secrets
items.description: Secret weapons of World War II, ranked by value versus cost. Radar finds a Japanese vessel; sixty seconds later the guns are ready. The film ends with a promise that America will never be unprepared again.

items.title: McLintock!
items.description: John Wayne runs a cattle empire and can't keep his house in order. Two hours of frontier stubbornness. Nobody wins. Everybody deserves it.

items.title: The Gun and the Pulpit
items.description: A gunslinger pretends to be a preacher. The town buys it. God keeps his opinion to himself.

items.title: Santa Fe Trail
items.description: Errol Flynn and Ronald Reagan ride the trail before the war changes everything. Hollywood history. Close enough.

items.title: War of the Wildcats
items.description: Oil and cattle don't mix. Wayne picks a side. The land doesn't care either way.

items.title: West of Hot Dog
items.description: Short film. Don't ask about the title. Just ride with it.

items.title: The Over-the-Hill Gang
items.description: Retired lawmen strap it on one more time. They're too old for this. That's the point.

items.title: The Mark of Zorro
items.description: Douglas Fairbanks. 1920. Silent steel and a mask that started it all. The original vigilante with a blade and a grin.

items.title: Angel and the Badman
items.description: Wayne plays a gunfighter taken in by Quakers. The gun or the girl. The oldest choice in the territory.

items.title: The Over-the-Hill Gang Rides Again
items.description: They came back. Nobody asked them to. That's never stopped a cowboy before.

items.title: Sagebrush Trail
items.description: Wayne rides to clear his name. Fifty-three minutes. No fat on the bone.

items.title: Gone with the West
items.description: A drifter rides into a dying town looking for the men who wronged him. The town was already dead. He just hadn't noticed.

items.title: The Lucky Texan
items.description: Wayne and an old prospector strike gold. The trouble shows up right on schedule.

items.title: West of the Divide
items.description: A man hunts for his father's killer and his kidnapped brother. The desert holds both answers.

items.title: Winds of the Wasteland
items.description: Pony Express riders buy a stagecoach line to a ghost town. The wind out there doesn't care about your business plan.

items.title: Paradise Canyon
items.description: An undercover agent rides into canyon country after counterfeiters. The canyon's the prettiest thing in the picture.

items.title: Abilene Town
items.description: Randolph Scott keeps the peace between cattlemen and homesteaders. The town sits right on the line. So does he.

items.title: Riders of Destiny
items.description: Wayne shows up singing. Somebody controls the water. The songs stop when the guns start.

items.title: Hell Town
items.description: Wayne inherits a ranch and a grudge that comes with it. The town earned its name.

items.title: The Man from Utah
items.description: A marshal goes undercover at a rodeo where riders keep dying. Utah sent the right man.

items.title: Apache Blood
items.description: A sole survivor tracks the soldiers who massacred his people. The desert is patient. So is he.

items.title: American Empire
items.description: Two Confederate veterans build a cattle empire after the war. The empire doesn't last. They never do.

items.title: The Border Patrolman
items.description: George O'Brien rides the line between countries. The border doesn't care who you are.

items.title: Billy the Kid Returns
items.description: Roy Rogers looks just like the Kid. That resemblance is either a gift or a death sentence.

items.title: Raiders of Old California
items.description: Gold Rush California. Everybody came looking for something. Most found trouble instead.

items.title: Rocky Mountain Mystery
items.description: A mystery at a radium mine in the Rockies. Randolph Scott asks questions the mountains won't answer.

items.title: The Star Packer
items.description: Wayne hunts the Shadow, a bandit who gives orders from behind a wall. Fifty minutes till the wall comes down.

items.title: Under California Stars
items.description: Roy Rogers plays himself. Horse thieves target Trigger. That was their first mistake.

items.title: Vengeance Valley
items.description: Burt Lancaster protects his no-good brother one too many times. The valley collects what's owed.

items.title: Six Gun Trail
items.description: Tim McCoy rides a trail that starts with a stagecoach robbery and ends where they always end.

items.title: Daniel Boone, Trail Blazer
items.description: Boone cuts a path through Kentucky. The wilderness was there first but it never filed a claim.

items.title: The Mysterious Rider
items.description: A stranger rides into town. Nobody knows his name. That's how he likes it.

items.title: Law of the Lash
items.description: Lash LaRue and his bullwhip clean up a frontier town. The whip does most of the talking.

items.title: Arizona Stage Coach
items.description: The Range Busters ride shotgun on a stage through Arizona territory. Bandits picked the wrong coach.

items.title: Rainbow Valley
items.description: Wayne goes undercover among road agents blocking a new highway. The valley's prettier than the people in it.

items.title: Randy Rides Alone
items.description: Wayne walks into a saloon full of dead men and gets blamed for it. Riding alone was the easy part.

items.title: Oh, Susanna
items.description: Gene Autry rides, sings, and sorts out a case of mistaken identity. The horse never gets confused.

items.title: The Arizona Raiders
items.description: Quantrill's raiders head west after the war. Arizona wasn't ready for what the war left behind.

items.title: Gangsters of the Frontier
items.description: Tex Ritter chases outlaws running a protection racket. The frontier has rules. These men forgot them.

items.title: The Young Land
items.description: California, just after the Mexican-American War. A killing forces the new territory to decide what kind of law it believes in.

items.title: Young Bill Hickok
items.description: Roy Rogers as Hickok before the legend hardened. Every legend was young once.

items.title: It Can Be Done, Amigo
items.description: Bud Spencer in the Italian West. Big fists, bigger appetite, and a con man who won't quit. The spaghetti is served.

items.title: Billy the Kid Wanted
items.description: Buster Crabbe as the Kid, framed again. Being wanted is a full-time occupation.

items.title: Blue Steel
items.description: Wayne chases a masked bandit called the Polka Dot Bandit. Even outlaws have a brand.

items.title: Bar-Z Bad Men
items.description: Johnny Mack Brown straightens out the bad men at the Bar-Z. The ranch is only as good as the men on it.

items.title: Outlaws of Boulder Pass
items.description: George Houston rides through the pass after a gang of cattle rustlers. The rocks don't take sides.

items.title: The Silver Trail
items.description: Rex Lease follows a trail of silver to a mining town with more crooks than prospectors.

items.title: Rogue of the Range
items.description: Johnny Mack Brown rides undercover into outlaw country. The range doesn't distinguish between law and lawless.

items.title: Two-Fisted Law
items.description: Tim McCoy and a young Wayne settle a ranch dispute with their fists. The law out here has knuckles.

items.title: The Painted Hills
items.description: Lassie in the gold country. A loyal dog avenges his prospector. The hills remember what men forget.

items.title: Alias John Law
items.description: Bob Steele rides under a borrowed name. Out here, a name is just another thing to leave behind.

items.title: Ghost-Town Gold
items.description: The Three Mesquiteers hunt for gold in a town that died waiting for it.

items.title: God's Gun
items.description: Lee Van Cleef plays twins. A priest and a gunfighter. The Lord works in heavily armed ways.

items.title: Saddle Mountain Roundup
items.description: The Range Busters ride again. Saddle Mountain has a problem. They brought the solution.

items.title: The Proud and the Damned
items.description: Confederate mercenaries in South America. The war ended but they didn't get the telegram.

items.title: Arizona Days
items.description: Bob Custer fights rustlers in the last days of silent pictures. The desert never needed the sound anyway.

items.title: Cavalcade of the West
items.description: Brothers separated as children. One becomes a lawman. One doesn't. The west sorts them out.

items.title: Sheriff of Tombstone
items.description: Roy Rogers pins on the star in Tombstone. The last sheriff didn't last long. Neither do most.

items.title: The Big Trees
items.description: Kirk Douglas wants the redwoods. The homesteaders say no. The trees have been saying no for a thousand years.

items.title: The Range Feud
items.description: Buck Jones and a young Wayne caught between feuding ranchers. The range doesn't forgive and it doesn't forget.

items.title: Buckskin Frontier
items.description: The railroad pushes west. Richard Dix pushes back. Steel and buckskin don't negotiate.

items.title: My Pal Trigger
items.description: Roy Rogers and the horse that matters more than any man in the picture. He's not wrong.

items.title: Under Western Stars
items.description: Roy Rogers' first starring ride. Water rights, dustbowl politics, and a song for every sunset.

items.title: Angel and the Badman
items.description: A gunfighter wakes up in a Quaker house with a bullet in him and nobody asking questions. The hardest thing he's ever met is a house with no guns in it.

items.title: The Arizona Kid
items.description: Roy Rogers rides during the Civil War. Arizona picked its own side. It always does.

items.title: Rough Riders' Round-Up
items.description: Rogers and the Rough Riders chase border smugglers. The round-up doesn't stop at the fence line.

items.title: Yodelin' Kid from Pine Ridge
items.description: Gene Autry yodels his way out of a feud between cattlemen and chicken farmers. Only Autry could make that work.

items.title: Come On, Cowboys
items.description: The Three Mesquiteers answer the call. Ranch trouble. The usual. The saddle never gets cold.

items.title: Arizona Gunfighter
items.description: Bob Steele draws fast in Arizona territory. The sun's in everyone's eyes. Except his.

items.title: Song of Arizona
items.description: Roy Rogers sings to Arizona and Arizona listens. The desert has always been a good audience.

items.title: Gunsmoke Ranch
items.description: The Three Mesquiteers clean up a ranch where the smoke never clears. Fifty-two minutes of settling accounts.

items.title: Red Blood of Courage
items.description: Bob Custer rides hard into trouble. Forty-six minutes. The blood runs quick and the courage runs quicker.

items.title: My Outlaw Brother
items.description: Mickey Rooney goes to Mexico to find his outlaw brother. Some family you ride toward. Some you ride away from.

items.title: The Naked Hills
items.description: A gold prospector spends his whole life chasing a strike. The hills strip a man down to what he really wants.

items.id: CowboyAndTheIndiansGeneAutryAppleTV/Cowboy and the Indians Gene Autry - Apple TV.mp4
items.title: Cowboy and the Indians
items.description: Gene Autry helps a displaced tribe. He sings. He means it. The horizon doesn't judge.

items.title: Frontier Outlaws
items.description: Buster Crabbe as Billy the Kid hunts outlaws on the frontier. Took one to catch them.

items.title: Shadow Ranch
items.description: Buck Jones rides into a ranch with a shadow hanging over it. 1930. They built them lean back then.

items.title: Cowboy and the Senorita
items.description: Roy Rogers and Dale Evans together for the first time. The trail ahead is longer than either of them knows.

items.title: Public Cowboy No. 1
items.description: Gene Autry versus cattle rustlers with radios and refrigerated trucks. The modern world came for the range. The range wasn't ready.

items.title: Sing, Cowboy, Sing
items.description: Tex Ritter sings and rides and nobody asks him to choose between the two.

items.title: Texas Terror
items.description: Wayne hangs up his guns after killing his friend. Texas has a way of making a man pick them back up.

items.title: Fighting Caravans
items.description: Gary Cooper on the wagon trail west. The caravans don't stop for weather, bandits, or second thoughts.

items.title: The Great Train Robbery
items.description: 1903. Twelve minutes. The first western ever made. A bandit points his gun at the camera and the whole genre starts.

items.title: Death Rides a Horse
items.description: Lee Van Cleef and a young man ride together hunting the same killers. Revenge is patient work. The horse doesn't mind.

items.title: Take Me Back to Oklahoma
items.description: Tex Ritter wants to go home. The outlaws between here and Oklahoma have other plans.

items.title: The Lawless Frontier
items.description: Wayne hunts a killer on the frontier where the law hasn't arrived yet. Somebody had to go first.

items.title: Tombstone Canyon
items.description: Ken Maynard rides into a canyon with a phantom and a secret. The canyon keeps what's buried.

items.title: Rage at Dawn
items.description: Indiana, 1866. The Reno brothers rob trains and own the county: judge, prosecutor, constable. Randolph Scott rides in as an outlaw and isn't one. The town settles it at night, at the jail, without him.

items.title: Born to the Saddle
items.description: Two ranch families, two horse-breaking styles, one rivalry. Some men were made for the saddle. Some just sit in it.

items.title: Aces and Eights
items.description: Tim McCoy plays a gambler with a fast draw. Aces and eights. The dead man's hand. Somebody always loses.

items.title: Brand of the Devil
items.description: Dave O'Brien fights outlaws branded with the devil's mark. The brand tells you everything you need to know.

items.title: A Bullet for the General
items.description: Mexican Revolution. An American mercenary rides with bandits. The politics are complicated. The bullet is simple.

items.title: Django
items.description: A man drags a coffin through the mud. What's inside is worse than what's outside. Italian dust. The real thing.

items.title: Run, Man, Run
items.description: A knife-throwing thief, a revolutionary's gold, and half of Mexico chasing both. The spaghetti boils over.

items.title: The Mercenary
items.description: A Polish mercenary sells his gun to the Mexican Revolution. Franco Nero. Jack Palance. The price keeps going up.

items.title: The Great Silence
items.description: Snow instead of dust. A mute gunfighter against Klaus Kinski in the Utah blizzard. The silence says everything the genre usually shouts.

items.title: The Big Gundown
items.description: Lee Van Cleef hunts a man across the border. The hunt is the point. The gundown was always coming.

items.title: Day of Anger
items.description: A street sweeper learns gunfighting from a master. Lee Van Cleef teaches lessons that don't wash off.

items.title: Face to Face
items.description: A Boston professor goes west for his health and becomes a bandit. The territory changes a man. Or reveals him.

items.title: Beyond the Law
items.description: Lee Van Cleef as a bandit who becomes a sheriff. The badge and the gun don't know the difference.

items.title: The Price of Power
items.description: A spaghetti western retelling of the Kennedy assassination. Set in Dallas. 1881. The price never changes.

items.title: The Bold Caballero
items.description: Zorro in early Technicolor. The mask looks better in color. So does the sword.

items.title: The Virginian
items.description: DeMille's western, off an old AMC tape with the ads in. The Wister novel gave the cowboy his code: when you call a man that, smile.

items.title: Tumbleweeds
items.description: William S. Hart's last ride. The Cherokee Strip land rush. 1925. The silent west, rolling to a stop.

items.id: rio-lobo-1970-john-wayne-western-civil-war/Rio Lobo (1970 John Wayne Western Civil War).mp4
items.title: Rio Lobo
items.description: Wayne's last ride with Howard Hawks. A Union colonel chases a traitor south to Rio Lobo. The sun's going down on everything.

items.title: Stagecoach
items.description: 1939. John Ford. Monument Valley. The Ringo Kid. The western that made Wayne a star and the desert a cathedral.

items.title: The Gunfighter
items.description: Gregory Peck as the fastest draw alive, tired of proving it. Every town has a kid who wants to try. The gunfighter just wants coffee.

items.title: Ride Out for Revenge
items.description: A marshal stands between a gold-hungry town and a displaced tribe. The ride out is the easy part. It's the standing that costs.

items.title: The Outcasts of Poker Flat
items.description: A gambler and a prostitute get run out of town into a snowstorm. Bret Harte wrote it. The mountains don't care who you were.

items.title: Snake River Desperadoes
items.description: The Durango Kid rides along the Snake River after a gang of desperadoes. The river keeps moving. So does he.

items.title: Branded a Coward
items.description: A man branded yellow gets a chance to prove the brand wrong. The iron leaves a mark. So does courage.

items.title: Kit Carson
items.description: Kit Carson guides a wagon train west through hostile territory. The map ends where the real country begins.

items.title: Last Stagecoach West
items.description: The last stagecoach on the line. The railroad's coming. Progress doesn't ask permission.

items.title: Stagecoach Outlaws
items.description: Buster Crabbe as Billy the Kid rides after stagecoach bandits. The coach keeps a schedule. The outlaws don't.

items.title: Bar 20
items.description: Hopalong Cassidy and the Bar 20 ranch. The silver hair, the black hat, the white horse. Hoppy rides.

items.title: Blazing Across the Pecos
items.description: The Durango Kid blazes across the Pecos after trouble. The river marks the line. He crosses it anyway.

items.title: Dead Man's Gold
items.description: Lash LaRue hunts gold that a dead man left behind. The gold doesn't care who carries it. The whip does.

items.title: Frontier Revenge
items.description: Lash LaRue rides for revenge on the frontier. The bullwhip cracks. The frontier listens.

items.title: Secrets of the Wasteland
items.description: Hopalong Cassidy in ancient cliff-dweller territory. The wasteland keeps its secrets until somebody digs too deep.

items.title: The Daltons' Women
items.description: Lash LaRue versus a town run by the Dalton gang's women. The men are dead. The women are worse.

items.title: Ragtime Cowboy Joe
items.description: Johnny Mack Brown in a tale of ragtime and range war. The piano keeps playing. The shooting starts anyway.

items.title: Colorado Kid
items.description: Bob Steele rides into Colorado trouble. Fifty-five minutes of frontier justice served cold.

items.title: Cheyenne Takes Over
items.description: Lash LaRue and Al St. John ride into Cheyenne. The town was doing fine without them. It'll do better after.

items.title: Nevada City
items.description: Roy Rogers in a fight over stagecoach versus railroad. Nevada City sits at the crossroads. The future picks one.

items.title: The Trail Beyond
items.description: Wayne rides into the Canadian wilderness looking for a missing girl. The trail goes past where the maps stop.

items.title: South of Santa Fe
items.description: Roy Rogers goes undercover at a mine south of Santa Fe. The silver's dirty. Rogers isn't.

items.title: Silver Spurs
items.description: Roy Rogers fights an oil baron trying to take over cattle land. The spurs are silver. The intentions aren't.

items.title: Songs and Saddles
items.description: A singing cowboy picture. The saddle's real. The songs float out over the flatland and don't come back.

items.title: Cavalry
items.description: The cavalry rides. The bugle calls. The dust rises. It always does.

items.title: Border Patrol
items.description: Hopalong Cassidy patrols the border where the law thins out. Hoppy rides the line steady as a fence post.

items.title: The San Antonio Kid
items.description: Red Ryder rides into San Antonio territory. The kid makes trouble. Red Ryder makes it stop.

items.title: Billy the Kid in Texas
items.description: Bob Steele as Billy the Kid, riding through Texas on somebody else's trouble. PRC budget. Full-sized grit.

items.title: The Big Show
items.description: Gene Autry plays twin brothers. One's a rodeo star. One's a ranch hand. The crowd can't tell the difference.

items.title: Revenge of the Virgins
items.description: Gold prospectors trespass on sacred land. The land takes it personally. Low budget. High strangeness.

items.id: OldBarnDanceGeneAutryAppleTV/Old Barn Dance Gene Autry - Apple TV.mp4
items.title: The Old Barn Dance
items.description: Gene Autry fights a crooked horse-trading scheme with songs and a Saturday matinee grin. The barn's still standing.

items.id: last-crooked-mile-1946-/Last Crooked Mile (1946) Philip Ford, Don ‘Red’ Barry republic.mp4
items.title: The Last Crooked Mile
items.description: The gang dies in a car chase, but the bank money is still out there, somewhere in a car sold to a carnival. An insurance man heads for the midway.

items.title: Time Table
items.description: Half a million dollars of train payroll and a robber posing as a doctor. The insurance man on the case has to postpone his Mexico vacation. Crime ruins everyone's plans.

items.title: Make Haste to Live
items.description: Eighteen years is a long time to plan a revenge. A New Mexico single mother buys a gun and tapes a message for her daughter, just in case.

items.title: Dillinger
items.description: Lawrence Tierney glowers his way from small time crook to Public Enemy Number One. He holds up a cinema on the way, which feels like a rude thing to do to a moviegoer.

items.title: Silver Blaze
items.description: Holmes takes a vacation and, naturally, finds a double murder, a missing racehorse and Moriarty. Arthur Wontner plays him as a man who has never relaxed in his life.

items.id: the-verdict-1946-sydney-greenstreet-peter-lorre-joan-lorring-paul-cavanagh-morto/The Verdict (1946) [Sydney Greenstreet, Peter Lorre, Joan Lorring, Paul Cavanagh, Morton Lowry, Holmes Herbert; Dir. Don Siegel; 720p].mp4
items.title: The Verdict
items.description: Sydney Greenstreet loses his Scotland Yard job over a wrongful execution and would love to see his smug replacement look foolish. Peter Lorre, an artist with macabre tastes, agrees.

items.title: The Big Combo
items.description: The brass tells a lieutenant to drop a mob boss because the stakeout is too expensive. He goes to the boss's girlfriend instead. The shadows are deep enough to hide a body in.

items.title: Impact
items.description: Pushed off a cliff by his wife's lover, a businessman survives, and the police put his wife in jail over it. Being dead turns out to be oddly convenient.

items.title: The Man Who Cheated Himself
items.description: A homicide lieutenant covers up a shooting for his lover, then draws the case himself. His eager kid brother is on it too. Family dinners will be awkward.

items.title: The Man Is Armed
items.description: A job gets pulled clean and the plan is to sit on the money for three years, until the statute of limitations runs out. Dane Clark leads; William Talman, later Perry Mason's Hamilton Burger, is in the cast.

items.title: Behind Green Lights
items.description: Dumping a political murder victim at the door of police headquarters shows either nerve or a poor sense of direction. A lieutenant has to find out which.

items.title: Breakaway
items.description: Metal fatigue is not what thrillers usually fight over, but here a dying professor passes the formula to a young man. Tom Conway is the suave detective who arrives unflappable.

items.title: Suddenly
items.description: Frank Sinatra, cast against type, takes a widow's house hostage to ambush the President passing through. A small town is about to have a very bad day.

items.id: pitfall1948_202001/Pitfall (1948, USA) Featuring Dick Powell, Lizabeth Scott, Jane Wyatt - Film Noir Full Movie.mp4
items.title: Pitfall
items.description: Bored with his desk and his family, an insurance adjuster goes to recover a thief's presents from his girlfriend, and finds an affair instead. A dull job looks better in hindsight.

items.title: Barbados Quest
items.description: Stamp collecting turns out to be a murderous hobby. A wealthy American hires private eye Tom Martin to find out if his rare stamp is a fake.

items.id: southside-1-1000-1950/Southside 1-1000 (1950) Don DeFore, Andrea King, George Tobias Gerald Mohr.ia.mp4
items.title: Southside 1-1000
items.description: Fake money, with plates engraved by a lifer inside San Quentin. A Secret Service agent poses as a big buyer to get near the gang. The danger is real.

items.id: crisscross1949_202003/Criss Cross 1949 - Burt Lancaster, Dan Duryea, Yvonne De Carlo_x264.mp4
items.title: Criss Cross
items.description: Burt Lancaster drives armored cars for a living, which in a noir is a warning. His ex wife keeps turning up, and so does Dan Duryea.

items.title: The Chase
items.description: Adapted from a Cornell Woolrich novel, so the jobless veteran who returns a wallet and lands a chauffeur's job for a man with violent enemies is already in trouble. Havana is the way out, at a price.

items.title: Strange Illusion
items.description: In his recurring dream, a young man watches his mother fall for a dangerous stranger. Then the stranger turns up, as dream strangers do. Edgar G. Ulmer directs it like a nightmare on a budget.

items.title: Midnight at Madame Tussaud's
items.description: One explorer bets he can spend the night alone in the Chamber of Horrors. Crooks, meanwhile, are after his ward's fortune. The wax figures stay calm.

items.title: The Web
items.description: Hired as a businessman's secret bodyguard, a lawyer shoots the man who turns up with a gun. Then he begins to suspect he was hired for exactly that.

items.title: Counterfeit
items.description: Chester Morris goes undercover with a gang that prints fake money to rescue a kidnapped Treasury engraver. He also finds time for two sisters. T men never clock out.

items.description: The plan: a crooked lawyer and a con woman pass a gambler off as a rich couple's long lost son. Edmond O'Brien is the gambler who has to sell it.

items.description: On a beach at night, a widow thinks she hears her late husband calling from the surf. A tall dark stranger conveniently knows all about such things. Turhan Bey is the stranger.

items.title: East of Piccadilly
items.description: Scotland Yard is hunting a London strangler, and so is a reporter who writes thrillers on the side. She found one of the bodies and intends to sell the story twice.

items.title: Fear in the Night
items.description: Waking from a dream of murder in a mirrored room, a bank teller finds bruises he cannot explain. DeForest Kelley, long before Star Trek, is the man waking up.

items.title: Assigned to Danger
items.description: The gang hiding at the lodge has a wounded leader, and the new guest says he is a doctor. He is an insurance investigator, which complicates the surgery.

items.title: City That Never Sleeps
items.description: Republic Pictures, one Chicago night, and a Chicago Police technical adviser in the credits so that someone is accountable. Gig Young, Mala Powers, Marie Windsor. "Two old fashions. No ice, no water, no sugar, no grenadine."

items.title: The Limping Man
items.description: Flying to London for an old flame, an American watches the man standing next to him at the airport get shot. Scotland Yard takes an interest in Lloyd Bridges.

items.title: One Girl's Confession
items.description: Cleo Moore is the waitress who steals $25,000 from the boss who cheated her father, hides it, and confesses. Hugo Haas wrote, directed and co stars, so fate and irony get plenty of screen time.

items.title: Sherlock Holmes' Fatal Hour
items.description: Out of a painting of a cardinal comes a voice, and it wants a card cheat to join a counterfeiting plot. Holmes blames Moriarty, which is usually the right answer.

items.title: Motor Patrol
items.description: Los Angeles motorcycle cops chase a hit and run the police think was deliberate. A trainee goes undercover as a car thief to get close. Traffic duty has never been so exciting.

items.title: The Fatal Hour
items.description: Boris Karloff takes a break from monsters to play San Francisco detective James Lee Wong. A friend of the police captain is murdered and the trail runs along the waterfront.

items.id: hi-jacked-1950_202607/Hi-Jacked (1950) Crime_Film Noir _ Jim Davis, Marsha Mae Jones, Sid Melton.ia.mp4
items.title: Hi-Jacked
items.description: Stop in the rain to help a stranded motorist and you wake up with the truck gone. A driver with a record is the police's first suspect. Never stop for a stranger.

items.title: Blackout
items.description: Temporarily blind, a man wanders into a house just after a murder. The killers spare him, the police do not believe him, and nobody can find a body.

items.title: Man Bait
items.description: One kiss between a bookstore manager and a clerk, and the thief she is dating smells blackmail. Hammer made it before it found its monsters, with Terence Fisher directing.

items.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers
items.description: A childhood secret that the town has built a career on. Stanwyck and Heflin walk back into it, and a very young Kirk Douglas is already sweating.

items.title: Sudden Fear

items.title: Odd Man Out
items.description: After a robbery goes sour, a wounded rebel leader drifts through the back alleys of Belfast with the whole city hunting him. Carol Reed directs James Mason through all of it.

items.title: The Devil Thumbs a Ride
items.description: Every hitchhiking warning you were ever given, in one car. A killer fresh from a holdup catches a ride to Los Angeles, picks up passengers and takes charge.

items.title: Human Desire
items.description: Glenn Ford comes home from Korea to his train and a rail supervisor's wife. Fritz Lang directs, and Gloria Grahame is the reason the engineer is in trouble.

items.id: spellbound1945_202001/Spellbound (1945, USA) Director Alfred Hitchcock Starring Ingrid Bergman, Gregory Peck - Film Noir.mp4
items.title: Spellbound
items.description: Ingrid Bergman, a psychiatrist, falls for the asylum's new director, who has some very odd aversions. Salvador Dali designed the dream, for Alfred Hitchcock.

items.title: The Upturned Glass
items.description: James Mason is a neurosurgeon lecturing students on a woman who fell from a window, and why he decided it was murder. He skips the police and handles it himself.

items.title: The Long Night
items.description: Anatole Litvak remakes Marcel Carné's Le jour se lève for RKO, with Henry Fonda in Jean Gabin's old part and Vincent Price permitted a bow tie. Most of it is spent at night.

items.title: Forbidden
items.description: Tony Curtis goes to Macao to fetch an old flame for a mobster, and she turns out to be engaged to the casino owner he just saved. Rescuing people is a poor career move.

items.title: Shadow of Terror
items.description: PRC Pictures, Lew Landers directing, a lot of desert. A man cannot remember who he is, and a ranch house fills with people who might know. "Jim, you mustn't dwell on yourself so intensely."

items.id: below-the-deadline-1946-/Below the Deadline (1946) William Beaudine, Warren Douglas.mp4
items.title: Below the Deadline
items.description: A veteran comes home to find his gangster brother dead and takes over the rackets in the name of revenge. His sweetheart would prefer he quit. Family business, though.

items.title: Detour
items.description: A pianist hitchhikes to Los Angeles, his ride dies on a rainy night, and he makes the worst decision available. Ann Savage then arrives as the meanest woman in noir.

items.title: Mr. Wong in Chinatown
items.description: A poisoned dart, a dying woman and a half written clue, all in detective James Lee Wong's front hall. Boris Karloff has fog, a waterfront and two suspects who start with J.

items.title: Appointment with Crime
items.description: A smash and grab crook with broken wrists does his time without naming the club owner who ran out on him. William Hartnell, the first Doctor Who, spends the sentence building a grudge.

items.id: allotment-wives-1945/Allotment Wives (1945) Kay Francis, Paul Kelly, Otto Kruger.ia.mp4
items.title: Allotment Wives
items.description: Women marry soldiers for their pay and their life insurance, and would like the soldiers not to come home. Kay Francis is in the middle of the racket. A wartime scam with excellent hats.

items.title: Kansas City Confidential
items.description: Masked men rob an armored car, and an ex GI takes the beating from the police. John Payne follows the trail to Mexico to find who set him up.

items.title: Scarlet Street
items.description: A mild cashier and amateur painter rescues a woman from a beating, and she lets him think she loves him. Edward G. Robinson, Joan Bennett and Dan Duryea make a bad triangle.

items.title: The Shadow Strikes
items.description: The Shadow catches safecrackers, then fools the police by pretending to be the lawyer whose safe it was. Rod La Rocque plays the hero of the pulps and radio, in a very good hat.

items.id: crime-of-passion-1957-barbara-stanwyck-sterling-hayden-raymond-burr/Crime of Passion (1957) [Barbara Stanwyck, Sterling Hayden, Raymond Burr, Fay Wray, Virginia Grey, Royal Dano, Stuart Whitman; 720p].ia.mp4
items.title: Crime of Passion
items.description: Barbara Stanwyck is a famous advice columnist who gives it all up to marry a detective. She turns out to be very ambitious on his behalf.

items.title: D.O.A.
items.description: A week's fun in San Francisco turns into a luminous poison and no antidote. A small town accountant spends what is left investigating his own murder.

items.title: The Naked Witch
items.description: Larry Buchanan's Texas-shot tale of a witch's grave that should have stayed buried. His first feature, made with more ambition than budget — and that's saying something.

items.title: Das Kabinett des Doktor Caligari ( The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari )
items.description: The first true horror film. A madman, a sleepwalker, and a carnival that will rewire your understanding of cinema. German Expressionism at its most unsettling.

items.title: Carnival of Souls
items.description: After surviving a car accident, a woman can't shake the feeling that something followed her out of the water. Herk Harvey made one film. He made it count.

items.title: The Ghoul
items.description: Boris Karloff as a dead Egyptologist who rises from his tomb to reclaim a stolen jewel. Thought lost for decades, this British horror was rediscovered in the Czech Republic.

items.title: Teenagers from Outer Space
items.description: An alien teenager defects to save Earth from becoming a giant lobster buffet. The romance is real even if the special effects aren't.

items.title: Haxan
items.description: Benjamin Christensen builds a lecture on witch hunts from woodcuts and staged scenes, and plays the Devil himself. Silent, a century old, and the Devil looks like he is having a great time.

items.title: The City OF The Dead
items.description: A student travels to a fog-choked Massachusetts village to research witchcraft. The locals are very welcoming. Christopher Lee sends her there — that should've been the first warning.

items.title: In The Year
items.description: Post-apocalyptic survivors huddle in a valley after nuclear war. The radiation outside is bad. What's evolving out there in the dark is worse.

items.title: Night of the Living Dead
items.description: The one that started it all. Romero's no-budget masterpiece that invented the modern zombie and changed horror forever. If you haven't seen it, tonight's the night.

items.title: The Most Dangerous Game
items.description: A shipwrecked hunter discovers his host's preferred prey walks on two legs. Pre-Code thrills shot on the same jungle sets as King Kong.

items.title: Attack of the Giant Leeches
items.description: Something's living in the Florida swamp. Something big, slimy, and very hungry. The locals keep disappearing and nobody's asking the right questions.

items.title: The Monster Maker
items.description: A mad doctor with a syringe and a grudge sets his sights on a pianist. J. Carrol Naish in the lab coat, Ralph Morgan in the cast, and PRC kept it short and mean. Do not shake hands.

items.id: mars-needs-women-sci-fi-1968-tommy-kirk-yvonne-craig-movie/Mars Needs Women (Sci-Fi, 1968) Tommy Kirk, Yvonne Craig _ Movie.mp4
items.title: Mars Needs Women
items.description: Tommy Kirk plays Dop, a Martian scouting Earth for brides, and Yvonne Craig is the scientist who has to deal with him. Larry Buchanan's budget shows, and so does his nerve.

items.title: War of the Robots
items.description: Italian Star Wars ripoff with all the ambition and none of the budget. From the same crew that brought you Cosmos: War of the Planets. The costumes alone are worth the trip.

items.title: The Phantom Creeps
items.description: Bela Lugosi as a mad scientist with a giant robot, an invisibility belt, and a plan for world domination. Everything a 12-chapter serial is supposed to be.

items.title: The Phantom Planet
items.description: An astronaut crash-lands on a tiny asteroid inhabited by tiny people. The atmosphere shrinks him to their size. Getting home won't be simple.

items.title: Snowbeast
items.description: Jaws, but with a ski resort and a yeti. A TV movie that delivers exactly what the title promises. Bo Svenson and Yvette Mimieux in the snow.

items.title: The Manster
items.description: One injection from an eccentric scientist and a reporter in Japan starts growing an extra eye on his shoulder. You can guess where that is headed. The title already told you, and it was right.

items.title: White Zombie
items.description: Bela Lugosi as a voodoo master in Haiti who turns the living into the walking dead. The film that put zombies on the screen. The sugar mill scene still haunts.

items.title: King of the Zombies
items.description: A plane crashes on a mysterious Caribbean island where a sinister doctor keeps a very unusual workforce in his basement. Mantan Moreland steals every scene.

items.title: Fiend Without a Face
items.description: A scientist's thoughts turn into invisible brains with spinal-cord tails, and an air base is the first to find out. Arthur Crabtree directs. The wait for them to show themselves is worth it.

items.title: The Phantom Ship
items.description: The mystery of the Mary Celeste — the real ghost ship found abandoned with no crew, no explanation. Bela Lugosi is aboard and he's the least suspicious person on the vessel.

items.title: The Brain from Planet Arous
items.description: A floating brain with glowing eyes moves into John Agar and gets ideas about running Earth. 1950s sci-fi at full wild-eyed commitment, and it never once blinks.

items.title: The Wasp Woman
items.description: Susan Cabot runs a cosmetics company, and the ads are only as good as her face. The fix is wasp enzymes. Corman made it fast and cheap, and beauty counters have not changed their pitch since.

items.title: Mesa of Lost Women
items.description: A mad scientist creates giant spiders and strange women in his Mexican mesa laboratory. Jackie Coogan in his most unhinged role. The flamenco guitar score never stops.

items.title: Attack of the Monsters
items.description: Gamera versus Guiron. Two boys are transported to an alien planet with knife-headed monsters and a civilization with plans for their brains. Literally.

items.title: The Eye Creatures
items.description: Larry Buchanan's low-rent reimagining of "Invasion of the Saucer Men." Bug-eyed aliens crash-land in Texas and the local teens are the only ones who notice.

items.title: The Snow Creature
items.description: A Himalayan expedition captures a yeti and takes it home to Los Angeles, which is where the plan stops being one. A mountain legend loose in the big city, in the classic creature-feature way.

items.title: The Golem
items.description: Paul Wegener co-directs and plays the clay giant himself, in Hans Poelzig's lumpy, hand-shaped Prague. A monster movie from before monster movies had rules, and it looks like it was sculpted.

items.title: Forbidden Planet
items.description: The Tempest in space, with Walter Pidgeon, Anne Francis and Leslie Nielsen playing it straight and Robby the Robot stealing it. The score is all electronic. The monster is a state of mind.

items.id: journey-to-the-center-of-time/Journey to the Center of Time.mp4
items.title: Journey to the Center of Time
items.description: Stanton, the hard-nosed new boss, inherits a research lab, and then the lab hands him a trip through time. A late-60s cheapie that goes where the budget doesn't, and means it.

items.title: Not of This Earth
items.description: Paul Birch wears sunglasses indoors because his eyes are the problem, and he needs your blood because his planet is dying. Roger Corman keeps it moving. Skip the checkup.

items.title: Svengali
items.description: A sinister music maestro who can bend women to his will through hypnosis discovers a girl with the perfect voice. John Barrymore at his most magnetic and most menacing.

items.title: The Magnetic Monster
items.description: Richard Carlson and the Office of Scientific Investigation chase an element that eats energy and keeps growing. Curt Siodmak, who wrote Donovan's Brain, delivers the science with a straight face.

items.title: Beginning of the End
items.description: Peter Graves versus giant grasshoppers marching on Chicago. The bugs are real grasshoppers crawling over photographs of the skyline, Bert I. Gordon economy at its purest. Chicago, hold on.

items.title: The Terror
items.description: A young officer in Napoleon's army pursues a mysterious woman to an old Baron's castle. Shot on leftover sets by Corman, Coppola, and a rotating cast of directors who wandered onto the lot.

items.title: Embryo
items.description: Rock Hudson plays a scientist who accelerates fetal development to create a full-grown woman in weeks. A 1970s Frankenstein where the creation is the most dangerous thing in the room.

items.title: Evil Brain From Outer Space
items.description: A monstrous evil brain from beyond the stars commands its minions to conquer Earth. Only Starman can stop it. Japanese tokusatsu edited for American drive-ins.

items.title: The Phantom from 10,000 Leagues
items.description: Something radioactive is living off the Pacific coast, and the seaside town is the last to know. Cheap, moody and damp, the way atomic-age monster pictures were built. Keep an eye on the shoreline.

items.title: Gammera the Invincible
items.description: The only Gamera film released theatrically in America. A giant fire-breathing turtle awakened from Arctic ice heads straight for civilization. The city doesn't stand a chance.

items.title: Werewolf in a Girls' Dormitory
items.description: A new teacher with a shadowy past arrives at a reform school for girls. Then the killings start. Italian-Austrian horror with a title that tells you everything and a film that delivers more.

items.title: The Screaming Skull
items.description: A newlywed couple moves into the husband's old house. The previous wife's skull starts turning up in places skulls shouldn't be. The studio offered free burial to anyone who died of fright.

items.title: The Mighty Thor Against The Queen Of The Amazons
items.description: The Norse god tangles with the Queen of the Amazons in this Italian peplum adventure. Muscles, mythology, and swords swinging in every direction.

items.title: Monster From A Prehistoric Planet
items.description: A captured baby reptile brings its gigantic parent to Tokyo. Never steal a monster's child. The Japanese kaiju Gappa: The Triphibian Monster, repackaged for American screens.

items.title: Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster
items.description: Ghidorah arrives from space with three heads and a plan for Earth. Ishiro Honda directs, and Godzilla, Rodan and Mothra are all in it, which makes for a crowded sky.

items.title: Wolf Blood
items.description: The oldest surviving werewolf film. A logging camp foreman receives a blood transfusion from a wolf after a near-fatal injury. The nightmares start immediately. Silent and strange.

items.title: Night of the Blood Beast
items.description: The first man in space comes home, and he did not come home alone. A one-hour quickie with a bird-headed monster who arrives right on schedule. Keep the lights on.

items.title: Mutiny in Outer Space
items.description: A creeping fungus is killing off astronauts, and the ship keeps getting smaller. A 1960s American space B-picture, spore-forward and light on budget. Check your sleeves.

items.title: The Phantom Carriage
items.description: Victor Sjöström directs and stars as David Holm, a drunk who is told, on New Year's Eve, about the coachman who collects the dead. The ghosts are double exposures, and they still hold.

items.title: Bride of the Gorilla
items.description: Deep in the jungle, a plantation manager begins transforming into something primal after crossing the wrong woman. Curt Siodmak wrote Lon Chaney's Wolf Man — he knew his curses.

items.title: The Day of the Triffids
items.description: A meteor shower blinds most of humanity. Then the mobile, carnivorous plants make their move. British sci-fi adapted from John Wyndham's classic novel.

items.title: Werewolf of Washington
items.description: A political reporter gets bitten by a werewolf in Hungary and brings his condition back to Washington, D.C. Watergate-era lycanthropy satire — the beast inside the Beltway.

items.title: Vampyr
items.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer's surreal, dreamlike vampire film. More atmosphere than plot, more dread than blood. One of the most haunting things ever committed to celluloid.

items.title: Destination Moon
items.description: George Pal's rocket goes to the moon with Heinlein on the script and Chesley Bonestell painting the surface, and Woody Woodpecker explains the physics. Technicolor, and serious about it.

items.title: The She Beast
items.description: Honeymooners in Transylvania crash their car into a lake — the same lake where a witch was drowned centuries ago. She's been waiting down there. Patiently.

items.title: Grave of the Vampire
items.description: A vampire attacks a couple in a graveyard. The child born from that night grows up with a single, burning purpose: to find his father and end him.

items.title: The Atomic Man
items.description: A man pulled from a river dies briefly, then revives — answering questions seven seconds before they're asked. He's unstuck in time, and someone wants him dead for what he knows.

items.title: The Angry Red Planet
items.description: Mars is red, and the picture is redder: the Martian scenes are tinted, with creatures drawn in by a process called CineMagic. A bat-rat-spider thing greets the crew. Ib Melchior directs.

items.title: Indestructible Man
items.description: Lon Chaney Jr. is executed for his crimes, then reanimated by a mad scientist. He comes back mute, super-strong, and with a very specific list of people to visit.

items.title: Horrors of Spider Island
items.description: A dance troupe crash-lands on a deserted island. A mutant spider bite transforms their manager into something considerably less charming. The title does not lie.

items.title: Nightmare Castle
items.description: A woman and her lover are tortured to death by her sadistic husband. They make their displeasure known from the other side. Barbara Steele in Italian gothic horror.

items.id: frankenstein-meets-the-space-monster-1965-full-movie-hd/FRANKENSTEIN MEETS THE SPACE MONSTER (1965)   𝙁𝙪𝙡𝙡 𝙈𝙤𝙫𝙞𝙚 🎥 𝙃𝘿.ia.mp4
items.title: Frankenstein Meets the Spacemonster
items.description: A Martian princess raids Puerto Rico for Earth women while a shot-down android lurches around. The title promises a fight, and the picture is busier than its name. Drive-in oddity, fully committed.

items.title: Frankenstein
items.description: Victor Frankenstein discovers something ancient living in the caves near his castle and decides to experiment. Not the Frankenstein you're expecting. Far, far stranger.

items.title: Caltiki the Immortal Monster
items.description: A blob from Mayan ruins eats radioactivity and keeps growing. Riccardo Freda directs, with Mario Bava's effects and photography doing the heavy lifting. It's hungry, which is the plot.

items.title: The Vampire Bat
items.description: When villagers start dying with their blood drained, suspicion falls on bats, then on the town eccentric. The truth is stranger than either theory. Fay Wray screams again.

items.id: it-came-from-beneath-the-sea/It Came From Beneath the Sea.mp4
items.title: It Came From Beneath the Sea
items.description: Ray Harryhausen's radioactive octopus surfaces from the Philippine Trench with a taste for the Pacific Coast. The Navy has questions. The stop-motion is the answer to all of them.

items.title: Revolt of the Zombies
items.description: World War I troops discover the ancient secret of zombification in Cambodia. One man wants to weaponize it. Another wants to use it for love. From the creators of White Zombie.

items.title: Escapement
items.description: An insurance investigator pulls one thread on an electronic dream therapy clinic and finds it selling more than sleep. Also sold as The Electronic Monster. A British sci-fi thriller you rarely see.

items.title: Night Tide
items.description: A young sailor falls for a mysterious woman who performs as a mermaid at a seaside carnival. Her previous boyfriends have a habit of disappearing. Dennis Hopper before he went fully off the deep end.

items.title: Godzilla vs. Monster Zero
items.description: Aliens from Planet X ask to borrow Godzilla and Rodan, strictly as a favor. Nick Adams plays the astronaut who finds this suspicious. Ishiro Honda directs, and the favor goes about as you'd think.

items.title: Zontar the Thing From Venus
items.description: An alien intelligence convinces a scientist to help it seize control of Earth by disabling all power and technology. Larry Buchanan's Texas-budget remake of "It Conquered the World."

items.title: Cat Women of the Moon
items.description: Astronauts reach the moon and find telepathic queens in black leotards running the place. The camp grandmother of every moon-women movie since, and it keeps a straight face. Mind your thoughts.

items.title: Jesse James Meets Frankenstein's Daughter
items.description: Exactly what it sounds like. The outlaw and the mad scientist's granddaughter cross paths in the Old West. William Beaudine directed this at age 74 and didn't look back.

items.title: Prince of Space
items.description: A caped hero in a bug-eyed helmet squares off against the Phantom of Krankor. A Japanese serial cut down to one feature, so the episodes arrive in a hurry and nobody stops to explain.

items.title: YONGARY - Monster from the Deep
items.description: South Korea's answer to Godzilla. A massive reptile is awakened by nuclear testing and stomps toward Seoul. The child protagonist finds the whole thing delightful.

items.title: The Giant Gila Monster
items.description: A 70-foot lizard terrorizes a small Texas town. The local hot-rodding teens are the only ones who can stop it. Drive-in perfection — big monster, fast cars, no apologies.

items.title: Devil Girl from Mars
items.description: A leather-clad Martian and her robot land at a Scottish inn, shopping for men. British second-feature camp with Hazel Court, and the guests are about to have a very long night.

items.id: beyond-the-door-1974/Beyond the Door 1974 Trying for 1000 please subscribe.ia.mp4
items.title: Beyond The Door
items.description: A San Francisco woman's pregnancy takes a demonic turn. Italy's answer to The Exorcist, complete with levitation, possession, and ancient evil. The apartment will never feel safe again.

items.title: Teenage Zombies
items.description: Water-skiing teens stumble onto an island where a female scientist is developing a zombification agent for a foreign power. They picked the wrong island for a day trip.

items.title: THE ATOMIC SUBMARINE
items.description: A cyclops under the Arctic ice, courtesy of Spencer Gordon Bennet, a veteran of cliffhanger serials. Bob Steele, once a B-western cowboy, rides the Navy sub instead of a horse. The eye is enormous.

items.title: Dracula vs. Frankenstein
items.description: The two legendary monsters finally share the screen in Al Adamson's fever dream of a film. Lon Chaney Jr.'s final role. Nothing about this movie makes sense and that is its power.

items.title: The Neptune Factor
items.description: Ernest Borgnine and Yvette Mimieux go down in a submarine after a lost undersea lab and meet things that were not in the brochure. Seventies sea-monster adventure, with the deep taking its time.

items.title: The Time Travelers
items.description: Scientists switch on a time portal and step into a ruined future with mutants at the door. Ib Melchior directed, so expect big ideas on a small budget, and a lot of nerve.

items.title: The Monolith Monsters
items.description: Meteorite fragments that grow when wet threaten a desert town. Not alive, not dead — just expanding, crystallizing, crushing. One of the most original monster concepts of the 1950s.

items.title: The Killer Shrews
items.description: Trapped on an island during a hurricane with giant, venomous shrews. The escape plan involves oil drums and running. You'll understand when you see it.

items.title: Quatermass 2
items.description: Quatermass follows falling meteorites to a plant that is a little too secret. Val Guest directs Hammer's version of Nigel Kneale's serial, and trust in officials is in short supply.

items.title: Moon of the Wolf
items.description: A Louisiana sheriff investigates savage killings in the bayou and starts suspecting something older than any law on the books. Southern Gothic werewolf tale with swamp fog atmosphere.

items.title: Target Earth
items.description: Giant robots walk into a deserted Chicago, and the few people left have to find each other before anything else. Moody, cheap, and the empty streets do most of the work.

items.title: The Mad Monster
items.description: A disgraced scientist creates a wolf-man from his simple-minded gardener and sends him after the colleagues who laughed at his theories. Revenge is a dish best served hairy.

items.title: First Man Into Space
items.description: A test pilot touches the edge of space and comes back with a craving for blood. Tense British science fiction played straight, which suits the dread. Lock the barn door.

items.title: Creature Of Destruction
items.description: A hypnotist regresses a woman to a past life that should have stayed buried. What comes back through her isn't just a memory. Larry Buchanan's color remake of "The She Creature."

items.title: Things to Come
items.description: H. G. Wells's future history opens at Christmas in Everytown, with war coming out of the sky. The air raids reached the screen four years before the real ones. The prophecy is the scary part.

items.title: Ghost Patrol
items.description: A scientist invents a ray that can stop airplane engines mid-flight, crashing them so he can loot the wreckage. A cowboy is the only one suspicious enough to investigate.

items.title: I Eat Your Skin
items.description: Del Tenney, the man behind The Horror of Party Beach, takes his budget to a tropical island and finds zombies waiting. The sun is out, which makes it worse. Pure drive-in, and proud of it.

items.title: The Invisible Man
items.description: James Whale's masterpiece. Claude Rains unwraps his bandages and there's nothing underneath. The special effects still work. The megalomania is contagious.

items.title: The Amazing Transparent Man
items.description: A mad scientist makes a convict invisible, then sends him to steal radioactive material. Ulmer, who made Detour, directs. You can see the atomic nerves in it. The convict, not so much.

items.title: Vengence of the Zombies
items.description: Paul Naschy, Spain's king of horror, stars in this tale of voodoo revenge and satanic rituals. When the dead come back in a Naschy film, they come back angry.

items.id: the-last-man-on-earth-1964_20251031/The Last Man on Earth - 1964/The Last Man on Earth - 1964.ia.mp4
items.title: The Last Man on Earth
items.description: Vincent Price survives a plague that turned everyone else into the undead, and every sunset is a siege. The first screen version of Richard Matheson's I Am Legend, and a lonely one.

items.title: The Hideous Sun Demon
items.description: Robert Clarke stars and directs, and when the sun hits him he becomes a lizard man. A beach-town monster picture with a problem a hat can't fix. Stay in the shade.

items.title: Moon Zero Two
items.description: A salvager on a moon colony takes a job hauling in a sapphire asteroid, and Hammer trades the castle for the crater. A space western, claim jumpers and showdown included.

items.title: Beast from Haunted Cave
items.description: Criminals hiding out in a snowy cabin discover the nearby cave isn't empty. Monte Hellman's directorial debut — half heist film, half creature feature, all atmosphere.

items.title: How to Make a Monster
items.description: A studio makeup man turns actors into monsters for revenge. AIP made it as an in-joke on its own teenage-monster pictures, and the finale was shot in color. Take the hint and keep watching.

items.title: Bride of Frankenstein
items.description: The monster lives. The doctor lives. Now they'll build a mate. James Whale's sequel that surpasses the original in every dimension. The Bride's scream is cinema history.

items.title: The Brain Eaters
items.description: Parasites from the center of the Earth attach to people's necks and take control of their minds. The town doesn't notice until it's almost too late. It's never too late in these films. Almost.

items.title: Destroy All Monsters
items.description: Every Toho monster is living on Monsterland, which seems like a fine idea until someone else gets the controls. Ishiro Honda directs the biggest roll call in Godzilla's family.

items.title: Unknown World
items.description: The Prophet of Doom is certain the bomb is coming, so he builds a drill-nosed metal boxcar and heads for the center of the Earth. A publisher's son pays. Cold War anxiety, with a very large drill.

items.title: The Creeping Terror
items.description: A carpet-like alien creature slowly absorbs the citizens of a small town. The "monster" is literally someone under a rug. Legendary in its awfulness. Essential viewing for connoisseurs of the terrible.

items.title: The Green Slime
items.description: Astronauts blow up an asteroid, bring back a souvenir, and the space station fills with tentacled green things. Kinji Fukasaku, later of Battle Royale, directs. The colors are as loud as the monsters.

items.title: Diary of a Madman
items.description: Vincent Price is a French magistrate haunted by the Horla, Maupassant's invisible thing, which talks from the far side of mirrors. Price has to act opposite nothing. He is good at it.

items.title: Bloody Pit of Horror
items.description: A photographer stumbles into a castle where a former executioner now uses his tools on anyone who trespasses. Italian horror that means every drop of its title.

items.title: The Naked Witch
items.description: A witch's grave in a small Texas town. Someone opens it. Someone always opens it. What crawls out has been waiting since the 1700s.

items.title: The Shadow of the Cat
items.description: Two servants kill their mistress on her husband's orders. The only witness is her cat, and it holds a grudge. Hammer gives it a whole mansion to stalk through. Mind the shadows.

items.title: The Long Hair of Death
items.description: A village burns a woman as a witch because the lord wanted her, and calls it justice. Barbara Steele is in the castle, so the matter is not closed. Italian gothic, candle-low, no relief.

items.title: The Phantom of the Opera
items.description: Beneath the Paris Opera House, a disfigured genius lives in darkness and silence — except for the music. Lon Chaney's iconic silent performance in the role that defined horror romance.

items.title: The Last Man on Earth
items.description: He stakes the sleepers by day and barricades the door by dusk. Vincent Price, alone, while the neighbors know his name and call it, nightly. Sleep is the one thing he cannot afford.

items.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
items.description: Conrad Veidt plays Cesare the sleepwalker, and the sets are painted at wrong angles on purpose. Nothing in the frame stands straight. Turn the lights down and see if your room agrees.

items.title: The Frozen Ghost
items.description: Lon Chaney Jr. plays a stage mentalist who is sure his stare killed a heckler, and the wax museum he walks into does not help. An Inner Sanctum mystery from Universal: low, moody, properly uneasy.

items.title: Horror Express
items.description: Something ancient is locked in a crate on the Trans-Siberian Express. When it gets out, it absorbs the knowledge and memories of everyone it kills. Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing trapped on a train with no stops.

items.title: Carnival of Souls
items.description: She walked out of the river after the accident, but something in her changed. The abandoned carnival pavilion calls to her. The figures inside are waiting. Herk Harvey's only film — one was enough.

items.title: The Man They Could Not Hang
items.description: Boris Karloff is wrongly hanged, brought back by his assistant, and has the jury over to the house. None of them leave the way they came. A Columbia chiller with real menace.

items.title: Naked Massacre
items.description: Based on the real Richard Speck murders. Eight student nurses. One intruder. No mercy. This one doesn't flinch from the horror of what actually happened.

items.title: Black Sunday
items.description: Barbara Steele plays a witch and the girl who looks exactly like her, which is the whole problem. Mario Bava's black-and-white nightmare opens with a mask, and the mask is not a metaphor.

items.title: The City of the Dead
items.description: A student travels to a fog-choked village to study witchcraft. The village burned a witch 300 years ago. The village hasn't changed since. Christopher Lee knows why.

items.title: Night of the Living Dead
items.description: They're coming to get you, Barbara. Romero locked the dead outside and the living inside and watched what happened. The most important horror film ever made.

items.title: Isle of the Dead
items.description: Val Lewton's plague picture, directed by Mark Robson. Karloff's Greek general seals an island in quarantine, and the whispers about a vrykolakas begin. Lewton never shows more than he must; that's the trick.

items.title: The Most Dangerous Game
items.description: A shipwrecked man finds a host who hunts the most dangerous game. You already know what that is. Pre-Code, pre-censorship — the hunt is real.

items.title: End of the World
items.description: Signals from space line up with disasters across the globe. A scientist and his wife follow them to a remote convent. Christopher Lee is inside. The signals were addressed to someone there.

items.title: The Satanic Rites of Dracula
items.description: Peter Cushing's Van Helsing works with Scotland Yard now, and the cult he is tracking wants the world ended. Dracula in 1970s London: Hammer's last go at Lee in the cape.

items.title: House on Haunted Hill
items.description: Vincent Price. A haunted mansion. A locked door experiment with a $10,000 prize. The ghosts don't care about the money. They just want you to stay.

items.title: Waxworks
items.description: A wax museum hires a writer to give its figures stories, and Conrad Veidt and Emil Jannings turn up inside them. Paul Leni's silent nightmare, built on sets that lean like bad dreams.

items.title: First Spaceship on Venus
items.description: An international crew lands on Venus and discovers the ruins of a dead civilization — and the thing that killed it. East German-Polish sci-fi that plays its cosmic horror straight.

items.title: Tormented
items.description: Bert I. Gordon, the giant-bug man, makes a ghost story: a past love who will not stay gone, and a wedding she means to disrupt. The groom is the only one who knows why.

items.title: Deep Red
items.description: Dario Argento's giallo masterpiece. A musician witnesses a murder through a window and becomes obsessed with solving it. Every answer leads to something worse. The kills are operatic.

items.title: The Rogue's Tavern
items.description: Travelers take shelter in a roadside tavern. Then the doors lock. Then people start dying. A locked-room mystery where the room itself might be the killer.

items.title: How Awful About Allan
items.description: A man goes blind after a traumatic incident and is cared for by his possessive sister. But he can hear things in the house. Things that move when they shouldn't. Aaron Spelling produced this TV horror.

items.title: Driller Killer
items.description: Abel Ferrara's grimy, unflinching descent into madness. A struggling artist in a decaying New York apartment begins killing the people around him. Is it real? Does it matter? The city eats everyone eventually.

items.title: Satan's Cheerleaders
items.description: Cheerleaders on a road trip cross paths with a satanic cult in a small town. The pom-poms won't save them. 1970s drive-in horror with more occult menace than the title suggests.

items.title: The Sadist
items.description: Based on the real Riverside murders. Three people held hostage by a thrill-killer in a junkyard. No supernatural element. Just a man, his gun, and the desert heat. The horror is entirely human.

items.title: Svengali
