items.description: A sinister music maestro bends women to his will through hypnosis. John Barrymore disappears completely into the role — charming, terrifying, pathetic, and monstrous in the same breath.

items.title: The Corpse Vanishes
items.description: Young brides are vanishing from their bridal beds. Bela Lugosi needs them — not alive, not dead, but something in between. The orchids in his greenhouse require very specific nutrients.

items.title: The Terror
items.description: A Napoleonic officer follows a phantom woman to a crumbling castle. What he discovers inside makes no sense. It was never meant to. Corman, Coppola, and three other directors tried to finish this film.

items.title: The Horrible Dr. Hichcock
items.description: Barbara Steele marries a London surgeon with a dead first wife and a very particular hobby. Italian Gothic, fog by the yard, lurid the way the genre intended. Lock the bedroom door.

items.title: Dracula Prince of Darkness
items.description: Christopher Lee returns as Dracula and never says a word, which is the right call. Four English tourists ignore the warnings and take shelter in his castle. Hammer at its most patient.

items.title: This Is Not a Test
items.description: A civil defense drill becomes real when nuclear missiles launch. A deputy blocks a bridge and forces the motorists to stay. The fallout is coming. The people in the cars are already turning on each other.

items.title: Pulse
items.description: Technology turns against its users as ghostly signals begin bleeding through screens and phone lines. The dead have found a new way in, and every device in your home is a doorway.

items.title: Last Woman on Earth
items.description: Three survivors of nuclear apocalypse on a tropical island. One woman. Two men. Roger Corman strips civilization down to its worst impulses and watches what happens.

items.title: The Screaming Skull
items.description: A newlywed couple moves into his dead wife's house. The skull keeps appearing — in the garden, on the doorstep, at the foot of the bed. The studio promised a free coffin to anyone who died of fright.

items.title: The Unknown
items.description: Lon Chaney is a circus knife-thrower with no arms, which is the least troubling thing about him. Tod Browning's carnival is grotesque, obsessive, and in no hurry to let anyone leave.

items.title: The Last Warning
items.description: Paul Leni, of The Cat and the Canary, puts a dead actor's ghost in a Broadway theatre and a stage full of people who should have stayed home. Silent, with a dark old house and sinister stagecraft.

items.id: sweeney-todd-the-demon-barber-of-fleet-street-1936/Sweeney Todd The Demon Barber of Fleet Street 1936.ia.mp4
items.title: Sweeney Todd
items.description: Tod Slaughter came to the pictures from stage melodrama and never stopped playing to the gallery. Decades before Sondheim, this is the barber and the pie shop at full theatrical volume.

items.title: The Phantom Carriage
items.description: Victor Sjöström directs and stars as David Holm, a drunk who is told, on New Year's Eve, about the coachman who collects the dead. The ghosts are double exposures, and they still hold.

items.title: Shock
items.description: A woman at a hotel window sees a man kill his wife, and her mind shuts down. The psychiatrist they send for is Vincent Price. He is the man she saw. The only witness is now his patient.

items.title: Vampyr
items.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer's surreal vampire film moves like a waking dream through fog and shadow. Less story than sensation. The burial-alive sequence will make you forget to breathe.

items.title: Dead People
items.description: The dead walk among the living, and no one can tell the difference until it's too late. A town where the boundary between worlds has simply dissolved.

items.title: The World Gone Mad
items.description: The Depression was current events when this thriller was made, and it puts the villains in boardrooms. Pat O'Brien leads. Nothing supernatural here, which is the problem.

items.title: The Devil's Daughter
items.description: A woman from Harlem inherits a Jamaican banana plantation. The half-sister who ran it has vanished. Nina Mae McKinney plays her. The drums keep getting louder. Somebody is playing them.

items.title: Nightmare Castle
items.description: A woman and her lover are tortured to death by her husband. They come back wrong. Barbara Steele in Italian gothic horror — the castle is a tomb and everyone in it knows it.

items.title: A Bucket of Blood
items.description: Walter Paisley wants to be an artist, and a dead cat is where it starts. Roger Corman's beatnik cafe, with Dick Miller at its center. The applause is the dangerous part.

items.title: The Vampire Bat
items.description: Villagers are drained of blood. Suspicion falls on bats, then on the town eccentric. The real answer is scientific — and worse. Fay Wray, Lionel Atwill, and Melvyn Douglas in pre-Code horror.

items.title: Trauma
items.description: Psychological horror about a woman's breakdown after a traumatic event. The terror is internal, relentless, and offers no escape because the threat lives inside her own mind.

items.title: Mill of the Stone Women
items.description: A young man comes to research a Dutch sculptor's windmill of lifelike women, and women keep going missing. Italian-French Gothic, dubbed and dream-like. The statues are the best-looking cast.

items.id: beyond-the-door-1974/Beyond the Door 1974 Trying for 1000 please subscribe.ia.mp4
items.title: Beyond the Door
items.description: A pregnant woman in San Francisco begins speaking in voices that aren't hers. Italy's answer to The Exorcist. The entity inside her has waited centuries and it's not leaving without the child.

items.title: The Bat Whispers
items.description: Roland West remade his own silent The Bat with sound: a caped killer, a haunted mansion, and miniature shots that still hold up. The dread is early-talkie, slow and very sure of itself.

items.id: the-man-who-turned-to-stone.-1957/The Man Who Turned to Stone (1957)/mp4/The Man Who Turned to Stone.1957.ia.mp4
items.title: The Man Who Turned to Stone
items.description: Girls at a detention home keep dying of heart failure, and the doctors who run the place have been alive a very long time. Victor Jory heads a staff with a secret for staying young and a basement for keeping it.

items.title: Tower of London
items.description: Vincent Price as Richard III murders his way to the throne, and Roger Corman makes sure the dead come back to complain. Black and white, Gothic, and Price enjoys every betrayal.

items.title: Messiah of Evil
items.description: Something is wrong with the town of Point Dune. The meat counter has changed. The people have changed. They gather at the edge of the water and wait. Willard Huyck's coastal nightmare is unshakeable.

items.title: The Man With Nine Lives
items.description: Boris Karloff is the doctor found frozen in a sealed cabin, who thaws out and goes straight back to his experiments. A real professor's dog-revival headlines inspired it. Icebound and eerie.

items.title: The Monolith Monsters
items.description: Meteorite fragments that grow when wet threaten a desert town. Not alive, not dead — just expanding, crystallizing, crushing everything underneath. One of the most original threats in 1950s horror.

items.title: Hands of the Ripper
items.description: Eric Porter's psychiatrist is sure he can cure the Ripper's daughter. Every scene after that is the argument against him. Hammer in a Victorian parlour, where the tea is the safest thing.

items.title: Moon of the Wolf
items.description: A Louisiana sheriff investigates savage killings in the bayou and begins to suspect something ancient and lunar is responsible. David Janssen in Southern Gothic werewolf terror.

items.title: The Woman in Green
items.description: Sherlock Holmes investigates a series of murders where the victims are all found with a single, impossible mark. Basil Rathbone as Holmes versus a killer whose method defies rational explanation.

items.title: Jennifer
items.description: A supernatural revenge tale where the instrument of vengeance is a young woman who doesn't know what she is. The snakes know. The cats know. Jennifer is the last to understand.

items.title: The Black Castle
items.description: Karloff and Lon Chaney Jr. lurk in an Austrian count's castle, where a man has come looking for his missing friends. Swordplay, torture chambers, a crocodile pit. Decline the tour.

items.title: Vengeance of the Zombies
items.description: Paul Naschy, Spain's king of horror, calls the dead back from their graves. They return with voodoo rage and satanic purpose. When Naschy raises the dead, they come back angry.

items.title: Ghosts of Hanley House
items.description: A group of strangers spends the night in a house where people have died before. The doors close by themselves. The shadows move on their own. The dead want to show the living something.

items.title: Captain Kronos Vampire Hunter
items.description: Brian Clemens, of The Avengers, wrote and directed it: a swordsman, a hunchback, and vampires who take youth instead of blood. The village ages by the week. Hammer tried something new.

items.title: Daughter of Horror
items.description: A woman wanders through a nightmarish city of grotesque faces and inescapable dread. Expressionist horror told without dialogue, only jazz and screaming. Dementia in its purest form.

items.id: dementia-13-1963-horror-full-movie-francis-ford-coppola/Dementia 13 (1963)   Horror   Full Movie   Francis Ford Coppola.ia.mp4
items.title: Dementia 13
items.description: An early Francis Ford Coppola, made for Roger Corman: an Irish castle, a family in mourning and an axe. The shoestring shows, and so does a director learning fast. Sleep somewhere else.

items.title: Tomorrow's Children
items.description: A young woman, a welfare board and a sterilization order. No monster, only paperwork. It was sold as a warning, and censors fought it anyway. Dread with a rubber stamp.

items.title: Midnight Manhunt
items.description: A corpse goes missing from the morgue and the hunt through midnight streets and back alleys reveals that multiple parties want the body — and some of them aren't alive.

items.title: The Lost Missile
items.description: A nuclear missile goes off-course and orbits the Earth, generating a heat beam that incinerates everything below its path. The clock is ticking and the science to stop it doesn't exist yet.

items.title: The Bat
items.description: Agnes Moorehead rents a house with a killer's reputation, and the killer wears a bat's face and a claw. Vincent Price is the neighborhood doctor, so trust no one. Check the windows twice.

items.title: Before I Hang
items.description: Karloff is a doctor condemned for a mercy killing, and the youth serum he tests on himself works a little too well. The monster here has a conscience, which is worse.

items.title: The Penalty
items.description: Chaney strapped his legs up behind him to play a man with none. Wallace Worsley directed; the two reunited for The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: So Sad About Gloria
items.description: Elvira keeps the red couch at KHJ-TV, the Los Angeles station where Movie Macabre began, and spends the breaks on the phone or stretched out. "Tonight, we're doing something fun and different here on the show."

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: Horror of Death
items.description: Elvira is hosting from the red couch, and she has notes on the title: "The horror of death. How is that for a scary sound and title, huh?" The original ad breaks are still in, Sprite and KFC included.

items.id: ElviraThrillerVideoTheTurnOfTheScrew1974/Elvira - ThrillerVideo - The Turn of the Screw 1974.mp4
items.title: Elvira's ThrillerVideo: The Turn of the Screw
items.description: Candles, crossed swords and a hostess who admits "In this outfit, I'm kinda hard to miss." The film first aired on ABC in two parts, with Lynn Redgrave.

items.title: MonsterVision: Friday the 13th
items.description: Joe Bob Briggs vows to run as many of the series as the night allows, starting at the start. Camp Crystal Lake, a young Kevin Bacon, and a hockey mask that has not been invented yet.

items.id: joe-bob-briggs-presents-the-dev-ills-reign-with-commercials/Joe Bob Briggs presents The Dev Ills Reign (with commercials!).mp4
items.title: MonsterVision: The Devil's Rain
items.description: Joe Bob Briggs on a trailer porch with a cooler, billing a 1975 picture with Shatner, Borgnine and Travolta as "the first movie to feature disintegrating face goo special effects." We believe him.

items.id: hell-comes-to-frogtown-usa-up-all-night/Hell Comes To Frogtown USA Up All Night.ia.mp4
items.title: USA Up All Night: Hell Comes to Frogtown
items.description: Gilbert Gottfried in a smoking jacket in the back of a limousine, introducing "Rowdy Roddy Piper as a post-nuclear Johnny Appleseed." USA ran this sort of thing until five in the morning. The 900 number ads are still in it, as a courtesy.

items.title: Commander USA: Blood Song
items.description: Commander USA adds green to the red, white and blue for St. Patrick's Day, with a saint chasing moles out of Poland. The slasher has Frankie Avalon, a long way from the beach party.

items.title: Svengoolie: How to Make a Monster
items.description: Svengoolie reruns his 2020 episode with a new opening where he talks about it. Commercials removed. The 1958 picture is set in a studio make-up room, and a Fractured Flickers silent reel follows.

items.title: Big Chuck and Lil John: The Brain That Wouldn't Die
items.description: Big Chuck and Lil John pay tribute to Ghoulardi, who at his peak owned 70 percent of Cleveland's late night audience, with his old skits dropped in. The movie is the one about a head in a pan.

items.title: Sammy Terry: Tower of London
items.description: Sammy Terry, caped and masked, haunts WTTV 4 in Indianapolis and brings Vincent Price to a castle with a great many bad dinners. "In the dead of night, when the moon is high and the ill winds blow."

items.title: Penny Dreadfuls' Shilling Shockers: Warning From Space
items.description: Penny Dreadful's attic show started on public access in Providence and Boston and reached over 200 New England towns. The film is a dubbed Japanese saucer picture, its aliens one eyed starfish.

items.title: Monster Madhouse: Grave of the Vampire
items.description: Karlos Borloff, Lizardman and a clown take over a basement set at full volume, callers and music video filler included. The 1972 vampire picture was written by David Chase, years before The Sopranos.

items.title: MonsterVision: Christine
items.description: On his patio set, Joe Bob Briggs tallies the Drive In Totals, three pints of blood and one motor vehicle chase. John Carpenter's jealous 1958 Plymouth, from the Stephen King novel, does the rest.

items.title: Count Gore De Vol's Creature Feature: The Ape
items.description: Count Gore De Vol held down Washington and Baltimore Saturday nights for fourteen years, and the cobwebs show it. Monogram's Boris Karloff programmer, with an ape loose near a circus.

items.title: Crematia Mortem's Creature Feature: Scars of Dracula
items.description: Crematia Mortem, the Ghostess with the Mostess, held down Kansas City's Creature Feature from 1981 to 1990. Hammer's 1970 Christopher Lee vampire picture gets the wicker chair treatment.

items.id: h-bc-scared-to-death/1976 Jun 25, Scared to Death SD.ia.mp4
items.title: The Hoolihan and Big Chuck Show: Scared to Death
items.description: The oldest known Hoolihan and Big Chuck Show fills its breaks with dogs, sketches and a tribute to King the Wonder Dog. The movie is Bela Lugosi's only starring role in color, narrated by a corpse.

items.title: Saturday Fright Special: Mesa of Lost Women
items.description: A werewolf in a top hat deals out a Crypto Quiz, Scarewolf's Travel Tips and trailers between reels. The movie is a famously baffling desert picture with Jackie Coogan.

items.title: Zacherley: Moon of the Wolf
items.description: Zacherley returns to Philadelphia's WCAU, gray faced behind doll heads and bones, promising a Karloff cocktail to grow hair. The movie is a 1972 sheriff and werewolf mystery with David Janssen.

items.title: The Ghoul Show: Frankenstein's Daughter
items.description: "I make magical pumpkins," says The Ghoul, carving one between reels in an orange wig and dark glasses. Someone rebuilt a Cleveland and Detroit Halloween night, ads and ident included.

items.title: Beware Theater: Creature from the Haunted Sea
items.description: Arachna of the Spider People and Deadly, a talking skeleton, promise really bad movies and deliver. Roger Corman's Cuban revolution comedy has a mostly imaginary monster. The pie fight is a bonus.

items.id: monster-movie-night-the-giant-gila-monster/monster movie night The giant gila monster.ia.mp4
items.title: Monster Movie Night: The Giant Gila Monster
items.description: Bobby Gammonster and a vulture puppet named Boris T. Buzzard turn Gargoyle Manor into a backyard drive in. The feature is an oversized lizard picture produced by Gunsmoke's Ken Curtis.

items.title: Dark Vault of Public Domain: Attack of the Monsters
items.description: A fez, a smoking jacket, a test pattern and Japanese music videos set the table. Then Gamera, the giant turtle, fights a knife headed monster as two boys fly a saucer into trouble.

items.title: Bordello of Horror: Night Tide
items.description: The Bordello of Horror crew gathers at a purple card table, a green-haired host with a cross among them, and interrupts Dennis Hopper's sailor-and-mermaid picture nine times. The last one comes in a pink feather boa.

items.title: Meet Cleaver Theatre: I Bury the Living
items.description: Butch R. Cleaver hosts from a Cincinnati armchair with a dummy head, and tonight's villain is Enya, by way of a twelve CD box set. The film is Richard Boone and a cemetery map where the pins kill.

items.id: DrDreckJesseJamesMeetsFrankensteinsDaughter/Dr Dreck Jesse James Meets Frankensteins Daughter.mp4
items.title: Dr. Dreck: Jesse James Meets Frankenstein's Daughter
items.description: Dr. Dreck and Moaner run a drive in where the speaker warning assumes you are an idiot. William Beaudine's 1966 western puts a famous outlaw in a mad doctor's laboratory.

items.id: wolfman-macs-chiller-drive-in-werewolf-in-a-girls-dormitory-7-z-5-dtq-4-ysso/Wolfman Mac's Chiller Drive-In_ Werewolf in a Girls' Dormitory-7Z5Dtq4Ysso.mp4
items.title: Wolfman Mac's Chiller Drive-In: Werewolf in a Girls' Dormitory
items.description: Wolfman Mac, a werewolf in denim with a skeleton sidekick, runs a drive in on My TV stations. The movie is an Italian girls' school murder mystery where the wolves take the blame.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: Human Duplicators
items.description: Elvira opens by sorting film cans and fretting over a thin inventory, and Barbara Billingsley, June Cleaver herself, drops by at the close. Richard Kiel towers through a 1965 sci fi picture.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: Scream Baby Scream
items.description: In the last break Elvira shows off drawings of herself and admits she wore far more makeup back then. The movie is a horror picture set in an art class, a fine place for a bad portrait.

items.title: MonsterVision: Child's Play
items.description: Longhorns overhead, Joe Bob Briggs calls this one halfway decent, then admits he is exaggerating. Brad Dourif voices the killer doll Chucky, and the Drive In Totals close the night.

items.id: CommanderUSASimonKingOfTheWitches/Commander USA - Simon King of the Witches.mp4
items.title: Commander USA's Groovie Movies: Simon King of the Witches
items.description: Commander USA is a wacky, slightly seedy blue collar superhero broadcasting from beneath a New Jersey mall. The picture is a 1971 occult oddity with Andrew Prine as a warlock in a storm drain.

items.id: horror-incorporated-august-18-2001-teenagers-from-outer-space-woc/Horror Incorporated August 18 2001  Teenagers From Outer Space WOC.ia.mp4
items.title: Horror Incorporated: Teenagers from Outer Space
items.description: Jake Esau plays Count Dracula, eternal moon child of the night, on Minneapolis TV, local ads and station promos intact. The picture is cheap invaders from space in a small town, plus a giant lobster.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: The Godsend
items.description: Elvira by way of Honolulu, mail order stereo speaker ads and all. The movie is a British evil child chiller, where a stranger leaves a family something it never asked for.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: Yeti
items.description: Elvira presents a picture about a very large yeti and the expedition that finds him, and warns us a close friend is waiting to come on the show. "Well, it looks like I've really gone and done it this time." No ad breaks in this copy.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: The Great Alligator
items.description: Bongos out, jungle in, Elvira milking the word great for all it is worth, around a 1979 Italian picture with Barbara Bach and a very large reptile.

items.title: Elvira's Movie Macabre: Pigs
items.description: Elvira, on a red velvet seat in her candlelit set, presents a 1972 country picture she calls Pig and blames on her boss at the station. Early on she has a bit about tacks in her shoe. "Who put the brass tacks on my shoe?"

items.title: MonsterVision: The Lost Boys
items.description: Joe Bob Briggs holds court on TNT ahead of Joel Schumacher's boardwalk vampires. Kiefer Sutherland leads the pack, and the two Coreys are the kids who notice.

items.title: Son of Svengoolie: Frankenstein
items.description: Son of Svengoolie opens his summer special at the piano with Doug Graves, singing about a Chicago summer. Then comes James Whale's 1931 original with Boris Karloff, and a Chevy dealer in the breaks.

items.title: Son of Svengoolie: Supersonic Man
items.description: Rich Koz hosts the last Son of Svengoolie on Chicago's WFLD, running the sketches viewers asked for. The movie is a cheerfully cheap Spanish superhero romp, a fine way to leave.

items.id: ghoulshow19831029markofthevampire/Ghoul Show - 1983-10-29 - Mark of the Vampire.mp4
items.title: The Ghoul Show: Mark of the Vampire
items.description: The Ghoul runs the night from the Hudson Haunted House in northeast Ohio, with a Bela Lugosi vampire picture to introduce and a crowd leaning on the fence. "Hey, how many here like Twinkies?" No commercials in this copy.

items.id: the-ghoul-show-the-corpse-vanishes/The Ghoul Show - The Corpse Vanishes.ia.mp4
items.title: The Ghoul Show: The Corpse Vanishes
items.description: The Ghoul, in a lab coat covered with buttons and a frog puppet for help, hosts from Cleveland's WB55. Bela Lugosi snatches brides to keep his wife young, in a Monogram quickie.

items.id: 1983-june-17-and-now-the-screaming-starts/1983 June 17 - And Now the Screaming Starts.ia.mp4
items.title: Big Chuck and Lil John: And Now the Screaming Starts
items.description: Big Chuck and Lil John fill the commercial breaks with their own sketches and sign off in nightshirts. The picture is Amicus gothic with Peter Cushing, Herbert Lom and a severed hand.

items.title: Big Chuck and Lil John: The Mummy
items.description: Big Chuck and Lil John break in with a trivia quiz and a promised pizza fight, local Cleveland ads and all. Peter Cushing and Christopher Lee carry the Hammer film, Egypt first and then England.

items.id: SammyTerryAnniversarySpecial1972GhostOfFrankenstein/Sammy Terry - Anniversary Special 1972 - Ghost Of Frankenstein.mp4
items.title: Sammy Terry: The Ghost of Frankenstein
items.description: Sammy Terry's 1972 anniversary show on WTTV Indianapolis: a birthday cake, dancers, a high school band and a birthday greeting from "Vincent Price", wrapped around The Ghost of Frankenstein (1942), with Lon Chaney Jr. as the Monster.

items.title: Sammy Terry: The Curse of Frankenstein
items.description: Sammy Terry, a pun on cemetery, rose from his coffin on Indianapolis TV from 1962 on. Hammer's color shocker with Peter Cushing and Christopher Lee gets the green faced blessing.

items.title: Off Beat Cinema: Zontar, the Thing from Venus
items.description: Three hosts in sunglasses and berets, a couch in Buffalo and a stack of viewer mail. The film is Larry Buchanan's cut price remake of a Corman monster movie, which is the right kind of bad.

items.title: Commander USA: The Alligator People
items.description: Commander USA, with a puppet on his arm, throws the first annual Halloween special on USA Network. The movie is a 1959 swamp picture with Beverly Garland and Lon Chaney Jr.

items.title: Big Chuck and Lil John: Frankenstein Must Be Destroyed
items.description: Big Chuck and Lil John at their desk, cutting a Frankenstein picture with sketches, one of them a visit from the tax man. A home recording gone blue and purple, and the breaks are the main event.

items.title: Zacherley: Gorilla at Large
items.description: Zacherley, the Cool Ghoul, keeps a coffin, a punch bowl and a gorilla in 3D glasses for company. The film is a 1954 carnival murder mystery shot in 3D, with Anne Bancroft and Raymond Burr.

items.title: Suspense Theatre: A Howling in the Woods
items.description: Nashville's Count of Five, Bob McGehee in a tuxedo, hosts a 1971 NBC movie that puts Barbara Eden and Larry Hagman together a year after I Dream of Jeannie ended. Some host breaks are cut; the commercials stay.

items.id: chiller-theater-finale-the-wolf-man-full-and-partial-it-came-from-outer-space/chiller theater Finale The Wolf Man Full and Partial It Came From Outer Space.mp4
items.title: Chilly Billy's Chiller Theater: The Wolf Man
items.description: Chilly Billy Cardille closes twenty years of Pittsburgh's Chiller Theater in a tuxedo, with cake and the clips he saved. Lon Chaney Jr. howls, then a spaceship crashes and the tape gives out.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1936) — Restored & Colorized
items.description: Buster Crabbe had an Olympic swimming medal before he ever boarded Dr. Zarkov's rocket. Universal gave this serial an unusually big budget, and most of it seems to have gone into Ming's throne room.

items.id: 1938-06-14-flash-gordons-trip-to-mars-chapter-13-the-miracle-of-magic-1938_202510/1936-04-06 - Flash Gordon Chapter 1 The Planet of Peril (1936).mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon's Trip to Mars — Chapter 13: The Miracle of Magic
items.description: Deep in the second serial, with Earth still dying under the Nitron lamp and Queen Azura still throwing magic around like it's science. By Chapter 13 the cliffhangers are pure muscle memory — and they still work.

items.title: Flash Gordon's Trip to Mars (1938) — The Complete Serial, Colorized
items.description: The second Flash Gordon serial sends Flash, Dale and Zarkov to Mars to stop a Nitron ray draining Earth's atmosphere, with Clay People, a magic queen and rockets held together by sparks and faith.

items.title: Buck Rogers (1939) — The Complete Serial
items.description: Buster Crabbe again — Universal's one and only spaceman — waking from 500 years of suspended animation into a world run by the gangster Killer Kane. All 12 chapters, each ending with Buck in some fresh doom he'll shrug off next reel.

items.title: Buck Rogers (1939) — Colorized Serial Feature
items.description: The full 12-chapter serial stitched into one feature and run through AI colorization: Buck and Buddy Wade thaw out after five centuries and join Wilma Deering's rebels against Killer Kane. The Nirvano gas did its job; now it's Buck's turn.

items.title: Planet Outlaws (1953)
items.description: The 1939 Buck Rogers serial recut into a single feature and reissued for the atomic age. Same Buster Crabbe, same Killer Kane, same wire-hung rockets — now with fourteen years of trimming and a new title card.

items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers (1949)
items.description: Live on DuMont, on a prop budget that was famously tiny, and nearly all of it is lost; this is one of the survivors. A missed cue is not a flaw in the tape, it is live TV defending the galaxy.

items.title: Captain Video — Misc Episode No. 2 (c. 1950)
items.description: Over a thousand episodes of Captain Video went out live on DuMont. Roughly two dozen survive, and this is one of them — Richard Coogan holding the line against the evil Dr. Pauli five nights a week.

items.title: Captain Video (1951) — Colorized Cliffhanger Serial
items.description: Columbia's theatrical spin-off of the TV show: Judd Holdren's Captain Video versus Vultura of the planet Atoma and a traitorous scientist, Dr. Tobor. Spell that last one backwards and you'll know what kind of serial this is.

items.id: space-patrol-s-01e-01-low-480x-360p/Space Patrol S05e02 Web of Arachna.ia.mp4
items.title: Space Patrol (1950)
items.description: Buzz Corry and Cadet Happy of the United Planets keep the 30th century safe, live on ABC and paid for by Ralston cereal. The merchandise was a business of its own, and the show was its best commercial.

items.title: Space Patrol — The Space Patrol Code Belt (1951)
items.description: The episode is named for the show's own Code Belt, and the original Wheat Chex and Rice Chex spots are left in, so the line between show, sponsor and merchandise is as blurry as it was on air.

items.title: Space Patrol — Threat of the Thormanoids (1952)
items.description: Aired live in May 1952, featuring a young Lee Van Cleef as one of the invading Thormanoids. Yes — the squinting gunfighter from the spaghetti westerns started out menacing a man named Cadet Happy.

items.id: tom-corbett-mercurian-invasion/01 First Day at the Space Academy.mp4
items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — The Mercurian Invasion (1950)
items.description: The first Tom Corbett storyline: Solar Guard cadets, the rocket cruiser Polaris, and trouble from Mercury, aired three times a week on CBS in October 1950. Several chapters are lost — what survives is here.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Condensed Serials (1951)
items.description: Five storylines from the Space Academy, condensed: Martian revolts, training runs, and the endless project of turning teenagers into Solar Guardsmen. Homework, but in space, and somehow gripping.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Runaway Rocket (1954)
items.description: The final episode on DuMont before Tom jumped to NBC — making Tom Corbett one of the only shows ever broadcast on all four major networks. Everyone wanted the space cadet. This is the runaway rocket he left on.

items.title: Rocky Jones, Space Ranger — Beyond the Curtain of Space (1954)
items.description: Rocky's first three-chapter adventure, later re-edited into the TV feature 'Beyond the Moon.' Unlike its live rivals, Rocky Jones was actually shot on film — which is why it survives looking this good.

items.title: Rocky Jones, Space Ranger — Rocky's Odyssey (1954)
items.description: Three chapters of Richard Crane doing clean-cut space-police work aboard the Orbit Jet, later recut into the feature 'Gypsy Moon.' Every Rocky Jones story came in threes, like a very wholesome epic poem.

items.id: rocky-jones-space-rangers-1954-s-01e-01-beyond-the-curtain-of-space-chap-1-low-360p-1/Rocky Jones, Space Rangers 1954 S01e20 Kips Private War [low, 360p]-20.mp4
items.title: Rocky Jones, Space Ranger — Beyond the Curtain of Space, Chapter 1 (1954)
items.description: Rocky Jones was filmed while other space shows mostly went out live, which is why it survives. Square-jawed, upright rocket, the United Worlds in good hands.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe (1940)
items.description: The third and final Buster Crabbe serial: Ming spreads a plague called the Purple Death, and Flash returns to Mongo to end this thing for good. For real this time. Probably.

items.title: Flash Gordon — Akim the Terrible (1954)
items.description: Flash works for the Galactic Bureau of Investigation, and King Akim has brainwashed one of its agents into an assassination attempt. The galaxy was shot in West Berlin. Total commitment.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Breath of Death (1954)
items.description: Dale gets sent to a prison planet to fix its oxygen machinery, which goes exactly as well as sending Dale to a prison planet ever goes. An escaped prisoner, a hijacked spaceship, and 25 minutes to sort it all out.

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Vegas in Space (1979)
items.description: Cesar Romero, TV's Joker, and Joseph Wiseman, the first Dr. No, both turn up in a casino in space. Vegas but in space was a full episode premise then, and the disco-era Buck commits to it.

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century (1979) — Pilot
items.description: NBC's Star Wars-era Buck Rogers opened with a pilot that played movie theaters first. Gil Gerard's Buck thaws out into the 25th century with a robot sidekick who says 'bidi-bidi-bidi.'

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century (1979)
items.description: The feature-length pilot: astronaut Buck Rogers comes out of 500 years of suspended animation into a post-nuclear Earth with alien invaders at the door. Same premise as 1939, updated with disco and a much bigger effects budget.

items.title: Captain Video — Misc Episode No. 5 (1952)
items.description: Al Hodge as the Captain and Don Hastings as the Video Ranger, live on DuMont, chasing the escaped villains Chauncy Everett and Horace across the galaxy. One of the handful of surviving episodes of a show that aired more than a thousand.

items.title: Captain Video — Misc Episode No. 5 (1952, Alternate Transfer)
items.description: Another transfer of the same surviving 1952 broadcast — because when only two dozen episodes of a thousand-episode show exist, you keep every copy. This is the series that put the word 'video' into American living rooms.

items.id: captain-video-and-his-video-rangers-episode-2-of-4-mkv/Captain Video and His Video Rangers - V01E02.mp4
items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: Second of a four-episode surviving run from TV's first science fiction series, broadcast live on DuMont. Every scratch on this kinescope is doing preservation work.

items.title: Space Patrol — Operation Rescue (1953)
items.description: Buzz Corry and Cadet Happy mount a rescue, live on ABC in February 1953, original commercials intact. The commercials are for cereal. The commercials were always for cereal.

items.title: Space Patrol — The Laughing Alien (1953)
items.description: An alien whose whole deal is laughing, performed live with no retakes possible, plus the original Wheat Chex and Rice Chex spots. Somewhere between the sponsor breaks, genuinely eerie television happens.

items.title: Space Patrol — The Martian Totem Head (1954, 16mm)
items.description: A 16mm film dub of a kinescope of a live broadcast — three generations of technology deep, and Buzz Corry still comes through. This is what preservation looked like before anyone called it that.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Ambush in Space (1955)
items.description: Late-era Tom Corbett from May 1955: the cadets of the Polaris fly into an ambush, and Space Academy training takes it from there. The show had been running five years by now and could have done this in its sleep. It didn't.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Fight for Survival (1955)
items.description: From June 1955, the home stretch of the series: cadets stranded, supplies short, and the Solar Guard curriculum finally put to a real test. The title is not being coy.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — The Missing Mail Ship (1955)
items.description: A mail ship vanishes between planets and the Polaris crew goes looking, brought to you — repeatedly, in the original spots — by Kraft Caramels. In the 24th century, mail still flies and candy still sponsors.

items.title: Rocky Jones, Space Ranger — Menace from Outer Space
items.description: Missiles from deep space strike Earth and Rocky takes the Orbit Jet out to find whoever's throwing them. A full three-chapter adventure cut into feature form — Saturday matinee physics, weekday-morning morality.

items.id: RockyJonesSpaceRangerCrashOfTheMoons/Rocky Jones, Space Ranger - Crash of the Moons.mp4
items.title: Rocky Jones, Space Ranger — Crash of the Moons
items.description: Two moons on a collision course, one stubborn ruler who refuses to evacuate, and Rocky Jones caught in the middle. The most famous Rocky Jones story of them all — a disaster movie made with three sets and total sincerity.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1954) — Episodes 15 & 29
items.description: Two episodes of the Berlin-shot TV Flash, including 'The Weapon That Walked,' from Steve Holland's year in the cockpit. Flash in 3061, working cases for the Galaxy Bureau of Investigation like a space G-man.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1954) — Episodes 16 & 35
items.description: 'Mission to Masca' and a companion episode from the syndicated series that moved Flash to the year 3061. Steve Holland's Flash is less matinee idol, more federal agent with a rocket.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1954) — Episodes 18 & 38
items.description: 'The Rains of Death' plus one more from deep in the season. By this point the West German production had its formula down: one cosmic threat, two sets, three acts, done by dinner.

items.title: Buck Rogers (1939) — Chapter 11
items.description: One chapter from the back half of the 1939 serial, which means Buck starts in mortal peril he escaped from last week and ends in brand-new mortal peril. That's not a spoiler. That's the format.

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Awakening
items.description: The two-parter that launched the series: Buck wakes up in the 25th century, Earth's a fortress, and Princess Ardala's flagship is parked outside with intentions. The pilot did well enough in theaters that NBC ordered the whole ride.

items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: A surviving live broadcast from TV's first sci-fi series — which, to fill airtime, would cut away from the space adventure to clips of old westerns. DuMont called the cowboys 'Video Rangers' too and hoped nobody would ask questions.

items.title: Captain Video
items.description: The same surviving episode in a different digitization. This is the show that made 'video' a household word — five nights a week, live, on a budget that wouldn't cover a modern show's coffee.

items.id: captain-video-and-his-video-rangers-episode-3-of-4-mkv/Captain Video and His Video Rangers - V01E03.mp4
items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: Third of four surviving consecutive episodes from the DuMont original. Watching them in a row is the closest anyone will ever get to a 1950s weeknight.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK, 1962) — Series 1: The Swamps of Jupiter
items.description: Not the American Space Patrol — this one's British, made with marionettes by Roberta Leigh, and it plays like Thunderbirds' strange, serious cousin. Puppet spacemen in the swamps of Jupiter, delivered completely straight.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK, 1962) — Series 2: The Unknown Asteroid
items.description: Series two of Roberta Leigh's marionette space program: Captain Larry Dart and his Venusian and Martian crewmates investigate an asteroid that isn't on the charts. The puppets don't blink. Neither will you.

items.id: space-patrol-1963/Space Patrol (UK) S01E01 The Swamps of Jupiter.mp4
items.title: Space Patrol (1963)
items.description: A rare stretch of the 1963 British Space Patrol, the series that did interstellar patrol work with puppets and miniatures years before anyone had the budget to do it any other way.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Monster of Space (1955)
items.description: The cadets meet something the Space Academy syllabus didn't cover, with the original Kraft Caramels spots intact. A monster episode from a show that usually trusted physics more than monsters.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Pursuit of the Deep Space Projectile (1955)
items.description: Something fast and unidentified is crossing the solar system and the Polaris gives chase. Aired April 1955 with its Kraft commercials still attached, like a fly in amber made of caramel.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet (1955) — The Deep Space Projectile
items.description: Tom, Astro, and the cadets of the rocket cruiser Polaris on another training mission that immediately stops being a training mission. The show kept a real rocket scientist on retainer so the homework would add up.

items.id: flash-gordon-tv-1954-colorized-s01e06-the-claim-jumpers/Flash Gordon TV 1954 colorized s01e06 The Claim Jumpers.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (1954) — The Claim Jumpers (Colorized)
items.description: Flash and Dale come to the aid of an old asteroid prospector whose ore pile has attracted robbers — a Western with the serial numbers filed off and a rocket parked out front. Colorized from the West German original.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Planet of Death (1954)
items.description: The series premiere: Zarkov wants to test his anti-gravity device on a remote world where a scientific expedition just died mysteriously, and the GBI says absolutely not — which means Flash is definitely going.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Forbidden Experiment (1955)
items.description: Zarkov's being held prisoner on Beta M-1 by someone called the Lion Man, and Flash and Dale go get him. The title experiment is forbidden for reasons the episode is happy to demonstrate.

items.id: buck-rogers-s-1-e-23-24-flight-of-the-war-witch/Buck Rogers-S1 E23-24 Flight of the War Witch.mp4
items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Flight of the War Witch
items.description: The season one finale, in two parts: Buck crosses into another universe and has to work with Princess Ardala, whose usual plan involves conquering Earth, against a warrior queen worse than either.

items.id: buck-rogers-s-1-e-3-4-planet-of-the-slave-girls/Buck Rogers-S1 E3-4 Planet of the Slave Girls.mp4
items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Planet of the Slave Girls
items.description: Buster Crabbe, who played Buck Rogers in the 1939 serial, guest-stars here and flies alongside Gil Gerard. The plot is a poisoned food supply and a slave-labor world; the casting is the real story.

items.id: buck-rogers-s-2-episode-06-the-golden-man-3/Buck Rogers s2 episode 01 time of the hawk(0).ia.mp4
items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Time of the Hawk
items.description: Season two moved Buck onto the deep-space ship Searcher and turned the show into a stranger, moodier voyage. The feature-length opener: Buck is sent after Hawk, the last of a race of bird people, who has sworn vengeance on all humankind.

items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: Another of the roughly two dozen surviving Captain Video broadcasts — live 1950s television, performed without a net and preserved almost by accident.

items.id: captain-video-and-his-video-rangers-episode-4-of-4-mkv/Captain Video and His Video Rangers - V01E04.mp4
items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: The last of a four-episode surviving block from the DuMont original. When this one ends, that's genuinely most of what's left of a show that aired over a thousand times.

items.id: captain-video-and-his-video-rangers-v01e01/Captain Video and His Video Rangers - V01E01.mp4
items.title: Captain Video and His Video Rangers
items.description: First of four surviving consecutive episodes of television's first science fiction series. It cost almost nothing, it aired live, and every sci-fi show you've ever loved is downstream of it.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK) — Series 1: The Miracle Tree of Saturn
items.description: Roberta Leigh's marionette crew investigates a botanical miracle near Saturn. In the US it was retitled Planet Patrol, leaving Space Patrol to the cereal-sponsored American show.

items.title: Tom Corbett, Space Cadet — Episode Collection
items.description: A run of Tom Corbett adventures from the show that kept a rocket scientist on retainer to vet the scripts, so the Space Academy's physics would actually hold up. 1950 to 1955, four networks, one very responsible vision of the future.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Race Against Time (1955)
items.description: Mars is voting on whether the Galaxy Bureau of Investigation gets to keep existing, and criminals shoot down the Earth delegation to rig the outcome. Bureaucratic funding battles, but with ray guns.

items.id: flash-gordon-tv-1955-colorized-s01e35-the-earths-core/Flash Gordon TV 1955 colorized s01e35 The Earth's Core.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (1955) — The Earth's Core (Colorized)
items.description: Flash investigates trouble at the center of the Earth, because in 3061 even the planet's insides are GBI jurisdiction. Colorized from the black-and-white original.

items.id: flash-gordon-tv-1955-colorized-s01e36-deadline-at-noon/Flash Gordon TV 1955 colorized s01e36 Deadline at Noon.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (1955) — Deadline at Noon (Colorized)
items.description: A bomb planted in 1953 Berlin threatens the Earth of 3061, and Flash has under an hour to fix history. A time-travel episode from a show shot in West Berlin — they knew exactly which city to endanger.

items.title: Buck Rogers — Commodore 64 Game Footage
items.description: By the 1980s Buck Rogers had been a comic strip, a radio show, a serial, and two TV series — so of course he became a Commodore 64 game. Gameplay footage from the far future of 8-bit graphics.

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century — Buck and the Princess
items.description: Princess Ardala returns to Earth intending to secure her empire by marrying the finest genetic specimen she knows — which is Buck's whole problem. Feature-length 25th-century palace intrigue.

items.title: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century (1979) — Theatrical Cut
items.description: The version that played in actual movie theaters in early 1979, months before the TV series aired. NBC test-marketed a space hero on the big screen and America said yes.

items.title: Rocketmen vs Robots — Rocketmen Space Patrol
items.description: The Rocketmen defend humanity from the invading Killbots — vintage flying-suit footage doing what it does best: a man on a wire, a leather jacket, and complete conviction.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK)
items.description: More marionette space procedure from Roberta Leigh's operation — the British Space Patrol ran three series of interplanetary casework without a single human face on screen.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK) — The Wandering Asteroid
items.description: An asteroid slips its orbit and the puppet crew of Galasphere 347 goes to work. Rare children's television of the string-and-model school — the same tradition that gave the world Supercar and Thunderbirds.

items.title: Flash Gordon — Deadline at Noon (1955)
items.description: An enemy travels 1,250 years into the past to plant a bomb in 1953 Berlin, and Flash, Dale, and Zarkov have less than an hour to find it. Made in West Berlin by a show that clearly enjoyed endangering its own neighborhood.

items.title: Flash Gordon — Struggle to the End (1955)
items.description: The mad witch of Neptune makes her final play for the universe, and Flash is the one thing between her and total domination — again. Third round of a grudge match the show clearly loved staging.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Brain Machine (1955)
items.description: The evil witch of Neptune captures Flash and wheels out the brain machine — 'again,' the synopsis notes, wearily. Mid-trilogy entry in the witch arc, with all the menace a West German soundstage could generate.

items.title: Buck Rogers — Planet Outlaws (Feature Cut)
items.description: Buck and Buddy crash a dirigible at the North Pole, release the experimental Nirvano gas, and wake up 500 years later to a world run by Killer Kane. The 1939 serial compressed into one sitting — cliffhangers included, waiting removed.

items.title: Space Patrol — Interplanetary Smugglers (1952)
items.description: Commander Buzz Corry and Cadet Happy hunt smugglers in the 30th century, and the original commercials made it onto the tape. Smokin' rockets, as Happy would say.

items.title: Flash Gordon — Saboteurs from Space
items.description: A distorter ray stops every machine on Earth and hauls the Skyflash toward an unknown planet. The sparkler-rocket commitment is total, which is exactly why we picked it.

items.title: Space Patrol (UK) — Series 3: The Telepathic Robot
items.description: A robot that reads minds meets a crew made entirely of marionettes — Roberta Leigh's Space Patrol asking the big questions with small puppets.

items.id: SpacePatrolS01e43TheSpacePatrolCodeBelt/Space Patrol - S01e43 - The Space Patrol Code Belt.mp4
items.title: Space Patrol — The Space Patrol Code Belt
items.description: The episode where the plot runs through the show's own mail-away decoder belt, in the sharpest transfer available. Merchandising and storytelling fused into a single broadcast — 1951 invented synergy and didn't even bill for it.

items.title: Space Patrol (Colorization Test)
items.description: A volunteer ran this 1950s kinescope through DeOldify, an automatic colorizer, just to see what would happen. By the uploader's own account some scenes look great and some are flickery, messy and ugly.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Race Against Time (1955)
items.description: Criminals shoot down the Earth ship headed to a vote on the GBI's future, and Flash races to save both the passengers and the agency's budget line. Democracy in the year 3061 is surprisingly fragile.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Witch of Neptune (1955)
items.description: The opening chapter of the witch trilogy: Neptune's resident sorceress sets her sights on the universe and Flash gets in the way. The 1954–55 series at its pulpiest.

items.title: Flash Gordon: The Greatest Adventure of All (1979)
items.description: Filmation's animated Flash Gordon feature — made for TV, gorgeous by Saturday-morning standards, and rare enough that this laserdisc rip circulates like treasure. The serial mythos, redrawn with genuine love.

items.id: Space-Patrol-TheDeadlyRayGun/Space Patrol - S02e36 - The Deadly Ray Gun.mp4
items.title: Space Patrol — The Deadly Ray Gun
items.description: In the words of the archivist who uploaded it: a toy commercial wrapped in a cereal commercial that somehow still manages to be entertaining. On this channel, that's not a criticism — that's a genre.

items.id: SpacePatrolS03e28MysteriousOceansInSpace/Space Patrol - S03e28 - Mysterious Oceans in Space.mp4
items.title: Space Patrol — Mysterious Oceans in Space
items.description: Buzz Corry investigates oceans where oceans have no business being. Season three of the live ABC series, still improvising the 30th century one broadcast at a time.

items.title: Space Patrol — The Martian Totem (16mm)
items.description: A 16mm dub of the Martian Totem episode — a physical film print of a live TV broadcast, which is the only reason you're seeing it at all. Kinescopes were the black-box recorders of early television.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1980)
items.description: The Dino De Laurentiis technicolor fever dream: Sam J. Jones as Flash, Max von Sydow as Ming, sets like a hallucination, and a soundtrack by Queen. The serials walked so this could rocket-cycle.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1982) — Beginnings (Fan Edit)
items.description: A fan stitched scenes from Filmation's animated feature into a proper opening chapter for the TV series, because the series never had one. Serial-style dedication, forty years late and exactly on brand.

items.id: flash-gordon-animated-movie-1980/Compromised Frame Rate - Flash Gordon Animated + Movie (1980).ia.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon Animated
items.description: Filmation's animated Flash Gordon as captured off the air onto a Betamax tape, other broadcast material still clinging to the edges. The tape is the artifact; Flash is just what's on it.

items.title: Space Patrol and Husky (1963)
items.description: The British puppet Space Patrol, featuring Husky — the crew's Martian, who is a marionette, and who has a personality anyway. Public domain and proud of it.

items.title: Space Patrol — Kinescope Telecines
items.description: An archivist with a stack of Space Patrol kinescopes and a good telecine rig is capturing them one by one and uploading them here, for free, for whoever shows up. This channel exists because people like this exist.

items.id: vhs-tape-mtv-standup-comedy-1991-liquid-television-wphl-channel-17-stand-by-me-n/VHS Tape - MTV Standup Comedy 1991, Liquid Television, WPHL Channel 17 Stand By Me, News Break, Dr. Who Credits, NJN Commercials, Flash Gordon.ia.mp4
items.title: MTV Standup, Liquid Television, Flash Gordon & More ('91)
items.description: Someone left a VCR running in the early 90s and caught MTV standup hosted by Chris Elliott, Liquid Television, a local station's ads and, somewhere in there, a stretch of Flash Gordon. Channel surfing, fossilized.

items.id: flash-gordon-2007-season-1-complete-720p-amzn-webrip-x-264-i-c/Flash Gordon 2007 Season 1 Complete 720p AMZN WEBRip x264 [i_c]/Flash Gordon (2007) S00E01 Pilot (1).mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (2007) — Season 1
items.description: The Sci Fi Channel reboot that swapped rocket ships for a dimensional rift and asked Flash to commute to Mongo. Fans grumbled. But seventy years on, somebody was still making Flash Gordon television — the serial's oldest promise, kept.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Claim Jumpers
items.description: Flash and Dale, chasing space pirates, stop to protect an old asteroid prospector and his mound of precious ore from robbers. A gold-rush Western wearing a spacesuit, and wearing it well.

items.title: Flash Gordon — The Return of the Androids
items.description: Agents of an evil queen revive androids that spent 300 years locked in an ancient vault, then point them at Flash and the Earth, in that order. Vintage robot menace from the Berlin-made series.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 1: The Purple Death
items.description: The final serial begins: a plague is leaving purple marks on the foreheads of the dead, Ming is obviously behind it, and Flash, Dale, and Zarkov head back to Mongo. Chapter one of twelve. The cliffhangers start immediately.

items.id: TheNewAdventuresOfFlashGordonS01E04ToSaveEarth/The New Adventures Of Flash Gordon S01E01 A Planet In Peril.mp4
items.title: The New Adventures of Flash Gordon — To Save Earth
items.description: Filmation's 1979 animated series sends Flash back to the job description in the title. Drawn with real care, and truer to the Alex Raymond strip than most live-action attempts.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1936) — Chapter 2: The Tunnel of Terror
items.description: Aura helps Flash escape, Zarkov gets drafted into Ming's laboratory, Dale gets fitted for a wedding she didn't agree to, and Flash befriends the leader of the Lion Men. Chapter two, and the serial is already spending plot like it's free.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 3: Walking Bombs
items.description: The Purple Death campaign continues as Flash contends with Ming's latest delivery system — and no, the chapter title is not a metaphor. To be continued, obviously.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1936) — Chapter 3: Captured by Shark Men
items.description: Flash crashes the wedding, gets captured by King Kala of the Shark Men, and is forced to wrestle a giant octosak for Ming's amusement. The octosak is a prop. The wrestling is real effort. This is the whole serial in one scene.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 4: The Destroying Ray
items.description: Chapter four: Ming's arsenal gets a new ray, Flash gets a new problem, and last week's certain death gets quietly walked back in the first ninety seconds. Tradition.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 4: The Destroying Ray (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: The Destroying Ray in the Phantasmagoria Theater transfer — Ming aims his newest weapon while the Purple Death spreads back on Earth. Serial chapters travel the archive in duplicates; this is one of the good ones.

items.title: Flash Gordon
items.description: A half-hour of vintage Flash Gordon television from the archive's deeper shelves. The file says episode 5; the ray guns speak for themselves.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 5: The Palace of Horror
items.description: Chapter five drags Flash through Ming's Palace of Horror — the serials named their locations the way kids name haunted houses, and committed just as hard.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 5: The Palace of Horror (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: The Palace of Horror again, by way of the Phantasmagoria Theater collection. When a serial survives in this many copies, it's because a lot of people refused to let it go.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 6: Flaming Death
items.description: Flaming Death — chapter six, in which the fire is real, the peril is weekly, and the antidote to the Purple Death remains stubbornly out of reach.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 6: Flaming Death (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: Chapter six in the Phantasmagoria Theater transfer. Flash survives whatever killed him last week, then walks directly into something worse. He always does. That's the job.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 7: The Land of the Dead
items.description: The Land of the Dead — a chapter title that promises everything a 1940 kid's dime could buy. Flash, Dale, and Zarkov press deeper into Mongo while Ming's plague clock keeps ticking.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 7: The Land of the Dead (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: Same land, same dead, alternate transfer. Twelve chapters, one goal: the antidote to the Purple Death — and Ming's comeuppance, if there's time.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 9: The Pool of Peril
items.description: Chapter nine. There is a pool. It is perilous. The serial's naming department never once oversold — everything in these titles genuinely appears and genuinely menaces.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 9: The Pool of Peril (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: The Pool of Peril, Phantasmagoria Theater edition. Three chapters from the finish, and the cliffhangers are climbing over each other to get on screen.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 10: The Death Mist
items.description: The Death Mist rolls in for chapter ten. Every week a new menace with 'death' in its name; every week Flash breathes it, dodges it, or punches its inventor.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 10: The Death Mist (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: Chapter ten again, preserved twice over. The Purple Death gave this serial its stakes; the Death Mist is just Ming showing off.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 11: Stark Treachery
items.description: Stark Treachery — the penultimate chapter, where a serial traditionally spends its last betrayal before the finale. Somebody in Ming's orbit is about to pick a side.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 11: Stark Treachery (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: The treachery, starkly, in the Phantasmagoria transfer. One chapter to go, and Universal knew this was the last Flash Gordon serial they'd ever make. It plays like they knew.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 12: Doom of the Dictator
items.description: The final chapter of the final serial: Ming falls, the Purple Death is beaten, and Buster Crabbe hangs up the blond for good. Four years, three serials, forty chapters — the universe, conquered. Roll credits.

items.title: Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe — Chapter 12: Doom of the Dictator (Phantasmagoria Theater)
items.description: Doom of the Dictator, alternate transfer. The last reel of the last Flash Gordon serial — after this, the character had to wait fourteen years and cross an ocean to get back on screen.

items.title: Flash Gordon
items.description: Another late episode from the vaults — the numbering says 35, the run time says 1950s television, and Flash says whatever the script needs him to say with total conviction.

items.id: flash-gordon-s-01-e-23-the-water-world-mennace/Flash Gordon - S01E23 - The Water World Mennace.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (1954) — The Water World Menace
items.description: From the 1954–55 series shot in West Berlin and syndicated across America — a menace on a water world, handled in 25 minutes flat. About half the episodes survive in the public domain; this is one of them.

items.id: adventures-of-flash-gordon/Adventures Of Flash Gordon - Chapter 01 - A Planet In Peril.ia.mp4
items.title: The Adventures of Flash Gordon (Animated)
items.description: Flash Gordon in cartoon form — the comic-strip hero looping back toward the drawn line he came from. Alex Raymond's creation has never stayed in one medium longer than a decade.

items.title: Flash Gordon (Feature)
items.description: A feature-length Flash Gordon from the archive, uploaded with a one-word description: 'flash.' Honestly, what else is there to say — the man's been saving the universe since 1934. He needs no introduction, and this upload agrees.

items.title: Flash Gordon and the Planet of Death (1954, Colorized)
items.description: The 1954 series premiere run through a full restoration gauntlet — DeOldify color, AI upscaling, cleaned audio — by someone who decided a public domain Flash Gordon deserved the deluxe treatment. Nobody paid them. That's the point.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1936) — Chapter 1: The Planet of Peril
items.description: Mongo is on a collision course with Earth, so Zarkov hustles Flash and Dale into his rocket, and Ming sends Flash to the arena before the first chapter is up. Nearly every rocket on this channel launches from here.

items.id: flash-gordon-s-trip-to-mars-serial/FLASH GORDON-S TRIP TO MARS Ch01 New Worlds to Conquer.ia.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon's Trip to Mars — Serial Chapter
items.description: A chapter from the 1938 middle serial, in which Mars, Ming, and Queen Azura conspire against Earth's atmosphere. Fifteen chapters of Martian trouble; this reel is one of them.

items.id: flash-gordon-serial/Flash Gordon Ch01 The Planet of Peril.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon — Serial Chapter
items.description: One reel of vintage Flash Gordon chapter play, uploaded with a title as blunt as a rocket fin. The cliffhanger arrives on schedule.

items.id: flashgordonspacesoldiers01theplanetofperil/Flash Gordon Space Soldiers 01 - The Planet of Peril.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon: Space Soldiers — Chapter 1: The Planet of Peril
items.description: The 1936 serial under its TV syndication name — it was retitled 'Space Soldiers' in the fifties so viewers wouldn't confuse it with the new Flash Gordon series. Same Mongo, same Ming, same chapter-one arena fight.

items.id: flash-gordon-the-complete-serial/Flash Gordon Ch01 The Planet of Peril.ia.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon — The Complete Serial (Chapter)
items.description: A reel from the original chapter play that made Flash Gordon the king of the Saturday matinee. Come in at any chapter — the recap crawl will catch you up. That's what it's for.

items.id: flash-gordon-tv-show/Flash Gordon S01 E01The Planet of Death.ia.mp4
items.title: Flash Gordon (1954 TV Series)
items.description: An episode of the syndicated fifties series that moved Flash to the year 3061 and gave him a badge: agent of the Galaxy Bureau of Investigation. Shot in West Berlin, aired everywhere, public domain forever.

items.title: Flash Gordon — VCD Collection
items.description: Fifties TV Flash — androids, death rays, arch-criminals — preserved on Video CD, a format nearly as obscure as some of these episodes. Have no fear, Flash is here; the VCD was the endangered one.

items.title: Flash Gordon: The Movie (TV Compilation)
items.description: Someone stitched three episodes of the fifties TV series into one feature, a trick Universal pulled on its Flash serials years earlier. Androids, death rays and arch-criminals, with no chapter breaks.

items.title: Flash Gordon — Chapter 1
items.description: The opening chapter of the 1936 serial, described by its uploader as 'bad acting but fun to watch.' We'd like to formally push back on half of that. Buster Crabbe was committing.

items.title: Old Time TV: Flash Gordon (Two Episodes)
items.description: Two 1954 Flash Gordon episodes wrapped in an 'Old Time TV' presentation with host Joe Taft — a rerun show about reruns, now itself an artifact. Nostalgia, fully recursive.

items.title: Flash Gordon (1954)
items.description: The freshly paroled Queen Credentia of the planet Diana overhears plans to push the Sky Flash past the speed of light, and immediately un-reforms. Parole boards in 3061 remain optimistic.

items.id: tales-of-tomorrow-1951-53/Tales of Tomorrow (1951 - 53)/Season 1 (1951 - 52)/Sn01Ep01 Verdict from Space.ia.mp4
items.title: Tales of Tomorrow: The Complete Available Episodes (1951–53)
items.description: Before Serling, before the Control Voice, there was this: live science fiction on ABC, no second takes, no net. Fifty surviving episodes of television performed the way you'd perform a séance — once, in the dark, hoping something answers.

items.title: Blunder (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A physicist is about to run an experiment his colleagues believe could ignite the planet. They race to reach him before he throws the switch. Live television, 1951 — the sponsor breaks are the only part where you can breathe.

items.id: 1952.-tales-of-tomorrow-s-01-e-17-20-000-leagues-under-the-sea-the-chase_202308/1952. Tales of Tomorrow - S01E17 - 20,000 Leagues Under The Sea - The Chase.ia.mp4
items.title: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, Part 1: The Chase (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Captain Nemo, staged live in a New York studio with a cardboard Nautilus and total conviction. Verne's captain keeps his prisoners below the waterline, and one of them is starting to like it down there. Part one of two.

items.title: Science Fiction Theatre: Season 1, Episodes 1–13
items.description: Host Truman Bradley opens each episode with a simple experiment and assures you all of this is extrapolated from real science. Then the scientists on screen find something science can't explain.

items.title: Science Fiction Theatre: Season 2, Episodes 1–13
items.description: Thirteen more dispatches from the frontier where 1956 believed science was headed. Truman Bradley narrates like a man reading lab results that worry him slightly. Colorized by an admirer decades later — the future keeps getting revised.

items.title: The Magic Suitcase (Science Fiction Theatre)
items.description: A battered suitcase turns out to hold something no laboratory can duplicate — a power source that shouldn't exist, owned by a man who doesn't seem to want anything for it. The scientists get one look. That's the problem with one look.

items.id: season-1_202310_202310/One Step Beyond S1E1 The Bride Possessed.ia.mp4
items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 1 (Syndicated Edit)
items.description: John Newland, the calmest man on television, guides you through cases the show swore were documented fact. Season one of the anthology that claimed it wasn't fiction at all — and never once winked.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 2 (Syndicated Edit)
items.description: Season two of the series that opened every episode by promising you a matter of human record. Premonitions, hauntings, messages that arrive before their senders. Newland presents each one like evidence at an inquest nobody ordered.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 2
items.description: Alcoa presents: the unexplained, weekly. The second season of the show that beat The Twilight Zone to air by eight months and insisted, politely and forever, that every word was true.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 1 Collection
items.description: The first season, 1959 — Serling opening the door and inviting America somewhere it couldn't find on a map. The one that started with an empty town and never really let anyone back in.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-1959-s-01-e-01-where-is-everybody/The Twilight Zone 1959 S01E01 Where Is Everybody.mp4
items.title: Where Is Everybody? (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: The very first one. A man in a flight suit walks into a town with hot coffee on the stove, lights burning, jukebox playing — and no people. He'd settle for one other person. The town has other plans.

items.id: thetwilightzone_20240917/02x01 - Rei Nove Não Irá Voltar.mp4
items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 2 Collection
items.description: Season two — the year the Zone perfected itself. Fortune-telling machines, faces you shouldn't trust, small towns you shouldn't stop in. Serling wrote most of it himself, on a deadline, chain-smoking. It shows in the best way.

items.title: 'Way Out: Season 1 (Colorized)
items.description: Roald Dahl hosted fourteen episodes of this in 1961, his face floating in the dark like something you owed money to. CBS ran it opposite The Twilight Zone and it was somehow crueler. Colorized print of everything that survives.

items.id: roald-dahl-way-out-1961/Way Out (1961)/Way Out Ep01 William & Mary.mp4
items.title: 'Way Out (1961)
items.description: The anthology Roald Dahl hosted for one season before television decided it had gone too far. Fourteen macabre half-hours, then cancellation. What remains is here, and it still feels like it's getting away with something.

items.id: WayOut1961/05. I Heard You Calling Me.mp4
items.title: 'Way Out (1961)
items.description: Fourteen episodes, one host, zero comfort. Roald Dahl introduces each story with the smile of a man who already read your ending. Live-era New York television at its most quietly vicious.

items.title: The Outer Limits: Season 1 (Colorized)
items.description: There is nothing wrong with your television set. Thirty-two episodes, colorized, from a show where the network demanded a monster every week and the writers made the monster the least frightening part.

items.title: The Outer Limits: Season 1
items.description: The full first season of the show that opened by taking your TV hostage. The Control Voice promises to return your set at the end of the hour. It returns most of it.

items.id: 1963-the-outer-limits-s-1-e-1-the-galaxy-being-1987-kstw-seattle-woc-720p/1963 The Outer Limits S1E1 The Galaxy Being (1987 KSTW Seattle) WOC 720p.ia.mp4
items.title: The Galaxy Being (The Outer Limits, 1987 Seattle Broadcast)
items.description: Cliff Robertson plays a radio engineer who aims his dish at the noise between stations, and something in Andromeda answers. The series' first night on the air, taped off Seattle's KSTW in 1987 with the ads still in.

items.id: 1971-night-gallery-s-2-e-2-death-in-the-family-1986-kbhk-san-francisco-720p/1971 Night Gallery S2E2 Death In The Family (1986 KBHK San Francisco) 720p.ia.mp4
items.title: A Death in the Family (Night Gallery, 1986 Broadcast)
items.description: A mortician who lives alone, except he doesn't, exactly. An escaped convict picks the wrong funeral home to hide in — or the right one, depending on how you feel about family. Taped off San Francisco television in 1986.

items.id: art-of-darkness-a-night-gallery-retrospective-2002-09-02/Art of Darkness A Night Gallery Retrospective 2002-09-02.mp4
items.title: Art of Darkness: A Night Gallery Retrospective
items.description: A 2002 cable special walking back through Serling's gallery after closing time — the paintings, the fights with NBC, the show he hosted but was never allowed to steer. Even the retrospective sounds a little haunted.

items.title: Knife in the Dark (Danger)
items.description: A claustrophobic little episode of CBS's Danger, written by a young Rod Serling still learning what a closed room can do to people. Somebody in it has a knife. The title is honest. The rest of it isn't.

items.title: One Way Out (Four Star Playhouse)
items.description: A tight little 1955 anthology entry where the exits close one at a time. Golden-age television understood something the movies forgot: a man, a room, and a bad decision are all you need. Syndication print, slightly worn, appropriately so.

items.title: Nightmare at Ground Zero (Suspense)
items.description: A henpecked artist makes the mannequins the Army sets out for an atomic test: whole dummy families, waiting for the flash. Rod Serling wrote it six years before the Zone.

items.title: All the Time in the World (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: This anthology went out live, so a world frozen in time meant actors holding perfectly still on cue. A thief is handed a bracelet that makes the rest of the world stand still, and a museum full of art to empty.

items.title: The Little Black Bag (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A washed-up doctor finds a medical bag that fell backward out of the future, full of instruments that cannot fail. C. M. Kornbluth's story, performed live, with Joan Blondell in the cast.

items.title: The Miraculous Serum (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A serum that cures anything, tested on a dying woman because there was no time to test it on anything else. Live 1952 science fiction, where the cure always arrives before the fine print.

items.title: The Stones Began to Move (Science Fiction Theatre)
items.description: An Egyptologist asks the question the textbooks keep dodging — how did the stones get up there? — and meets a man who may be able to demonstrate. Truman Bradley presents it all as sober scientific inquiry, which somehow makes it worse.

items.title: Facsimile (Science Fiction Theatre)
items.description: From the anthology that swore everything was extrapolated from real research: an affliction that shouldn't be able to travel the way it's traveling. The scientists compare notes and don't like the pattern. Neither will you.

items.id: one-step-beyond-season-3/One Step Beyond - s03e01 - Tidal Wave.ia.mp4
items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 3
items.description: John Newland hosts these final cases without once letting his composure slip. Alcoa presents everything your grandmother swore happened to a cousin of hers, dramatized and dead serious.

items.id: ThePeterHurkosStory1960OneStepBeyondTVSeriesUSAPart2/The Peter Hurkos Story (1960, One Step Beyond TV series, USA) part 1.mp4
items.title: The Peter Hurkos Story, Part 2 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Peter Hurkos fell off a ladder in 1941 and, by his own account, woke up knowing things. Here he works with police on real cases, and the show plays it straight, no wink anywhere. Part two.

items.title: Frightmares Presents: One Step Beyond, Volume 1
items.description: Hosts Kane and the Frightmaster present two old episodes the way horror hosts always have: with love, static, and no budget. The show inside still claims it's all true. The hosts make no such promise.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 3 Collection
items.description: Season three — Serling deep in the run now, writing on airplanes, dictating twists into a wire recorder. Small towns, last men, deals that hold up exactly as written and not one inch further.

items.title: A Quality of Mercy (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: The Philippines, the last days of the war. A young lieutenant, hungry to prove himself, orders an assault on a cave full of wounded enemy soldiers. Serling served in those islands, so this one isn't hypothetical to him.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-1959-s-04-e-16-on-thursday-we-leave-for-home/The Twilight Zone 1959 S04E01 In His Image.mp4
items.title: On Thursday We Leave for Home (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Thirty years on a desert planet with two suns, and Captain Benteen has kept his colony together as their memory, preacher and king. Then the rescue ship lands. James Whitmore carries the hour, the one season the Zone ran long.

items.id: the-outer-limits-tv-1963-s01e05-the-sixth-finger/The Outer Limits TV 1963 colorized s01e05 The Sixth Finger.mp4
items.title: The Sixth Finger (The Outer Limits)
items.description: A scientist builds a machine that plays evolution forward, and a Welsh coal miner signs up to see what is next. David McCallum plays him months before Illya Kuryakin made him famous. The AI colorization is a best guess.

items.title: The Outer Limits: Season 2 (Colorized)
items.description: Seventeen colorized episodes from the season after Joseph Stefano, screenwriter of Psycho, left the producer's chair. The budget shrank and the show was cancelled, and it still made hours the genre keeps trying to match.

items.title: Chiller Network Block: Monsters + Night Gallery (2007)
items.description: A VHS rip of the now-dead Chiller network, July 2007: two episodes of Monsters, then Night Gallery after dark. A channel that no longer exists, taped by someone who suspected it wouldn't. They were right. They usually are.

items.title: Green Fingers (Night Gallery)
items.description: An old woman refuses to sell her house to a developer, because her garden isn't finished. Elsa Lanchester can make anything grow. Anything. Cameron Mitchell's developer learns the local expression for it the hard way.

items.title: Youth on Tap (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A young man is offered good money for a simple blood donation, by a client who is very old, very rich, and very specific about the donor. Live from 1952: the economy of youth, explained with a needle.

items.id: tales-of-tomorrow-what-you-need/Tales of Tomorrow' - What you need (1952).mp4
items.title: What You Need (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A shop that sells not what you want but what you will need — a pair of scissors, a train ticket, one glove. The proprietor has already seen why. Henry Kuttner's story, staged live seven years before The Twilight Zone borrowed the same door.

items.title: Yesterday's Tales of Tomorrow (Channel Pittsburgh)
items.description: A Pittsburgh community station reruns live TV from 1951 inside a 2018 broadcast — an anthology inside an anthology, a signal bounced off two different pasts before it reached you. It's Tales of Tomorrow all the way down.

items.title: The Time Element (Westinghouse Desilu Playhouse)
items.description: A man keeps dreaming he's in Honolulu, and the date keeps being December 6, 1941, and nobody will listen. Serling's 1958 proto-pilot — the one whose ratings convinced CBS to let him build the Zone. The door opened here.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Episode Collection
items.description: Public-domain cases from the series that filed the paranormal under nonfiction. Newland called them 'matters of human record.' The record, as always, declines to comment.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 1 Collection
items.description: First-season cases from the anthology John Newland hosted and directed like a coroner with excellent manners. Everything presented as documented. Nothing explained. That was the whole format, and it never needed fixing.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Season 2 Collection
items.description: Second-season files: premonitions honored, warnings ignored, houses that keep what they catch. Newland walks you through each one and leaves before the lights come back up.
