items.id: the-twilight-zone-1959-s-05-e-22-an-occurrence-at-owl-creek-bridge/The Twilight Zone 1959 S05E01 In Praise of Pip.mp4
items.title: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A Confederate saboteur stands on a bridge with a rope at his neck. The series bought Robert Enrico's French short film and aired it as an episode, the only time it outsourced a twist. Bierce wrote the story in 1890.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-1959-s-01e-34-the-after-hours-1080-p-bluray-x-265-ime/The Twilight Zone (1959) - S01e34 - The After Hours (1080P Bluray X265 Ime).ia.mp4
items.title: The After Hours (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Marsha White takes the elevator to the ninth floor to buy a gold thimble. The department store does not have a ninth floor. The saleswoman knows her name. One of the Zone's quietest and most patient traps — it waits until closing time.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 2 (Colorized)
items.description: All twenty-nine episodes of season two, colorized — the year of the fortune-telling machine, the year of the bandaged face. Purists will object. The Zone has always been comfortable with objections.

items.id: 1964-the-outer-limits-s-1-e-12-children-of-spider-county-1987-kstw-woc-720p/1964 The Outer Limits S1E12 Children Of Spider County (1987 KSTW) WOC 720p.ia.mp4
items.title: The Children of Spider County (The Outer Limits, 1987 Broadcast)
items.description: Four brilliant young men from the same rural county all vanish in the same month, and a stranger in a dark suit comes to collect the fifth. He says he's family. Taped off Seattle TV in 1987, commercials and all.

items.id: 1964-the-outer-limits-s-1-e-19-the-invisibles-1987-kstw-seattle-woc-720p/1964 The Outer Limits S1E19 The Invisibles (1987 KSTW Seattle) WOC 720p.ia.mp4
items.title: The Invisibles (The Outer Limits, 1987 Broadcast)
items.description: A secret society implants creatures at the base of powerful men's spines, and a government agent goes undercover to be recruited. One of the coldest hours the series ever aired, and the parasite is not the unsettling part.

items.id: the-outer-limits-tv-1964-s02e05-demon-with-a-glass-hand/The Outer Limits TV 1964 colorized s02e05 Demon with a Glass Hand.mp4
items.title: Demon With a Glass Hand (The Outer Limits)
items.description: Robert Culp has no memory and a glass hand that answers questions, but only when it has enough fingers. Harlan Ellison's script, shot in Los Angeles's Bradbury Building, all iron lace and daylight.

items.title: Tales of Tomorrow: Season 1 Collection
items.description: First-season broadcasts from the live anthology that did science fiction with wet paint and one camera rehearsal. When an actor forgot a line, the future just paused and waited. Sometimes you can see it happen.

items.title: The Children's Room (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A library has a room only certain children can find, stocked with books in a language only they can read. A professor discovers his son is on the reading list. Live from 1952 — the recruitment was already underway.

items.id: TalesOfTomorrow20000LeaguesUnderTheSeaTheChasePart1_201708/Tales of Tomorrow - 20,000 Leagues Under The Sea - The Chase Part 1.mp4
items.title: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, Part 2: The Escape (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: The conclusion of live television's two-week attempt at Jules Verne: prisoners of the Nautilus plotting their way back to the surface, while Nemo decides whether the surface deserves them. The escape is the easy part.

items.title: Midnight (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A late entry from the final season, and the title is the whole warning. On this series midnight was never just a time — it was an appointment. Presented, as always, as a matter of record.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 3 (Colorized)
items.description: Thirty-seven episodes of the third season, colorized decades later. The year of the kanamits and the little girl who fell through the bedroom wall. Some doors get repainted. They still open onto the same place.

items.id: the-outer-limits-tv-1964-s02e07-the-invisible-enemy/The Outer Limits TV 1964 colorized s02e07 The Invisible Enemy.mp4
items.title: The Invisible Enemy (The Outer Limits)
items.description: The first expedition to Mars went silent in minutes. The second, with Adam West aboard, lands to find out why — and learns the desert has a current, and things that swim in it. The sand is calm. That's the trick of it.

items.id: the-outer-limits-s02e09-i-robot/The Outer Limits TV 1964 colorized s02e09 I, Robot.mp4
items.title: I, Robot (The Outer Limits)
items.description: A robot named Adam stands trial for the murder of the man who built him, and a tired lawyer takes the case nobody wants. Leonard Nimoy plays the reporter, two years before the ears. The verdict matters less than what Adam does with it.

items.id: 1965-the-outer-limits-s-2-e-17-the-probe-1987-kstw-seattle-woc-720p/1965 The Outer Limits S2E17 The Probe (1987 KSTW Seattle) WOC 720p.ia.mp4
items.title: The Probe (The Outer Limits, 1987 Broadcast)
items.description: Plane crash survivors drift in a life raft until something scoops them up, and the room they wake in isn't a room. It was the last first-run episode ABC aired.

items.title: Tales of Tomorrow: Season 2 Collection
items.description: Second-season transmissions from the live anthology — bigger swings, same single take. By 1952 they were staging Frankenstein and deep-sea voyages between commercial breaks, live, and mostly getting away with it.

items.title: Flight Overdue (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A famous aviatrix vanishes over the ocean, and the world files her under lost. Four years later her husband learns where the flight actually ended. Live from 1952, when Amelia Earhart was still a fresh wound and everyone watching knew it.

items.title: The Crystal Egg (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: An antique dealer notices a customer wants one particular crystal egg far too badly, so he does the sensible thing and shows it to a physicist. H.G. Wells wrote the original in 1897. The egg has been watching us at least that long.

items.title: Tonight at 12:17 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A pregnant woman becomes fixated on one specific minute of the night, and the fixation turns out to be mutual. The series presents her case as documented fact, with the timestamp already filled in. Check your watch.

items.title: Night of April 14 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A young woman dreams of drowning in freezing water, then her fiancé surprises her with honeymoon tickets: a sailing to New York in April 1912, on a brand-new ship. Restored with the original Alcoa titles and bumpers.

items.id: onestepbeyonds1e15theaerialist/One Step Beyond s1e15 The Aerialist.mp4
items.title: The Aerialist (One Step Beyond, Colorized)
items.description: Two trapeze artists argue, and then there's an accident, and then a man is carrying guilt at altitude every night. Something up there in the rigging starts carrying it with him. Colorized print of a case the show filed under 'true.'

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 4 (Colorized)
items.description: The strange season — eighteen hour-long episodes CBS demanded and Serling privately doubted. Twice the runtime, the same number of exits. Colorized. Some of these are gems that needed the room; the rest are hallways.

items.id: twilight-zone-s-5-e-27-sounds-and-silences-1964-16mm-b-w-eastman-print/Twilight Zone S5E27 Sounds and Silences (1964 - 16mm B&W Eastman Print).ia.mp4
items.title: Sounds and Silences (The Twilight Zone, 16mm Print)
items.description: A man in love with noise finds the volume of his life turning against him. The uploader calls it one of the Zone's most mediocre half-hours, but it's a 16mm print with the original Pall Mall and Thrill commercials left in.

items.id: twilight-zone-la-quatrieme-dimension-s-1-e-00-the-time-element-ep-pilote-vost-fr-1958/Twilight Zone - (La Quatrième Dimension) - S1E01 - Solitude (Where is Everybody).ia.mp4
items.title: The Time Element (Twilight Zone Pilot, French Subtitles)
items.description: A gambler keeps dreaming his way back to Hawaii on December 6, 1941, and nobody there believes what he knows. Serling's script aired on Desilu Playhouse in 1958, a year before the series, here in French.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Dec. '95)
items.description: The nineties revival, taped off a CBS affiliate in 1995 with the commercials still breathing between acts. The Control Voice got a new timbre and the same authority. Somebody's VCR did the preserving; the transmission does the rest.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Nov. '95)
items.description: Another hour of the revival series as it actually arrived in living rooms — station bugs, ad breaks, November 1995. The uncanny works best with interruptions. Gives you time to doubt yourself.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Nov. '95)
items.description: Episode seven of the new Outer Limits, preserved off-air from 1995. The revival ran seven seasons by remembering the original rule: the monster is a delivery system. The package is always about you.

items.title: The Dune Roller (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Fragments of a meteorite scattered along a lakeshore, and every fragment trying to get back to the mother stone. A scientist gets between the pieces and the reunion. Live from 1952 — geology with intent.

items.title: Frankenstein (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Shelley's monster performed live in 1952, with Lon Chaney Jr. under the makeup. Legend says Chaney thought the broadcast was a rehearsal and gently set down the furniture he was supposed to smash. Watch his hands. The legend has evidence.

items.title: The Diamond Lens (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A man builds the perfect microscope and finds a world in a single drop of water — with someone in it. Fitz-James O'Brien's 1858 obsession story, staged live: the smaller the universe, the harder it holds you.

items.title: Earthquake (One Step Beyond)
items.description: San Francisco, April 1906. A hotel bellboy keeps seeing the city fall down, and everyone around him keeps having a lovely evening. Caruso is singing tonight. The date is the spoiler.

items.title: The Bride Possessed (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The very first case: a honeymooning bride's accent vanishes, replaced by the voice of a woman who has something to finish. Her husband married one person and is now living with another.

items.title: Night of April 14 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: She dreams of ice water closing over her head. He books them passage to New York — April 1912, the ship everyone's talking about. The series swears this premonition was documented. The maiden voyage kept its own records.

items.title: Vaulting: Twilight Zone — The Movie (Retrospective)
items.description: Morgan Leger reviews the 1983 Twilight Zone movie from inside a Serling impression: four segments, and the on-set accident that has shadowed the film ever since. A fan's eye on a film that is hard to watch lightly.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Dec. '95)
items.description: The revival, episode eight, complete with mid-nineties commercials — which at this distance are their own anthology of the uncanny. Two time capsules for the price of one tape.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Oct. '95)
items.description: Episode thirteen of the new series, taped off broadcast in October 1995. The Control Voice returns your television at the top of the hour, same as it did in 1963. It has never once been late.

items.title: The Outer Limits on CBS (Oct. '95)
items.description: Another off-air hour from the revival's first season, October 1995, ads intact. Whoever ran this VCR did it faithfully, week after week. The archive is built out of people like that.

items.title: Blunder (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Scientists race the clock to stop a colleague whose experiment might crack the planet open. He's brilliant, he's certain, and he isn't answering the phone. Live television's first great everybody-dies-if-he's-wrong hour.

items.id: tales-of-tomorrow/Tales Of Tomorrow S01 E01 Verdict From Space.ia.mp4
items.title: Tales of Tomorrow: Episode Collection
items.description: Assorted transmissions from the 1951–53 live anthology — the show that did android uprisings and doomsday devices with theater actors, card tables, and a red ON AIR light. The seams show. The seams are the point.

items.title: A Child Is Crying (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A child who does not behave like a child — who knows things, and calculates things, and cries about what the calculations say. The military takes an interest, which is exactly what the crying is about. Live, 1953.

items.title: Emergency Only (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A man laughs off a party psychic's predictions, then watches each one arrive on schedule — the stranger, the train, the knife. The last prediction is still pending. He's stopped laughing. The show files it all under 'documented.'

items.title: The Dark Room (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An American photographer in Paris rents a cheap apartment and starts photographing a model who poses beautifully and arrives unannounced. The film develops. The question is what develops on it.

items.title: Twelve Hours to Live (One Step Beyond)
items.description: He storms out after the argument; she starts seeing exactly where he is and exactly how much trouble he's in. Nobody believes the wife, which is traditional. She has twelve hours to make the vision wrong.

items.id: shatterday-the-new-twilight-zone-1985-tv-series/Shatterday - The New Twilight Zone 1985 TV Series.ia.mp4
items.title: Shatterday (The Twilight Zone, 1985)
items.description: A man dials his own apartment from a bar, and he answers: the better version of himself, home, settling in, taking over. Harlan Ellison's story, with Bruce Willis in the lead. The 1985 revival opened with this.

items.title: The Twilight Zone (1985): Season 1 Premiere
items.description: The eighties revival's opening night — Bruce Willis calling home and finding himself already there. The new Zone traded black-and-white for synth scores and kept the only thing that mattered: the door.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-1985-s-02-e-01-the-once-and-future-king/The Twilight Zone 1985 S02E01 - The Once and Future King.mp4
items.title: The Once and Future King (The Twilight Zone, 1985)
items.description: An Elvis impersonator falls backward through the year 1954 and meets the genuine article before the world does. Two men, one face, one throne. The impersonation ends where all tribute acts secretly want to end.

items.title: The Outer Limits (June '01)
items.description: An hour-plus of The Outer Limits as it aired on a Miami UHF station in June 2001, commercials included. Channel 69, the far end of the dial — exactly where transmissions like this have always preferred to live.

items.title: Fury of the Cocoon (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A jungle expedition finds a giant cocoon where a meteor came down, and something inside it is waiting. Tales of Tomorrow was mostly live, so the horror had to fit in a studio.

items.title: Past Tense (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Boris Karloff as a doctor with a time machine and a plan: carry penicillin back to 1923, before anyone had it, and sell it. Karloff does quiet desperation here, no makeup required.

items.id: TalesOfTomorrowTombOfKingTarus/Tales of Tomorrow - Tomb of king Tarus.mp4
items.title: The Tomb of King Tarus (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: Archaeologists open a sealed Egyptian tomb on live television — aired Halloween night, 1952. The king inside has been waiting four thousand years, which is long enough to plan a proper reception. Curses keep excellent calendars.

items.title: Epilogue (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A man comes home from drying out, sober and skeptical of everything — then his son is buried alive in a cave-in, and the thing that leads the rescue party doesn't take skepticism personally. Filed by the series, as always, under fact.

items.title: Premonition (One Step Beyond)
items.description: As a girl she saw the ballroom chandelier come down on her, in detail, in daylight. She's avoided the room ever since. Now her engagement party is being planned, and the family insists on the ballroom. The chandelier has been patient.

items.id: S1E9THEDEADPARTOFTHEHOUSE_201804/S1E9 - THE DEAD PART OF THE HOUSE.mp4
items.title: The Dead Part of the House (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A lonely girl moves into a new house and makes three friends in the upstairs nursery. The adults assume she means her new dolls. The adults are working from incomplete information.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-1985-s-03-e-01-the-curious-case-of-edgar-witherspoon/The Twilight Zone 1985 S03E01 - The Curious Case of Edgar Witherspoon.mp4
items.title: The Curious Case of Edgar Witherspoon (The Twilight Zone, 1985)
items.description: An old man tends a machine of junk that fills his apartment, because he says it keeps the world from tipping over. His niece wants him committed, which is reasonable and beside the point.

items.title: Twilight Zone + News on ITV ('89–'91)
items.description: Local news and weather from the East Midlands, and The Twilight Zone sitting in the schedule like a stone in a shoe. Taped off ITV's Central, with a 1977 film and the 5pm news after it.

items.id: 1992.10.31-woio-twilight-zone-marathon-bet-midnight-love/1992.10.31 - WOIO - Twilight Zone Marathon - BET - Midnight Love [β].mp4
items.title: Halloween Twilight Zone Marathon (Oct. '92)
items.description: Halloween night on Cleveland's WOIO, Channel 19: four hours of Twilight Zone with the local commercials left in, then BET's Midnight Love videos to close. Someone's Beta deck ran through all of it.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Outer Limits Night (April 2007)
items.description: A Wednesday night of The Outer Limits, April 25, 2007, taped by a collector the Archive knows only as Oakley. Somebody was still feeding tapes to a VCR.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Outer Limits Night (June 2007)
items.description: Another marathon slab from the Oakley collection — a full evening of the revival series, commercials fossilized in place, June 2007. The Control Voice, four hours, no skipping. As intended.

items.title: The Window (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: The scheduled play breaks up mid-broadcast and the cameras pick up something else: a window, and something nobody was meant to see. Live television interrupting itself, played completely straight.

items.title: Ahead of His Time (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: One admirer's favorite episode of the live anthology — a man out of step with his own era, in a series that specialized in them. The tape survived because somebody loved it specifically. That's the only reason anything survives.

items.title: Ice From Space (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: A test rocket comes back carrying a block of ice it didn't leave with. The ice doesn't melt. The room gets colder. The Air Force takes the measurements while the measurements are still possible. Live from 1953.

items.title: The Vision (One Step Beyond)
items.description: French soldiers on a World War I battlefield drop their weapons and walk away. At the court-martial each gives a different account of what he saw, and none is easy to believe. One Step Beyond swears it happened.

items.title: The Devil's Laughter (One Step Beyond)
items.description: They hanged John Marriott and the rope broke. They tried again and it broke again. Marriott stops being afraid, because he's seen how he actually dies — and it isn't here, and it isn't this. The gallows takes it personally.

items.id: S1E12THERETURNOFMITCHELLCAMPION/S1E12 - THE RETURN OF MITCHELL CAMPION.mp4
items.title: The Return of Mitchell Campion (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A man steps off the boat onto an island he's never visited, and everyone there welcomes him back. They know his name. They remember what he did. His passport says otherwise, but passports have never impressed this series.

items.id: twilight-zone-rod-serlings-lost-classics-1994-ai/Twilight Zone Rod Serlings Lost Classics (1994)/Twilight Zone Rod Serlings Lost Classics (1994) (AI).ia.mp4
items.title: Twilight Zone: Rod Serling's Lost Classics (1994)
items.description: Two scripts found in a trunk after Serling died, produced for television in 1994 with James Earl Jones presiding. The man had been gone nineteen years and was still making deadlines. Upscaled print, original included.

items.title: The Making of the Twilight Zone Tower of Terror (1994)
items.description: Disney builds a haunted hotel and drops the elevator, and this promotional special explains how — imagineers speaking of Serling the way engineers speak of load-bearing walls. The Zone as theme park. He'd have written a twist about that.

items.id: outerlimitsdemonwithaglasshand1/outer limits = demon with a glass hand-1.mp4
items.title: Demon With a Glass Hand, Part 1 (The Outer Limits)
items.description: The opening movement of Ellison's masterpiece: a man with ten days of memory, a glass hand short three fingers, and a building full of things wearing human faces. Every answer costs a flight of stairs.

items.title: The Premonition (The Outer Limits, Italian Subtitles)
items.description: A test pilot breaks a speed record and comes down in a world stopped dead, and something else that is still moving. An Italian-subtitled print of the original Outer Limits.

items.title: The Outer Limits: Uncensored Collection, Part 2
items.description: Part two of an uncensored Outer Limits collection: the episodes the uploader says the DVDs left out. Please do not attempt to adjust your picture; any extra frames are meant to be there.

items.title: Substance X (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: October 1952, live: a substance with a placeholder name and effects nobody placed an order for. Another dispatch from the anthology where the science was speculative and the airtime was terrifyingly real.

items.title: The Spider's Web (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: From the final weeks of the live anthology, May 1953: a web, a fly, and twenty-six minutes to work out which one you've been watching. Henry Jones stars. Performed once, preserved barely.

items.title: The Dune Roller (Tales of Tomorrow)
items.description: The lakeshore meteorite whose scattered pieces want to be whole again — and roll, uphill if necessary, to arrange it. Rescued from a bootleg site by someone who called it a classic. The fragments reunite; so do the fans.

items.title: The Secret (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Ignored by a husband who treats her like furniture, a wife invents an imaginary lover for company — attentive, warm, always home. Then the evidence starts suggesting she didn't invent him so much as answer his ad.

items.title: The Aerialist (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A quarrel between trapeze partners, a missed catch, a man who'll never walk — and the partner who flies on, carrying a guilt that starts pulling rank up there in the lights. The net catches bodies. It has no policy on the rest.

items.title: The Burning Girl (One Step Beyond)
items.description: New town, hostile aunt, a father who's already decided she's an arsonist. The girl swears she never touches the matches — and she's telling the truth, which is far worse. Fire keeps finding her distress like it's subscribed.

items.title: New Year's Eve 2000: SciFi Twilight Zone Marathon
items.description: Three hours of the SciFi Channel's millennium New Year's marathon, taped with commercials intact. A century turned over while Rod Serling ran on a loop — the correct way to have done it. The taper knew.

items.title: Summer 2000: SciFi Twilight Zone Marathon
items.description: Hours of the summer 2000 Twilight Zone marathon off the SciFi Channel, back when it was spelled SciFi and not SyFy. The uploader started watching the show that same year, and the commercials from then are still in.

items.id: rod-serling-beyond-the-twilight-zone/Rod Serling, Beyond The Twilight Zone.ia.mp4
items.title: Rod Serling: Beyond the Twilight Zone (E! True Hollywood Story)
items.description: The biography, cable-documentary style: the paratrooper who came home with shrapnel and nightmares and wrote his way through both. The narrator of American unease finally gets narrated.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Outer Limits Night (November 2007)
items.description: Four hours of Outer Limits off cable, November 2007, from the Oakley collection — one taper's standing appointment with the Control Voice. The tape doesn't curate. That's its virtue.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Outer Limits Overnight (February 1992)
items.description: A leap-night 1992 entertainment tape, wall to wall Outer Limits with the ad breaks intact. February 29th only exists once every four years; Oakley spent it recording. History vindicates this choice.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: All Outer Limits (February 1992)
items.description: The companion tape: nothing but Outer Limits, four straight hours, taped off the air in February 1992. Somewhere in the static between episodes is the exact texture of staying up too late thirty years ago.

items.title: The Haunted U-Boat (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A German submarine develops a knocking sound that only starts when she dives, as if something outside the hull wants in. Or someone. The crew surfaces and surrenders rather than hear it again — a matter, the show insists, of naval record.

items.title: Image of Death (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The Marquis murdered his wife and got away clean — except for the stain on the wall, which the servants can't scrub out, and which is slowly acquiring a face. The inspector just wants to ask a few questions. The wall has answers.

items.title: The Captain's Guests (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A young couple buys a New England house that once belonged to a sea captain of terrible reputation. The captain still considers it his. The husband is starting to agree with him — that's the part the wife can't forgive the house for.

items.id: 2001-fall-twilight-zone-marathon-tape-2001-a.-converted/2001 Fall - Twilight Zone Marathon Tape 2001 A.Converted.ia.mp4
items.title: New Year's Eve 2001: SciFi Twilight Zone Marathon (Tape A)
items.description: New Year's Eve into 2002 on the SciFi Channel, the annual ritual where a nation greets midnight with Rod Serling instead of confetti. Taped by someone who had found the show a year earlier, commercials included.

items.title: The Twilight Zone (2002 Series)
items.description: The second television revival: Forest Whitaker holding the door Serling built, UPN holding the budget. A season of early-2000s twists, some land, some don't, and the misses are their own time capsule.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Outer Limits Weekend (February 1993)
items.description: Tape 223 in the Oakley collection: an Outer Limits block from the weekend of February 27 and 28, 1993. The number says there were many more. Archives are built by people who never asked whether they should stop.

items.title: Journey to the Outer Limits (Reel 1)
items.description: There is nothing wrong with your television set. This is an expedition documentary that only shares a name with The Outer Limits: young climbers testing what they thought they could survive. Mostly uphill.

items.title: MonsterVision with Penn & Teller: The Outer Limits
items.description: Penn & Teller, professional fooling experts, host TNT's MonsterVision and seem delighted to be fooled by The Outer Limits anyway. A cable channel introducing older television, which is what we do here too.

items.title: Echo (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Acquitted of his wife's murder, a man retreats to the countryside to escape the reporters — and starts seeing a mirror image act out what the jury couldn't prove. The verdict was reasonable doubt. The reflection has none.

items.title: Front Runner (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Two jockeys, one track, an old rivalry — and in the middle of the race, a rider gets help from a direction the racing form doesn't cover. The series presents it as turf-club fact. Photo finishes can't photograph everything.

items.title: The Riddle (One Step Beyond)
items.description: On a train through India, a husband takes one look at a beggar on the platform and becomes certain — violently certain — that the man means to kill him. He's never seen him before. That's the riddle. The answer predates them both.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Twilight Zone Night (October 2007)
items.description: A Twilight Zone night taped off cable weeks after Halo 3 launched, so the breaks sell a shooter between Serling's sermons. Two futures on one tape, both already past.

items.title: The Oakley Tapes: Twilight Zone Night (January 2008)
items.description: Tape zero: a January 2008 cable block of The Twilight Zone, recorded whole — episodes, promos, ads, the lot. The show was pushing fifty and still pulling overnight audiences. Some doors don't close for renovations.

items.title: The After Hours (Twilight Zone, 2008 Marathon Broadcast)
items.description: Marsha White goes up to the ninth floor of a department store for a gold thimble, which is odd, because the store has no ninth floor. Taped during a New Year's marathon.

items.title: The Galaxy Being (The Outer Limits Pilot)
items.description: The first transmission: a radio station engineer, bored with the licensed frequencies, tunes into Andromeda and gets a reply made of light. The pilot that taught television to say 'we are controlling transmission' and mean it.

items.id: TheOuterLimits1x0102TheSandkings/The Outer Limits/Season 1 - Complete/The Outer Limits - 1x01-02 - The Sandkings.mp4
items.title: The Sandkings (The Outer Limits '95 Premiere)
items.description: A man keeps a colony of alien creatures that build castles, then build worship, and he enjoys being the god more than he should. George R.R. Martin's story opened the 1995 Outer Limits revival.

items.id: demon-with-a-glass-hand/The Outer Limits - Demon With A Glass Hand (1964)  [674x360].mp4
items.title: Demon With a Glass Hand (The Outer Limits)
items.description: Robert Culp runs through the Bradbury Building all night, taking directions from a glass hand with three fingers missing. Harlan Ellison wrote it, and later won an acknowledgment on The Terminator.

items.title: Delusion (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A man with a rare blood type refuses to save a girl's life by donating, because the gift comes with visions of her future. The show, as ever, swears it was true.

items.title: Ordeal on Locust Street (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Behind the drawn curtains of a respectable house lives a son the family describes to no one. A hypnotist arrives claiming he can help, if they'll let him go where the boy actually lives. Desperation says yes before anyone defines 'where.'

items.title: Brainwave (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Wartime, open water, a dying captain. The only surgeon in reach is a hospital corpsman, taking instructions by radio from a doctor on another ship. Every step is a stranger's voice.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-king-nine-will-not-return-2010-02-07-0/The Twilight Zone-(King Nine Will Not Return)-2010-02-07-0.mp4
items.title: King Nine Will Not Return (Twilight Zone, 2010 Broadcast)
items.description: A B-25 captain wakes in the desert beside his crashed bomber and his crew is missing — seventeen years missing. Season two's opener, taped off a 2010 rebroadcast: sand, heat, one man, and arithmetic that won't come out right.

items.title: Doomsday (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Burned for a death she didn't cause, a village woman curses an Earl's line: the eldest son of each generation will die before his father.

items.title: Night of the Kill (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Davey Morris comes home after being missing and says he spent the time with a large, friendly creature. His parents humor him until the footprints turn up, then until the food starts disappearing.

items.title: The Inheritance (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A gigolo in a seedy bar explains how he came to possess a dead countess's necklace, and why he'd very much like to stop possessing it. He's not superstitious. He's just been keeping count.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-season-1/The Twilight Zone (1959) - S01e01 - Where Is Everybody (1080P Bluray X265 Ime).ia.mp4
items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 1 Episodes
items.description: First-season entries from 1959 — the vintage year of lonely astronauts, dusty main streets, and wishes granted at full published price. Serling wrote most of them between cigarettes. Every anthology since is a footnote with better lighting.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-s-02-e-07-nick-of-time_202503/The Twilight Zone S02E07 Nick of Time.mp4
items.title: Nick of Time (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A honeymooning couple breaks down in Ridgeview, Ohio, and the diner's penny fortune teller keeps answering correctly. Richard Matheson wrote it, and William Shatner plays a man who finds it hard to stop asking.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-season-2_202411/The Twilight Zone (1959) - S02e01 - King Nine Will Not Return (1080P Bluray X265 Ime).ia.mp4
items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 2 Episodes
items.description: Second-season files: the year the Zone learned to sit still and let the dread come to it. Diners, hospital wards, deserted theaters. Twenty-two minutes in, you'll check the room you're sitting in. That's the design.

items.title: The Open Window (One Step Beyond)
items.description: On a hot night, artist Anthony March watches a woman in the apartment opposite do something terrible. He crosses over and the room is empty. Then, some days later, he sees her again.

items.title: Message From Clara (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A night-school student falls for his teacher, and then the handwriting starts — his dead girlfriend's script, in a living woman's hand. Someone is borrowing the teacher to finish a conversation. The lesson plan did not include this.

items.title: Forked Lightning (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Two strangers find their lives wired together by a psychic connection neither asked for. The closer they get to understanding it, the less either of them likes where it seems to be leading.

items.title: UV's MGM Nightmare 6: The Twilight Zone
items.description: A Halloween special from a homegrown video series, using the Zone as its haunted house. Fan-made unease in the Serling tradition: no budget, full commitment, twist included. He'd have approved of at least two of those.

items.title: Reunion (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Germany, 1939: young glider pilots hear of the invasion of Poland and plan a reunion picnic for the first Sunday after the war. The war has other plans for the guest list.

items.title: Dead Ringer (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Esther sees buildings burning before they burn, and swears the arsonist is her long-lost sister — a sister she claims she can summon just by willing it. The town humors her. The fires don't.

items.title: The Stone Cutter (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Old Simon Lockhart visits the stonecutter's yard and finds his own tombstone already carved — name correct, date pending, and the date is this week. The stonecutter doesn't recall doing the work. The chisel has its own sources.

items.title: Father Image (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A son inherits a theater his father kept secret, and goes in to find out why. Someone inside has been waiting a long time. The letter at the end explains everything except how it is possible.

items.title: Vaulting: The Ten Worst Twilight Zone Episodes
items.description: A retrospective counts down the ten worst Twilight Zone episodes and keeps it kind: can the show really be that bad? Not quite. Spoilers throughout, so skip ahead if you haven't seen the clunkers.

items.title: Her Pilgrim Soul (The Twilight Zone, 1985)
items.description: A holographic projector begins displaying a woman nobody programmed, and she remembers a whole life. Alan Brennert's script is the 1985 revival's tenderest hour.

items.id: 630115TheJackBennyProgramS13e16TwilightZoneSketch/63-01-15  The Jack Benny Program  s13e16  Twilight Zone Sketch.mp4
items.title: The Jack Benny Program: Twilight Zone Sketch (with Rod Serling)
items.description: Jack Benny hires Rod Serling to improve the show, Serling decides comedy makes no sense to him, and Jack counters with Twilight Zone. Then the fog rolls in and Rochester doesn't recognize his boss.

items.id: S2E14MAKEMENOTAWITCH/S2E14 - MAKE ME NOT A WITCH.mp4
items.title: Make Me Not a Witch (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A farm girl wakes up able to hear everyone's thoughts, and prays to be rid of it — her parents call it devilry, her priest calls it something else. Before the gift goes, it has two lives to save. The title is her actual prayer.

items.title: The Hand (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A piano player kills a woman in a jealous rage and washes up carefully afterward. His hand disagrees with the verdict of clean. No stain anyone else can see — but he plays for a living, and the keys are white, and the hand remembers.

items.title: Earthquake (One Step Beyond)
items.description: April 1906, the Palace Hotel, San Francisco: Caruso sings tonight and a bellboy keeps seeing the walls come down. Everyone he warns has tickets. History has already printed the morning headline — the boy's just the only one who's read it.

items.id: a-penny-for-your-thoughts-the-twilight-zone/A Penny for Your Thoughts-The Twilight Zone.mp4
items.title: A Penny for Your Thoughts (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A bank clerk's coin lands on its edge, and suddenly every mind in the office is audible to him — including the quiet ones, which is the problem. The Zone at its gentlest: a superpower priced at one cent and revoked the same way.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season 1 DVD Collection (Portuguese Subtitles)
items.description: Além da Imaginação: the complete first season as Brazilian DVD ISOs, official Portuguese subtitles included. No dub was ever made — Serling's voice was apparently considered non-negotiable. Correct call.

items.title: Forests of the Night (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Three hunters wait out the rain with a Chinese game that promises to make a man what he is not. The mildest of them plays. Blake asked what immortal hand or eye framed the tiger; this episode asks what happens when the frame comes off.

items.title: Call From Tomorrow (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An actress shattered by her daughter's death comes home from the sanitarium to a quiet house — and then hears the child calling. Not from the past, which would be grief. From somewhere with a schedule. The title is doing honest work.

items.title: Who Are You? (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A girl comes through scarlet fever convinced she is another child, one from the next town who recently drowned. Two mothers, one patient, and a grief looking for somewhere to go.

items.title: The Lateness of the Hour (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A daughter suffocating in her family's perfect house, with perfect servants and perfect comfort, demands her father shut down the machines that run it. He resists. This one was shot on videotape, and the airlessness is the point.

items.title: The Obsolete Man (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: The State has abolished books, so librarian Romney Wordsworth is declared obsolete and sentenced to die, method of his choosing, televised. Burgess Meredith picks carefully. Serling's purest sermon.

items.title: Ring-a-Ding Girl (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A movie star whose hometown fan club sends a ring, and in its stone she sees faces begging her to come home today, now, instead of catching her scheduled flight. She changes her plans.

items.title: The Lovers (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Something unseen in a Viennese tavern objects to a waitress and the regular who adores her. Most hauntings want a house. This one wants a breakup.

items.title: Vanishing Point (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Ruth Graham walks into a room of the rented house mid-argument and doesn't walk out. Her husband stands trial for a body no one can produce. Then he learns who lived there before.

items.title: The Mask (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A flyer bails out over the Sahara and should have died in the sand. When they find him alive, the rescue team stops congratulating themselves the moment he lifts his head. What the desert did instead of killing him is the episode.

items.title: The Sixteen-Millimeter Shrine (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Ida Lupino plays an aging screen queen who runs her old pictures in a dark room, all day, every day, and prefers the woman on the film to the one in the chair. Sunset Boulevard, with a projector.

items.title: The New Exhibit (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: The wax museum is closing, so its devoted caretaker moves the murderers' gallery into his basement — Jack the Ripper, Burke and Hare. Wax is very patient.

items.title: The Fever (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Franklin Gibbs despises gambling, which is why it takes the slot machine most of a night to get him. Then it starts calling his name in a voice of falling coins. The Zone's portrait of addiction, one pull at a time.

items.title: The Haunting (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Colin suspects his best friend and his fiancée, so when the climbing rope needs holding, he doesn't hold it. The wedding proceeds as planned. So does something else — weddings, it turns out, are easy to attend uninvited.

items.title: The Explorer (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Three explorers stagger out of the desert alive, guided to safety, they say, by young Eric Borgner. Dr. Hansen has come to Germany to thank the father. The father's reaction is the whole episode.

items.title: The Clown (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A jealous man kills his young wife, and afterward, in every mirror, there's a mute clown — closer each time, greasepaint immaculate, hands ready. The carnival was in town the night it happened. It never entirely left.

items.id: the-four-of-us-are-dying-the-twilight-zone/The Four Of Us Are Dying-The Twilight Zone.mp4
items.title: The Four of Us Are Dying (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Arch Hammer can rearrange his face into any dead man's: a trumpet player, a gangster, whoever's useful tonight. One cheap hotel room, four faces, and a bill that comes due. Shot like a jazz nightmare, all neon and switchblades.

items.id: 118-on-thursday-we-leave-for-home-3/000-Interview with Rod Serling and Mike Wallace (3).ia.mp4
items.title: On Thursday We Leave for Home (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Captain Benteen has kept his people alive on a burning rock for thirty years with stories of green Earth. Now the rescue ship is here. James Whitmore carries every minute of the hour.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-s-02-e-07-nick-of-time/The Twilight Zone S02E07 Nick of Time.mp4
items.title: Nick of Time (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: A stalled car, an Ohio diner, a devil-headed machine that answers questions for a penny. Shatner's honeymooner keeps feeding it, and it keeps being right. No smoke, no claws, just a booth two people have to choose to stand up from.

items.title: I Saw You Tomorrow (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Arriving at a country estate, a man watches a murder happen in front of him — then blinks, and the hall is empty, and the victim hasn't checked in yet. She arrives that evening, alive and on schedule. Both schedules.

items.title: Encounter (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A pilot radios that a mountain is descending out of the clouds toward him — his last transmission, because mountains don't do that. The search party finds what's left, and something extra. The series notarizes the whole file.

items.id: S2E30THEPETERHURKOSSTORYPT1/S2E30 - THE PETER HURKOS STORY, PT 1.mp4
items.title: The Peter Hurkos Story, Part 1 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: After a fall from a ladder and a coma, a Dutch house painter shakes a hand and knows everything about its owner. Part one of the series' only two-parter.

items.id: the-twilight-zone-s-02-e-10-a-most-unusual-camera_202502/The Twilight Zone S02E09 The Trouble with Templeton.mp4
items.title: A Most Unusual Camera (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Two small-time crooks steal a camera that photographs what hasn't happened yet, and take it straight to the racetrack. The Zone's cleanest lesson in greed, and the camera never lies.

items.title: The Twilight Zone: Season One (DVD Collection)
items.description: Thirty-six first-season episodes: lonely men, granted wishes, small towns with flexible geometry. American television's strangest institution arrived already finished.

items.title: Nick of Time (The Twilight Zone)
items.description: Ridgeview, Ohio. Four hours until the car is fixed, a fortune machine on the table, and William Shatner asking it just one more question. Richard Matheson wrote the rarest kind of Zone episode: the trap you're free to leave at any time.

items.id: S2E31THEPETERHURKOSSTORYPT2/S2E31 - THE PETER HURKOS STORY, PT 2.mp4
items.title: The Peter Hurkos Story, Part 2 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Hurkos works with a parapsychologist and the police, touches the evidence and reads it like mail. Then the real Peter Hurkos walks on camera, the show's boldest move, resting its whole 'this is true' wager on one man's face.

items.title: Delia (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Delia is perfect, and then gone. A disillusioned man on a tropical island searches for her for eight years, and the search unravels him.

items.title: The Visitor (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Ellen summons her husband to end the marriage, and he crashes his car on the way out. Then a young man knocks: her husband's exact double, much younger. She lets him in.

items.id: thetwilightzonetvrecordings/The Twilight Zone TV Recordings/1960 The Twilight Zone S1E29 Nightmare As A Child (1988 WGN Chicago) 720p.mp4 .ia.mp4
items.title: The Twilight Zone
items.description: Assorted Zone broadcasts taped off various stations, commercials noted where they survive. Not the pristine DVD masters — the show as it actually reached people, with static and station IDs. The fifth dimension, received over rabbit ears.

items.title: Gypsy (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An escaped convict meets a gypsy on the road who convinces him the safest place he can possibly be is back inside the prison he just fled. He climbs back over the wall. The reason waiting on the outside is the episode.

items.title: Contact (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Bill Dermott's new pocket watch keeps excellent time and terrible company — a voice in his head, planning a murder in detail, on a schedule. The watch was a gift from his wife. Secondhand things come with second hands.

items.title: The Lonely Room (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A shy young man looks out a certain window and sees himself on the street below, confident, smiling, walking with a beautiful girl. A better life, visible from one room only. He goes looking for the reason.

items.title: Twilight Zone / Planet of the Apes (Fan Edit)
items.description: Someone spliced the Zone and Planet of the Apes into one transmission — which is less heresy than homework, since Serling wrote both. A fan edit reuniting the two halves of one writer's obsession with mankind flunking its own exam.

items.title: Twilight Zone: The Movie (1983)
items.description: Four directors take the Zone to the cinema, three remakes and one original story. The sharpest is George Miller putting John Lithgow on the wing at 20,000 feet, a seat Shatner once held on the series.

items.title: House of the Dead (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Hours before his ship sails for England, Lieutenant Fraser's fiancée vanishes. His search runs through Hong Kong's side streets, and everyone he meets seems to know more than they say.

items.title: Goodbye Grandpa (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Two kids lose the grandfather they loved past reason, and then the house starts producing evidence that goodbye didn't take. The gentlest kind of haunting — the kind grief orders in advance. The series, naturally, has the receipts.

items.title: The Storm (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Three years after a painter's death, his last canvas is unveiled, finished. A former classmate and her husband travel to his village to ask who held the brush. They get a cold welcome first, then a story.

items.title: Tidal Wave (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Honolulu, a tsunami bearing down, and a woman in a wheelchair alone in her house, praying for help. What turns up is an elderly, lost, stone-deaf man, and she doesn't think that was luck.

items.title: Anniversary of a Murder (One Step Beyond)
items.description: He thought he got away with it: a drunk drive home from his mistress, a boy killed, no witnesses. Then his dictaphone starts playing the boy's voice. Dictaphones only record and play back. That's the whole problem.

items.title: The Death Waltz (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A garrison flirt in 1860s New Mexico plays her suitors against each other until one of them dies of it. There's a dance at the fort anyway. He was always going to claim the waltz she promised him — the promise didn't specify alive.

items.title: The Return (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Korea: a corporal separated from his patrol is written off as dead, and somebody guides him down off that frozen ridge anyway. The unit's own records can't make the rescue arithmetic work. The show presents the discrepancy and rests.

items.title: If You See Sally (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Pa Ellis blames his daughter for her brother's death, then asks her to come home. She sets out hitchhiking. The vanishing hitchhiker is an old American road legend, and this episode gives it a family and a reason.

items.title: Moment of Hate (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A driven executive becomes convinced her anger doesn't stay in her head — that when she hates someone precisely enough, the world edits accordingly. She'd like to be wrong. Her calendar of enemies keeps thinning.

items.title: To Know the End (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Emily MacDougall starts seeing death and destruction in flashes, in wartime England, and the man she loves stands in every one. Knowing the end doesn't let her skip the middle.

items.title: The Trap (One Step Beyond)
items.description: At the edge of sleep, a man keeps slipping into someone else's life — a parallel one, running alongside his own, and lately running closer. Two tracks, one switch. The title tells you which way it throws.

items.title: The Voice (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Neighbors in a New England town stand trial for burning a barn, supposedly to kill a girl's pet raccoon. The reporter covering it doesn't buy that motive, until a small, disembodied voice starts talking to him.

items.title: The Promise (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Carl Bremer, a German ex-POW, stayed on in London after the war to work bomb disposal. With his wife about to give birth, he takes one last call, against her wishes.

items.title: Tonight at 12:17 (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Laura's pregnancy comes with a side effect the doctors don't cover: she knows things now, and all of them point at one specific minute of tonight. 12:17 means nothing to anyone else in the house. It will.

items.title: Where Are They? (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Case files instead of a story. Newland recounts rocks falling from an empty sky over Chico, California, and a stranger who showed Washington officials a fuel made from water, then vanished for good.

items.title: Legacy of Love (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Marianne Darelle is drawn to a seaside town she has never seen, where she finds a married man who was drawn there too, by something he can't explain either.

items.title: Rendezvous (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The Marines say her husband is lost at sea; she declines the information. Then, in a park, a mugger picks the wrong widow — or the right one, given who intervenes. The title is the episode's thesis: some appointments survive the obituary.

items.title: The Executioner (One Step Beyond)
items.description: 1862: a captured Confederate boy and his dog, and a Union colonel who enjoys his authority in the small, unforgivable ways. The colonel shoots the dog. The war has rules; what starts collecting on the colonel afterward doesn't.

items.title: The Last Round (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A broke prizefighter takes a visit from a fellow boxer with an old legend to share — the kind of legend that's really a warning wearing gloves. The bell rings for everyone eventually. This episode is about hearing it early.

items.title: Dead Man's Tale (One Step Beyond)
items.description: In a flophouse room, a broke newsman sleepwalks to the typewriter and produces a story he's never heard — signed by a prospector, about gold, with directions. The typing is his. The prose isn't. Ghostwriting, in the original sense.

items.title: The Sacred Mushroom (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Most of this series restages other people's stories. Here John Newland goes himself, with associates, to a remote Mexican village to test whether a rare mushroom can sharpen extrasensory perception.

items.title: The Gift (One Step Beyond)
items.description: In England, a phony fortuneteller and her rakish son rook the gullible, until the gift she has long prayed for arrives for real and startles her. Con artists know what lying looks like, and this isn't it.

items.title: Persons Unknown (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An escaped convict hides in a Mexican monastery on the one night an Aztec warrior's ghost is said to walk the halls. When a body turns up, his defense is the ghost, which is a hard thing to put on the stand.

items.title: Night of Decision (One Step Beyond)
items.description: At Valley Forge, Washington is shown a victory and, after his death, a civil war he doesn't know how to stop. The vision tale first appeared in print decades after the winter it describes.

items.title: The Stranger (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An earthquake in Asia Minor, three survivors dug from the rubble, all telling the same story: a fourth man kept them alive, and he's still down there. They dig. What the fingerprints say about the fourth man is why this episode exists.

items.title: Justice (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A man confesses to killing a child. His whole congregation swears he was asleep in a pew when it happened. The episode lets the impossibility sit there in the courtroom like a third witness.

items.title: The Face (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Since childhood, Stephen Bolt has dreamed one face — a stranger's, coming closer, lately with a knife. He's never met the man. He's certain he will. The episode is a countdown wearing a plot, and Bolt can hear it ticking better than anyone.

items.title: The Room Upstairs (One Step Beyond)
items.description: In their rented London house, Esther hears a child crying upstairs. Her husband hears the pipes. The room in question is quite specific about who's allowed to hear it — and about what it wants from her when she finally opens the door.

items.title: Signal Received (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Aboard HMS Hood in 1941, two sailors hear a radio broadcast announcing their ship sunk with heavy loss of life, while a third hears he'll live to a ripe old age. That third man turns up in the studio to tell it himself.

items.title: The Confession (One Step Beyond)
items.description: On a soapbox, Harvey Lawrence tells the street he killed a man. The flashback finds him a young prosecutor who deliberately let a defendant hang, and years later the past catches up with him.

items.title: The Avengers (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The Nazi general's château party copies one held 150 years earlier, and his guests are villagers he means to send to the camps. The original guests take a close interest in the invitation list.

items.title: The Prisoner (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Ruth Goldman survived the Nazi camps, and the German officer who oversaw her imprisonment has come to her door. She kills him. When she confesses, the examining doctor has something to add.

items.title: Blood Flower (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A carefully neutral professor sniffs a rare Latin American flower, unaware of whose blood fed it, and begins acquiring convictions that aren't his. Politics as possession. The flower just replaces the gardener.

items.title: The Sorcerer (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A German officer in the Great War hires a psychic to check on his girl back home, and the vision shows him an infidelity. So he asks for something stronger than information. Middlemen always charge handling fees.

items.title: The Villa (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A parlor hypnosis game at an Italian villa goes somewhere the medical student running it can't follow: the entranced woman screams of a girl trapped nearby. You can wake the hypnotized. Waking what they found is another matter.

items.id: one-step-beyond-the-sacred-mushroom.-best-5-episode-051-s-6qe-v-1-tw/▶ _One Step Beyond__ The Sacred Mushroom.  (Best 5 Episode)-051S6qeV1Tw.mp4
items.title: The Sacred Mushroom (One Step Beyond, Horror Host Print)
items.description: A One Step Beyond print kept on hand for horror hosts, the costumed late-night ghouls who need something eerie to introduce. With a title like that, you can see why they kept it.

items.title: Delia (One Step Beyond, Bill Sprague Collection)
items.description: A romance, a woman who may never have been there at all, and a series that swore its stories were true. This one comes from Bill Sprague's tape collection, and it works best the less you know going in.

items.title: Earthquake (One Step Beyond, Bill Sprague Collection)
items.description: The 1906 San Francisco premonition episode, preserved by a collector whose upload notes mostly concern his war with internet trolls. The bellboy sees the city fall; the uploader sees the comment section coming. Both were right.

items.id: OneStepBeyondTheRoomUpstairs/▶ _One Step Beyond__ The Room Upstairs. (rare episode).mp4
items.title: The Room Upstairs (One Step Beyond, Bill Sprague Collection)
items.description: A wife hears a child crying in the room upstairs. One Step Beyond never needed more than that: a quiet house, one person listening, and a host swearing it really happened.

items.id: BillSpragueCollectionOneStepBeyondTheHouseOfTheDead/▶ _One Step Beyond__ The House of the Dead. (rare episode).mp4
items.title: House of the Dead (One Step Beyond, Bill Sprague Collection)
items.description: The Hong Kong episode — a vanished fiancée, a frantic search, a house where the tenancy requirements are strict — via the Sprague collection, whose curator's upload note threatens trolls with this exact house. Fair enough. It has vacancies.

items.title: Earthquake (One Step Beyond)
items.description: San Francisco, 1906: the bellboy who saw it coming, the hotel full of people who wouldn't listen, Caruso on the bill. Uploaded with the simple instruction 'no complaints please.' The bellboy tried complaining too. See how that went.

items.title: Epilogue (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A newly sober man, a son under a collapsed hillside, and a rescue guided by something his sponsor never covered. The episode where the series argues that belief isn't optional once the evidence starts digging.

items.title: Goodbye Grandpa (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Grandfather dies; the children he adored refuse to finalize the paperwork of grief — and the house appears to side with the children. A haunting so gentle it barely raises its voice. It doesn't need to. It's family.

items.id: OneStepBeyondHouseOfTheDead/One Step Beyond - House of the Dead.mp4
items.title: House of the Dead (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Departure day in Hong Kong, a fiancée missing, and a search that narrows to one house the locals won't name twice. Lieutenant Fraser goes in, because love is not a superstitious institution. The house appreciates that about him.

items.title: The Bride Possessed (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A new bride starts describing a place she has never been. Months before The Twilight Zone opened its door, this show walked through one and swore it was real.

items.id: OneStepBeyondTheBurningGirl/One Step Beyond - The Burning Girl.mp4
items.title: The Burning Girl (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Luana Anders as a teenager everyone calls a firebug — new town, cruel aunt, and fires that start when her distress peaks, always just out of arm's reach. She never holds the match. That's rather the point.

items.title: Brainwave (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A corpsman with no surgical training, a dying captain, and a doctor's voice on the radio walking him through the incision — a voice whose provenance falls apart under review. Wartime radio carried many signals. The series kept this one.

items.title: The Dark Room (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A photographer in France, a rented flat, and a model who keeps turning up without appointments. What the developer bath reveals is between them and the chemicals. One Step Beyond, as ever, insists it's true.

items.title: The Dream (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Wartime England, a marriage under the Blitz, and a dream that carries operational intelligence it has no right to. From the series that treated the sleeping mind as an unlicensed radio receiver. Filed, as always, under documented.

items.title: The Last Round (One Step Beyond)
items.description: January 1961: a washed-up boxer, a visitor from the fight game, and a legend about the ring that insists on a rematch with reality. The bell you hear at the end of this one wasn't rung by anybody in the building.

items.title: The Riddle (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A train through India, a beggar, and a husband gripped by murderous certainty about a stranger he cannot possibly know. One Step Beyond tells it as a case, sworn true.

items.title: Delusion (One Step Beyond)
items.description: His blood could save a dying girl, and he says no, because every donation shows him the recipient's future and he is tired of watching. A gift that is the whole problem.

items.title: One Step Beyond: Public Domain Episode Collection
items.description: A bundle of cases from the show that ran three seasons on one promise: everything you're about to see was reported by somebody, somewhere, as true. The copyright lapsed. The claim never did.

items.id: OneStepBeyondLegacyOfLove/One Step Beyond - Legacy Of Love.mp4
items.title: Legacy of Love (One Step Beyond)
items.description: She's never been to this seaside town, but her feet know the turns, and the married man at the end of the route has been waiting without knowing for what. Two strangers with matching déjà vu. Somebody left them the feeling in a will.

items.title: Persons Unknown (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A convict, a monastery, the one night a dead Aztec warrior is said to hold the corridors — and a murder for which the only living suspect blames the legend. The episode weighs his story with a straight face. So does the coroner.

items.title: The Navigator (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A sailing ship finds her course altered overnight and a soaked, silent stowaway below decks. They clap him in irons. The new heading is what nobody can explain, and it is the better mystery.

items.title: The Aerialist (One Step Beyond)
items.description: After the accident, one trapeze artist still flies and the other never will again. The guilt goes up with him every night. Circus people don't say haunted. They say 'off tonight.'

items.title: The Inheritance (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A cruel countess, her gigolo, her timid maid, and a necklace that passes between them. One Step Beyond swore every story it told was true, and this one is about who ends up holding the box.

items.title: The Mask (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Shot down over the Sahara, Lt. Wilenski walks out of the desert alive — and his rescuers can't stop staring at what he brought back instead of a sunburn. March 1960 broadcast. The desert takes payment in unusual denominations.

items.title: The Tiger (One Step Beyond)
items.description: A new governess sends the beloved nanny packing and gives a little girl a punishment room in the basement. Her one friend is a tiger nobody else can see.

items.title: Anniversary of a Murder (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Hit-and-run, no witnesses, a year of getting away with it — then the office dictaphone starts playing back a recording nobody made. Machines don't hold grudges. They hold recordings, which is worse.

items.title: Call From Tomorrow (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An actress climbing back from a breakdown hears her dead daughter's voice in the house — not an echo of the past but a call with a purpose, timed to the minute. January 1960 broadcast. Some calls come collect, from ahead.

items.title: Contact (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The antique pocket watch was a lovely anniversary gift. It keeps time, and it keeps something else — a voice in the new owner's head, rehearsing a murder that hasn't happened. May 1960 broadcast. Wind it at your own risk.

items.title: Esther and Emily (One Step Beyond)
items.description: An episode of One Step Beyond, filed on this tape as Esther and Emily, from Uncle Earl's Classic TV vault. The series presented every case as documented and left the explaining to you.

items.title: Ordeal on Locust Street (One Step Beyond)
items.description: The respectable house on Locust Street has a locked room and a son nobody mentions. The hypnotist who offers to treat him asks for total darkness and no interruptions. The family grants both, which tells you how long they've been desperate.

items.title: The Day the World Wept: The Lincoln Story (One Step Beyond)
items.description: Lincoln dreams of a coffin in the East Room and a guard telling him who died. His friend Ward Hill Lamon wrote the dream down years later, and historians still argue over whether it happened.

items.title: Vanishing Point (One Step Beyond)
items.description: She walked into the spare room during the argument and the room declined to return her. The murder trial collapses without a body; the house's rental history doesn't. From Uncle Earl's Classic TV Channel — a floor plan with an appetite.

items.title: RetroVision Theater Presents: One Step Beyond
items.description: A homegrown retro showcase that checks out early for the family holidays, but not before sharing some One Step Beyond episodes. Little framing, plenty of enthusiasm. The stories do the rest.

items.title: The Best of One Step Beyond: Season One
items.description: First-season highlights in one long sitting, where the formula is clearest: a steady host, a story sworn true, nothing explained. John Newland plays it like the world's calmest claims adjuster.

items.title: Patriotic Popeye
items.description: Famous Studios stopped making Popeyes in 1957, and this is one of the last: a Fourth of July where the lawn is a flag and the nephews have fireworks. Story by Caryl Meyer.

items.title: Private Eye Popeye
items.description: Olive Oyl plays the femme fatale, which is a stretch the cartoon commits to, and Popeye plays gumshoe. Tom Johnson and Frank Endres animated it, so the deerstalker was in good hands.

items.title: Shuteye Popeye
items.description: Popeye snores, the mouse in the bedroom wants sleep, and the two go to war over it with dresser drawers, a hose and a policeman at the window. In the end Popeye is the one with his fingers in his ears.

items.title: Popeye: I Don't Scare
items.description: Tom Johnson and Frank Endres animated this one, and Winston Sharples wrote the music, so the Friday the 13th jinx is in competent hands. Bluto does the rest of the haunting.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Fiddlesticks
items.description: Ub Iwerks's first cartoon after leaving Disney, and the first Flip: a frog at the piano and a violinist mouse in red shorts who resembles Mickey's original concept, Mortimer Mouse.

items.title: Woody Woodpecker: Pantry Panic
items.description: The third Woody Woodpecker cartoon: he stays north against the groundhog's advice, winter freezes the swimming hole mid dive, and a hungry cat has the same idea about the kitchen.

items.title: Popeye: Taxi-Turvy
items.description: Famous Studios made 125 Popeyes, and in this one Bluto's idea of a taxi business is taking the other taxi's money. Tom Johnson and Frank Endres animated it.

items.title: Betty Boop: Snow White
items.description: The Queen consults her mirror, Betty Boop is sent out into the snow, and ends up in a glass coffin carried by small men. A ghost and a skeleton get the big number to themselves. Seven minutes.

items.title: Betty Boop: Minnie the Moocher
items.description: Cab Calloway voiced the ghost and was rotoscoped to dance it, and in 1994 the cartoon was voted number 20 of the 50 Greatest Cartoons ever. Betty only wanted to leave home.

items.title: Popeye: Fright to the Finish
items.description: Al Eugster and William B. Pattengill animated this one and Winston Sharples scored it, so the haunted house at least has a good soundtrack. Somebody in a bedsheet is working hard.

items.title: Popeye: Ancient Fistory
items.description: The title puns on history, and the story is Cinderella with the roles handed out to the Popeye cast. Robert Connavale did the scenics, so the kingdom looks the part.

items.title: Popeye: Big Bad Sinbad
items.description: Popeye takes his nephews to the Nautical Museum and tells them how he beat Sinbad, the greatest sailor in the world, on an island. The museum statue gets swapped. "And that's why I'm the greatest sailor in the world." Five minutes.

items.title: Superman: The Mechanical Monsters
items.description: A mad scientist sends giant robots after a fifty million dollar jewel exhibit, banks and a museum. Lois Lane is in the way. Superman takes it personally. The Daily Planet has the headline by the end. Ten minutes.

items.title: Mighty Mouse: Wolf! Wolf!
items.description: Wolves set a table for three, find a cleaver and begin. Help drops in from the sky wearing a cape and announcing "Here I come to save the day," which at this address is both a theme song and a promise.

items.title: Superman: Electric Earthquake
items.description: The seventh Superman cartoon, and the first to come out and say that all of this has been happening in Manhattan. To mark the occasion, a mad scientist tries to shake the island loose.

items.title: Color Classic: The Cobweb Hotel
items.description: The spider who manages the Cobweb Hotel is voiced by Jack Mercer, and his guests are newly married flies. It came out on May 15, 1936. Nobody has left a review.

items.title: Casper the Friendly Ghost: There's Good Boos Tonight
items.description: Casper finds a book called Animal Friends, follows its advice into the dark and settles on a fox cub he names Ferdie. The title riffs on Gabriel Heatter's radio sign off, "There's good news tonight."

items.title: Betty Boop and Grampy
items.description: Grampy makes his first appearance here, on August 16, 1935, an eccentric inventor of Rube Goldberg labor saving devices, and he introduces himself by mail. The gang is invited.

items.title: Felix the Cat: The Goose That Laid the Golden Egg
items.description: One of only three Felix cartoons Van Beuren made in 1936, a revival of a cat who had been around since 1919. The goose is kidnapped by Captain Kidd, which is a very reasonable pirate plot.

items.title: Gabby: All's Well
items.description: A diaper, a baby and Gabby, who is not equal to the job. David Tendlar and William Nolan animated it, and Sammy Timberg wrote the music. The baby has given neither a review.

items.title: ComiColor: Jack Frost
items.description: A young grizzly would like to see winter rather than sleep through it, and Old Man Winter finds out. Carl Stalling did the music, and the short came out on Christmas Eve.

items.title: Hector's Hectic Life
items.description: Hector gets blamed for a mess three puppies made, and nobody asks the dog. Story by Joe Stultz and Larry Riley. The channel finds Hector not guilty.

items.title: Noveltoon: Naughty But Mice
items.description: Bill Turner and Larry Reilly wrote the story, which sends a city mouse in a straw hat to teach the country mice about a cat. Dave Tendlar and Al Eugster animated the smoke.

items.title: Betty Boop: Betty Boop's Rise to Fame
items.description: A newspaper man asks Fleischer how many drawings make a cartoon. Twelve to fourteen thousand, he is told. Betty turns up on the drawing desk and the two look back over her career.

items.title: Betty Boop and the Little King
items.description: A king in the royal box is only supposed to watch, and Betty Boop is working the ring with a horse. This audience has other ideas. Her series had three years left.

items.title: Grampy: Be Human
items.description: Grampy's labor-saving devices are of the Rube Goldberg variety, and this time the labor being saved is the animals'. The farmer is introduced to the invention in person.

items.title: Betty Boop's Big Boss
items.description: Betty works for a boss who chases the help. The police are called, a crowd answers a Girl Wanted sign on the top floor, and a ladder gets involved. It ends in a hug and a shadow.

items.title: The Talking Magpies
items.description: John Foster wrote the story and Philip A. Scheib the music, and two magpies talk over all of it. Moving in is easy. Being liked takes longer.

items.title: Betty Boop for President
items.description: Betty Boop's opponent is a man called Mr. Nobody, which is the most honest candidate any ballot ever had. Both of them sing the platform, because in cartoons that is what a platform is.

items.title: Betty Boop: Betty in Blunderland
items.description: Betty's Wonderland comes by way of a jigsaw puzzle, and Shrink-Ola is the best product name on the whole channel. Nobody in Wonderland has ever read a label first.

items.title: Betty Boop: The Old Man of the Mountain
items.description: A beard down to the ankles is the old man's entire personality, and the cartoon builds a mountain around it. Cab Calloway and his orchestra supply the hot number, and Betty supplies the running.

items.title: Betty Boop: Chess-Nuts
items.description: In chess the game is always longer than you planned, and this cartoon shows the cost: beards and spiders. Bimbo and Betty are pieces on the board, and they have views.

items.title: Pudgy: Happy You and Merry Me
items.description: Pudgy is the errand boy this time, carrying a note from Betty to the drugstore. Trouble arrives as a cat and her kittens, which beats a villain. Betty's series had three years left.

items.title: Little Audrey: Goofy Goofy Gander
items.description: Story by I. Klein, music by Winston Sharples, and a Mother Goose who personally shows Audrey around. Comic book crooks are the only part the nursery rhymes did not plan for.

items.title: Betty Boop: Stop That Noise
items.description: A hammock in the country is Betty Boop's cure for city noise, and the country supplies a coyote who is no quieter than the traffic. The cartoon suggests insomnia travels.

items.title: Betty Boop: Musical Mountaineers
items.description: Betty runs out of gas in the mountains and knocks at a cabin full of hillbillies. They have rifles, a stove and a lot of questions. Betty answers with a song.

items.title: Betty Boop and Grampy: House Cleaning Blues
items.description: Grampy builds labor saving devices of the Rube Goldberg variety, so Betty's mountain of dishes becomes an engineering problem. The soap was not consulted.

items.title: Betty Boop: Poor Cinderella
items.description: Betty plays Cinderella in colour, a redhead in rags. A fairy godmother turns a pumpkin into a coach and warns her about the clock. "Remember, remember, remember."

items.title: Betty Boop and Pudgy: Training Pigeons
items.description: Betty keeps pigeons on the roof of her tenement building, the kind of detail a cartoon of this era delivers without comment. Pudgy fancies himself a hunting dog about it.

items.title: Betty Boop: Judge For a Day
items.description: Betty, who cleans the courthouse, dreams on the bus that she is the judge, and the sentences fit the crime. A thoughtless smoker learns about second hand smoke, and an impersonator gets Tarzan and the Shadow in his ears.

items.title: Betty Boop and Little Jimmy
items.description: Betty needs rescuing from her own exercise equipment, and the only help to hand is Little Jimmy, who is easily confused. In cartoon terms, that makes it a fair fight.

items.title: Little Lulu: Bargain Counter Attack
items.description: Lulu's department store havoc takes a crew: animation by Nick Tafuri, John Walworth and Tom Golden, music by Winston Sharples. The section manager had no crew, and it shows.

items.title: Betty Boop's Crazy Inventions
items.description: Grampy, the series' resident inventor, does not turn up until 1935. In 1933 Betty has to make do with a trade show of other people's doodads, and an umbrella is the best exit.

items.title: Betty Boop and Pudgy: Not Now
items.description: Pudgy takes the night shift on the rooftops while Betty sleeps, chasing a black cat with great seriousness. Nobody asked him to, which is the best kind of guard dog.

items.title: Betty Boop: Parade of the Wooden Soldiers
items.description: Rubinoff and his orchestra provide the music, which is a great deal of music for a toy department. The stuffed gorilla did not get the memo about staying on the shelf.

items.title: Betty Boop: Swat the Fly
items.description: The villain is a fly, and the cartoon treats it as a siege. Pudgy joins the defence and takes most of the damage, which was always going to be the dog's job. Nap earned.

items.title: Willie Whopper: The Air Race
items.description: Ub Iwerks, who animated Plane Crazy by himself, mostly in secret, was apparently still thinking about planes. Willie Whopper's air race has a locomotive with wings.

items.title: Betty Boop: Morning, Noon and Night
items.description: Betty Boop made 90 theatrical cartoons between 1930 and 1939, and this one is organised like a timetable, with a black cat and a very small chick getting in the way of it.

items.title: Betty Boop: A Song a Day
items.description: Grampy first turned up in August 1935, and by this one he is already being consulted as a professor. In a hospital full of animals, a specialist is the right call.

items.title: Betty Boop: She Wronged Him Right
items.description: Betty is the girl in peril at the Tanktown Theatre, where a top-hatted villain and a mortgage arrive right on schedule. Nobody in this house asked for novelty.

items.title: Betty Boop: The Impractical Joker
