items.description: The point of this one is Grampy's Rube Goldberg treatment for a practical joker, and the house takes part. Anyone who has been pranked will find it a satisfying remedy.

items.title: Betty Boop: I Heard
items.description: A live orchestra opens the show, then comes Betty Boop's tavern, a mine and a very long way down. The cellar is haunted by more ghosts than the cartoon strictly needs. Thunder and screaming are involved.

items.title: Betty Boop: Whoops! I'm a Cowboy
items.description: Betty Boop will only marry a bronco buster, so the man in love does the sensible thing and enrols at a dude ranch. Cartoon courtship has always been a matter of qualifications.

items.title: Betty Boop: Baby Be Good
items.description: Betty Boop made 90 theatrical cartoons, and this is the one where her entire audience is a baby who will not sleep. The strategy is a bedtime story, which is every parent's strategy.

items.title: Betty Boop: The Scared Crows
items.description: Betty Boop left the screen in 1939, and the uploader rates this as her best that year. A house full of lively crows is a good way to go out, with Pudgy on barking duty.

items.title: Betty Boop: Mother Goose Land
items.description: Betty Boop reads Mother Goose in bed, wishes herself into the book and is taken at her word. Humpty Dumpty and an enthusiastic spider await. "Jack fell down and broke his crown."

items.title: Betty Boop with Henry, the Funniest Living American
items.description: The funniest living American, per the title, needs a puppy and takes a job in Betty Boop's pet shop to earn one. The monkey and the birds make the working day long.

items.title: Betty Boop: Betty Boop's Ker-Choo
items.description: Betty enters the big car race under the weather and wins anyway, a result most of us would take. Bimbo and Koko are entered too and cannot match a sneeze like that.

items.title: Betty Boop: The Candid Candidate
items.description: Grampy runs for mayor with Betty Boop on the stump, and wins by exactly one vote. Then he has to do the job. Six minutes, and it covers most of what there is to know about politics.

items.title: Betty Boop: Is My Palm Read
items.description: A fortune teller wants Betty Boop to himself and shows her things in a crystal ball. It goes badly: a desert island, a jungle full of ghosts and a hollow log over a cliff.

items.title: Betty Boop: More Pep
items.description: Uncle Max draws Betty Boop and Pudgy out of an inkwell. Pudgy is tired, so Betty draws him a pep machine. It works on the whole city, which is a lot of city. "You gotta have pep."

items.title: Popeye for President
items.description: The race is an exact tie, so the presidency comes down to Olive Oyl, as everything does. Popeye and Bluto campaign with chores, since policy was never their strength.

items.title: Popeye: Spree Lunch
items.description: Wimpy wants lunch and Popeye runs the diner. Jumping beans, a magnet and a rival cook get involved. Wimpy ends up at a table of ham and cake. "I will gladly pay you Tuesday."

items.title: Popeye: Nearlyweds
items.description: Olive Oyl has been in the strip since 1919, nearly ten years before Popeye showed up, so by 1956 the engagement is overdue. Bluto, naturally, files an objection.

items.title: Popeye: A Haul in One
items.description: Olive Oyl is moving house and Popeye and Bluto both volunteer to carry. One sofa, one piano and a lot of towels later, somebody is tied to the back of the truck. "Watch me pack."

items.title: Popeye: Little Swee'Pea
items.description: Nobody asked Swee'Pea whether the zoo was a good idea. He crawls off to find the elephant, and Popeye has to take on an elephant and a crocodile in the baby's honour.

items.title: Popeye: Insect to Injury
items.description: Popeye has a fence and a house to keep, and a swarm of insects with ideas of their own. The fence and the plumbing do not survive. It ends at a small measuring glass.

items.title: Popeye: I'm in the Army Now
items.description: Bluto was invented for a single comic strip story, and here he is in line at the recruiting office with Popeye anyway, because the fight needs somewhere to go. Olive Oyl has a stake in the outcome.

items.title: Superman: The Arctic Giant
items.description: Superman cartoons ran on $30,000 a short, and a good share of it seems to have gone on a monster thawing out of the Arctic. Bud Collyer is the voice, as ever.

items.title: Popeye: The Paneless Window Washer
items.description: Popeye and Bluto compete for the privilege of washing Olive Oyl's windows, which means a skyscraper, a scaffold and a very long way down. Bluto finishes face down on a cash register.

items.title: Snow Foolin'
items.description: Animals take up winter sports and fall over in all of them. Then the bouncing ball arrives for a Jingle Bells sing along, and a turtle comes round with hot coffee.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Bold King Cole
items.description: A king brags that he is afraid of nothing. The ghosts of his castle take that as an invitation. Felix is in the room and mostly watches. "We're not afraid at all."

items.title: Superman: Destruction Inc.
items.description: Saboteurs, a coastal gun, a TNT truck and a clock stuck at twelve. Lois Lane gets the story and Superman gets the truck. Eight minutes of things very nearly exploding.

items.title: Superman: Secret Agent
items.description: A woman carries a briefcase the spies badly want, and the road to the airport has a bridge in it. Superman winds up on the Capitol steps and the cartoon finishes on a flag.

items.title: Superman: The Bulleteers
items.description: Police headquarters is flattened by a car shaped like a bullet, so Lois Lane is on the story before the dust settles. Superman, voiced by Bud Collyer, who also played him on radio, is on the car.

items.title: Popeye: Bride and Gloom
items.description: Popeye and Olive Oyl plan their wedding, and Olive dreams ahead to the children: four small sailors, a baby at the harp and a staircase that gets used as a slide. The plans change.

items.title: Casper: The Friendly Ghost
items.description: The first Casper cartoon, from a children's book manuscript of the late 1930s. He wants a friend, and everyone runs, even the man who came about the mortgage.

items.title: Bugs Bunny: The Wabbit Who Came to Supper
items.description: Friz Freleng directed, Mel Blanc and Arthur Q. Bryan did the voices, and Uncle Louie wrote a will no hunter could keep. Bugs reads the fine print with pleasure.

items.title: Superman: Showdown
items.description: The headline says Superman is a criminal, and Bud Collyer, who voiced him, gets to sound wronged. Lois Lane is at the typewriter, so the story will be told.

items.title: Superman: The Mummy Strikes
items.description: A narrator explains a pharaoh and his twelve year old son, a box from the catacombs gets opened, and a mummy gets up. Lois Lane ends the cartoon wrapped in bandages. Fire everywhere.

items.title: Superman: The Magnetic Telescope
items.description: A man builds a magnetic telescope, pulls a comet toward the city and takes the warnings as criticism. "The pull of gravity will bring it crashing to Earth any minute!" is the cartoon's one reasonable line.

items.title: Herman: Cheese Burglar
items.description: It takes one mouse with a taste for cheese to get a cat and a dog working as a team, which is a better result than most treaties get. The kitchen takes the damage.

items.title: Hep Cat Symphony
items.description: Noise complaints in this house are handled by a cat, and the mice in the walls have formed an orchestra. It is hard to argue with either of them, although the cat tries the drum.

items.title: Bugs Bunny: Falling Hare
items.description: Bugs reads up on gremlins at an army air field and scoffs. A gremlin with a mallet takes the remark badly and follows him into the bomber. Altitude is involved. So is a bomb with a face.

items.title: Popeye: Customers Wanted
items.description: Two penny arcades side by side is a bad idea for everyone but the pennies, and Popeye and Bluto prove it. This is one of the 108 Popeyes Fleischer Studios made.

items.title: Superman: Billion Dollar Limited
items.description: A train carrying gold runs at night with gangsters in black cars chasing it, and Superman is there to see the train aimed at the sky. Thirty thousand dollars bought every short in the series after the first.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: A Swiss Trick
items.description: Tom and Jerry get across the Alps on a contraption, which is how the Alps should be done, and play for the tavern on the way. The mountains have no opinion of brass.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Neptune Nonsense
items.description: Van Beuren Studios brought Felix back for a brief three-cartoon revival in 1936. Here he is doing right by a goldfish, which is a decent use of nine lives.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Piano Tooners
items.description: Tom and Jerry are hired to tune pianos, and tune is the generous word: the job is mostly disassembly. The mice, at least, play along.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Pencil Mania
items.description: Tom and Jerry wander through a world of drawings that move: ostriches, a vegetable chorus singing "We have no bananas today", a strongman and a car on a spring. It ends with a chase down a country road.

items.title: Daffy Duck: Book Revue
items.description: Daffy Duck has dressed for the occasion: a bookshop, after hours, and he picked a very purple suit. In a place where everyone judges a book by its cover, that is a decision.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Rocketeers
items.description: The Royal Experimental Society fires off a rocket and Tom and Jerry go with it, into the sea. They meet a sea monster, a skeleton with a fishing rod and a ballroom of mermaids. The society is not as lucky.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: A Spanish Twist
items.description: The pair end up in Spain with no plan and a dancer, which is the plan of most cartoons set in Spain. The bull ring has a chorus line, an idea no real arena has had.

items.title: Little Lulu: Bored of Education
items.description: Lulu and Tubby fall into their American history book, sail with Columbus and watch a soldier run for his life. Back in class the teacher has fallen asleep. History carries on without him.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: A Fireman's Life
items.description: Also titled Hook & Ladder Hokum, which describes this fire department better. Tom and Jerry run it with a checkerboard, a very tall horse and a hose that rears up like a snake.

items.title: Felix the Cat: April Maze
items.description: Felix's name combines feline and felicity, and a picnic with his nephews tests the second half. The weather, for one, is not interested in felicity.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: In the Bag
items.description: A thousand dollar reward turns the Old West into a stage show for Tom and Jerry. The tuba is the one thing that does not belong, and it is the only part that has a tune.

items.title: Betty Boop: So Does an Automobile
items.description: Betty Boop's final year gave her a hospital for sick automobiles, which sounds like a retirement plan. The print is good, the sound very good and the picture a little small, says its uploader.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Pots and Pans
items.description: Every cartoon kitchen has the same labour problem: the food files its own complaints. Tom and Jerry run this lunch wagon for customers who want soup, and a train they never ordered.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Soda Squirt
items.description: Flip the Frog runs a drugstore soda fountain, and it does not survive the lunch rush. A bruiser, a cherry pie and a great many customers later, the shop is rubble. It is his last cartoon.

items.id: LittleOrphanWillie1930FlipTheFrogSoundCartoon/Little Orphan Willie 1930 Flip The Frog Sound Cartoon.mp4
items.title: Flip the Frog: Little Orphan Willie
items.description: Ub Iwerks planned a series for a character called Tony the Frog and ended up with Flip, who here takes in a baby a stork left behind. It is 1930, so nobody asks for references.

items.title: ComiColor: Balloon Land
items.description: Ub Iwerks directed this one, with Billy Bletcher credited as the actor. A world made entirely of balloons has exactly one natural predator, and the Pincushion Man is it.

items.title: Casper the Friendly Ghost: Spooking About Africa
items.description: Casper, one of 55 Friendly Ghost shorts, spends this one fixing an elephant's sneezing: Wheezy has blown the feathers off a peacock and the monkeys out of their perches.

items.id: TheFreshVegetableMystery/Fleischer cartoon Color Classic The Fresh Vegetable Mystery 1939) (old cartoon public domain).mp4
items.title: Color Classics: The Fresh Vegetable Mystery
items.description: The detective is a potato, which is the right choice for a force that has to look at a lot of eyes. Color Classics ran to 36 shorts, and this is the one with the vegetable kidnapping.

items.title: Daffy Duck & Egghead
items.description: Egghead is a prototype Elmer Fudd and just as bad at ducks, which gives a barely recognizable Daffy the whole short to torment him. A duel in the reeds settles nothing.

items.id: BimbosInitiation_201802/Betty Boop Bimbo's Initiation 1932 HD Grim Natwick Fleischer Studios.mp4
items.title: Bimbo's Initiation
items.description: Bimbo meets the Mystic Order of the Koo-Koo-Ma-Hatcha, whose chant is Do It or Die, in a cartoon from July 1931. Billy Murray voices Bimbo, and Mae Questel is Betty.

items.title: The Milky Way
items.description: Rudolf Ising directed this, and on his watch the Milky Way holds every kind of milk, Milk of Magnesia included. The kittens do not check the label. Neither would you, at that age.

items.id: TheMuseum1930TobyThePupSoundCartoon/The Museum 1930 Toby The Pup Sound Cartoon.mp4
items.title: Toby the Pup: The Museum
items.description: Every cartoon museum comes alive after hours, and Toby the Pup chose to be there for it. The exhibits get the music and the large hairy dog gets the bad mood.

items.title: Gabby: Swing Cleaning
items.description: Gabby, the town crier of Lilliput, helps clean the castle and has strong views on how it is done. Brooms, buckets and one cuckoo clock are involved. "That looks better than it did before!"

items.title: Cubby Bear: Croon Crazy
items.description: Cubby Bear's radio show has no guests, so he is every guest. It is a one bear variety hour, and the title suggests the voices were the point.

items.title: Fantasies in Color: The Snowman
items.description: Furry animals of the far north build a snowman and throw snowballs at it. He takes it personally. He comes to life, towers over them and sits down at an ice piano. The ending has a rainbow.

items.title: Silly Symphony: Winter
items.description: Winter in the woods, told without a word. A deer skates, a raccoon fishes through the ice, a bear goes sliding, and a great deal of snow falls on all of it. Seven minutes, dark and quiet.

items.title: Noveltoon: Much Ado About Mutton
items.description: A wolf eyes three sheep, a billboard promises a trumpet band and a small lamb in red keeps getting in the way. Explosions help. Seven minutes of Western town and bad intentions.

items.title: The Betty Boop Limited
items.description: Betty, Bimbo and Koko take the Betty Boop show on the road, by rail. The train runs late, the passengers are large, and the garter gets its own close-up. "Come on, Betty, hurry up, we're late."

items.title: Popeye: Toreadorable
items.description: Bluto keeps the ticket booth at the bullring and the bull keeps its own counsel. Popeye ends up in the ring, and in a matador's suit. Bluto ends up on the bull. Six minutes of dust.

items.title: The Little King: Christmas Night
items.description: The Little King has everything but company, so he spends Christmas with two tramps. The cartoon agrees with him, which is the kindest thing it does. Santa drops in and nobody complains.

items.title: We're in the Money
items.description: Warren and Dubin wrote the song and Rudolf Ising had a department store sing it in 1933, when the title was either optimism or a sick joke. It plays as both.

items.title: Somewhere in Dreamland
items.description: The first Color Classic in three-strip Technicolor, and Fleischer spends the new colour on a Christmas dinner. Two hungry children dream it and the local merchants make it real.

items.title: Christmas Comes But Once a Year
items.description: Grampy only arrived in 1935, in a Betty Boop cartoon, and a year later he was running Christmas for some sad orphans. The channel calls that a promotion.

items.title: The Shanty Where Santa Claus Lives
items.description: Santa's guest list has one name on it and it belongs to a poor boy. The channel can think of no better use of a North Pole invitation, and neither could Santa.

items.title: Foxy: Smile, Darn Ya, Smile!
items.description: Rudolf Ising directed this one for Warner Bros., and Foxy's answer to every problem on the line is to sing at it. Even the billboards cheer up, which is more than the streetcar company could hope for.

items.title: Popeye: Cooking With Gags
items.description: Bluto plays tricks on Popeye and Olive on April Fool's Day. A picnic basket, a brick grill, a beehive and a canoe are involved. Spinach has the last word.

items.title: Popeye: Assault and Flattery
items.description: A clip show with a courtroom around it: Bluto and Popeye each present scenes from their own earlier cartoons as evidence. By then there was no shortage of exhibits.

items.title: Popeye: Parlez Vous Woo
items.description: Famous Studios made Popeye cartoons until 1957, and this is one of the late ones. The International offers Olive a Magnificent Kiss, capitals included, and Popeye has spinach.

items.title: Jerky Turkey
items.description: Tex Avery tells the story of the first Thanksgiving as if it happened in 1945, which is when he made it. The Pilgrims queue for cigarette rations. The turkey deals on the black market. History teachers should not use this one.

items.title: Popeye: Out to Punch
items.description: Bluto trains for a boxing match with a punching bag and a hard run. Popeye is rushed to the ring in a car and gets there, just. The rest is between the ropes.

items.title: Popeye: Floor Flusher
items.description: Olive has a leaky faucet and Popeye fixes it with what he can find, while Bluto wrecks the basement pipes. A piano, a flood and a can of spinach are involved.

items.title: Popeye: Gopher Spinach
items.description: Popeye tries four different ways to get rid of one gopher, and the gopher's reply is a good deed. Pests in cartoons rarely have such manners.

items.title: Popeye: Greek Mirthology
items.description: Popeye's four nephews will not eat their spinach, so he tells them about his ancestor Hercules. A bearded rival, a tightrope over a canyon and a patch of spinach follow. Ice cream for everyone.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Jolly Fish
items.description: Tom and Jerry go fishing over a stage full of pianos and a lobster with a love life. The title card says Dick and Larry, the name the Van Beuren pair were given in the 1950s.

items.title: Heckle and Jeckle: Sno Fun
items.description: Somebody dumpster diving for books found this Terrytoon on a DVD and uploaded it, so Heckle and Jeckle's stint with the Mounties reaches you by way of a bin.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Gold Rush Daze
items.description: The narrator is a gas station attendant with a captive customer, which is the best audience a tall tale can have. The gold gets bigger every sentence.

items.title: Little Audrey: The Lost Dream
items.description: Little Audrey goes to bed and into Dream Land. A cat-like companion walks her down Dream Street to a stage door, then past a sign that says Danger Keep Out. A large beast is behind it. She wakes up.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Beauty and the Beast
items.description: Too many snacks past bedtime, and the Sandman does the rest. In Toyland the girl is welcomed with a song until the book opens and a beast comes out. A cannon is the cartoon's solution.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Barnyard Bunk
items.description: These are Van Beuren's Tom and Jerry, not the cat and mouse, and the Archive notes the series was later renamed Dick and Larry. The farm has the Depression. They have saxophones.

items.title: Baby Huey: Quack-A-Doodle-Doo
items.description: The first Baby Huey cartoon: a very large egg hatches a very large duckling, and the other ducklings want nothing to do with him. When a fox comes looking for supper, his size finally has a use.

items.title: Color Classics: All's Fair at the Fair
items.description: A country couple visit the World's Fair and marvel at the modern wonders. Machines flatten cars, saw logs and shave customers, and robot hands do the rest. Everyone ends up dancing.

items.title: Goofy Goat Antics
items.description: A goat plays the accordion to a hall of animals, with a scowling cat and a toothy caterpillar waiting in the wings. Ted Eshbaugh made it as "Goofy Goat", and the color print, if there was one, is lost.

items.title: Gabby: Gabby Goes Fishing
items.description: Gabby promises a small boy he will show him how fishing is done. The fish has plans of its own. A boat, one very large splash and Gabby is the one who gets caught.

items.title: Gabby: Fire Cheese
items.description: Gabby offers to help the fire department, which is the sort of offer fire departments learn to dread. He is the town crier, so all of Lilliput will hear about it.

items.title: Dancing on the Moon
items.description: Color Classics ran to 36 shorts, and this is the one where the honeymoon is on the moon. It's 1935, and nobody can check the lunar scenery, so the studio goes all out.

items.title: Porky Pig: Boom Boom
items.description: Beans, the cat Warner pushed alongside Porky in the mid-1930s, gets a long stretch beside him and a great many bandages. The studio kept the pig and quietly let the cat go.

items.title: Nursery Scandal
items.description: Mother Goose falls for a scarecrow and the rest of the storybook has opinions, in a Van Beuren take that spices up the folk tale cast. The goose is not amused. She has a point.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: The Tuba Tooter
items.description: A small town band needs a tuba and one arrives by boat. Dancing breaks out in the street, then a crowd, then a police wagon. Tom and Jerry end up riding inside the tuba.

items.title: Little Dutch Mill
items.description: Fleischer's second Color Classic is Hansel and Gretel with a miser for the witch, a village so tidy you could eat off it, and a pretend blind man counting his coins. The series was a bid to keep up with Disney.

items.title: The Sunshine Makers
items.description: Gnomes bottle sunshine as milk and deliver it by dragonfly. Goblins in top hats cannot stand it and march on the village. The gnomes answer with bottles. "I don't want to be happy."

items.title: Mickey Mouse: The Barn Dance
items.description: The third Mickey Mouse cartoon ever released. He takes Minnie to a barn dance, a bigger rival turns up, and Mickey ends the night on the floor. Everybody starts somewhere.

items.title: Chicken A La King
items.description: A Mae West style duck turns the sultan of the chickens' head, and a duck in a green cap objects. The flock joins in. It is the 17th Color Classic, made to compete with Silly Symphonies.

items.title: Peeping Penguins
items.description: Four baby penguins and an empty hunter's cabin are a combination no parent wants to hear about. They try the phonograph first, which is the sensible instinct.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: Plane Crazy
items.description: Mickey builds an airplane out of whatever the farm had lying around and takes Minnie up for her first flight. There are loops, a cow and a great deal of falling. Mickey lands among stars.

items.title: Bosko: Big Man from the North
items.description: Bosko is a Mountie sent into the snow to bring in a wanted man. He gets as far as the saloon piano. The fugitive eventually leaves the building wearing considerably less than he arrived in.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: The Gallopin' Gaucho
items.description: The second Mickey Mouse cartoon produced and the second published, so at least this one kept its place. He rides in on an ostrich, which is a confident way to be number two.

items.title: Aladdin and His Wonderful Lamp
items.description: Ub Iwerks animated Mickey's earliest cartoons before striking out alone, and his own studio spent years on fairy tales like this one. A beggar proposes to the princess; the palace objects.

items.title: The Little Stranger
items.description: A chick hatches in a duck's nest and cannot do any of the things ducklings do. The tenth Color Classic, made when Fleischer was trying to keep up with Disney.

items.title: Superman: The Underground World
items.description: Superman shorts after the first got $30,000 apiece, and this one spends it underground. It came out on June 18, 1943, with Lois on the expedition and Clark conveniently elsewhere.

items.title: Superman: Volcano
items.description: Thirty thousand dollars was the budget of a Superman short after the first, and this one spends it on a volcano on the island of Monokoa, a plan to steer the lava into the sea and a woman on a cable over the lava.

items.title: The Song of the Birds
items.description: A boy with a new gun learns what it is for from a family of robins, who turn out to be better teachers than most. The channel advises a handkerchief and a long breath.

items.title: Play Safe
items.description: The title is the moral, and the boy skips it entirely. The dog is the only one in the cartoon who sees the second train coming. The channel recommends never starting a locomotive.

items.title: Humpty Dumpty
items.description: A kitchen of eggs is menaced by the Bad Egg, who has a top hat, a moustache and a stove. Humpty Dumpty and his sweetheart take it personally. Several eggs end up in a frying pan.

items.title: A Car-Tune Portrait
items.description: A hand draws a lion on a blank page and the lion walks out to conduct an orchestra of animals. A cat plays the xylophone by standing on it, and the monkeys line up along one long pipe.

items.title: Color Classics: Educated Fish
items.description: The class is on fishing: hooks, worms and a frying pan, all diagrammed on the blackboard. One young fish was looking elsewhere. The lesson is repeated, live, with a real hook.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: Hawaiian Holiday
items.description: Mickey and Minnie throw a beach party with Donald, Goofy and Pluto. Goofy meets a surfboard, Donald meets a pond, and Pluto meets a turtle with opinions. The bees are a late addition.

items.title: Popeye the Sailor
items.description: Popeye reads that he is a movie star, takes Olive Oyl to the carnival and finds Bluto already there. The sideshow is brief. The chase ends in a train wreck, with Popeye standing on top of it.

items.title: Screen Songs: Little Brown Jug
items.description: A Screen Song about woodland creatures and a lot of cider. Turtles carry jugs, elephants dance and pigs sing the title song, with the words on screen for anyone at home.

items.title: Color Classics: Little Lambkins
items.description: A toddler sabotages the electric washer, the ironing robots and the rest of the new house until his parents move back to the country. It is the 31st of the 36 Color Classics, and a little weird, as the plot suggests.

items.title: Color Classics: The Playful Polar Bears
items.description: The 26th of 36 Color Classics, and the one where the hunters come to the bears' home and not the other way round. The channel's sympathies are with the bears.

items.title: Bosko: The Booze Hangs High
items.description: Nickelodeon cut the moment the father pig brings up a corncob, flicks off the one kernel left and posts it back in through a trapdoor. That is the moment to wait for.

items.title: Ding Dog Daddy
items.description: A yellow dog tries every way over, under and through a garden wall to get to a poodle, and the bulldog on the other side does not approve. A bottle gets involved. It ends in a ruin.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Fox Pop
items.description: Chuck Jones frames the whole thing as a fox explaining himself to two birds, so the radio is smashed before we learn why. By the end of the sob story you are on the fox's side.

items.title: Red Riding Hood
items.description: Harry Bailey and John Foster directed this version, where the wolf is big and bad and still loses to a grandmother on jazz tonic. Dinner bell or wedding bells is the question.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: The Mad Doctor
items.description: Pluto is strapped to the machinery and Mickey, who has no plan, goes in anyway. The mad doctor built a whole castle and forgot to lock the door.

items.title: Toonerville Trolley: Trolley Ahoy
items.description: Mr. Bang bets ten dollars that the Toonerville Trolley will not reach the main line on time. A tornado joins the race. The trolley gets there, and somebody still wants his ten dollars.

items.title: Toonerville Trolley: Toonerville Picnic
items.description: The doctor said seashore, peace and quiet, for the nerves. Mr. Bang goes and announces he came for exactly that, and a rough sea, a trolley and a house that floats off take it as a dare.

items.title: Buzzy Boop
items.description: Buzzy Boop takes a train to a house full of children and a dog, and a barrel, a fence and a lasso get involved. Black and white, mostly music, and very little explanation.

items.title: Little Boy Blue
items.description: A wolf in overalls takes an interest in Little Boy Blue's sheep. A haystack, three ostriches and a snowy cottage get in his way, and he ends up wound around a tree on springs.

items.id: GoopyGeer1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Goopy Geer 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Goopy Geer
items.description: Goopy Geer plays a party from the piano. A cow eats spaghetti, a flamingo wears a tutu and three cats wait on their soup. The piano takes it hardest.

items.id: EatinOnTheCuffOrTheMothWhoCameToDinner1942/Eatin' on the Cuff or The Moth Who Came to Dinner (1942).mp4
items.title: Looney Tunes: Eatin' on the Cuff
items.description: A man at a piano tells the story of a moth who moves into a gentleman's vest. A spider with a cackle takes an interest. In the end they build a nest and live on the cuff.

items.title: Woody Woodpecker: The Barber of Seville
items.description: Woody sings Rossini's Largo al Factotum, the Shaving Song, to customers who only came in for a haircut. The real barber is out getting his physical, the plot's one excuse.

items.title: Reg'lar Fellers: Boy Meets Dog
items.description: A boy and his dog from the Reg'lar Fellers comic strip, then a bed, then a court of gnomes with a stenographer and a judge under a mushroom. Nine minutes, mostly wood and wallpaper.

items.title: Small Fry
items.description: The lesson in this one is for Tommy Cod, who has quit school for the pool hall. He's a fish. It's a pool hall. They knew what they were doing.

items.title: Sinbad the Sailor
items.description: Sinbad sails out, meets a pirate captain with a sword and lands on an island with a gorilla and a very large bird. The ending involves an explosion and a pile of treasure.

items.title: You Don't Know What You're Doin'!
items.description: A conductor, a pig on a tricycle, a theatre packed with animals and a black cat who dances with great commitment. The finale involves a small car and a cliff edge.

items.title: Hollywood Capers
items.description: Beans gets past the studio guard disguised as Oliver Hardy, after W.C. Fields and Charlie Chaplin go through ahead of him. Everyone in Hollywood is a caricature here, Beans included.

items.title: ComiColor: Don Quixote
items.description: A man reads too many books about knights and rides out on a horse that has seen better days. Windmills, a dragon, a wizard at a piano. It ends in a padded cell, which seems fair.

items.title: Screen Song: Marriage Wows
items.description: Bertha and Edgar are the ones getting married, but the singing is your job: the words to "For Me and My Gal" go up on screen and the woods have turned out. Everyone is expected to join in, you included.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: A Corny Concerto
items.description: A bald conductor in a tailcoat introduces two waltzes. A small pig hunts a rabbit through a purple forest to one. A black duckling gets the other. "And now we will present the beautiful Blue Danube."

items.title: Heckle and Jeckle: Steeple Jacks
items.description: The Archive's uploader calls this "a rather OK copy", which is more than the bulldog foreman can say of his day: two magpies, a girder and a long way up.

items.title: ComiColor: Old Mother Hubbard
items.description: The king's number, "Though I'm a king, it don't mean a thing," is Duke Ellington's swing standard in a crown. Ub Iwerks put the whole nursery rhyme to swing; even the bare cupboard has rhythm.

items.title: ComiColor: The Headless Horseman
items.description: The legend of Sleepy Hollow, adapted from Irving. A lanky schoolmaster, a plump rival and a farmer's daughter share a sofa and a dinner. A clock has a face. The horseman is on his way.

items.title: Betty Boop: M.D.
items.description: Betty sells Jippo from a medicine wagon, and the poster lists stopping breathing among the benefits. The Archive's uploader says it isn't in the Betty Boop listings; an older friend called it rare.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: A Day at the Zoo
items.description: A narrator walks the audience through a zoo and reads out every cage. A keeper has the monkeys to see to, the owl is wise, and the lion has the last word. "Of course, you all know how fast they multiply."

items.title: Looney Tunes: Ain't Nature Grand!
items.description: A cheerful round-headed fellow wanders a meadow where a bird goes after a worm, spiders line up and a dragonfly carries a long pole. It ends with a fountain of bugs. Nature is grand, as promised.

items.title: Bugs Bunny: The Wacky Wabbit
items.description: A prospector with a pickaxe digs holes across the whole desert looking for gold, and a rabbit keeps coming up in them, calm, with a carrot. By the end the gold is in somebody's teeth.

items.title: Betty Boop: Halloween Party
items.description: The uploader found this one on an old film reel at their grandmother's, which is the best provenance a Halloween cartoon could have. Betty throws the party and the guests let themselves in.

items.id: UbIwerksComiColorMarysLittleLamb1935/Ub Iwerks Comi-Color - Mary's Little Lamb (1935).mp4
items.title: ComiColor: Mary's Little Lamb
items.description: Mary takes her lamb to school, which is against the rule. The teacher chases it around the blackboard, the desks and a globe while the class watches. Ub Iwerks supplies the colour and the lamb supplies the trouble.

items.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: The Merry Old Soul
items.description: The uploader found this one in an encrypted box on a DVD, which is how a good rabbit cartoon should be stored. A dentist's chair is an unlikely door to a castle, and it works.

items.title: The Black Duck
items.description: A black duck among white ones draws opinions, then a cat, a caged rabbit and a fox arrive to add to them. The uploader had been told it was rare and had never seen it either.

items.title: Aesop's Fables: A Toytown Tale
items.description: Van Beuren's toy shop has a band that plays itself, which saves on musicians and is a fine arrangement for everyone but the musicians. A tin villain with a trunk spoils the mood.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Moonlight for Two
items.description: Merrie Melodies began as a way to plug songs Warner Bros. owned, so the banjo, fiddle and jug are the commercial. A stove has opinions, a gun gets involved, and two dogs shake hands, more ending than a jingle needs.

items.title: Noveltoons: Sudden Fried Chicken
items.description: Herman is better known for outwitting Katnip the cat, so managing a rooster is a change of pace. The poster says $1,000 for one round, and the order is ring, bar, hospital. Nobody said the plan was good.

items.title: Popeye the Sailor
items.description: Popeye's first cartoon was officially a Betty Boop, which makes this carnival a guest spot he outgrew fast. Olive Oyl and Bluto are already in place, along with the fight that will run for decades.

items.title: Bosko: Sinkin' in the Bathtub
items.description: Where Looney Tunes began: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising's Bosko, a harmonica, a wagon and a very long downhill ride, in the cartoon that started Warner Bros.' cartoon line. The cow is the best supporting player.

items.title: Betty Boop: Be Up to Date
items.description: A travelling department store is a sound business plan in a town that has never seen an appliance, and Betty Boop runs it. The uploader reports this one was missing from the site.

items.title: Rainbow Parade: Molly Moo-Cow and the Butterflies
items.description: A butterfly collector in a top hat comes through the meadow with a net, and Molly Moo-Cow does not approve. She grows wings of her own, gets the butterflies out, and leaves wearing a cape of petals.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Texas Tom
items.description: Tom turns cowboy at a dude ranch, guitar included, to impress a lady cat. This copy still has the smoking scene that censors cut elsewhere, according to the uploader.

items.title: Aesop's Fables: Dizzy Day
items.description: A day of drilling in bearskin hats goes the way cartoon drills always go, which is sideways. Van Beuren Studios made it, and the guards' discipline ends at the first zebra.

items.title: Bimbo: The Herring Murder Case
items.description: Bimbo plays detective in a deerstalker, with a gorilla and a widow among the suspects. The widow performs in the Betty Boop manner, and Koko the Clown turns up too.

items.title: Screen Songs: Just a Gigolo
items.description: Max Fleischer invented the bouncing ball in his Ko-Ko Song Car-Tunes, and here it is years later keeping a cabaret in time. Irene Bordoni sings, and you are expected to follow.

items.title: Betty Boop: A Hunting We Will Go
items.description: Bimbo started out as the star of the Talkartoons, and here he is toting a gun while Betty Boop supplies the conscience. Somebody noticed this one was missing from the Archive and fixed that.

items.title: Betty Boop: Ha! Ha! Ha!
items.description: Betty Boop plays dentist and the laughing gas gets loose. A meter climbs from groans to hysterics, then the clock, the mailbox and the car start laughing too. "Don't make me laugh!"

items.title: Betty Boop: Admission Free
items.description: Betty runs the change booth at a penny arcade, so admission is free but the machines are not. Somebody found this one missing from the site and put it right.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Land of the Midnight Fun
items.description: Tex Avery sends up the travelogue: a cruise to the Arctic and a narrator who treats swordfish and skating girls as geography. The ship goes out on parade and comes back in heavy fog.

items.title: ComiColor: Summertime
items.description: Ub Iwerks made a series of shorts about the seasons, imaginative pictures of abstract ideas, and the uploader hopes to post the others. Summer's forecast here is a sun with a bad temper.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: Clock Cleaners
items.description: Mickey, Donald and Goofy are sent to clean the town clock tower. Donald loses a fight with the mainspring, a stork objects to the nest, and Goofy goes out on a ladder. The tower wins.

items.title: ComiColor: The Valiant Tailor
items.description: ComiColor Cartoons ran to twenty-five shorts, mostly fairy tales, in the two-color Cinecolor process. A tailor against a giant is the genre's idea of a protagonist.

items.title: Screen Songs: Kitty from Kansas City
items.description: Rudy Vallee stands at a railway station and sings about a girl who weighs two forty three. The bouncing ball keeps time. Trains, cliffs and a very large woman do the rest.

items.title: Betty Boop: Red Hot Mamma
items.description: Betty Boop goes to bed and wakes up in hell. It starts hot, passes through a freshman devil orientation, and ends with ice on everything, her bedroom included.

items.title: Prest-O Change-O
items.description: Someone asked for this one by name, and the uploader found it in a stash of old YouTube downloads. A magician's house is a very good place for a dog to be out of his depth.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: Giantland
items.description: Mickey tells his nephews how he beat a giant, and the telling is clearly doing most of the work. He lands in the coffee, which is the part you would leave out if it were true.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Ceiling Hero
items.description: A narrator introduces modern aviation: a flying log cabin, skywriting for hot dogs, a pilot chasing a record on an altimeter that reads to 200,000 feet. Ambulances turn up in the desert.

items.title: Simon the Monk: Monkeydoodle
items.description: Simon the Monk rides a drooping elephant through the jungle, stops at the Sto-Mack Gas station and falls out with a tiger. The jungle phone is a pay station. Eight minutes of rubber limbs.

items.title: Gerald McBoing-Boing
items.description: Dr. Seuss wrote Gerald as a record story, UPA drew him flat and stylish, and the cartoon won an Oscar. A boy who speaks in sound effects finds out the town has a radio station.

items.title: Screen Song: Ain't She Sweet?
items.description: Screen Songs were distributed by Paramount from 1929 to 1938, and the ball bounced the whole time. Here it follows a woman in a leopard print dress. Sing, do not wait to be asked.

items.id: 1932FleischerScreenSongWhenTheRedRedRobinComesBobBobBobbin/1932 Fleischer Screen Song-When the Red Red Robin Comes Bob Bob Bobbin.mp4
items.title: Screen Song: When the Red Red Robin Comes Bob Bob Bobbin' Along
items.description: Harry Woods wrote the song, and the Fleischers added the bouncing ball and a cannon marked Tapeworm. The woods go dark for the singalong, and the birds carry the worm off between them.

items.id: 1934FleischerScreenSongLetsAllSingLikeTheBirdiesSing/1934 Fleischer Screen Song-Let's All Sing Like the Birdies Sing.mp4
items.title: Screen Song: Let's All Sing Like the Birdies Sing
items.description: Max Fleischer invented the Follow the Bouncing Ball technique, and a song about birdies is a fair test of it: the ball has to land and the whole room has to sing.

items.id: 1934FleischerScreenSongThisLittlePiggyWentToMarket/1934 Fleischer Screen Song-This Little Piggy Went to Market.mp4
items.title: Screen Song: This Little Piggy Went to Market
items.description: Singin' Sam sings a nursery rhyme to a Quick Show Theatre that has just sat through a newsreel of silly headlines. Screen Songs made the audience the chorus, so do not just sit there.

items.title: Screen Song: Popular Melodies
items.description: A small painter draws what the song asks for. A man with a guitar sings it in live action, Betty Boop is drawn on a board, and a horned face fills the screen near the end.

items.id: 1932FleischerScreenSongIAintGotNobody/1932 Fleischer Screen Song-I Ain't Got Nobody.mp4
items.title: Screen Song: I Ain't Got Nobody
items.description: Four men in suits sing about having nobody while a television dial flips between cartoons: a mounted moose, a cat with a horn, a cat in a bad mood. The bouncing ball keeps the words.

items.id: 1931FleischerScreenSongByTheLightOfTheSilvryMoon/1931 Fleischer Screen Song-By the Light of the Sil'vry Moon.mp4
items.title: Screen Song: By the Light of the Silvery Moon
items.description: The moon reaches into a radio first, which is a lot of ambition for a song about moonlight. Max Fleischer invented the bouncing ball, and by now it is working on every word.

items.title: Little Lulu: Cad and Caddy
items.description: Lulu's fee is one lollipop, and the golfer's mistake is forgetting he agreed to it. Revenge is her department, and the title leaves no doubt who the cad is.

items.title: Screen Songs: The Stein Song
items.description: Rudy Vallee was one of the guest stars Screen Songs became known for, and he sings the whole thing while the ball keeps time. Five fish join the chorus, which you can do too.

items.id: 1930FleischerScreenSongInTheGoodOldSummertime/1930 Fleischer Screen Song-In the Good Old Summertime.mp4
items.title: Screen Songs: In the Good Old Summer Time
items.description: Max Fleischer invented the bouncing ball for his Ko-Ko Song Car-Tunes, and by this one it has a whole summer to cross. Sing along, no one is listening.

items.id: BoskoAndHoney1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Bosko and Honey 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Bosko and Honey
items.description: Bosko and Honey, a piano, a violin, a bicycle and a house that rains indoors. Seven minutes of the two of them being chased around their own furniture. Honey wears the bow.

items.title: Mickey Mouse: Fiddling Around
items.description: Mickey plays the violin on a stage, with a spotlight and a shadow that does not quite match him. The violin fights back. He finishes in a heap on the floor, but he finishes.

items.title: Daffy Duck and the Dinosaur
items.description: The sign says There is no substitute for duck, and it is the cartoon's whole philosophy. Daffy gets the title billing and the caveman gets the appetite.

items.title: Flip the Frog: The New Car
items.description: Flip gets a car, and it is very small and has opinions about corners. A policeman has a word, a few parts come off, and the last scene is a railroad track. Seven minutes of mechanical bad luck.

items.title: Baby Huey: Pest Pupil
items.description: Baby Huey is expelled from kindergarten, a letter says so. The grown-ups try a piano lesson and a chemistry set. A whale gets involved. He finishes in a mortarboard.

items.title: Screen Songs: Little Annie Rooney
items.description: A bouncing-ball sing-along about Annie Rooney, her sweetheart and a birthday cake with too many candles. Betty Boop turns up as a statue in the corner. "Soon we'll marry, never to part."

items.title: Pluto's Purchase
items.description: Mickey does not tell Pluto the sausages are a gift for Butch the bulldog, so when Butch tries to take them, Pluto guards them with everything he has. A faithful delivery and a poor briefing.

items.title: Bosko's Party
items.description: Bosko throws a party and finds out how much of his house can move. Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising keep the guest list short and the furniture lively.

items.id: TheQueenWasInTheParlor1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/The Queen Was in the Parlor 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Merrie Melodies: The Queen Was in the Parlor
items.description: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising took "Old King Cole was a merry old soul" at its word and built a whole castle around it. The dog in the suit of armour is a separate matter.

items.title: Betty Boop: Crazy Town
items.description: Most Betty Boop collections leave this one out, and Crazy Town is about the only place a missing cartoon would feel at home. Bimbo and Betty arrive by handcar.

items.id: BettyBoopYoureNotBuiltThatWay1936H264AAC360p/Betty Boop - You’re Not Built That Way (1936)_H264_AAC_360p.mp4
items.title: Betty Boop: You're Not Built That Way
items.description: The Archive sums it up as trying to be something one cannot be, which is the life of a small dog. Pudgy takes it up with a bigger dog, and Betty Boop supervises.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: Lady, Play Your Mandolin!
items.description: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising built a whole cafe around one request to a mandolin player. The fuzzy waiter works the room, and he is the best thing in it.

items.title: Heckle and Jeckle: Out Again, In Again
items.description: Heckle and Jeckle have been in jail before, and the title says they expect to be back. Escape by train is a good plan, and the cartoon makes sure it is not a perfect one.

items.title: The Wizard of Oz
items.description: A twister takes Dorothy off to Oz, where her name is spelled out in toy blocks, the guards are shaped like eggs and the wizard has a throne room to himself. A hen lays the finish.

items.title: Screen Songs: Let Me Call You Sweetheart
items.description: A woman in a window sings it straight and the words bounce along underneath. In between, Betty Boop waits on a bench, a baby is cross and a mustache is furious. Then a cat bears down on some chicks.

items.title: Merrie Melodies: A Great Big Bunch of You
items.description: A junk wagon unloads and the pile comes to life. A man in checked trousers plays a piano the size of a barn, toy soldiers march, three of him dance in cages and it all ends back in a heap.

items.title: Bosko: Bosko's Store
items.description: The telephone is the villain here: every order Bosko takes costs him another corner of the shop. Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising keep a song in reserve for the end.

items.title: Mighty Mouse: A Fight to the Finish
items.description: Oil Can Harry ties Pearl Pureheart up before the first cheer, because Mighty Mouse, who began as the Superman spoof Super Mouse, only arrives when called. The narrator begs you back next week.

items.title: Circus Capers
items.description: A circus parade, a lion who needs convincing, a barrel marked powder and a clown mouse who would like a word with a certain lady mouse. Near the end, a large duck and her ducklings walk in.

items.id: BoskosDogRace1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Bosko's Dog Race 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Bosko's Dog Race
items.description: A sign offers five thousand dollars to the winner of a dog race. Bosko has a large, droopy dog and a great deal of confidence. Training is brief and physical. A loudspeaker calls the race.

items.id: FreddyTheFreshman1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Freddy the Freshman 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Freddy the Freshman
items.description: Freddy goes to college in a car that is more of a suggestion. There is a pep rally with a brass band, a football team much larger than he is, and a stadium full of people who expect something.

items.title: Hold Anything
items.description: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising made this one, and every girder in it keeps time to the music. Building sites have never been so well rehearsed, or so unlikely to pass an inspection.

items.id: BoskoAtTheZoo1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Bosko at the Zoo 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Bosko at the Zoo
items.description: Bosko and a girl bike to the zoo. The aquarium has a very angry fish, a snake looks up, a porcupine objects and an ostrich sits on her nest. Then a gorilla gets loose and the crowd gets involved.

items.title: Betty Boop: Jack and the Beanstalk
items.description: The uploader says a cow smoking a cigar got this one banned. Bimbo climbing into the clouds, a giant's spaghetti, and Betty in his kitchen asking for split pea soup apparently passed.

items.id: DumbPatrol1931HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Dumb Patrol 1931 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Dumb Patrol
items.description: A small pilot takes a small plane to a war and meets a very large plane with a grin. In between he finds a grand piano standing in a ruined house, and plays it.

items.id: BoskoTheLumberjack1932HughHarmanRudolfIsing/Bosko the Lumberjack 1932 Hugh Harman, Rudolf Ising.mp4
items.title: Bosko the Lumberjack
items.description: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising put Bosko in the forest beside a lumberjack twice his size, and the odds are what you would think. The bear in the cabin has views on that too.

items.title: Bugs Bunny: Operation Rabbit
items.description: Wile E. Coyote, "Super genius", builds a dome shaped device at his workbench and sends it into the desert. Bugs Bunny waits with a carrot and is not worried. There are crates of dynamite. There is a crane.

items.title: Big Hearted Bosko
items.description: Hugh Harman and Rudolf Ising's Bosko is confident about the ice, the dog and, we assume, the large black cat at the door. The fishbowl has no such confidence.

items.title: Tom and Jerry: Tight Rope Tricks
items.description: At the circus a ballerina, a monkey, an elephant, a lion and two men in suits share a tent. The tightrope walker is the draw. The elephant ends up carrying the piano and everyone who was near it.

items.title: Bosko the Doughboy
items.description: Bosko holds a muddy trench with a bayonet, a leaky roof and a very large friend who is afraid of everything. A round black shell turns up at the end. Nobody takes it personally.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Galloping Fanny
items.description: The Fanny of the title seems to be Fanny Lou, the iceman's horse, who has eloped with Cubby Bear's: the best excuse any jockey ever had. The race goes ahead anyway.

items.title: Cubby Bear: How's Crops?
items.description: Whole crops vanish overnight and the Farmers Gazette offers a reward. Cubby Bear takes the case, which involves a wolf in a top hat, a Bean Dept with three doors and a long run of watermelons.

items.title: Aesop's Sound Fables: The Haunted Ship
items.description: Waffles and Don climb into a sunken ship run by a skeletal Davy Jones, furnished with turtles who sing Sweet Adeline and have had a few. Skeletons salute. Somebody plays the piano.

items.title: Cubby Bear: World Flight
items.description: The world, as drawn for Cubby Bear: a pagoda here, a dome there, a map to join them. It is the most accommodating globe on the channel, and the flight is over before the popcorn.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Love's Labor Won
items.description: Cubby Bear's courtship has frogs for a choir, a swan for an audience and a snail for a stagehand. It is the best staffed date on the dial.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Bubbles and Troubles
items.description: Cubby Bear has to get his girl back from pirates, among soap suds, a treasure chest, a ship's cannon and one character inflated like a balloon. The ship's wheel changes hands.

items.title: Cubby's Stratosphere Flight
items.description: Stratosphere flights were front-page news, so Cubby Bear takes one and lands at the North Pole, where a polar bear plays an ice piano. The house he left behind has a worse day.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Fiddlin' Fun
items.description: A chariot race for a bear on bicycle wheels is the right kind of anachronism for an arena with a turnstile at Gate Z. The pig fiddles regardless, which is professionalism.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Sinister Stuff
items.description: A villain in a top hat tempts Cubby Bear's girl with gum, "Kiss me, and I'll buy you gum." There is a bank, a wanted poster, a tandem for four and a sawmill log with Cubby tied to it.

items.title: Rainbow Parade: Spinning Mice
items.description: A boy lets a horde of mice into a girl's doll house, and one of them speaks, which is where the playroom ends and the cartoon begins. A bearded gnome with cages of mice is its idea of a follow-up.

items.id: molly-moo-cow-and-rip-van-winkle-van-beuren-1935/Molly Moo-Cow and Rip Van Winkle (Van Beuren 1935).mp4
items.title: Molly Moo-Cow and Rip Van Winkle
items.description: Molly Moo-Cow wanders in on a bowling party of dwarfs and stays for the beer. A cow is not what the legend of Rip Van Winkle had in mind, and Rip is the one who loses sleep.

items.title: Pastry Town Wedding
items.description: A town built of cake holds a wedding, and its recipe for one is "a teaspoon full of love and a tablespoon of money". The proportions are the most realistic thing here. This copy is a 16mm dub.

items.id: parrotville-old-folks-1935-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/Parrotville Old Folks (1935) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: Parrotville Old Folks
items.description: Rainbow Parade was Van Beuren's colour series, and Parrotville was where it kept its old folks. A draught blows snow in, a clock sprouts tiny workmen, and the monkey takes all of it personally.

items.id: parrotville-post-office-1935-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/Parrotville Post Office (1935) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: Parrotville Post Office
items.description: A Black Parrot holds up the Parrotville post office, and a postmaster, a mail sack and two small parrots deal with him. The kids collect the $5,000. Van Beuren closed its studio the next year.

items.id: rag-dog-1935-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/Rag Dog (1935) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: The Rag Dog
items.description: Kittens, a bowl of milk, a Scottie in a red sweater and a stuffed spotted dog that gets dragged into things. By the end all of them are crowded around the milk, some of them in it.

items.title: Cubby Bear: The Nut Factory
items.description: Cubby Bear is called in to find missing dentures, and the answer is a squirrel industry that needed something to crack nuts with. Industry always finds a way.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Barking Dogs
items.description: It's 1933, so the villain is a mortgage. It is signed A. Wolf, who keeps a desk, a nameplate and several sacks of money. Cubby Bear takes two very long dogs round to see him about it. The cartoon knew its audience.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Fresh Ham
items.description: Cubby Bear runs a vaudeville agency and plays piano while he waits for acts: a top-hatted duck, a long-necked opera singer, some stretchy clowns. The wreath that reads SUCCESS ends up in the trash.

items.id: the-parrotville-fire-department-1934-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/The Parrotville Fire Department (1934) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: The Parrotville Fire Department
items.description: Burt Gillett left Disney after Three Little Pigs to run Van Beuren's cartoons. In his Parrotville the fire department plays cards until the bell, and the hose is the longest thing in town.

items.id: cubby-bear-e-03-the-last-mail-1933/Cubby Bear E03 - The Last Mail (1933).mp4
items.title: Cubby Bear: The Last Mail
items.description: Cubby Bear drives a sleigh pulled by squirrels through a snowstorm to deliver the last mail. Along the way: a general store, a violin, a bird with a Red Cross flag and a tree house with a skull on the door.

items.title: The Merry Kittens
items.description: The dog is the real star here: well-meaning, patient and acting as protector to three kittens who take unfair advantage. Anyone who has ever babysat will recognise him.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Cubby's Picnic
items.description: Cubby Bear takes his girl on a picnic with a beer barrel, a brass band, a boat and a whale. "Love is the popular pastime." The day ends with the two of them in a barrel marked SAND.

items.title: Aesop's Fables: Rough on Rats
items.description: An uploader calls this one pretty cute, and the channel will not argue: three kittens keep a store and the rats move in. The Archive says it is one of the later Aesop's Fables.

items.id: toonerville-trolley-1936-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/Toonerville Trolley (1936) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: Toonerville Trolley
items.description: The Skipper has a morning train to meet and a trolley with other ideas. A cow, a bull, a mud hole and a large woman in an apron all get involved. The bulletin board says the train is due next week.

items.id: bird-scouts-1935-van-beuren-studios-rainbow-parade-short-cartoon/Bird Scouts (1935) Van Beuren Studios Rainbow Parade Short Cartoon.ia.mp4
items.title: Rainbow Parade: Bird Scouts
items.description: A black cat takes an interest in the Bird Scouts, the way cats traditionally do. Scouting is all about being prepared, which makes this troop a bad choice of prey.

items.title: The King's Tailor
items.description: A ComiColor fairy tale from Ub Iwerks, scanned from a Castle Films 16mm print the uploader admits was not very good; some of the shakiness is his own doing. A small tailor, a large king, flies with spears.

items.title: Willie Whopper: Davy Jones' Locker
items.description: Willie Whopper, the little boy with a big imagination, tells of a sea voyage that ends below. Neptune, mermaids, a pirate crew and one very large fish are all down there. A lion in a tuxedo takes the bow.

items.id: flip-the-frog-3x-03-what-a-life/Flip the Frog - 3x03 - What a Life.ia.mp4
items.title: Flip the Frog: What a Life
items.description: Flip the Frog came to cinemas through MGM, and this snowy street with a hat held out for coins is its idea of hard times. The band, at least, is not out of work.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Fire-Fire
items.description: Firemen who finish their checkers game before answering the alarm are the most believable thing in this Flip the Frog cartoon. Everything after the call is cartoon.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Funny Face
items.description: New Faces for Old is the best ad a cartoon doctor could run, since nobody has ever read the fine print. Dr. Skinnum keeps a wall of spares, and a Flip the Frog cartoon has room for all of them.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Laughing Gas
items.description: Flip was originally going to be called Tony the Frog, which would have made a dentist cartoon sound like a mob job. The gas, thankfully, is the funny kind.

items.id: flip-the-frog-3x-07-the-office-boy/Flip the Frog - 3x07 - The Office Boy.ia.mp4
items.title: Flip the Frog: The Office Boy
items.description: Flip beats four other applicants for the job, which turns out to be the easy part. The secretary runs the office, and the water cooler has an agenda of its own.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Stormy Seas
items.description: A parrot makes a sound lookout if the storm is going to talk back. Flip's ship even gets a wave with a face, and by the last scene nobody aboard seems surprised.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Bulloney
items.description: Flip the Frog was the first star Ub Iwerks built after leaving Disney, where he had drawn Mickey. Here Flip lands in a town of posters, mustaches and one bull, and several people regret it.

items.id: flip-the-frog-3x-11-the-goal-rush/Flip the Frog - 3x11 - The Goal Rush.ia.mp4
items.title: Flip the Frog: The Goal Rush
items.description: Burp U against Nertz U, final score 12 to 13, which is closer than most football cartoons let it get. A cow and a pig take the field, and the pigskin was never in on it.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Movie Mad
items.description: Flip wanders onto a studio lot, and the movies are not as keen on him as he is on them. His series ran 38 cartoons, for Celebrity Pictures and MGM, which counts as getting in.

items.title: Flip the Frog: School Days
items.description: Flip the Frog's three years on screen became Ub Iwerks's most famous work, and a school day is where you can see why. A cross teacher is only a cross teacher until the cartoon finds something funnier.

items.id: flip-the-frog-2x-02-the-soup-song/Flip the Frog - 2x02 - The Soup Song.mp4
items.title: Flip the Frog: The Soup Song
items.description: Flip the Frog ran to 38 cartoons, and this is the one where the soup is a production number. Order it, stay for the floor show and check the bowl for flies.

items.title: Flip the Frog: Circus
items.description: Flip came to sell hot dogs and the big top has other ideas. One of 38 Flip the Frog cartoons made between 1930 and 1933, which is a great deal of frog.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Felix in Hollywood
items.description: A starving actor wants to go to Hollywood, and Felix pays the fare by gumming up a town for a bankrupt shoe store, then travels as a bag. At the studio his tail becomes a cane, and Charlie Chaplin catches him at it.

items.title: Krazy Kat: The Bill Poster
items.description: Pasting posters is the easy part of Krazy's day. The hard part is his girlfriend's small brother, who turns a polite visit into an endurance test.

items.title: Krazy Kat: The Peace Conference
items.description: The cartoon's theory of diplomacy is a trick Comedy Gun in Krazy Kat's pocket. Every power scraps and nobody listens until it goes off, which as policy is cheap and as a gag works.

items.title: Krazy Kat: Piano Mover
items.description: Krazy has to get a piano to the top of a skyscraper using a winch, a pulley and a beat up horse wagon. He ends on a ledge, where Kitty arrives to sing, dance and make trouble. Moving day, in short.

items.title: Krazy Kat: The Apache Kid
items.description: Krazy is dancing with his girl at a nightclub when a hoodlum in a striped shirt carries her off. The rescue involves a sword, a dark cellar and a dance that never really stops. Seven minutes.

items.title: Krazy Kat: The Autograph Hunter
items.description: Krazy has an autograph book and a restaurant full of people who want to eat in peace. He pursues them through the dining room and the kitchen door. The plates take the worst of it.

items.title: Color Rhapsody: Mountain Ears
items.description: It is billed as a musical cartoon about a feud, which tells you the feud will be settled by tempo. A boy in a fur cap with a slingshot is the only one with a plan.

items.title: Krazy Kat: Ritzy Hotel
items.description: The Archive says Krazy meets many wild events as a bellboy, and the channel believes it: no bellboy in animation was ever paid enough. The Ritzy is no exception.

items.title: Krazy Kat: Bowery Daze
items.description: The tough guy starts trouble and the crowd settles it by committee, which is its own kind of jury. The piano plays on, the one professional in the building.

items.title: Krazy Kat: Weenie Roast
items.description: Krazy Kat takes his girl to the beach for a weenie roast. The fire has opinions, a fun fair roller coaster comes into it, and both end up in a fountain shaped like a daisy. Six minutes.

items.title: Krazy Kat: The Stork Market
items.description: This cartoon's theory of where babies come from: a machine on a cloud, storks on the payroll, and Krazy Kat covering the lunch shift alone when a rush order lands. As theories go, we've heard worse.

items.title: Krazy Kat: Krazy Spooks
items.description: On a stormy night Krazy's car dies outside an old house with a skeleton in it, and the real problem is the gorilla, who runs off with Kitty. Happy the pup found the skeleton first.

items.title: Bon Bon Parade
items.description: A boy wishes his way into candyland, where a cupcake king waits and three cherubs do the Three Stooges. The Stooges had been at Columbia about a year, so even the sugar was topical.

items.title: Fox and Crow: The Magic Fluke
items.description: The Fox leaves a nightclub act for the concert hall, and the Crow sees him off with a gift. The gift is a baton, loosely speaking. Nobody at the symphony was warned.

items.title: Fox and Crow: Punchy de Leon
items.description: The title is a pun on a famous explorer, and the quest is the fabled Fountain of Youth. Fox and Crow have never aged a day, which is the argument against needing it.

items.title: Christopher Crumpet
items.description: Christopher's argument for a rocket ship is that otherwise he will become a chicken, and what father could stand against such logic? Marvin phones the Air Force, a very reasonable response.

items.title: Color Rhapsody: The Foxy Pup
items.description: One write-up finds it vaguely anti-foxhunting and rates the Technicolor top notch. The pups chase the fox by accident, which is as much argument against the hunt as a cartoon needs.

items.title: Fox and Crow: Robin Hoodlum
items.description: John Hubley directed this Fox and Crow, and the Academy nominated it for an Oscar. It's the one where the Crow, usually the smart one, is the Sheriff and the Fox is the outlaw.

items.title: What a Night
items.description: Directed by Frank Moser and Paul Terry and released on January 25, 1935. A birthday dinner for cats turns into a haunted house visit, which is what you get for not reading the invitation.

items.title: The Baby Seal
items.description: A baby seal makes friends with a small black dog and annoys a large white one, on a beach with a doghouse and a goldfish bowl. A goat offers no help. The large dog takes it badly.

items.title: Ickle Meets Pickle
items.description: Connie Rasinski directed the last black and white Terrytoon, released on November 6, 1942, and filled it with two identical gentlemen in bowler hats who cannot agree. A fitting farewell.

items.title: Paint Pot Symphony
items.description: Two workmen on a skyscraper scaffold meet a red-crested bird with paint pots and a spray gun. By the end everyone in reach is green and the sign by the door says Wet Paint. It was accurate.

items.title: Life with Fido
items.description: Connie Rasinski directed this Terrytoons short, and its whole argument is that being adopted is not optional. Fido runs, hides and sulks. The ducks have all day.

items.title: Gaston Is Here
items.description: Gaston, a pink pencil man in a beret, works his way through a film studio, a stage, a street of trench coats, a rocket and a desert signpost. Flat colour and sharp corners. His face is in the end card.

items.title: Her First Egg
items.description: A hen and a rooster get their first egg, and a great many black birds with axes take an interest. A mouse in an airplane has other plans. Six minutes, no dialogue, one very crowded sky.

items.title: The Three Bears
items.description: Three bears, a girl in a blue bow with a violin, a piano that gets away and a man with a rifle at the door. A dog gets a drum. The bears finish in their pajamas, dancing.

items.title: The Cuckoo Bird
items.description: A cat chases a cuckoo, ends up in the Cat and Dog Hospital, and finds the bird has come along. Surgeons, students and a nurse at a switchboard are drawn into it. The cat leaves with a new opinion of clocks.

items.title: My Lady's Garden
items.description: Frank Moser and Paul Terry directed this Terrytoons short, and between them they gave a flower bed a fire brigade. Few gardens come with one. Fewer need it.

items.title: King Looney XIV
items.description: A Terrytoons revolution, directed by Frank Moser and Paul Terry, in which the oppressed are mice, the tyrant is a cat, and the cat's entire army is a trumpet. The mice bring a battering ram.

items.title: Terry Bears: Papa's Little Helpers
items.description: A father buys a television and his cubs help with the antenna, which is the oldest way to lose a Saturday. It is now a cartoon on your television, which seems fair.

items.title: The Lion's Friend
items.description: Frank Moser and Paul Terry staged the fable as a school lesson, so the audience is a class of pigs and puppies and the moral lands on them. They seem to be paying attention.

items.title: The Oil Can Mystery
items.description: A caption has to tell you how serious this is, since a villain in a top hat and checked trousers can't manage it alone. Terrytoons, directed by Frank Moser, with a girl, a cliff, a rope and a train.

items.title: Farmer Al Falfa: Noah's Outing
items.description: Farmer Al Falfa is basically Noah, with modifications, and the dinosaur on the crew is one of them. Terrytoons took the Ark seriously as a boat and as a cast.

items.title: Welcome Little Stranger
items.description: A black chick hatches into a barnyard of white chickens and the rooster takes it badly, with a great deal of smoke. Seven minutes of barnyard disapproval. The chick is the one who goes in after him.

items.title: Gandy Goose: The One-Man Navy
items.description: The idea comes from Gandy's girlfriend, who is also a goose, and Gandy takes it considerably further than she meant. A doghouse is a hull if you believe in it.

items.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: Hungry Hoboes
items.description: Oswald, whom Ub Iwerks designed at Disney's request, rides a freight and plays checkers with Peg-Leg Pete, who is his friend and his nemesis at once. It is a very specific relationship.

items.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: The Ol' Swimmin' Hole
items.description: At Disney's request Ub Iwerks designed the character who became Oswald, and the Lucky Rabbit's luck here is a no swimming sign. Oswald treats it as a rumour.

items.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: Trolley Troubles
items.description: Oswald drives a trolley full of animals, a cow stands on the line and the rails turn into a roller coaster. The passengers lean the way the track tells them to. Six minutes by rail.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: The Alaska Sweepstakes
items.description: Walt Disney created Oswald, but Universal kept the rabbit in 1928 and handed him to Walter Lantz, who has him racing sleds in Alaska. The dog does the skiing.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: The Case of the Lost Sheep
items.description: Two sheep run into the pie man and the pies lose. Oswald, standing in the wreckage, would belong to Disney again in 2006, in a deal that sent sportscaster Al Michaels to NBC.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: Doctor Oswald
items.description: A cold goes through the house and Oswald sets up as the doctor. The medicine shelf keeps Cold Cure Capsules next to 32 Caliber Bullets. Seven minutes of sneezing, bottles and a cough drop ad.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: Farming Fools
items.description: A farm run by three chimpanzees would be a poor idea outside a cartoon, and the bull is the only one in here with the standing to say so.

items.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: Confidence
items.description: 1933. A farmyard of jumpy fowl, a hen who needs a doctor, a banker in a top hat and Oswald in the middle of it with something to prove. He finishes dancing in front of the whole flock.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: Fun House
items.description: A pig runs an amusement park with a NO DOGS ALLOWED sign. Oswald's dog gets in anyway, on roller skates, past a skate adjuster and a shooting gallery. The pig is not pleased.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: The Wily Weasel
items.description: A weasel wants the eggs, and the barnyard's defence is Oswald and a farm dog who does not win every round. The title promises wily, and the channel is prepared to be impressed.

items.title: Oswald Rabbit: Everybody Sings
items.description: A tour of Birdville, on the wing, tourists welcome. A rhythm band plays at the Songbird Inn, an air raid sentry keeps watch and three crows turn up with swords. Seven minutes of song.

items.title: Oswald: The Kiddie Revue
items.description: A revue for kids is the safest kind of talent show, since nobody can be voted off. Oswald runs the Opry House, and Gladys Goose is working on a bubble as big as her ambitions.

items.title: Oswald: The Birthday Party
items.description: A telegram brings the duck quintuplets to Oswald's birthday, where a huge dog and five tiny ducklings share the floor until one bone settles it. Lantz wound down the series in 1938 and find a woodpecker by 1940.

items.title: Oswald: Music Hath Charms
items.description: Hillbilly Hollow has a bug problem and a plan to fiddle and sing its way out of it. A sign explains that hot jazz charms the savage beast. The bugs have a mushroom palace of their own.

items.title: Oswald: Slumberland Express
items.description: Oswald rides a train whose last stop is a dream, which lets the cartoon skip the part where anything has to add up. The Sandman is at the controls, so nobody can complain.

items.title: Cubby Bear: Goode Knight
items.description: Cubby Bear plays Robin Hood for a king, a princess in a pointed hat and a villain in a black cloak. A tournament, a lot of arrows and a chorus about Robin Hood. The castle walls get climbed.

items.title: Oswald: The Duck Hunt
items.description: Oswald sings 'A hunting we will go' on the way to the duck blind, which warns every duck in range. The decoys are the only ones who stay put.

items.title: Oswald: Night Life of the Bugs
items.description: The bugs of Camp Oswald put on a night fair called Bugtown Frolics: a shoot the chutes in a washtub, a grandstand on a typewriter and a caterpillar towing a matchbox wagon. A large bird in a bonnet turns up.

items.title: Oswald: The Battle Royale
items.description: Oswald signs up to fight Punchy Pig, the World's Champion Wrestler, who fills most of the screen. A referee counts, a hole opens in the ring floor, and Oswald is in it.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Feline Follies
items.description: A tomcat courts a white cat over fences and garbage cans, plays the banjo for her and is watched by a kitchen full of dancing mice. A sign promises tomorrow night at the ash can.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Felix Revolts
items.description: A silent-era walkout: the town bans cats, and Felix, whose name is feline plus felicity, leaves with every cat in the neighbourhood. The rats take over, and life isn't so great.

items.title: Felix the Cat: Skulls and Sculls
items.description: The sound was added after the fact by Jacques Kopfstein for Copley Pictures, which is why a score plays while nobody says a word. The skull chase opens much like Bimbo's Initiation.

items.title: Noveltoons: The Oily Bird
items.description: A bird would like an inchworm for supper and brings an axe, a fire pot, a vacuum cleaner and a magnet. The worm answers with a trumpet. Seven minutes of a very determined appetite.

items.id: y-2mate.is-felix-the-cat-sure-locked-homes-vj-uehi-o-5e-m-480pp-1703326720/y2mate.is - FELIX THE CAT SURE LOCKED HOMES-_VjUehiO5eM-480pp-1703326720.ia.mp4
items.title: Felix the Cat: Sure-Locked Homes
items.description: Felix spends a night in a big locked house with a spider, a web, a toy train and a shadow with opinions. A policeman arrives to settle it. The moon is out and the score does the talking.

items.title: Out of the Inkwell: Fishing
items.description: Koko was modeled on live film of Max Fleischer's brother Dave in a clown costume, so a clown fishing next to real men is a family affair. The real men are the supporting cast.

items.title: Out of the Inkwell: Invisible Ink
items.description: Every time Max Fleischer dips his pen the nib goes missing, because Koko the clown lives in the inkwell and takes it. Even erased, he comes back. Koko was modeled on film of Max's brother Dave.

items.title: Inkwell Imps: Koko's Earth Control
items.description: Max Fleischer filmed his brother Dave in a clown costume to make Koko, and here Fitz the dog is the one who goes near the lever. A sign has never stopped a dog.

items.title: Out of the Inkwell: Bubbles
items.description: Koko the clown wants bubbles, and so do the live people at the soda counter and out in the street. The bubbles get bigger than anyone planned. The print is rare and it shows, fondly.

items.title: Out of the Inkwell: The Cartoon Factory
items.description: Koko the clown meets a machine on wheels with long jointed arms that turns out toy soldiers, and the soldiers march off the page into a real room. Sound was added in the early 1930s.

items.title: Alice on the Farm
items.description: Julius finishes the milking before going after whoever took Alice, which says something about priorities on a farm. The duel afterwards needs a bucket of starch, and the cartoon is sure of it.

items.title: Alice in the Wooly West
items.description: Julius rides out showing off with a rope, bandits rob a stagecoach with Alice aboard, and the chase ends on a rock. Julius takes his fur off to fool the bad guy, then hides when Alice arrives.

items.title: Alice in the Big League (Silent)
items.description: Alice calls the game as she sees it and the stands answer in glass. Anyone who has argued with an umpire will find this a restrained response from a crowd of animals.

items.title: Silly Symphony: The Skeleton Dance
