items.description: Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole run into a crook disguised as a granny with a knitting bag. Squiddly Diddly gets mixed up with a wrestler, and Winsome Witch pitches for a team of boys. The granny has the bag and the confidence.

items.id: the-secret-squirrel-show/The Secret Squirrel Show E03 - Have Broom Will Travel.mp4
items.title: The Secret Squirrel Show: Have Broom, Will Travel
items.description: Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole take a case from the Chief, Squiddly Diddly deals with pirates, and Winsome Witch chases a man in a brown coat through a forest of colored trees. She is a witch. The trees are not questioned.

items.id: the-secret-squirrel-show/The Secret Squirrel Show E04 - Masked Granny.mp4
items.title: The Secret Squirrel Show
items.description: Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole take a case that runs through a Little Red Riding Hood wolf. Squiddly Diddly boards a ship with a captain and his cannon. The Chief files it all under routine.

items.id: the-secret-squirrel-show/The Secret Squirrel Show E05 - Show Biz Squid.mp4
items.title: The Secret Squirrel Show: Show Biz Squid
items.description: Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole chase a villain by car, then by flying carpet. Squiddly Diddly lands in a film shoot. Changing vehicles mid-chase is standard agency procedure.

items.id: the-secret-squirrel-show/The Secret Squirrel Show E06 - Prince of a Pup.mp4
items.title: The Secret Squirrel Show: Prince of a Pup
items.description: Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole confront a mad scientist in his control room, as one does. Squiddly Diddly floats through a pool day. Winsome Witch takes two kids to a castle where a prince dances with a princess.

items.id: the-secret-squirrel-show/The Secret Squirrel Show E08 - The Canvas Back Squid.mp4
items.title: The Secret Squirrel Show: The Canvas Back Squid
items.description: The Chief calls Secret Squirrel and Morocco Mole about a villain, and they go. Squiddly Diddly puts to sea. Winsome Witch helps two kids with a Cinderella story, because a witch is the obvious person to ask.

items.id: jonny-quest-e-07-calcutta-adventure/Jonny Quest E23 - The House of Seven Gargoyles.ia.mp4
items.title: Jonny Quest: The House of Seven Gargoyles
items.description: Dr. Quest and Race Bannon drive a vintage car to a mountain castle where something valuable is kept, and others have come for it too. The seven gargoyles watch, and hold their tongues.

items.title: Jonny Quest: Terror Island
items.description: A giant red lobster turns up off Hong Kong, and Dr. Quest follows it to its address: an island laboratory with a cage for every nightmare. He calls it a good lead.

items.id: jonny-quest-e-07-calcutta-adventure/Jonny Quest E25 - Monster in the Monastery.ia.mp4
items.title: Jonny Quest: Monster in the Monastery
items.description: An elderly monk in a tall yellow hat meets Dr. Quest and Race Bannon at a mountain monastery, and a large hairy beast makes it a working visit. Jonny, Hadji and Bandit watch in parkas.

items.id: jonny-quest-e-07-calcutta-adventure/Jonny Quest E26 - The Sea Haunt.ia.mp4
items.title: Jonny Quest: The Sea Haunt
items.description: Odd things start happening on the Quests' ship at sea, and the cook's cleaver is the least of it. Dr. Quest looks into who is actually aboard. Bandit follows the oil.

items.title: The Smurfs: The Astrosmurf
items.description: A Smurf in a space helmet is determined to take a rocket trip while Gargamel and Azrael lurk. The village ends up dealing with a tribe of green cave people. Gargamel is not the strangest thing in this one.

items.title: The Smurfs: Jokey's Medicine
items.description: Jokey Smurf is handing out wrapped gift boxes again, and the village is accepting them again. Gargamel gets hold of a potion and a box of his own. Smurf Village treats this as a recurring appointment.

items.title: The Smurfs: Vanity Fare
items.description: Gargamel leaves a magic mirror in the forest, and vain Smurfs line up to look. Papa Smurf has to get them back. It is Gargamel's most efficient plan to date, and it cost him one mirror.

items.id: the-smurfs-1981_202601/Season 1/The Smurfs - S01E04 - St. Smurf and the Dragon.mp4
items.title: The Smurfs: St. Smurf and the Dragon
items.description: The Smurfs meet a dragon, Gargamel catches it, and the village sets out to get it back, with his hot-air balloon in the chase. Gargamel is, as ever, the only one who thinks a dragon is a catch.

items.id: the-smurfs-1981_202601/Season 1/The Smurfs - S01E05 - The Magical Meanie.mp4
items.title: The Smurfs: The Magical Meanie
items.description: The Smurfs find a magic vase with a genie inside, and the genie is a meanie. Gargamel wants the vase, naturally. The village files a being of unlimited power under new neighbor.

items.title: The Smurfs: Sorcerer Smurf
items.description: A Smurf comes into magic powers, and Papa Smurf is concerned. Gargamel has noticed too. The village responds as it does to every development, by gathering in a field and looking up at a hill.

items.title: The Rock: Know Your Role
items.description: A Rock highlight tape from the year he took over the microphone and the crowd learned to say his lines along with him. Come for the promos. The eyebrow does a lot of the work.

items.title: USWA vs. ECW ('97)
items.description: Memphis's USWA was in its dying days when ECW's roster crashed the studio, and Jerry Lawler had to sell an invasion. One promo can't be bothered whether it's aimed at Brian Christopher or Hulk Hogan.

items.title: WWF Wrestling (January 1993)
items.description: Raw's first month, and it looks it: a small hall and a three-man desk. Hacksaw waves the flag, a fan wants Paul Bearer for mayor, and the Royal Rumble Report does the selling.

items.title: WWF Prime Time Wrestling and Superstars (July 1991)
items.description: A VHS mixtape of the WWF's two syndicated staples, cut together from the road to SummerSlam, when Hogan and the Warrior were getting ready for Slaughter's side. The tape is the Saturday morning you remember.

items.title: 'Cause Stone Cold Said So
items.description: Stone Cold Steve Austin in the year a company's boss was the villain and the crowd cheered whoever defied him. The title is the whole argument, and the tape doesn't try to improve on it.

items.title: WWF Royal Rumble ('91)
items.description: The night Sgt. Slaughter took the title off the Ultimate Warrior, and Hogan answered by winning the Rumble. A UK release, so it ends on a Middlesex post office box to write to.

items.title: XPW My Bloody Valentine ('00)
items.description: XPW was the Los Angeles promotion that took ECW alumni like Axl Rotten and John Kronus and cranked the dial. The night's best entrance is a motorcycle that won't start, and the announcer says so.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (Mar. '97)
items.description: Sid opens the show as champion, WrestleMania 13 is under two weeks off, and the Undertaker is the man coming for the belt. AAA luchadores get their turn in the ring.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (Apr. '97)
items.description: A month after Austin blacked out in Bret's Sharpshooter at WrestleMania 13 and the crowd switched sides, Raw is still sorting out its heroes. Bret ends up in an ambulance; Vince ends up alone with Austin.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (June '97)
items.description: The Hart Foundation plays Canada against the American crowd, and Steve Austin is the man everyone wants to see hit them. In between, Mankind sits for a candid interview and Sid returns to face the Undertaker.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (July '97)
items.description: Bret Hart and Brian Pillman address a crowd waving Canadian flags, and Steve Austin comes looking for the Hart Foundation. Four months on, Bret leaves the company in Montreal.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (Oct. '97)
items.description: Kane has been around two weeks and gets his red-lit entrance; Ken Shamrock suplexes through a match, and Jim Cornette delivers an editorial to camera. The Attitude Era was still warming up.

items.title: WWF Raw Is War (Dec. '97)
items.description: Three weeks after the Montreal Screwjob, D-Generation X do their Vince McMahon and Jim Ross impressions, and Rocky Maivia and Steve Austin turn up. Taka Michinoku opens with a light-heavyweight match.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (Jan. '96)
items.description: Hogan, Savage and Miss Elizabeth in Las Vegas, all on the same side. Six months on, Hogan turned heel at Bash at the Beach, and WCW never looked like this again.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (Mar. '96)
items.description: WCW before Scott Hall walked through the crowd that May: Flair and Arn close the show talking to Mean Gene like the Horsemen still run the place, and for one more Monday they might.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (June '96)
items.description: Scott Hall crashed Nitro two weeks earlier; tonight Kevin Nash walks out beside him. The third man in their threat, revealed at Bash at the Beach in July, was Hulk Hogan.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (July '96)
items.description: Nitro at Disney-MGM Studios, two weeks after Hogan turned at Bash at the Beach. Sting talks to Mean Gene; within months he'd trade the neon for black paint and a baseball bat.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (Sept. '96)
items.description: The nWo ends up at the announce desk, and why not: Nitro was early in an 83-week run of beating Raw in the ratings. Chris Jericho wrestles early, a long way from the top.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (Oct. '96)
items.description: The nWo has been coming at WCW since July, and this show opens outside the building and closes at the announce desk. Jeff Jarrett and Colonel Parker get a word in with Mean Gene between.

items.title: WCW Monday Nitro (Nov. '96)
items.description: The Monday after World War 3, with Nitro beating Raw in the ratings week after week. Piper gets in Bischoff's face, and a casket rolls to the ring.

items.title: Eastern Championship Wrestling (Feb. '94)
items.description: Still an NWA affiliate, still working a Philadelphia bingo hall, with Joey Styles already on the mic. Seven months later Shane Douglas would throw down the NWA belt, and Eastern became Extreme.

items.title: Eastern Championship Wrestling (Mar. '94)
items.description: Still Eastern Championship Wrestling, an NWA affiliate in Philadelphia, five months before Shane Douglas would make it something else. A fan rebuilt this hour from broadcast audio and whatever video survived.

items.title: Eastern Championship Wrestling (Apr. '94)
items.description: Paul Heyman, booking ECW since 1993, shouts into a phone like the place is already his. Terry Funk and Arn Anderson talk up a tag, and a Singapore Caning Match is set for May 14.

items.title: Eastern Championship Wrestling (June '94)
items.description: Mick Foley is not yet Mankind; here he is Cactus Jack at the ECW Arena, with the Sandman and Woman brawling and Paul E. Dangerously getting the last word.

items.title: Eastern Championship Wrestling (July '94)
items.description: Shane Douglas, the Franchise, is weeks from throwing down the NWA title in Philadelphia and walking ECW out of the alliance. Here he's in the main event with the Ruffneck, still in the family.

items.title: Extreme Championship Wrestling (Aug. '94)
items.description: That same week Shane Douglas threw the NWA title down in Philadelphia, and Eastern was on its way to becoming Extreme. The show carries on regardless, 2 Cold Scorpio in the ring, a hotline ad in the break.

items.title: Extreme Championship Wrestling (Oct. '94)
items.description: A black-and-white farewell for the Sandman, shot like a movie, because ECW cut its TV like it knew you were taping it. Shane Douglas and 2 Cold Scorpio keep talking toward November to Remember II.

items.title: Extreme Championship Wrestling (Nov. '94)
items.description: Three months after Shane Douglas threw down the NWA belt and ECW decided to be its own thing, the TV hour is still finding its voice: Scorpio against Malenko, a Sandman promo, a ladder to close.

items.title: Mick Foley: Hard Knocks and Cheap Pops
items.description: Foley's first memoir reached number one on the New York Times list, so it's no surprise he can talk. Sitting inside a cage set, he explains how the best heel takes shreds of truth and turns them into something.

items.title: WCW Starrcade ('97)
items.description: WCW's year end card from the Starrcade desk through the main event, with the nWo clearing the ring and regrouping on the floor. The tape gives out a moment after the last bell, as its owner warns.

items.title: Neon Nights and Open Roads
items.description: A station wagon, a family, and every motel between here and the coast. The neon signs of NYC, Reno, and Las Vegas glow against the dark like postcards you mailed but never got back.

items.title: Mediterranean by Yacht
items.description: A European family drifts through the Greek islands and the Jordanian desert by yacht and by car, picnicking among ruins older than anyone's memory. The seventies never looked this timeless.

items.title: New York World's Fair Gardens and Neon at Night, 1939
items.description: A stranger filmed the World of Tomorrow in Kodachrome, gardens by day and neon after dark. The future looked great on color film, and the film has kept its end of the deal.

items.title: Southwest Family, Los Angeles Beaches
items.description: An LA family visits relatives scattered across the Southwest — Texas porches, mountain towns, and then back to the beach. The distances between them measured in sunburns and film stock.

items.title: Wartime Yosemite
items.description: Yosemite during the war, nearly empty. The Bay Bridge has no traffic. The Sierra Nevada belongs to whoever showed up. A national park in wartime silence, filmed like a secret.

items.title: Colorado Mountains and Wisconsin Dells
items.description: Colorado rock formations and a boat ride through the Wisconsin Dells. Two vacations spliced onto one reel, because that's how memory works — everything overlaps eventually.

items.title: Western States Road Trip, 1947
items.description: A road trip across the western states, shot by someone who never expected a stranger to watch. You're the passenger now, guessing the landmarks. Nobody in the car is going to tell you.

items.title: Alaska and Ketchikan, 1960
items.description: Fairbanks, Ketchikan and the wilderness between, shot by someone who labelled the box in shorthand and trusted the film to remember the rest. It mostly does.

items.title: Midwestern States Road Trip, 1961
items.description: The Midwest by car, state line by state line. It isn't the scenic half of America, which is why a family bothering to film it feels like a small gift. Watch for the barns.

items.title: Honolulu Statehood Celebration and a Sail off Waikiki
items.description: Tourists in Honolulu stumble into a statehood celebration at Iolani Palace. A newspaper boy holds up the headline. Then they go back to the beach, which is exactly what you would do.

items.title: Hawaii and Japan, 1957
items.description: The can says "1st Time Hawaii & Japan," and the film behaves like it: a camera pointed at everything, because everything is new. Take the window seat.

items.title: Pacific Palisades and San Francisco, 1929
items.description: Pacific Palisades and San Francisco at the end of the twenties. Telegraph Hill, the harbor, the steep streets. A city caught on film before it knew what it would become.

items.title: Detroit Family Travels, 1929
items.description: A Detroit family films its travels in the year of the crash. Nobody on screen knows what's coming, and the reel is kind enough not to tell them.

items.title: Canadian Rockies, Summer 1954
items.description: Summer in the Canadian Rockies, filmed by someone who wanted proof they'd stood there. They did. Seventy years on, you get to stand there too, which is the best trick home movies have.

items.title: Switzerland and France, 1938
items.description: A hike in the snowy Alps, then Paris: the Eiffel Tower and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The can just says EUROPE '38. It's silent, so you supply the footsteps.

items.title: Hawaii in the Fifties: Canyon, Beach, Crater
items.description: A 1950s tourist's Hawaii: Waikiki, the Royal Hawaiian, and a trip up to volcano country. The beach and the hotel are still there. The sunburns have long since faded, but the film kept them.

items.title: Nine States
items.description: Nine states in one reel. The Bicentennial summer of '76, seen through a windshield and a lens that tried to capture everything at once.

items.title: Around Arizona: Yuma Prison, Cacti and Death Valley
items.description: Yuma's old territorial prison, Montezuma Castle, the Casa Grande ruins, then Death Valley. The note on the can says 400 feet of film, and somebody spent every foot of it on Arizona.

items.title: Rose Parade and Crater Lake
items.description: Rose Parade floats, the blue water of Crater Lake, and all the stops in between. An Oregon reel that moves at the speed of a Sunday drive through the fifties.

items.title: The Rhine, the Swiss Alps and Versailles, 1920s
items.description: A Rhine cruise in the 1920s: the Heidelberg funicular, the Swiss Alps, a market in Bern, Versailles. Almost nobody is in frame, so it plays like the scenery is on vacation and you are the only guest.

items.title: Detroit and Milwaukee, 1951
items.description: Detroit celebrating its 200th anniversary and Milwaukee from above. Belle Isle ferries, downtown parades, and the Midwest putting on its best face for the camera.

items.title: San Francisco and Muir Woods
items.description: Boy Scout parades, a kids' party in the backyard, and then a trip to San Francisco — Muir Woods, the fog, the redwoods. Someone's dad filmed all of it and labeled the can carefully.

items.title: Honeymoon in Bermuda, 1956
items.description: Bermuda was the honeymoon destination of its day, and this couple filmed theirs. It's the most private footage on the station, and we're glad it ended up where anyone can sit in.

items.title: U.S. National Parks and the Philippines
items.description: A European family films California, Lake Placid and New York City in winter, then travels on to the Philippines and a dance performance. The itinerary is the plot, and it is a good one.

items.title: Peace Arch and Vancouver
items.description: A family crosses at Peace Arch with a Kodachrome camera in wartime, then walks Vancouver's Chinatown and downtown, uniforms everywhere in the frame. A postcard from a decade with a lot on its mind.

items.title: New Orleans and a Delta Queen Cruise, 1976
items.description: March aboard the Delta Queen: a peacock garden, sailing ships, and an alligator somebody wanted proof of. The can notes are shorthand only the filmmaker could read. We get the birds.

items.title: Japan by Cruise Ship, 1929
items.description: Tourists step off a cruise ship into temples, ceremonies and a long samurai parade, and join in wearing kimonos. Silent, and a very long way from home.

items.title: Wisconsin Fishing and Hiking, 1949
items.description: An Illinois couple heads north to Wisconsin for fall fishing and hiking. Golden light on the lake, goats climbing on a truck, and the quiet of the woods before winter sets in.

items.title: Europe by Ocean Liner
items.description: American women crossing the Atlantic on the Queen Mary, then touring England, Holland, and Switzerland. Early fifties Europe through wide eyes and a steady hand on the camera.

items.title: Boulder Dam, Las Vegas and the Grand Canyon, 1940s
items.description: It opens on a military airfield, then goes sightseeing: Boulder Dam, Las Vegas, the Grand Canyon. The can calls it 'August Vacation', and that covers it.

items.title: Yosemite and the Valley Road Trip
items.description: A Japanese American family sees Yosemite from Tunnel View, then visits vineyards and a rice farm run by people of Japanese heritage, maybe relatives. The valley is the postcard; the farms are the family.

items.title: Alaska in Winter
items.description: Alaska in winter — sled dog races, the railroad cutting through snow, ice skating, and the Fur Rendezvous festival in Anchorage. A frozen world that feels warmer the longer you watch.

items.title: Southern California Holidays and Hawai'i
items.description: A Southern California family through the seasons — Christmas morning, a parade in Lakewood, swimming pools in summer, and a trip to Hawai'i. The good years, all on one reel.

items.title: The Alps, Venice, and London
items.description: The Alps, the canals of Venice, the streets of London — all slightly soft-focus, like a memory that's beautiful precisely because it's fading.

items.title: Jamaica by Raft and Road
items.description: A raft trip down a Jamaican river, village streets, schoolchildren in the sun. Tourists with a camera, far from home, trying to hold onto a place they were only passing through.

items.title: Hawaii Volcanoes, Kona and Maui, 1963
items.description: A Japanese American family takes in the volcano, the black sand, a Kona motel, and a relative's grave on Maui. The can notes read like a receipt for a trip that mattered.

items.title: Taxco, New York, and the World's Fair
items.description: One reel, two very different stops: a Mexican silver town and the fairgrounds in Queens. Nobody explains the route, which is the pleasure of other people's slides. The fair is gone; the film isn't.

items.title: England, Scotland and Holland, 1938
items.description: Europe, per the container label: the Changing of the Guard, old stone across England and Scotland, and Holland a little while before the war. Tourist footage, which is its own kind of time capsule.

items.title: White Sands and Zion, 1960
items.description: Gypsum dunes that glow on film and red canyon walls that answer back, shot by a family that drove between two very different worlds. Silent, so the desert supplies the quiet.

items.title: A Bus Trip and a Small Zoo
items.description: A chartered bus, a small zoo, and people who seem perfectly happy with both. Sometimes the best trips are the ones with no particular destination in mind.

items.title: Louisiana to the Mississippi, 1950
items.description: From the LSU campus up to where the Mississippi meets the Ohio. A segregated Rosenwald school slides past on the way to Tennessee, and the camera keeps rolling. Nobody narrates it, so you do the noticing.

items.title: California Suburbs on the Move
items.description: California suburbs in the fifties — a road trip, a new house, the particular optimism of people moving somewhere the sun always shines. The boxes aren't unpacked yet.

items.title: Yellowstone Geysers and Roadside Bears, 1935
items.description: Yellowstone's geysers, plus black bears working the roadside beside a parked car. The can says "no people." The bears, as you will see, have a different view.

items.title: My Alaska Cruise, 1938
items.description: Alaska was a territory, not a state, when this traveler sailed north, and the title says "My" like it means it. A personal diary on film. Bring a coat.

items.title: Cross-Country to the Desert Southwest
items.description: Cross-country to the desert, a year before the Interstate Highway Act. This is the slow version of the trip, and the tape lets you take your time with it.

items.title: Yellowstone, Taiwan, Java and Iran
items.description: A couple takes a station wagon to Yellowstone, then the reel just keeps going: Iran, Taiwan, Java. Temples, bison, sand forts. The can says only "25," so naming the trip is up to you.

items.title: San Francisco, 1968
items.description: San Francisco in a year people mostly remember in headlines. Home movies remember it differently: the hills, and whatever the owner wanted to show the folks back home.

items.title: Hong Kong and China, about 1925
items.description: A westerner's trip through Kowloon and Hong Kong: crowded streets, British warships in Victoria Harbor. A traveler's view, and a narrow one, so watch what the camera chose to look at.

items.title: California Road Trip and Fishing
items.description: California in the forties — the coast, the open road, and a fishing spot that somebody loved enough to film. Sunlight on water and nowhere to be.

items.title: Pacific Coast Highway 101, 1957
items.description: Tacoma, down 101 through Oregon and California, rain in the forest, a drive through San Francisco. The can note reads like shorthand for a road trip, and the film fills in the rest.

items.title: Golden Gate International Exposition, 1940
items.description: The fair on Treasure Island, an island built in the bay for the occasion, caught in its second and last season. Most of the fair was torn down. This reel kept a visit.

items.title: Vacation to Oregon, 1968
items.description: Nobody was making history on this trip, just memories, which is the kind that sits in a closet for fifty years and then ends up here. Oregon, and someone who wanted to remember it.

items.title: St. Louis Family, Summers in the Fifties
items.description: A St. Louis family in the fifties — the airport, the lake, Grandpa's birthday, kids in the kiddie pool, and more Chevys than a dealership lot. The ordinary days that turn out to be the ones you remember.

items.title: Alaska From Above, 1959
items.description: Kodiak, Anchorage, Juneau and a lot of coastline in between, all through a plane window. Silent film suits it: the scale needs no help, and neither does the view.

items.title: Christmas Party to Mexico City
items.description: Christmas dancing, then Mexico City and Acapulco by car and pleasure boat. A family that knew how to celebrate, from the living room to the coast.

items.title: Rockies to New York
items.description: From the Rocky Mountains to New York, by way of every state in between. A fifties road trip that covers enough ground to fill a whole atlas.

items.title: Grand Canyon, Death Valley and Arizona Desert
items.description: The desert reel of a road trip: Hoover Dam, the Grand Canyon, Tonto ruins. The itinerary is written inside the can, so you can ride along as navigator.

items.title: Yellowstone and Rocky Mountain Road Trip
items.description: The can just says "Trip West," and that's the whole review. Yellowstone, then the Rockies, shot by someone who figured you'd understand why. You do.

items.title: Yellowstone, Summer 1963
items.description: Kodachrome kept its colors better than most film, so the geysers and hot springs look fresher than they have any right to. Steam, silence, and a rail to lean on.

items.title: Ontario Road Trip, 1955
items.description: A silent road trip through Ontario: highways, small towns, long stretches where nothing happens and the camera ran anyway. That's the good part. You decide where they're headed.

items.title: Las Vegas and the Desert Southwest
items.description: Las Vegas before the megaresorts, the desert Southwest before the interstates. Fifties neon and open highway, when the whole region still felt like a frontier.

items.title: California Landscapes, Farms, and Blimps
items.description: Forties California — farmland, coastline, and blimps drifting over the landscape like slow-moving dreams. Agriculture and aviation, side by side under the same sun.

items.title: Hawaii and Mexico, Chichen Itza to Xochimilco
items.description: Diamond Head and long-board surfing, then Chichen Itza, flower-covered boats at Xochimilco and a cliff diver. A tourist's reel, with the Kodak lab stamp still on the can.

items.title: Cape Ann and Gloucester, 1946
items.description: Gloucester has fished these waters for centuries, and painters came for the harbor light. A home movie shot just after the war files both under one afternoon, plus one brand-new camera.

items.title: Sun Valley and Banff, 1948
items.description: Sun Valley, Idaho, then Banff in the Canadian Rockies. The can says "Trip to Canada" and that is all the plot there is. Lodges and mountains, in the order somebody drove to them.

items.title: Rocky Mountains and Canada, 1962
items.description: Mountain passes and glacial lakes on both sides of the border, in silence. The camera holds a beat longer than it needs to, the way you do when you don't want to leave.

items.title: Southwest Vacation, 1947
items.description: Desert highways and red mesas, two years after the war. A free week, a car and a roll of film, all spent on dry country that still looks the same.

items.title: Russian River Vacation, 1960
items.description: Slow water, tall trees, a Northern California summer paced to a canoe. Some afternoons survive only because a camera was running. This is one of them.

items.title: Florida, 1968
items.description: Daytona Beach is one of the few places where driving on the sand was the attraction, and the camera rides along. The rest of the tour is gravy: palm trees, bright sun, a long quiet road.

items.title: Alaska by Air and Sea: Towns, Planes and Fishing Boats
items.description: Alaska by plane, boat and small town, with a long look at the fishing fleet. The uploader's description is one sentence long, so the film has to do the talking.

items.title: Manhattan, New England, and the Mackinac Bridge
items.description: Manhattan from a Circle Line boat, the UN, 30 Rock, then the long drive to Michigan — motels, roadside stops, and the Mackinac Bridge appearing out of the fog.

items.title: A New York Winter, 1956
items.description: A Christmas tree fetched from upstate, snow shoveled, a table full of relatives. The cold stays outside, in the shots anyway. Not much happens, and it's the warmest thing on this channel.

items.title: Cozumel, Havana and Miami by Yacht
items.description: A private yacht, unpaved streets in Cozumel, Havana's waterfront, and a Goodyear blimp ride to finish. Leisure at sea, silent, and nobody in a hurry to get anywhere.

items.title: Mexico and the Japanese Village, 1969
items.description: Guadalajara, Acapulco, a Vegas detour, then Buena Park's Japanese Village and Deer Park. The can lists the sisters and friends along for it. You never meet them, but you'd know them at a reunion.

items.title: By Motor Car Through the Alps
items.description: A postwar road trip through the Alps — the Grossglockner pass, Merano, the Danube valley, Nuremberg, and Garmisch. Europe still dusting itself off, already beautiful again.

items.title: Pacific Northwest to the Canadian Rockies, 1951
items.description: Olympic National Park, Grand Coulee Dam, Banff and Jasper: the itinerary of someone who meant to see everything and kept the reel as proof. It's silent, so you supply the 'look at that.'

items.title: Cabin at the Lake
items.description: A cabin at the lake, a birthday party, a Christmas tree. The kind of place a family goes back to every year until the kids grow up and the cabin gets sold to strangers.

items.title: Havana, Washington and the Train Home, 1929
items.description: The camera falls for the train. The Tehachapi Loop, where the track crosses over itself, gets the last stretch of a cruise-ship trip that began in Havana. Home movies, and the home stretch.

items.title: June Lake to Lassen, 1951
items.description: Reel 15, says the can, so somebody shot at least fourteen more. This one takes a family through June Lake, Mammoth Lakes, Lassen Park and Shasta Dam.

items.title: Western Scenics and Englewood, Colorado
items.description: Western scenics and the town of Englewood, Colorado. Wide-open landscapes and a small-town Main Street that probably still looks the same if you squint.

items.title: New York World's Fair Bakery, Fountains and Fireworks, 1939
items.description: A bakery, fountains and fireworks in a stranger's silent Kodachrome. The fair's wonders were many, and this person filmed the ones that make a good day. You can almost smell the bread.

items.title: Long Beach, 1950s
items.description: Long Beach in the 1950s. Sun, sand, and a family making the most of a Saturday afternoon. The Pacific Ocean doesn't care what year it is.

items.title: Vancouver and Coastal British Columbia, 1960
items.description: A cabin, a boat, and a note inside the can pointing at Vancouver. Sightseeing on the water, camping in the trees. It's a quiet trip, and the quiet is the reason to stay.

items.title: California Summer, 1962
items.description: Pool parties and beach days, filmed by someone who didn't know they were making a time capsule. Decades on, the sunlight is still doing most of the directing.

items.title: Michigan to the Redwoods
items.description: A Michigan family of older adults drives west to the California redwoods. U.S. 101, Paul Bunyan statues, and the arid interior on the way home. The road trip as retirement gift.

items.title: Death Valley and the Eastern Sierra, 1938
items.description: Wildflowers along a road to Death Valley and the High Sierras, in May and June. The film shrank and scratched with age and couldn't be scanned whole, so this is the part that made it home.

items.title: East Coast in Autumn and Winter
items.description: A Midwestern family heads east for fall foliage and keeps going through winter. The Adirondacks, a farm visit, aerials of the Capitol mall, and the Jefferson Memorial still under construction. America mid-century, mid-build.

items.title: Army Family Road Trips and Double Exposures
items.description: An Army family on the road in the fifties, filming everything with an artsy eye and a taste for double exposures. The landscapes blur together the way they do when you've moved too many times.

items.title: Yellowstone Geysers and Old Faithful
items.description: A Yellowstone road trip where the sky steals the reel: storm clouds, a jet's contrail and Old Faithful, filmed again and again. Somebody was not going to miss it a second time.

items.title: New England Beach Town
items.description: A New England beach town in the forties. Boardwalk, salt water, sand between your toes, and the quiet rhythm of a summer that hasn't changed since your grandparents were young.

items.title: Sitka and a Juneau Parade
items.description: Sitka's streets, then a Juneau parade with a Baker's Dozen float: thirteen women in baker's hats. Somebody counted. The reel label lists more stops, so the trip keeps going.

items.title: Maryland Snow and the Shore
items.description: Maryland under fresh snow, then the beach. Winter and summer on the same reel, because someone wanted to remember both. The seasons pass in a few frames.

items.title: Western States Road Trip, 1930s
items.description: The western states in the 1930s, before the interstates, before the motels had neon signs. Unpaved roads, vast horizons, and a country that was still mostly empty.

items.title: Norway, Venice, and Switzerland
items.description: Norway's fjords, Venice's canals, Switzerland's peaks — three countries on one reel, each one a different shade of breathtaking. The grand tour, condensed to twenty minutes.

items.title: San Francisco Bay and Waterfront
items.description: San Francisco Bay in the 1940s. The waterfront, the boats, the fog rolling in. A city built on water, filmed by someone who loved watching it from the shore.

items.title: East Coast Road Trip, 1951
items.description: New York, Washington and Detroit, with the miles between them left in. The monuments are famous; the long stretch of highway in between is rarely on film, and it's the best part.

items.title: Michigan Family Goes Cross-Country
items.description: A Michigan family loads the car and drives across the country in the forties. Every state a new reel, every reel a new landscape. The odometer doesn't lie.

items.title: Bahamas and Florida, 1950
items.description: From the Bahamas up through Florida: palms, water, and a trip that clearly went the way someone hoped. A short escape, on film, for anyone who needs one today.

items.title: Italy 1948: Rome, the Palio, Venice and Pompeii
items.description: James Zellerbach and family sail the Queen Mary for Europe, ride on to Rome, then Siena for the Palio and Venice for the regatta. Home movies, with Italian newsreel spliced in.

items.title: California Life With Swimming Pool
items.description: California in the sixties, with a swimming pool in the backyard. Suburban paradise — kids splashing, adults lounging, and the sun doing what the sun does out there.

items.title: Southern California Family Days
items.description: A Southern California family in the sixties, doing what families do — beach trips, backyard afternoons, the everyday rituals that only matter to the people in them.

items.title: A Texas Family Farm
items.description: A Texas family farm in the 1950s. The farmyard, the family lined up for the camera, and the quiet pride of people who built something with their hands.

items.title: Alaska's Matanuska Valley
items.description: Alaska's Matanuska Valley — farmland carved out of wilderness, mountains on every horizon, and the endless daylight of a northern summer. The last frontier, tamed just enough.

items.title: Kamakura, Nara and Snowy Japan, circa 1925
items.description: The Great Buddha at Kotoku-in, the deer of Nara Park and a busy train station, filmed by tourists about a century ago. The deer are still the best part of Nara.

items.title: Adirondacks Trip, 1940s
items.description: The Adirondacks in the forties. Forest trails, lake views, and someone's mom holding a rifle like she knows exactly what she's doing. Vacation, but make it resourceful.

items.title: Kashmir: Delhi, Houseboats and a Glacier
items.description: Floating markets, boat tours and horseback rides up into the mountains. The can says only one word, Kashmir, and it turns out that was enough.

items.title: A Los Angeles Beach Family
items.description: A Los Angeles family at the beach in the fifties. Cookouts, kids in the sand, friends stopping by. The good life, California-style, no filter needed.

items.title: Travels in California
items.description: Pasadena roses, the Huntington Gallery, Santa Barbara, Seal Rocks, Monterey, Yosemite — a California grand tour on a single reel. Every stop a postcard, every postcard perfect.

items.title: Canadian Waterways and Canoe Camping
items.description: Canadian waterways in the 1930s. Canoe camping, still lakes, and the kind of wilderness that swallows sound. Just the paddle, the water, and whatever's on the far shore.

items.title: Arizona from the Air, Then Catalina
items.description: A couple sees Arizona from the air, then lands on Catalina Island and the Santa Monica shore. The can just says CALIFORNIA, as if nobody expected strangers to ask which part. Consider this us asking.
